## Seeded from PLAN §19

- **D1** Tauri 2 over Electron/Electrobun — smallest mature option.
- **D2** Vanilla TS, no framework — size, tweakability, AI legibility; leaks handled by `DisposableStore`.
- **D3** esbuild over Vite — speed, one dependency.
- **D4** Monaco over CodeMirror 6 — diff editor, familiarity, LSP-shaped providers; lazy-loaded.
- **D5** Git CLI over gix — zero size; gix lacks push/full clone/rebase/reset.
- **D6** Dispatcher in frontend host; Rust services underneath; external clients forwarded.
- **D7** Small core agent toolset + discovery meta-tools — local models can't handle hundreds of tools.
- **D8** ACP + MCP for external agents and tools.
- **D9** All network via Rust — CORS, key safety, enforceable extension permissions.
- **D10** Browser via injecting proxy + iframe until Tauri multiwebview is stable.
- **D11** Agent default edit mode = changeset review; auto-apply is a per-session toggle.
- **D12** No product name in code; `product.json` is the single source.
- **D13** Closed source; permissive-license dependencies only.
- **D14** Persistence = JSON/JSONC/JSONL files with atomic writes and versioned schemas.
- **D15** Biome for lint/format; `node --test` for TS tests (no test framework dependency).

## Milestone 1 — Walking skeleton

### D16 — Spike 1: editor = `monaco-editor-core` + `@shikijs/monaco` (documented fallback), not modern-monaco
*Deviation from PLAN §3/§10.* Checked against modern-monaco 0.4.2 source (`dist/core.mjs`,
`dist/shiki.mjs`, `dist/cache.mjs`) and its README:

- The editor core is loaded with `import(url)` where the URL defaults to `https://esm.sh/...` and can
  only be redirected with an inline `<script type="importmap">`. That needs an inline script under
  our CSP and keeps the 7.6 MB editor core outside the esbuild bundle (not code-split, not minified with the app).
- Grammars and themes are fetched from a CDN (`cdn` option, default esm.sh) through a cache layer that
  writes to **IndexedDB** whenever it exists — PLAN §9.4 forbids app state in IndexedDB (workers share the origin).
  Avoiding it means emulating esm.sh's URL layout (`/tm-grammars@<ver>/grammars/<id>.json`) inside our bundle.
- Shiki defaults to the **Oniguruma WASM** engine; PLAN §3 wants the JavaScript regex engine.
- Its TS/CSS/HTML/JSON language services also load through importmap URLs (and `typescript` from a CDN).

It *can* be forced offline, but not cleanly, so per KICKOFF we took the fallback behind the same
`EditorEngine` interface (`src/extensions/editor/engine.ts`):

- `monaco-editor-core` 0.57.0 (MIT; deps `marked` MIT, `dompurify` MPL-2.0/Apache-2.0), bundled by esbuild
  as its own entry (`assets/monaco.js` + `monaco.css`), imported only after the shell paints.
- `@shikijs/monaco` 4.5.0 (MIT, 9 KB) + `shiki` 4.5.0 core (MIT) with `createJavaScriptRegexEngine` (no WASM).
- Token colors come from our own `src/styles/themes/vs-dark.json` (`tokenColors` = Dark+), so UI and syntax
  colors share one VS Code-format theme file.
- 38 curated grammars, each a lazy chunk loaded on first use (`monaco/grammars.ts`). Unknown files → plaintext.
- Editor worker = separate classic-script entry (`dist/workers/editor.worker.js`).

**Proved in the real app** (Tauri debug build with the production CSP, Linux/WebKitGTK under Xvfb): a `.ts` file
read through the Rust `fs_read` command (raw bytes) renders with Dark+ highlighting; no network access.

**Cost:** no TS/JS/CSS/JSON IntelliSense in M1 (modern-monaco's built-in LSP providers). These come back via
the LSP host in M3 (or Monaco's language workers if we decide that's cheaper). Logged as an M2/M3 item.

### D17 — Spike 2: terminal = ghostty-web 0.4.0 + portable-pty 0.9 over a Tauri Channel (no fallback needed)
- ghostty-web (MIT, zero deps) embeds its 423 KB WASM as a `data:` URL and compiles it with `WebAssembly.compile`.
  CSP therefore allows `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (script-src) and `data:` in `connect-src` (a `fetch` of the embedded
  bytes; not network).
- PTY output is sent as raw bytes (`InvokeResponseBody::Raw`) over a `Channel`; the exit is one JSON message.
  Flow control: the frontend acks bytes after they are painted (`pty_ack`); Rust pauses reading above 512 KB
  unacknowledged and resumes below 128 KB (same idea as VS Code), so floods can't swamp the webview.
- Output is decoded with a streaming `TextDecoder` before `term.write()` so multi-byte characters survive chunk
  boundaries and ghostty's OSC title detection (string-only) works.
- **Proved in the real app:** interactive login shell (bash), ANSI colors, `ü 日本語 🎉`, `$TERM=xterm-256color`,
  `$COLUMNS` matching the fitted size.

### D18 — CSP details
`default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:;
font-src 'self' data:; connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost data:; worker-src 'self'; object-src 'none';
base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-src 'none'`. No remote origins anywhere.
- `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`: Monaco and ghostty create `<style>` elements and inline styles at runtime.
  `dangerousDisableAssetCspModification: ["style-src"]` stops Tauri adding a nonce there (a nonce would make
  browsers ignore `'unsafe-inline'`). Scripts keep Tauri's default (nonces/hashes, no inline scripts).
- `devCsp` additionally allows `http://localhost:1420` for esbuild's live-reload event stream.

### D19 — Generated files are git-ignored and regenerated by every npm script
`scripts/gen.mjs` derives `src/core/product.ts` and `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` from `product.json` (+
`src-tauri/tauri.base.json`), and `src/styles/tokens.css` from `src/styles/themes/vs-dark.json`. It runs on
`postinstall` and before `dev`, `build`, `check` and every frontend build, so they can't drift. Cargo-only
workflows need `npm run gen` once (README).

### D20 — App data location
Tauri's `app_data_dir()` / `app_config_dir()`, which are derived from `identifier` in `product.json`. So data
folders still follow `product.json`; `dataFolderName` stays reserved for a future dotfolder in the home dir.

### D21 — File watching watches the explorer's expanded folders, non-recursively
*Refines PLAN §3 "notify + debouncer".* Recursive watches on big repos exhaust inotify limits on Linux and cost
memory everywhere; M1 only needs explorer refresh. The explorer sends its expanded folders (`watch_set_dirs`);
Rust watches each non-recursively with `notify-debouncer-full` (150 ms) and sends batches over a Channel. M2's
"watcher-driven reload" adds open files to the watched set.

### D22 — TypeScript 7 (native compiler)
`typescript@7.0.2` is current on npm; `tsc --noEmit` is all we use it for and it is much faster. Two configs:
`tsconfig.json` (app, DOM types only) and `tsconfig.test.json` (tests, adds Node types), so Node globals never
leak into app code.

### D23 — Explorer shows ignored files dimmed (not hidden)
`fs_list_dir` walks one level with `ignore` (respects `.gitignore`/`.ignore`, also outside git repos) and
flags matches as `ignored` instead of dropping them — VS Code behavior; you can still open `dist/`.
`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db` are always hidden (VS Code's default `files.exclude`).

### D24 — Spike 3: baseline (Linux x86-64, measured in the dev VM)
Measured 2026-10-17 on a 2-vCPU VM, Xvfb + software rendering (no GPU), WebKitGTK 2.52. Re-measure on a
real laptop for each OS — these numbers are an upper bound for Linux, not a laptop benchmark.

| Metric | Value | Budget (PLAN §13) |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend `dist/` total | 7.86 MB (1.76 MB gzip) | — |
| Loaded before first paint (index.html + main.js + main.css) | 136 KB | — |
| Monaco bundle (`monaco.js` + `.css`, loaded after paint) | 3.99 MB + 182 KB | — |
| ghostty-web chunk (incl. embedded WASM, loaded on first terminal) | 623 KB | — |
| Release binary (`target/release/ide`, assets embedded) | 16.5 MB | — |
| `.deb` / `.rpm` installer | 5.53 MB / 5.54 MB | < 20 MB ✅ |
| Cold start → shell visible (process start → 2nd animation frame) | 310–350 ms typical; ~800 ms in 2 of 5 runs | < 500 ms (laptop) |
| Cold start → editor interactive (Monaco + Shiki ready) | 0.79–1.32 s | < 1.5 s ✅ |
| Navigation start → shell visible | ~53 ms | — |
| 20 000-file folder expanded | visible in < 0.6 s, smooth scrolling | < 1 s ✅ |
| Terminal flood `yes \| head -n 2000000` (debug build) | 3.7 s, UI stayed responsive | responsive ✅ |

The ~800 ms outliers come before our code runs (dbus/a11y session start-up per launch in the VM);
navigation → paint stayed ~50 ms. Timings come from `dev.perfReport` / `ide://dev/perf` (a release build
made with `node build.mjs --prod --with-dev`, so the binary is optimized but the dev commands exist).
Windows and macOS installers were not built in this environment.

### D25 — Zero network verified at the OS level
Besides the CSP (no remote origins), a full session (open folder and file, terminal, palette, state dump)
was traced with `strace -f -e trace=connect` across all 45 app/WebKit processes and threads: only
`AF_UNIX` sockets (X11, D-Bus, nscd). No `AF_INET`/`AF_INET6` connections.

### D26 — Audit entries include a small output summary
`AuditEntry.output` (fitted to 500 JSON chars) next to `input` (1 000), so the log says what a command
did (e.g. which file `explorer.delete` removed when it used the selection). Nested commands
(`terminal.toggle` → `view.show` → `terminal.create`) are logged individually with the same caller.

### D27 — Built-in extension tier and the `workbench` built-in
Built-ins are `extension.json` manifest + `activate(ctx)` with privileged `WorkbenchServices`. Layout,
view and window commands live in a `builtin.workbench` extension so even the shell's own actions are
contributed the same way (keybindings come only from manifests). All M1 built-ins activate at startup
(`"activation": ["*"]`); lazy activation events arrive with third-party extensions (M6).

### D28 — Palette lists every enabled command, prompting for required inputs
Instead of hiding commands that need arguments, the palette asks for each required field of the
command's input schema (enums as a pick list). Optional fields are left to the command's defaults
(e.g. Rename uses the explorer selection). This keeps "every command is reachable by a human" true.

### D29 — Paths in command inputs may be relative to the workspace
`editor.openFile`, `explorer.*`, `terminal.create` accept absolute paths or paths relative to the
workspace root (`resolveInRoot`), which is what models naturally produce. State paths report relative
paths (plus `absolutePath` for the active editor). Rust still scope-checks every resolved path.

### D30 — Lucide icons via a generated sprite (dev dependency `lucide-static`, ISC)
`scripts/build-icons.mjs` copies only the listed icons into `src/ui/icons/sprite.svg` (5.5 KB, committed).
`lucide-static` is a devDependency used only by that script; nothing from it ships except the sprite.

### D31 — Natural sort and file-type icons in the explorer
Listing order matches VS Code: folders first, then case-insensitive natural order (`file-2` < `file-10`),
done in Rust (`fs/sort.rs`). File icons are a small extension → icon map (`fileIcon` in `ui/Icon.ts`).

### D32 — Unsaved-changes and window-close flow
Closing a dirty tab asks Save / Don't Save / Cancel (native dialog). Closing the window (title-bar button,
Alt+F4, Cmd+Q) and switching folders ask once for all dirty tabs (`WorkspaceService.onWillClose`), then
flush per-workspace state. All pty processes are killed on app exit (`RunEvent::Exit`).

## Milestone 1.5

### D33 — Design tokens are hand-authored; the VS Code-derived token generation is retired
`src/styles/tokens.css` is DESIGN.md Appendix A verbatim plus two additions: the terminal ANSI palette
(§15.4) as `--terminal-ansi-*` component tokens and `--syntax-theme` (`dark-plus` / `light-plus`, read
by the editor). `vs-dark.json` and its generator are gone. `scripts/check-colors.mjs` (part of
`npm run check`) fails on any hex/rgb/hsl value in `src/` outside `tokens.css`, `styles/themes/` and
`core/themes/`. The VS Code importer stays as a tested DOM-free mapper (`core/themes/importer.ts`,
§19 table) applied at runtime by `ThemeService.setOverrides`; there is no UI to load a theme file yet.

### D34 — Appearance state and commands
`ThemeService` sets `data-theme` / `data-density` / `data-panels` on `<html>` and fires a change event
one frame later (consumers re-read computed tokens). Commands: `ui.setTheme`, `ui.toggleTheme`,
`ui.setDensity`, `ui.setPanelStyle`, plus `ui.showAppearanceMenu` (⚙ in the activity bar) and
`ui.showAppMenu` (☰ in the title bar). Preferences live in global `state.json` (`saveGlobal` now
merges keys instead of overwriting); a copy in `localStorage` is read synchronously at boot so the
first paint already has the right theme. Reduced motion follows `prefers-reduced-motion`; a
`data-motion` toggle is in the tokens but has no command yet.

### D35 — Monaco theme = Shiki syntax theme + token colors, re-applied live
Shiki loads `dark-plus` and `light-plus`. `editorThemeFromTokens` resolves ~60 Monaco color keys from
computed tokens (§15.1, alpha tokens as `#rrggbbaa`) and the engine redefines the Monaco theme under
the syntax theme's own name, merged over Shiki's colors, then calls the Shiki-wrapped `setTheme` so
the tokenizer's color map switches too. Re-run on every theme/override change. Fix of a latent M1
issue: `shikiToMonaco` wraps `monaco.editor.setTheme`/`create` on every call (we call it after each
grammar loads), so the originals are restored before each call instead of stacking wrappers.
Editor defaults per §15.1: minimap off, sticky scroll (3), no bracket colorization, line cursor 2px,
no smooth caret, padding-top 8, 13px / 1.6.

### D36 — Editor: one Monaco editor per tab over shared documents
`EditorService` now owns *documents* (one per file, ref-counted by the tabs showing it); each editor tab
is a dock view with its own Monaco editor and view state. A split edits the same model, dirty state is
per document, and the Save / Don't save / Cancel prompt appears only when the last tab of a dirty
document closes. Documents load without Monaco: until the engine is ready a tab shows the first 40
lines as plain mono text (§16). Line endings: Monaco keeps a file's EOL (CRLF stays CRLF on save), new
or single-line files are LF; the status bar shows it and `ide://editors` reports it. Documents are
keyed by `pathKey` (case-insensitive, `/`≡`\` for Windows paths). Renames keep content, dirty state
and tabs (the tab's persisted path follows). `editor.nextTab/previousTab` became `layout.nextTab/
previousTab` (any view type), and Ctrl/Cmd+W is `layout.closeTab`.

### D37 — The dock: model, renderer and commands
DOM-free tree operations in `src/core/dock/` (unit-tested), `DockModel`/`DockService` (state, live
views, operations; unit-tested with fake views) and the DOM in `src/workbench/dock/`. The renderer
rebuilds splits only when the tree's *shape* changes (directions, group ids, hidden flags) and
otherwise just updates flex sizes, so moving a tab or resizing never recreates views. Group elements
and view elements are moved, not rebuilt. Commands beyond docs/dock.md §7: `layout.focusTab`,
`layout.setSplitSizes` (splitter commits, hidden from the palette), `layout.toggleRegion` (title-bar
toggles), `layout.togglePanel` (Ctrl/Cmd+J), `layout.focusAgent` (Ctrl/Cmd+L), `layout.nextTab` /
`previousTab`, and argument-free wrappers `layout.focusGroup.<dir>` / `layout.moveTabToGroup.<dir>`
for keybindings. Placement inputs use a new schema `union` (JSON Schema `anyOf`).
Details: *regions* are geometric — "right" = groups touching the dock's top and right edges but not
its left, "bottom" = touching the bottom but not the top, never groups holding editors; hidden groups
keep their sizes so restore returns them unchanged. Ctrl/Cmd+J never hides a group that also holds
editors (it toggles between that tab and the last editor instead). `welcome` is an editor-like
singleton that closes when an editor opens. Views can be transient (`persist(): false`: read-only
state dumps, the iframe test view) and are dropped on save. Restored terminal tabs start a new shell.

### D38 — Live terminal re-theming by rebuilding ghostty's VT core and replaying output (superseded by D48)
ghostty-web 0.4 resolves default colors into cells when the WASM terminal is created; neither
`options.theme` after `open()` nor OSC 10/11/4 recolor existing cells (tested). On a theme change
each terminal therefore sets the new theme, calls `reset()` (new VT core, same pty), updates the
canvas renderer's colors and replays its recent raw output (up to 2 MB ≈ the 10k-line scrollback),
then forces a full repaint. The shell is untouched; full-screen apps redraw on their next update.
Density/panel changes don't trigger it (colors compared first). The same rebuild runs 200 ms after
the column count changes: ghostty-web 0.4's reflow onto a wider grid duplicated the tails of wrapped
lines in testing (a forced full repaint didn't help, so it is in the buffer), while a replay lays the
text out correctly. Also, ghostty-web focuses itself in `open()`; we suppress that so background tabs
(restored or default terminals) don't steal focus. Remove both workarounds when ghostty-web fixes them.

### D39 — In-app dialogs instead of native message boxes
Save changes and destructive confirmations now use `ui/Dialog.ts` (§12.10: themed, primary action
rightmost on every platform, Escape/scrim cancel, focus trap). The native folder picker stays.
`dialog:allow-message/ask/confirm` were removed from the capability.

### D40 — Startup timings in every build
`workbench.startupTimings` ("Show startup timings", also in the Appearance menu) shows a toast:
process start → shell visible → extensions active → folder restored → editor ready, and `ide://perf`
returns the phases. Replaces the dev-only `dev.perfReport` / `ide://dev/perf`, because the numbers
that matter (Windows cold start) come from release builds on users' machines.

### D41 — Windows hardening
- **Shell:** `pwsh.exe` on PATH → `%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`
  → `%ComSpec%` → `cmd.exe`, PowerShells with `-NoLogo` (pure selection function, unit-tested on all OSes).
  ConPTY via portable-pty as before; env (`TERM`, `COLORTERM`), cwd and resize unchanged.
- **Paths:** canonicalized `\\?\C:\…` and `\\?\UNC\server\share\…` are simplified for display and
  comparison (`simplify_verbatim`, tested); long paths keep working because Rust's std re-adds the
  verbatim prefix internally beyond MAX_PATH. TS side: `pathKey`/`samePath`/`isWithin`/`rebase`
  compare Windows paths case-insensitively with either separator; UNC roots handled in
  `dirname`/`basename`; agent paths like `C:/x` are normalized to `C:\x`; `displayPath` uses `\`.
- **Watcher:** notify's `ReadDirectoryChangesW` backend reports renames as from/to events; both
  parents refresh. No change needed beyond review; covered by manual test §9.
- **WebView2 accelerators:** Tauri 2.12 doesn't expose `AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled`, but
  WebView2 skips its accelerators when the page cancels the keydown. `browserDefaults.ts` cancels
  Ctrl+P/F/G/R/J/H/U/S/O/N/T/D, F3/F5/F7/F12, Ctrl+Shift+I/J/C/R/… and Alt+←/→ in the bubble phase
  when nothing in the IDE handled them, and suppresses the browser context menu outside text fields.
- **Title bar:** custom controls (close hover uses `--status-danger-fg`), maximize ↔ restore glyph
  follows the window state, drag region + double-click maximize via Tauri's drag region.
  *Snap layouts* (the flyout when hovering maximize) need the native caption button hit-test
  (`HTMAXBUTTON`), which Tauri 2.12 can't provide for undecorated windows — `Win+Z` and
  `Win+arrows` still work. Proposal: revisit when Tauri adds it (tauri-apps/tauri#4531).
- **Scaling and color scheme:** Tauri's manifest is per-monitor-v2 DPI aware; ghostty-web scales its
  canvas by `devicePixelRatio`; `color-scheme` follows the IDE theme. Window background is now
  `--bg-app` (#111214) to avoid a flash.
- **Installer:** NSIS, per-user (`installMode: currentUser`), lzma; WebView2 bootstrapper is
  downloaded at install time only when missing (silent). Not built in this Linux environment, and the
  Windows-only Rust branches could not be compiled here (no Windows target available offline) —
  they are small and reviewed, but need a first Windows build to confirm.

### D42 — Explorer opens files on mouse release
So dragging a file onto the dock doesn't also open it where it was. Row height follows `--size-row`
(the tree rebuilds when density changes, keeping expanded folders).

### D43 — Dev-only automation handle
Dev builds expose `window.__ide = { dispatcher, state, dock, theme }` so UI smoke tests can drive
commands and read state from Playwright (Chromium) against `build.mjs --with-dev` output. Production
builds don't include it (`__DEV__`).

### D44 — Sentence case command titles
All built-in command titles and menu labels were converted to sentence case (DESIGN.md §4.3, §17),
e.g. "Toggle sidebar", "New terminal", "Open folder…".

### Sizes after M1.5 (vs D24)
| | M1 (D24) | M1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend total (`dist/`) | 7.86 MB (1.76 MB gzip) | 7.94 MB (1.78 MB gzip) |
| Initial shell (index.html + main.js + main.css) | 136 KB | 214 KB (63 KB gzip) |
| `monaco.js` | 3.99 MB | 4.00 MB |
| ghostty-web chunk | 623 KB | 623 KB |
| Release binary (Linux x86-64) | 16.5 MB | 16.6 MB |
| `.deb` / `.rpm` | 5.53 / 5.54 MB | 5.55 / 5.55 MB |

The shell grew by the dock (tree, renderer, drag and drop), the design system CSS, menus, dialogs and
the layout/appearance commands; it is still loaded before anything else and Monaco stays out of it.
Startup in the release build (same VM, software rendering, 3 runs): process start → webview started
~730 ms (dbus/a11y session start-up in the VM, before our code) → shell visible ~830 ms (~95 ms after
the webview starts) → folder restored ~970 ms → editor ready ~1.5 s. On Windows, expect the WebView2
process start-up to dominate a cold start (first launch after boot); `workbench.startupTimings`
reports it on real machines.

### DESIGN.md: deviations and proposals
1. **Snap layouts flyout** — not achievable with Tauri's custom title bar today (D41). Proposal: keep
   the custom title bar; accept `Win+Z`.
2. **File icon tints** (§9: "desaturated language hue at ~70%") have no tokens. Icons are monochrome
   `--fg-muted` for now. Proposal: add `--file-icon-{ts,js,rust,json,md,…}` component tokens to
   Appendix A (both themes) so the hues are reviewed with the palette.
3. **Unfocused group's active tab**: §12.3 says `--fg-default`, §1.2 says inactive groups dim to muted.
   Implemented §12.3 (the accent underline is the focus signal). Proposal: state in §12.3 which wins.
4. **Scrollbar fade-out after 800 ms** (§10) is approximated in CSS (thumb visible on hover/scroll
   container hover) — no JS timers per scroll container. Proposal: accept the CSS-only version.
5. **Light theme raised surface** = `#FFFFFF (+ border)`: active tabs get a 1px `--border-default`
   ring in light mode so they don't vanish on the white group surface.
6. **Not yet built** (no deviation, just later): tab FLIP reorder and `--ease-spring` landing,
   overflow menu button on tab strips, tree indent guides on hover, activity-bar hover-hold label
   flyout, tooltip component (native `title` for now), skeleton rows, breadcrumbs, webview token
   stylesheet injection (§20.1).

### Proposed scope for Milestone 2 (as of M1.5; kept for history, M2 shipped)
(From PLAN §16, refined by what M1 and M1.5 showed.)
1. **Settings & keybindings files**: `settings.json` / `keybindings.json` (JSONC, user + workspace),
   `editor.*`/`terminal.*`/`workbench.colorCustomizations` settings; theme import UI on top of the
   existing importer.
2. **Quick open** (`Ctrl/Cmd+P`) over a Rust file index (`ignore` walk, streamed over a Channel).
3. **Search/replace** (`grep-searcher`, streamed results) as a `search` dock view.
4. **Watcher-driven reload** of open documents (clean → reload, dirty → conflict banner, §12.12).
5. **Terminal shell integration** (OSC 133 for bash/zsh/fish/pwsh, ANSI-stripped ring buffer,
   `ide://terminals/<id>/commands`); restored terminals could replay their last output.
6. **Command-script test runner** (`--run-test-script`, `caller: test`) + CI on 3 OSes; promote the
   dev Playwright smoke (D43) to CI.
7. **MCP server** exposing `agent: core|discoverable` commands as tools and state paths as resources.
8. **Monaco language workers** for TS/JS, JSON, CSS and HTML, bundled offline and lazy-loaded per
   language (no CDN); `problems` dock view fed by their diagnostics.
9. Startup timings (`ide://perf`) checked in CI against the PLAN §13 budgets, on Windows too.

## Milestone 1.6

### D45 — DESIGN.md v2 adopted as written
Tokens are Appendix A of DESIGN.md v2 verbatim (neutral grays, one blue accent, `--accent-text`,
`--file-icon-*`), plus the terminal ANSI and `--syntax-theme` tokens kept from M1.5. Active tab and
active activity-bar item = `--bg-surface-raised` fill (no underline, no accent bar); the caret and
cursor are `--fg-default`; the accent appears only where §3.3 allows (focus ring, primary button,
active selection in a focused list, links, checkboxes/switches when on). Every clickable control
has `cursor: pointer`. Monaco and xterm colors are derived from the same tokens and re-applied live.

### D46 — Layout can never grow past the window
Every grid/flex child in the workbench and dock has `min-width: 0` / `min-height: 0`; `html`, `body`
and the workbench root are `overflow: hidden`. Tab strips scroll sideways (wheel → horizontal, 4px
scrollbar, active tab kept in view), group actions and a "⋯ All tabs" menu stay pinned at the right.
The title bar is the §10.1 grid; two adjustments: (1) the command field column is
`minmax(160px, min(560px, 44%))` — with a plain `560px` maximum, a 640px window gave the field all
free space and the app menu and workspace name collapsed to 0px; (2) menu items collapse into ☰ when
they *measurably* don't fit next to a 96px workspace name (ResizeObserver), instead of a fixed
container breakpoint, because label widths depend on font and locale. Consequence: at 1280px the
menus live in ☰; they appear inline from ~1460px. Regression: `dev.checkLayoutOverflow` (80 tabs,
640×480 and back; checks `scrollWidth/scrollHeight ≤ inner size` and that the close button is
on-screen). It passed in the Linux debug build; it becomes a command-script test in M2 (B8).

### D47 — Flush panels are the default; the old preference is dropped once
M1.5 stored theme/density/panels in global state (`ui`). On first start of M1.6 theme and density
move into user `settings.json` (only non-default values), the panel style is *not* carried over
(everyone starts on flush, as v2 specifies), and `ui` is removed from global state.

### D48 — Terminal renderer: ghostty-web → @xterm/xterm 6 + addon-fit (MIT); D38 retired
The Windows report (terminal grows, scrollbar creeps, ding) traced back to ghostty-web 0.4: no
reflow-safe resize (D38's rebuild-and-replay after every column change), no live re-theming (D38's
reset + replay), and resize feedback between its canvas and the container. No newer ghostty-web
release fixes these, so the documented fallback from PLAN §3 is used: `@xterm/xterm` 6.0.0 with
`@xterm/addon-fit` 0.11.0 (both MIT). xterm reflows on resize and applies `options.theme` live, so
both D38 workarounds are deleted. Size: the lazy terminal chunk is 336 KB (86 KB gzip) instead of
ghostty-web's 623 KB; xterm's CSS (5 KB) is in the shell stylesheet. Resize loop prevention: the host
is `position: relative; overflow: hidden; min-height: 0`, fits are coalesced to one per animation
frame, the size is clamped to ≥ 2×1, and the pty is resized only when cols/rows actually change.
`windowsPty: { backend: "conpty" }` is set on Windows so xterm handles ConPTY's reflow quirks.

### D49 — The Windows "ding": cause and `terminal.bell`
ghostty-web has no audio code, so the sound came from the shell: PSReadLine's default
`BellStyle Audible` calls `Console.Beep` (a real system sound under ConPTY) when it gets input it
can't use — here the floods of resize/replay sequences from D38 arriving while PowerShell redrew
its prompt. Removing D38 removes the trigger. The IDE now owns the bell: `BEL` from the program
fires xterm's `onBell`, and `terminal.bell` = `none` (default) | `visual` (the tab pulses) |
`sound` (a short quiet WebAudio tone). Shell integration (M2 B7) will additionally set
`Set-PSReadLineOption -BellStyle None` in PowerShell sessions it starts, so PSReadLine's own beep
can't bypass the setting.

### D50 — Settings: contributed schemas, two JSONC files, live reload
Settings are declared in manifests (`contributes.settings`: type, default, description, enum,
min/max, scope, order) and collected into a registry. Values: defaults < user
(`<config dir>/settings.json`) < workspace (`<folder>/.ide/settings.json`, the folder name from
`product.json`). Invalid values fall through to the next layer and are reported in
`ide://settings`; a file with a syntax error keeps its previous values while it's being typed.
Writes edit the JSONC text in place (comments and ordering survive). The Rust side allows the config
dir's `settings.json` / `keybindings.json` exactly (no other path outside the workspace) and watches
both locations. The settings editor is a singleton dock tab; `settings.set` / `settings.reset` /
`settings.openJson` are commands (agents can use them). Theme, density, panel style, sticky scroll,
terminal bell, auto reveal, font sizes, preview tabs are settings; `ui.setTheme` & co. write them.
Theme/density/panels are also cached in localStorage purely so the first paint matches.

### D51 — Explorer selection model, preview tabs, moves
Trees keep a selection *set* plus a focused row (pure `TreeSelection`, tested): Ctrl/Cmd toggles,
Shift extends. States follow DESIGN §12.4 (active vs inactive selection, focus outline, cut at
50%, drop target). Single click opens a preview tab (italic, replaced by the next preview, pinned by
editing, double-click or `layout.pinTab`); `workbench.editor.enablePreview` turns that off. Cut/copy/
paste and drag-to-folder are `explorer.cut|copy|paste|move` over two new Rust commands, `fs_move`
and `fs_copy` (workspace-scoped; a copy onto a taken name becomes "name copy.ext"). Closing a
background tab (the replaced preview, the welcome tab) no longer moves focus into the next tab — it
did, which took focus from the explorer on every single click.

### D52 — Editor context menu is the IDE menu
Monaco's own menu is off (`contextmenu: false`); right-click shows the IDE Menu with Monaco actions
run through `editor.runAction` (also usable by agents). Language actions (go to definition, rename,
format…) only appear when the engine reports a provider. Monaco's clipboard actions are commands, not
editor actions (`getAction` returns null), so cut/copy use `execCommand` on the focused editor and
paste reads `navigator.clipboard` (shown only where that API exists).

### D53 — App icons from `assets/logo.svg`
`npx tauri icon assets/logo.svg` accepts SVG directly (no rasterizing step needed); the generated
`icon.ico` contains 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 256 px. Only the desktop icons are kept (no Android/iOS
folders). The welcome tab shows the logo at 48px and uses it as its 16px tab icon (as an `<img>`
with a data URL: the SVG's clip-path ids would collide if inlined twice). The second uploaded logo
file was not used: it carried a product name and an embedded C2PA manifest.

### D54 — Tooltips are a component
`setTooltip(el, label, command?)` replaces native `title` everywhere: one delegated pointer listener,
500 ms delay (instant when moving between tooltipped controls within 300 ms), keybinding chip from
the command, hidden on pointerdown/keydown/wheel. Positioned with fixed coordinates and kept inside
the window.

### D55 — Title-bar menus are command lists
File, Edit, View, Go, Terminal and Help are tables of command ids (`menus.ts`); entries whose command
isn't registered or enabled are left out, so menus fill in as M2 adds commands. ☰ shows the same
menus as a two-level menu. Both are `ui.showMenu` / `ui.showAppMenu` commands.

### Sizes after M1.6 (vs M1.5)
| | M1.5 | M1.6 |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend total (`dist/`) | 7.94 MB (1.78 MB gzip) | 7.73 MB (1.71 MB gzip) |
| Initial shell (index.html + main.js + main.css) | 214 KB | 278 KB |
| Terminal chunk | 623 KB (ghostty-web) | 336 KB (xterm, 86 KB gzip) |
| `monaco.js` | 4.00 MB | 4.00 MB |

The shell grew by settings (registry, model, JSONC edit, settings editor), tooltips, menus, the
selection model and xterm's stylesheet.

## Milestone 2

### D56 — Language services: monaco-editor's workers, Shiki keeps the colors
`monaco-editor-core` → `monaco-editor` 0.57.0 (MIT; bundles the TypeScript language service,
Apache-2.0), same Monaco version. `monaco/core.ts` imports the editor API and every editor
contribution — monaco-editor's `editor.main` *minus* its ~80 Monarch language definitions (Shiki
colors everything, D16) and its LSP client. Language services: TypeScript/JavaScript, JSON,
CSS/SCSS/Less and HTML, each in its own classic worker bundled by `build.mjs` and created on first
use of the language (no CDN, no schema downloads). `.tsx`/`.jsx` keep their own language ids (for
Shiki's JSX grammars) and get the TS/JS providers registered on the same worker; `jsonc` gets the
JSON service the same way. Without the project on disk the TS worker only sees open files, so
"cannot find module" (2307/2792), "no declaration file" (7016) and "no JSX.IntrinsicElements" (7026)
are ignored rather than flagging every import. `settings.json` (user and workspace, from the
settings registry) and `keybindings.json` (command ids from the dispatcher) get JSON schemas.
esbuild copies Monaco's stylesheet next to every lazy language-mode chunk; nothing loads those
copies, so `build.mjs` deletes them.

| Worker (lazy) | Size | gzip |
|---|---|---|
| `ts.worker.js` | 6.71 MB | 1.48 MB |
| `css.worker.js` | 1.03 MB | 246 KB |
| `html.worker.js` | 738 KB | 196 KB |
| `json.worker.js` | 427 KB | 130 KB |
| `editor.worker.js` | 300 KB | 93 KB |

The frontend total goes from 7.73 MB to 16.6 MB (3.76 MB gzip), almost all of it the TS worker;
nothing loads before the shell paints, and the TS worker loads only when a TS/JS file opens.

### D57 — Quick open over a Rust file index
`src-tauri/src/index`: one `ignore` walk (honors .gitignore even outside git, skips `.git`, at most
300k files) when a folder opens, rebuilt in the background when its watcher sees a create, remove or
rename. On Linux the watcher adds one non-recursive inotify watch per indexed folder (≤ 8000)
instead of watching the root recursively, which would also watch every ignored folder
(node_modules) and can exhaust `max_user_watches`; on Windows and macOS one recursive watch is a
single handle. Fuzzy ranking runs in Rust (`index/fuzzy.rs`, tested): file-name matches beat folder
matches, word starts and runs score extra, words separated by spaces must all match. The frontend
puts recently opened files (per workspace, persisted) first and supports `file:line[:col]` and
`:line`. `QuickInput.pickDynamic` is the async variant of `pick` (latest query wins).

### D58 — Search: grep-searcher streaming, replace in Rust, results in the sidebar
`grep-searcher` + `grep-regex` (Unlicense OR MIT) walk with the same ignore rules plus include/
exclude globs (a bare folder name means `folder/**`, like VS Code). One Channel event per matching
file, then `done`; a new search cancels the running one; lines are clipped to 300 chars around the
first match and ranges are sent as UTF-16 offsets so JS can slice them directly. Replace re-applies
the pattern with the `regex` crate (MIT/Apache) and writes each file atomically; `$1` expands only in
regex mode. Search lives in the sidebar (PLAN §15: the sidebar holds explorer/search/git), results in
a Tree that refreshes once per frame while results stream. The replace preview runs the equivalent
JS RegExp on each match.

### D59 — Problems from the language services; icons in status-bar text
Diagnostics are Monaco's markers for files open in an editor (that is what the language workers
know about until LSP arrives in M5); hints are not listed. The `problems` tab, the status-bar counts
and `problems.list` / `ide://diagnostics` share one signal updated once per frame. Status-bar items
can embed icons as `$(icon-name)` in their text (VS Code's convention), used for the error/warning
counts.

### D60 — keybindings.json and the keyboard shortcuts tab
User rules (config dir `keybindings.json`, JSONC array; `"-command"` removes defaults, VS Code
style) are appended after the manifest defaults, so they win; the file is watched with the settings
files and reloaded live; a syntax error keeps the previous rules. Conflicts = two different commands
on the same chord sequence whose `when` clauses can both hold (identical clauses, or one of them
unconditional); differing non-empty clauses aren't flagged since we can't prove they overlap.
Recording a key suspends the global keyboard handler so the keys reach the recorder. Changing a
key appends `-command` + the new rule (comments in the file survive); "reset" rewrites the file
without the command's rules (comments are lost there; said in the command description).

### D61 — Reload from disk
A third Rust watcher instance watches the folders of open text documents (non-recursively). On a
change the file is re-read: same text → nothing (our own save); no unsaved edits → replaced in place
as one undoable edit and marked saved; unsaved edits → the §12.12 banner ("changed on disk":
Reload / Keep my changes); missing → "deleted on disk" banner. `search.replace` triggers the same
check directly. Settings files outside the workspace open in an editor are not reloaded this way
yet (the settings watcher reloads the *settings*, not the editor text).

### D62 — Shell integration (bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell)
Scripts in `src-tauri/src/pty/scripts/` are written to `<app data>/shell-integration/` and loaded
*after* the user's startup files: bash `--init-file` (sources /etc/bash.bashrc + ~/.bashrc, or the
login profile on macOS), zsh through a private `ZDOTDIR` whose files source the user's own
(.zshenv/.zprofile/.zshrc/.zlogin), fish `--init-command`, PowerShell `-NoExit -Command`. They emit
VS Code's OSC 633 marks (A/B prompt, C output start, D;exit, E;command line, P;Cwd=) so existing
tools that understand those keep working; OSC 133 A–D from other programs are also accepted. cmd
and other shells start unchanged (`terminal.shellIntegration.enabled` turns it off). Rust parses the
marks in the read loop into command records (command, cwd, timing, exit code, escape-free output ≤
64 KB, last 200) — `pty_commands`, `ide://terminals/<id>/commands`, `terminal.runCommand` (sends
a line and waits for its record: what agents use instead of screen-scraping). xterm parses the same
marks for gutter dots (gray = ok, red = failed); markers and decorations are "proposed" API in
xterm 6, so `allowProposedApi` is on. PowerShell sessions also get `Set-PSReadLineOption -BellStyle
None` (D49). Tab titles follow the reported cwd; restored terminals start in their last folder
(falling back to the workspace root if it is gone or outside the workspace). Verified with bash,
zsh and fish in the Linux sandbox; PowerShell needs the Windows pass.

### D63 — Command-script tests and the M2 permission policy
`<app> <folder> --run-test-script <file> [--user-data-dir <dir>] [--test-timeout <s>]` runs a JSONC
script of steps (`run` a command with `input`, read a `state` path, `wait`, retry with `timeoutMs`;
`expect` is a partial match with `$gte/$lte/$contains/$exists/$length/$not`; `expectError`) as
`caller: test`, prints TAP-like lines on stdout and exits 0/1 (124 if the timeout fires first).
`--user-data-dir` keeps runs off the real profile. `npm run test:ui` runs `tests/scripts/*.jsonc`,
each in a fresh copy of `tests/fixtures/sample`, under `xvfb-run` on headless Linux; CI builds a
debug app with dev commands (`src-tauri/tauri.test.conf.json`) and runs them on all three OSes.
Converted so far: the M1.6 layout-overflow regression and core flows (files, quick open, search,
diagnostics, settings, dock split, terminal + shell integration, keybindings). The permission
policy became `createM2Policy`: `test` allowed only during a run; `mcp` may read, asks for other
effects (once / for the session), always asks for destructive ones, and can't call UI-only
(`agent: "hidden"`) commands. Locally (Linux, Xvfb) both scripts pass; the GitHub Actions run itself
could not be exercised from this environment.

### D64 — MCP server
`rmcp` 3.5 (Apache-2.0) Streamable HTTP service behind a small hyper 1 server (MIT) on
`127.0.0.1:0`; `/mcp` only; `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (24 random bytes from `getrandom`,
compared in constant time) on every request; rmcp's loopback `Host` check and an `Origin` allowlist
of the server's own origins, so a web page can't reach it (DNS rebinding). Off by default
(`mcp.enabled`), status-bar indicator while on. Commands and state live in the webview, so Rust
holds a catalog the frontend pushes (on `command.registered` and every 5 s, only when changed) and
forwards `tools/call` and `resources/read` over a Channel, waiting up to 10 minutes for
`mcp_respond`. Tools: `agent: "core"` commands by name (dots → underscores, as MCP clients require
`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), the rest via `ide_find_commands` / `ide_run_command` (keeps the tool list short for
the model, PLAN §8). Calls run as `{ kind: "mcp", client }` (client name from `initialize`) under
`createM2Policy` (D63); commands with no effects (UI only) run without asking — a deliberate
choice: theme or layout changes are visible and harmless. The URL and token are also written to
`<app data>/mcp.json` (0600 on Unix, deleted on stop/exit) so scripts can re-register a client after
a restart. Verified here with a Node MCP client (initialize, tools/list, a core tool, find/run,
resources/list/read) and the permission prompt in the Linux build; the Windows + Claude Code steps
in docs/mcp.md need the Windows pass.

| Frontend total (`dist/`) | 7.94 MB (1.78 MB gzip) | 7.73 MB (1.71 MB gzip) | 16.70 MB (3.77 MB gzip) |
| Initial shell (index.html + main.js + main.css) | 214 KB | 278 KB | 338 KB (≈ 110 KB gzip) |

and the index; the installers mostly by the TypeScript worker. The Windows NSIS installer can only
be built on Windows (`npm run build` there).

Startup, release build, same VM (software rendering), fresh profile, sample folder, 3 runs
(`--run-test-script` reading `ide://perf`): webview started 745–765 ms after process start (dbus /
a11y session set-up in the VM, before our code) → shell visible +96–101 ms → extensions active
+112–119 ms → folder restored +248–269 ms → editor ready +883–937 ms. Shell-visible time is
unchanged from M1.5 (~95 ms) despite eight more built-in extensions; Monaco and every language
worker load after the shell.

## Milestone 3 — Git and language servers

### D65 — Git through the CLI, one repository per folder
The user's `git` (PLAN D5): no libgit2 (size, licence, and config/hooks/credential helpers already
work with the CLI). Every call is a `std::process::Command` with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (nothing can
wait for a password on a hidden terminal; Git Credential Manager's own window still works),
`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` (status never rewrites the index, so the git-dir watcher can't loop),
`core.quotepath=false`, no colors, and `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on Windows; all on blocking threads.
Status is `status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z --untracked-files=all` parsed in Rust (tested, including
renames and conflicts). The repository is the one containing the workspace root (it may be a
parent); paths cross IPC repo-relative with `/` or absolute inside the repo, nothing outside.
Refresh: a watcher on the git dir (HEAD, index, refs; lock files and objects ignored), file events
(save, create, rename, delete, replace), window focus, and a 5 s poll while focused (worktree edits
from a terminal); concurrent refreshes coalesce. Remote operations stream `--progress` lines over a
Channel (status bar + the 2px progress line); `pull` is `--ff-only` (no surprise merges from a
button) and the first `push` sets the upstream to `origin`. `git.*` commands are discoverable for
agents; `git.status` is a core tool. `git.discard` is destructive (confirms; deletes untracked files).

### D66 — Hunk staging by writing index text
Instead of building patches for `git apply --unidiff-zero` (fragile with CRLF, filters and
whitespace), a hunk is staged by computing the file's new index text in TS — a Myers line diff
(`core/diff`, tested incl. random round trips) of the index text and the buffer, with that one change
applied — and writing it with `git_write_index` (`hash-object -w --stdin --path` + `update-index
--cacheinfo`, keeping the mode). Texts are compared in working-tree form: the base comes from
`cat-file --filters` (smudge and line-ending conversion applied, like a checkout) and
`hash-object --path` applies the clean side, so `core.autocrlf` repos stage correctly (tested). The
same diff drives the editor's gutter bars, "Stage change" / "Revert change" in the editor menu and the
diff tab's toolbar; reverting edits the open document as one undoable edit (saved if it was clean).
Unsaved buffer edits are what gets staged, as in VS Code.

### D67 — File decorations and quick diff as workbench services
`FileDecorationService` (color token, badge letter, tooltip, strike/faded; providers answer
synchronously from a cache and bump a revision) feeds explorer rows and tabs (descriptors gain
`resource(state)`); folders get the color of their most important change and a dot, no badge.
`QuickDiffService` connects the git extension (base texts) to the editor extension (gutter bars,
diff tab, buffer texts) without either importing the other. The diff tab (`diff` dock view) is
Monaco's diff editor: working tree = index ↔ the shared document (editable, saves like its editor tab;
switches to inline when narrow), staged = HEAD ↔ index (read-only).

### D68 — Language-server host and client
Rust only moves bytes: `lsp_start` spawns the server (stdio, cwd = workspace root; on Windows `.cmd`
/`.bat` shims found via PATH/PATHEXT run through `cmd /C`, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`), frames
`Content-Length` messages both ways and streams messages, stderr lines and exit over a Channel.
The protocol is TS (`src/core/lsp`, DOM-free, tested with an in-memory server): JSON-RPC with
cancellation and timeouts, `file://` URIs as VS Code writes them (Windows drives, UNC), and a
`LanguageClient` doing initialize/initialized, full-text sync (a change without a range, accepted by
every server; incremental sync is an optimisation for later), diagnostics, and answers to the server
requests a client must handle (configuration, workspace folders, registerCapability, progress).
The editor attaches running clients to Monaco (`monaco/lsp.ts`): completion (+resolve, snippets,
insert/replace ranges), hover, signature help, definition/type definition/implementation,
references, highlights, document symbols (outline, breadcrumbs, `Ctrl+Shift+O`), formatting, range
formatting, rename; diagnostics become markers, so Problems and the status bar include them. A
Monaco editor opener sends cross-file navigation to `editor.openFile` (this also fixes TS go-to-
definition into unopened files); peek previews get read-only models for files that aren't open;
rename opens affected files as modified tabs so nothing is lost. Servers are defined declaratively
(`contributes.languageServers` — the built-in `builtin.language-servers` has rust-analyzer, Pyright,
gopls, clangd) and in the user-only `lsp.servers` setting (a workspace can't make the IDE start
programs before workspace trust, M6); they start when a document of their language opens, a missing
built-in server is quiet ("missing" in `lsp.list`), a missing user-configured one shows an error.
Agents get `lsp.hover`, `lsp.definition`, `lsp.references`, `lsp.symbols` (discoverable). Not yet:
code actions/quick fixes, semantic tokens, inlay hints, workspace symbols, `workspace/applyEdit`.
Tested with a Node mock server in `tests/scripts/lsp.jsonc` and by hand with Pyright 1.1.

## Milestone 4 — Agents

### D69 — Model providers: Ollama automatic, OpenAI-compatible by config
The agent talks to models through Rust (`src-tauri/src/ai`): the webview never holds API keys and
there is no CORS problem with local servers. Two wire formats cover almost everything people run:
Ollama's own API (`/api/tags` to list, `/api/show` for context length, capabilities and family,
NDJSON `/api/chat`), and OpenAI chat completions (SSE, tool-call fragments assembled; LM Studio,
llama.cpp server, vLLM, OpenRouter, OpenAI). Ollama needs no setup: it is probed at
`agent.ollama.url` (default `127.0.0.1:11434`) when the panel first shows, before each message,
when an agent tab is focused (at most every 30 s) and when the model menu opens (at most every 5 s,
waiting ≤ 400 ms) — background refreshes keep the list on screen — so a freshly pulled model or a
just-started Ollama appears without a click. Every model is listed — local ones first, `:cloud` ones
in a submenu. With no model chosen the first local model is used, so a user with Ollama running
can type a message immediately; `/api/show` tells whether it supports tools. Unreachable Ollama shows "Get
Ollama"; an empty list says `ollama pull qwen3:8b`. Extra providers: `agent.providers` (user
settings) or "Add model provider…"; keys via "Set API key…" go to `<appData>/secrets.json` (0600).
Requests are cancellable; `num_ctx` comes from `agent.contextLength` (16384 default — Ollama's 2–4k
default silently truncates agent prompts) capped by the model's own limit.

### D70 — Agent tools, changeset review and permissions
Ten core tools (small on purpose — local 7–14B models degrade with large tool lists): read_file,
list_dir, find_files, search, edit_file (search/replace with a whitespace-tolerant fallback),
write_file, run_command, get_state (`ide://`), find_commands and call_command (the dispatcher —
every IDE action is reachable without a tool per command). Models without native tool calling (or
whose provider answers "does not support tools") switch to a `<tool_call>{json}</tool_call>` text
protocol for the session. Edits never go straight to disk: they become a per-session changeset the
agent reads back as if applied; the panel shows diff cards and a changes bar, the diff tab
(`editor.openDiff {agent}`) accepts/rejects per hunk, and accepting writes through an open editor
(undoable). "Auto-apply" accepts at once. run_command asks unless it matches `agent.allowedCommands`
(word-boundary prefixes; chained commands need every part allowed); call_command goes through the
M2 permission policy with `askAgent`: read and no-effect commands run, others ask inline (once /
always for the session / deny), destructive ones ask every time, hidden ones are denied. Commands
run with `$SHELL -lc` (PowerShell on Windows), streamed, cancellable, process group killed.

### D71 — Checkpoints and transcripts in app data
Before an agent change is applied the file's previous content is saved per session and turn
(`<appData>/agent/checkpoints/<session>/<turn>.json`, first snapshot wins); "Restore checkpoint"
puts every file touched since that turn back (files the agent created are deleted). Transcripts are
`<appData>/agent/sessions/<id>.json`, restored with their tab. Nothing is written into the
repository, so the agent leaves no trace in git.

### D72 — MCP client
`agent.mcpServers` (user settings, the shape Claude Desktop and Cursor use: `{name: {command, args,
env}}`, `${workspaceFolder}` expanded) start on the first agent message, over the same Rust stdio
host as language servers with newline-delimited framing (D74). Their tools become
`mcp__<server>__<tool>`; tools marked `readOnlyHint` run freely, others ask like IDE commands. The
servers stop when the folder closes or the setting changes. Resources and prompts: later.

### D73 — External agents over ACP
Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Codex speak the Agent Client Protocol; the IDE is the client, so these
agents use the same panel, model menu ("External agents (ACP)") and review flow as the built-in one.
Their file reads see the session's pending edits, their writes go to the changeset, their
permission requests are the inline cards, terminals are non-interactive exec runs. Presets run
through `npx -y @zed-industries/claude-code-acp` / `codex-acp` and `gemini --experimental-acp` (the
user's own installs and logins; nothing bundled); `agent.externalAgents` adds or disables agents.
Checkpoints and the agent's own model choice stay with the external agent.

### D74 — Stdio host framing
The LSP host (D68) gained `framing: "lsp" | "ndjson"`, so one Rust component runs language servers
(Content-Length), MCP servers and ACP agents (one JSON message per line) with the same spawn rules
(Windows `.cmd` shims via `cmd /C`, no console window), stderr and exit reporting.

### D75 — Workbench fixes with M4
Menus: one `Menu` with submenus that open on hover (120 ms) and close with a delay (250 ms) so the
pointer can cross diagonally, ←/→ keys, disabled items; the menubar switches menus on hover once
one is open, like native menubars, and a second click on the open title closes it. Tabs: a tab
click activates it even when another group's terminal or editor has focus (the group's pointerdown
focus handler skips tabs), and tabs have a context menu (close, close others / to the right /
saved, copy path, reveal, split). Monaco's context-menu cut/copy/paste go through the Tauri
clipboard (the webview blocks `navigator.clipboard` reads). Explorer: inline new file/folder and
rename, drop-target highlight, OS file drops, Close folder, sticky ancestor rows. Source control:
the tree reuses node objects on refresh (rows went missing when a refresh raced a render) and row
buttons no longer lose their click to the tree's mousedown. The split drop preview animates with
`--motion-fast`.

### D76 — Release profile
Release builds strip symbols and use full LTO with one codegen unit (`[profile.release]` in
`src-tauri/Cargo.toml`). M4 added reqwest/rustls, two Tauri plugins and the agent, MCP and ACP
hosts; the unstripped binary had grown to 37 MB, most of it symbol tables. Build time goes up by a
few minutes; debug and test builds are unchanged.

### D77 — Fewer, larger files
The ~300-line limit had produced many tiny modules (a 4-line id helper, IPC wrappers of 7–20 lines,
READMEs of 4 lines in every folder) that were always read together. The limit is now ~1200 lines,
with the rule to split by responsibility. Consolidated: `src/core/ipc` (23 → 6 files: fs, system,
process, git, agent, invoke) and the Rust `ipc/` commands to match; one README per area (`src/core`,
`src-tauri/src`, `ui`) instead of one per subfolder; the agent's tools and commands, the tree's
keyboard/selection/sticky parts, the editor engine boundary + loader + host, the editor settings +
save transforms, and the workbench's small shared services (decorations, quick diff, language
clients) each in one file. `src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated/` is no longer tracked (tauri-build
writes it from `build.rs` on every build). Tracked files: 523 → 379, with no change in behavior.

### D78 — Viewers and tab actions
A viewer is a dock view for a file type plus a `ViewerContribution` in a shared registry
(`services.viewers`), so the editor extension routes to viewers without importing them: files
with a default viewer (images) open in it from `editor.openFile` (`asText` opts out, as does
"Reopen with… → Text editor"); preview viewers (Markdown, SVG) are offered by the editor's tab
action and Ctrl/Cmd+K V / Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V, opening in the editor group to the right or a new
split, like VS Code. Previews take the live text from `services.documents` (the editor publishes
open documents' text, changes and scroll position), so they update while typing; the Markdown
preview reuses the chat parser, extended with setext headings, task lists, images, strikethrough,
autolinks and source lines, and colors code with the engine's `colorize` (loading the grammar
first). SVG is drawn as an `<img>` from a blob: URL, so its scripts never run; CSP `img-src` gained
`blob:` for that and for workspace images (remote images in Markdown are not loaded, consistent
with no network loading). Views and view types can add **tab actions** (`TabAction`: icon, title,
command, input), shown in the group toolbar while their tab is active — terminal: new / clear /
kill; editor: preview to the side; previews: open source; images: zoom. Split shows only when it
does something (the tab can be duplicated, or the group has other tabs).

### D79 — Chat message actions
Each turn's final answer gets copy, retry (newest only, when idle) and the model or external agent
that wrote it; your messages get copy and edit. The newest answer's actions stay visible, older
ones appear on hover (like current chat apps). Retry drops the last turn and resends its message;
editing replaces the conversation after the edited message (`agent.retry`, `agent.editMessage`).
File changes from dropped turns stay in the review list, and applied ones stay restorable from
checkpoints — nothing on disk is silently reverted.

### D80 — Lean dev builds
`target/debug` had reached ~20 GB (debug info for every dependency; on Windows the PDBs fill
small drives — a dev build failed with "not enough space on the disk"). `[profile.dev]` now
keeps line tables for the app crate only and no debug info for dependencies: panics and
backtraces still show file:line, a clean debug build is ~2.5 GB, and builds are a bit faster.

### D81 — Agent edits: the format models are trained on, and forgiving matching
Precise edits from local models kept failing while whole-file writes worked. The tool asked for
a nested `edits: [{old, new}]` array — a shape small models fill badly — and then demanded an exact
match. `edit_file` now takes flat `path`, `old_string`, `new_string`, `replace_all`, the names
Claude Code and VS Code's agent use (the old shape and camelCase names are still accepted).
Matching goes exact → indentation-insensitive → whitespace-insensitive, each also tried with the
common transit mistakes undone (copied line numbers, literal \n, backslash-escaped quotes, HTML
entities such as &lt;div&gt;, curly quotes), then a last-resort near match: the one block of the
same length ≥ 90% similar (Levenshtein) and clearly better than any other, as Aider and Cline do.
A miss returns the model's own old_string and the file's text so the next attempt can copy it.

### D82 — Stream endings and a robust terminal start
Two ordering bugs: `ai_chat` and `exec_run` resolve when the native side finishes, but their
Channel messages can still be in flight, so a tool call (or the last output lines) occasionally
arrived after the turn had ended. The wrappers now resolve on the stream's own end ("done" event,
an end marker for exec), with a 2 s fallback. The terminal start drains ConPTY output from the
moment the console exists (a full pipe nobody reads can stall the start), runs off the async
runtime with a 10 s timeout (a late start is killed) and retries once.

### D83 — Markdown preview parity
Every block carries its source line, so scroll sync interpolates between blocks in both
directions (editor ↔ preview, with loop guards), the editor's cursor block is marked, `.md` links
open in the same preview, and re-renders update the DOM in place (images and code colors are
cached so nothing flickers while typing). The parser gained footnotes, definition lists, GitHub
alerts, ==mark==, H~2~O / x^2^, front matter and README-style HTML through an allowlist
sanitizer (details/summary, kbd, img, aligned blocks; no scripts, handlers or styles). Math
(KaTeX) is not supported yet.

### D84 — Provider errors: retry like a flagship client
Transient failures (HTTP 408/409/425/429/5xx, "overloaded", "rate limit", timeouts, connection
resets) are retried automatically up to 3 attempts with backoff (≈1 s, 3 s, 8 s plus jitter), but
only while nothing of the answer has arrived — a half-streamed reply is never replayed. A one-line
"Retrying… (2 of 3)" notice replaces itself in place. A final error shows a short message with the
provider's full text in its tooltip, plus Retry (resend the last turn) and Continue (resume from
where the answer stopped). Applies to every provider and to external (ACP) agents.

### D85 — Breadcrumbs and a per-file status bar
Each editor shows breadcrumbs (folders › file › symbols at the cursor, from the language providers'
document symbols through Monaco's outline service, debounced 350 ms) and a status bar under the
text: the file's errors and warnings (click: a list of just this file's problems), Diff, Ln/Col,
language. Every segment opens a searchable menu of its siblings; folders navigate in place. Both
are on by default (`breadcrumbs.enabled`, `editor.fileStatusBar.enabled`); with the file status bar
on, the window status bar drops its own Ln/Col and language.

### D86 — History: three layers, each cheap
1. **Text undo survives closing a file.** Closed files keep their Monaco model (the 20 most recent,
   each under 2 MB), so save → close → reopen → Ctrl+Z still works; a reopened file that changed on
   disk becomes one undoable step. Discarded unsaved edits are reachable the same way.
2. **Local history** (Rust, `<appData>/history/<hash>/`): every write the app makes to a workspace
   file (save, agent edit, replace all, git revert, restore) is snapshotted, along with what was on
   disk before the first one or after an outside change. Deduplicated, 50 per file, files over 1 MB
   skipped. "Open timeline" lists a file's versions; one opens as a diff (version ↔ file) with
   Restore.
3. **Workspace undo/redo** (`core/history`): explorer create/rename/move/copy/delete/import, replace
   all and accepted agent edits are entries with undo/redo closures (nothing is copied until undo
   runs). Deletes move into an app trash (`<appData>/trash`, swept after 7 days), so they can be
   undone. Undo refuses to overwrite a file that changed since. Ctrl/Cmd+Z in the explorer, and Edit
   → Undo when no editor has focus. `ide://history` lists both stacks; a history viewer can be
   built on these commands later.

### D87 — Menus: search and max height
Menus are at most min(70vh, 520px) tall and scroll. A menu or submenu can have a search box on
top (typing anywhere in it filters; ↑ from the first item returns to the box). Used for long
model lists (more than 12–15 models), long menu-bar submenus and breadcrumb menus. The explorer
and tab context menus follow VS Code's groups and order (open · reveal/terminal · find · chat ·
clipboard · paths · rename/delete).

### D88 — Inputs on overlays
Inputs inside menus, dialogs, the quick input and Monaco's find widget use `--bg-input-raised`
(the overlay surface lifted 5% toward the foreground) instead of the sunken editor input color,
which looked like a hole on a lighter surface. Light themes get the same derivation. Monaco's
find-widget buttons match the IDE's 22px icon buttons; its native `title` tooltips are shown with
the IDE tooltip.

## Milestone 5 — Browser

### D89 — Browser: proxy + frame for local pages, a window for the rest
Local dev servers and workspace files show in a dock tab's iframe served by a Rust reverse proxy
on 127.0.0.1 (one per target, random port). The proxy forwards with hyper's client (WebSocket
upgrades piped with `copy_bidirectional`, so HMR works), asks for identity encoding so HTML can
be edited, injects `<script src="/__ide/bridge.js">` after `<head>`, drops X-Frame-Options / CSP /
COOP / COEP, rewrites redirects, and rewrites Origin/Referer to the dev server's own origin.
Workspace folders are served as static files and previews reload when files change through the
IDE (saves, replace all, agent edits). Only loopback upstreams are accepted, and requests must
carry the proxy's own Host (DNS rebinding). The frame is sandboxed without top navigation or
popups; links to other origins go to the system browser.

Other sites open in a separate `WebviewWindow` (Tauri multiwebview is still unstable) with the
bridge as initialization script. Those pages get exactly one IPC command, `browser_bridge_post`
(capability `browser-external`, remote URLs `http(s)://*` incl. ports), which forwards reports
to the main window; calls go the other way as an `eval` of a fixed `__ideBridge.receive(<json>)`.
Everything the bridge sends is page data and is treated as untrusted (agent tools say so).

The bridge reports navigation, console messages, uncaught errors, failed fetch/XHR/resource loads,
and performs snapshot (an accessibility-style outline with `[ref=eN]` element refs), click, hover,
type (React-safe value setter), press, select, scroll, text, wait and eval. Calls answered across
a navigation resolve with `{ navigating: true }` instead of timing out. Agents get three tools
(`browser_snapshot`, `browser_act`, `browser_console`) only while a browser tab is open.

### D90 — Terminal links
Web addresses in terminal output are links (Ctrl/Cmd+click, like VS Code). Local dev-server
addresses open in the IDE's browser beside the terminal's group; others in the system browser.

### D91 — Agents and long-running processes
A server started with `run_command` used to die at the command's timeout while the model reported
it running ("unable to connect"). `run_command` now takes `background: true` for servers and
watchers: the command starts in its own terminal tab (`terminal.start`), keeps running, and the
tool returns its first output, any server URLs and how to stop it. A foreground command that times
out says plainly that it was stopped and to use `background`.

### D92 — Servers found in terminals
Like VS Code's port detection: addresses a terminal prints (`http://localhost:5173/`, "listening on
port 3000") are candidates; one becomes a server only once its port accepts a connection
(`net_port_open`, tried for a few seconds, so an echoed URL never counts), and is dropped when the
port closes or the command ends. Servers show in the status bar (click: open in the browser),
in a one-time toast with "Open in browser" (`browser.notifyOnServer`), on the empty browser tab and
in `ide://terminals`. Local addresses clicked in terminals or in chat open in the IDE's browser.

### D93 — Browser DevTools
DevTools under or beside the page (resizable, F12 / Ctrl+Shift+I, also while the page has focus —
the bridge forwards the IDE's few browser shortcuts): Elements (lazy DOM tree by bridge refs, hover
highlight with a box-model overlay in a closed shadow root, picker, attribute/text/HTML edits,
matched CSS rules, editable inline style, computed values, box model, `$0`), Console (levels,
groups, repeat counts, expandable objects, elements that reveal in Elements, stacks, a REPL with
history), Network (every request through the proxy with headers, bodies up to 2 MB, timing,
waterfall, type filters, preserve log, disable cache, copy as cURL; external windows report what
the bridge sees), Sources (what the page loaded, colored, opening workspace files in the editor),
Application (local/session storage, cookies). Device mode emulates sizes by sizing the frame.
Workspace-file previews update while typing: unsaved text is served by the proxy in place of the
file, and stylesheets swap without a reload. Network events and external windows' reports come
over one Tauri Channel (`browser_subscribe`), per AGENTS.md. Everything is a `browser.*` command;
agents get `browser_inspect` (network, request, DOM, styles, storage, device size, highlight).

### D94 — Terminal
Ctrl/Cmd+C copies when text is selected and interrupts otherwise; Ctrl/Cmd+V pastes. Web addresses
and file paths (`src/a.ts:12:5`, `x.cs(10,3)`, checked to exist relative to the terminal's folder)
are links with a pointer and a tooltip. With shell integration each command is colored with the
editor theme's syntax colors (`--syntax-*` tokens from dark-plus / light-plus;
`terminal.highlightCommands`), and the command whose output is on screen stays pinned at the top
(click: back to it). A context menu has copy/paste/select all, copy last command or output, clear,
split, new, rename and kill.

### D95 — VS Code compatibility
A folder's `.vscode/settings.json` is a settings layer under the IDE's own workspace settings
(translated: `terminal.integrated.*`, `editor.wordWrap` values, `workbench.colorTheme` → light or
dark; unknown keys ignored; the settings editor says "Set by .vscode/settings.json"). "Import
VS Code settings" copies the applicable user settings of VS Code, Insiders, Cursor or VSCodium.
Tasks use VS Code's tasks.json (`.vscode/` and the IDE's own folder; variables, args, dependsOn,
groups, platform blocks) plus package.json scripts with the project's package manager; Ctrl/Cmd+
Shift+B runs the build task. New settings with VS Code's names: `files.autoSave` (+ delay),
`editor.formatOnSave`, `editor.insertSpaces`, `editor.fontFamily`, `editor.lineNumbers`,
`editor.rulers`, `editor.bracketPairColorization.enabled`, `files.exclude`. launch.json (debugging)
is not supported yet.

### D96 — Screenshots for agents
The webview renders itself to a PNG (`screenshot_window`): WebKitGTK's `get_snapshot` on Linux,
WebView2's `CapturePreview` on Windows; macOS reports "not supported yet". No new crates: the
platform crates tauri/wry already link (webkit2gtk + cairo, webview2-com + windows) are declared
at the same versions. A page in the frame is cropped from the IDE's own snapshot (the iframe's
rect × device pixel ratio), so it is exactly what the user sees, device size included; a page in
its own window is that window's snapshot. `workbench.screenshot` / `browser.screenshot` save under
`<folder>/<workspaceFolderName>/screenshots/` or return base64 (`inline`, scaled to ≤ 1568 px).
The agent's `screenshot` tool (always offered) sends the image to the model as a user message after
the tool results (tool messages can't carry images in every API) — only the newest two, only for
models that take images (Ollama reports it; unknown counts as yes) — and shows a thumbnail in the
chat. Images aren't saved with sessions.

### D97 — Moving a whole group
Dragging a group by its tab strip's empty area (or a group's only tab) moves the group:
`layout.moveGroup` (same targets as `layout.moveTab`: another group's strip merges the tabs, an
edge splits, a dock edge splits the root). While dragging, the live group element itself is
transformed — never cloned or re-parented, so editors, terminals and iframes keep running — and
shrinks toward the pointer keeping its aspect ratio and the grabbed point under the cursor; the
iframe layer applies the same transform to browser iframes. On drop it glides into its new slot
(FLIP). The strip's right-click and its ⋯ open the group menu: New tab (file, open file, terminal,
browser, agent, problems, settings, keyboard shortcuts, welcome — `layout.newTab`), split in four
directions, new file, the group's tabs, maximize, close saved, close group.

### D98 — Chrome around the workbench
Title bar: the logo where the app menu ☰ was; the menus collapse into ☰ only after the command
field has shrunk (centered while it fits, then off-center, then the menus go). Layout toggles
appear on title bar hover, without a fill. The explorer's actions moved to its view header (new
file, new folder, collapse, ⋯ with refresh, reveal, terminal, find in folder, copy path, open and
close folder). Status bar: Go Live / Port (Live Server), a notifications bell (unread count, the
list with actions, do not disturb, clear; `ide://notifications`). The per-file bar shows
indentation (menu: spaces/tabs, size, convert), encoding and line endings like VS Code's, and has no
top border. The find widget sits on a surface close to the editor's. Filled status colors that
carry white text (`--status-danger-solid`, `--status-warning-solid`, `--window-close-bg`) are
separate from the text colors, which are too light under white. A browser tab's page can move into
its own window (`browser.popOut`; the tab keeps the toolbar, DevTools and agent tools, through the
proxy so live reload and the network log keep working; closing the window brings it back).

### D99 — Terminal and browser fixes (ide-m6.1)
Terminal: the containers are `overflow: clip`, so the browser can't scroll them to reveal xterm's
input while typing; the sticky line is a copy of the command's own buffer line (prompt, colors,
syntax-colored command) drawn on the terminal background at row height, VS Code-style; the
command line from the `E` mark is unescaped (`\x3b`); an overview ruler beside the scrollbar shows
commands (blue, red when they failed) and output lines that look like errors or warnings; no gap
right of the scrollbar; link tooltips say "Ctrl + click to …" and the pointer shows on links;
Windows passes the build number to xterm's `windowsPty` like VS Code (from `ver`). Clear
actions use the "ban" icon. Browser: the DevTools sash follows the dock side (it was stuck in
its first orientation) and updates once per frame; DevTools narrower than its saved size gives
way; the tab strip scrolls with dock/close always visible; DevTools colors are the editor's syntax
colors (`--syntax-*`, plus comment and selector); iframes follow slot resizes in the same frame;
the status bar's server item opens the server or shows the tab already on it; Go Live opens in
the editor area unless an editor is focused. Menus: one open at a time, closed when the window
regains focus, and orphaned menu elements are removed on the next click (a menu left behind when
focus went to a popped-out window).

### D100 — Browser toolbar order; reload starts a fresh log
Toolbar: back, forward, reload, the address field (device size and "own window" inside it, on the
right), element picker, DevTools, ⋯. The separate console-count button is gone: the DevTools button
carries error / warning badges and opens on Console when there are errors. Reload (and reload
without cache) clears console and network unless Preserve log is on. View registries (editor,
terminal, browser) only remove their own entry on dispose, so a tab restored under the same id
after a folder switch isn't dropped from them.

### D101 — Auxiliary windows (a tab in a window of its own)
VS Code's approach: the main webview calls `window.open("about:blank")`; Rust builds the main
window itself (config `create: false`) so it can answer `on_new_window` with a related webview
(same WebKitGTK context / WebView2 environment, `aux-N` label; any other `window.open` is denied;
WebKitGTK is told script may open windows). The main window's code then fills the new document:
stylesheets and `<html>` attributes are mirrored (and kept in sync), the icon sprite is added,
the keyboard service, browser-default suppression, menus and tooltips are attached per window
(Menu and Tooltips take the document of their anchor / last press). The tab's live view element
moves into it; the tab stays in its group as a placeholder (Show window / Bring back), so
commands, agents, state paths and DevTools work unchanged — it is the same object. Closing the
window brings the tab back; closing the tab closes the window. `layout.moveToNewWindow`,
`layout.returnFromWindow`, `layout.focusWindow`; `ide://layout` lists `detached`. Browser tabs
can move (the frame's bridge accepts the host from the aux window's opener, and hello re-binds
the reply origin); terminals and editors not yet (xterm's DOM renderer doesn't repaint rows in
another document). Screenshots of a moved page capture that window. Also: an external window's
bridge no longer reports its own IPC calls as network requests (they fed back endlessly), and
pages served by the proxy skip bridge-reported requests (the proxy logs them).

## Milestone 6 — Third-party extensions

### D102 — Third-party extensions: worker sandbox, permissions, VS Code declarative import
Extensions are folders with our `extension.json` (or a VS Code extension's `package.json`, of which
only the declarative parts are used: color themes, languages, TextMate grammars, snippets — VS
Code's API isn't offered, so its code never runs). Installed ones are copied to
`<appData>/extensions/<id>/`; "Load unpacked" uses a folder in place and reloads it when its files
change (mtime poll every 1.5 s, only while an unpacked extension exists). `registry.json` holds the
unpacked folders, disabled ids and granted permissions. Rust reads files only from a known
extension root by a relative path that can't leave it.

Code runs in one dedicated Worker per extension, started on its activation event (`*`/startup,
`onCommand`, `onView`, `onLanguage`). Before the extension's file is evaluated the worker deletes
fetch, XHR, WebSocket, importScripts, IndexedDB, nested workers and similar, so the only way out
is the `ide` RPC object (`core/extensions/rpc.ts`): commands, `ide://` state, events, workspace
files, notifications/quick pick/input, tree views, webview messages, settings, storage, `net.fetch`.
Every request is checked against the permissions the user granted (an install dialog lists them;
a version asking for more is stopped until granted again): fs.read / fs.write / shell / terminal /
network[:domain] / git / browser / agent / clipboard. Commands an extension runs go through the
dispatcher as `caller: ext`; the policy asks the extensions host, which maps the command's
namespace and effects to permissions (`requiredPermissions`) and confirms destructive ones with
the user. Its own commands, keybindings (only to its own commands), settings and views must use
its name as prefix (`<name>.` or the full id; built-in namespaces need the full id). Webview
panels load the extension's HTML from a local origin of their own (the browser proxy in static
mode) with a CSP that allows only the extension's own files, so a page can't reach the network or
the IDE except by `postMessage` to its worker. Color themes go through the existing VS Code
importer (UI tokens) and Shiki (syntax), `include` chains resolved; `workbench.colorTheme` picks
one (`ui.selectColorTheme`). Not yet: a marketplace/VSIX, extension-contributed agent tools beyond
discoverable commands, `.tmLanguage` XML grammars, and webviews in auxiliary windows.

### D103 — Workspace trust
A folder's tasks (.vscode/tasks.json, the IDE's tasks.json, package.json scripts) run programs from
the folder's files. Before the first one runs in a folder the user hasn't decided about, a dialog
asks whether to trust its authors; the answer is kept per folder in global state. Restricted
folders don't run tasks (status bar "Restricted mode", `workspace.manageTrust`), everything else
works. Settings that start programs (language servers, agent providers, external agents, MCP
servers) were already user-only, so a folder's settings can't set them; that is why trust doesn't
need to filter settings. Only the user (and test scripts, via `workspace.setTrust`) can change
trust; the commands are hidden from agents and MCP clients.

### D104 — Agent chat: one work group per turn
A turn used to show every thinking block, tool row and in-between note in sequence, so long tasks
filled the panel. Now (`view/turns.ts`, DOM-free, tested) each turn's work — thinking, tool calls
and the text the agent wrote between them — is one row, closed by default: while the agent
