works it shimmers with what it's doing ("Reading src/App.tsx…", accent dots), then summarizes
("Created 2 files, ran a command" + duration). Opening it lists the steps (tool rows still expand
to their output). The answer — the last text after the last tool call — shows under it as it
streams; text the agent writes before calling a tool shows there until the call comes, then moves
into the group. Diff cards that need accept/reject and error notices stay outside the group.
Streaming itself was never slowed down (text appears as the provider sends it); for people who'd
rather not watch it arrive, `agent.streamText: false` shows the answer at once when complete.

### D105 — Extensions anyone (or the agent) can make
`extensions.create` writes a template extension into the open folder (`.ide/extensions/<name>`):
extension.json (a command and a sidebar tree), main.js, ide.d.ts (the API types, bundled from
`src/api/index.d.ts` with a `?raw` import) and a README with the rules, then loads it unpacked so
saving reloads it. Its id is `local.<name>`. The agent can call it and then edit the files with
its normal (reviewed) edit tools; its system prompt says so, and `ide://extensions` gives it the
status and log to debug with. Permissions still need the user: adding one to the manifest stops
the extension until the user allows it.

### D106 — AI in the editor: Edit with AI and suggestions while typing
Two features outside the agent panel, both generating through `services.languageModel` (the agent
extension provides it over the same providers; no tools, no thinking, `maxTokens` — new in the
Rust chat request as Ollama `num_predict` / OpenAI `max_tokens` — and cancellable).
**Edit with AI** (Ctrl/Cmd+I, off until `editor.inlineEdit.enabled`; Ctrl+K is our chord prefix): a prompt bar in a view zone above the
selected lines (an overlay widget holds the input so it focuses and types normally). The model
gets the file around the selection with `<selection>` markers and returns replacement lines;
fences, tags and leaked thinking are stripped. The new lines apply as one undoable edit,
highlighted, with the old lines shown struck through in the zone; follow-up instructions refine
them; Esc rejects by undoing our edits (so the file isn't left dirty), Ctrl+Enter accepts. Agents
and tests use `editor.inlineEdit { instruction, startLine, endLine }` (hidden from agents in the
UI sense — they have their own edit tools). **Suggestions while typing**: off by default (every
pause is a model call); a Monaco inline-completions provider for every language asks after
350 ms with ~6 KB before and 2 KB after the cursor, 128 tokens max; replies are cleaned so they
don't repeat the line start or what follows. Separate model settings so a small fast model can
do completions while a bigger one edits.

### D107 — Agent edits are checked; done notifications; extensions UI; settings write race
**Edits checked before the model moves on.** The research round (docs/agent-roadmap.md) put
"feed diagnostics back after edits" first: Copilot's agent mode loops on compile errors, Aider
lints after each edit. Our edits are usually pending review, so there is no file to look at:
`engine.checkText` puts the proposed text in a scratch model *next to* the file
(`.ide-check-N.<name>`, so relative imports resolve the same; hidden from Problems), waits for the
TS/JSON/CSS workers to settle (≤ 2 s) and returns their errors. `services.codeCheck.newErrors`
drops the ones the file already had (same code + message), and edit_file / write_file append the
rest to their result ("fix them"), with "· 2 errors" on the row. `agent.checkEdits` turns it off.
Languages served only by language servers aren't checked yet (they only see real documents).
**Notifications** when the window isn't focused and the agent finishes (after > 5 s) or needs an
answer (`agent.notifyWhenDone`).
**Extensions view** reworked after VS Code's: filter box, Installed / Development sections,
two-line rows with an avatar (the manifest's `icon`, else initials on a tinted tile), publisher and
badges, a gear menu (same as right-click), and an extension page tab (Details = README, Features,
Permissions, Log). "Needs permission" is an Allow… button; an extension that starts asking for
permissions (added, or edited by the agent) opens the permission dialog right away, unless the
user already declined that same list; agents can open it with `extensions.grantPermissions`
(effects none: the dialog is the consent). Remove (unpacked: off the list, folder kept) and
Uninstall (delete files: installed copy, or the unpacked folder — to the IDE trash when inside the
open folder; Rust deletes only folders listed in the registry) are separate. Sidebar views of
extensions have Details / Disable / Uninstall on their activity bar icon's right-click, which also
hides icons (`workbench.activityBar.hidden`) and lists every view to show again.
**Settings** writes could be lost when several came in a row (Reset all, scripted changes): the
file watcher's reload raced the IDE's own writes and restored older text. Writes now go out in
order and a reload that overlaps one of our writes is dropped. Settings editor: Reset all (current
scope), a reset button on changed sections, right-click on sections and rows (reset, copy ID / as
JSON, show only changed: `@modified`). `settings.reset` takes `category` or `all`.
Also: the explorer uses VS Code's compact layout (8px per level, a file's icon in the same column
as a folder's chevron, guides under the parent's chevron); folder icons are a setting
(`explorer.folderIcons`, off), ready for icon themes later; the root row's tooltip shows to the right; Edit with AI is off until `editor.inlineEdit.enabled`;
`resolveInRoot` resolves `..`.

### D108 — Extensions can read and type into the active editor
An agent-built "insert timestamp" extension couldn't insert anything: the API had no editor
access, so it fell back to a notification. `ide.editor.active()` (path, language, cursor, selected
text; needs fs.read) and `ide.editor.insert(text)` (types at every cursor, replacing selections, one
undo step; needs fs.write) go through the new `editor.insertText` command, so the permission check
and audit are the usual ones. The template README now lists the API and the valid icon names (an
unknown icon showed a box), and the agent's prompt says to use ide.editor.insert for editor text.

### D109 — Agent memory: plan tool, summarizing compaction, context meter, @-mentions
From docs/agent-roadmap.md, the items that matter most for small local models:
- **Plan** (`update_plan`, Cline Focus Chain / Claude Code TodoWrite / Codex plan): the model sends
  its whole checklist with each step's status; the session keeps it (saved with the session), the
  system prompt carries it on every request — so it survives compaction — and a card above the
  message box shows it (expanded while working, collapsed to the current step when idle, gone when
  all done). The prompt asks for a plan on multi-step tasks.
- **Compaction**: before each model call, when the conversation (as messages) passes 80 % of the
  budget, the older part is summarized by the session's model (goal, decisions, files, commands and
  results, open errors, what's left; no tools, no thinking, 1500 tokens) into a `summary` item. The
  newest steps stay verbatim: the current turn when it fits in half the budget, else the newest
  steps that do, never splitting a tool call from its result. `toMessages` sends only what follows
  the newest summary, the summary opening the first user message. `/compact [focus]` (or
  `agent.compact`) summarizes everything so far on demand. The panel shows "Summarized N earlier
  messages" (expandable). Before this, old turns were silently dropped; that is still the fallback
  if summarizing fails. `agent.autoCompact` turns the automatic part off.
- **Context meter**: the share of the context the last request used (provider usage when reported,
  else an estimate from the characters sent), next to the send button, warning color above 80 %.
- **@-mentions**: typing @ at the start of a word opens a picker — files (the file index),
  Problems, Terminal output (the latest commands with output), Selection — added as chips; their
  content is looked up when the message is sent (`agent.mention`).

### D110 — Project memory and tidying it up; unloaded workspace extensions; approval cards
- **Project memory** (in-band memory with progressive loading, as in Claude Code's memory files and
  Anthropic's memory stores): `.ide/memory/<topic>.md` in the open folder, one bullet per note with
  its date and session. The agent writes with `remember` (topic + one fact) right away, without
  review — notes aren't code, they're visible and editable files, and secrets (key/token/password
  patterns) are refused. Writes are serialized; a note already there isn't added twice. The system
  prompt gets only an index (topic, note count, first notes; ~2.5k characters) plus when to save;
  `recall` reads a topic or searches notes. The IDE builds the index from the files, so it can't
  drift the way a model-maintained INDEX.md would. `agent.memory.enabled` turns it off.
- **Tidying up** ("dreaming": verify, organize, enrich — out of band, into a copy):
  `agent.dream` gives the model the memory and up to 8 saved sessions of this folder since the
  last tidy-up (transcripts, tool results shortened) and asks for the whole curated memory as
  `=== file: name.md ===` blocks (and `=== delete: … ===`). The result is proposed in a new session
  as ordinary pending changes (deletions are a new kind of pending change: accepting trashes the
  file), so the memory on disk is untouched until the user accepts, per file or per hunk; checkpoints
  and local history keep the old version. Files the model leaves out stay as they are (small models
  drop things). Notes written while a tidy-up waits for review are added to its proposal too, so
  accepting doesn't lose them (the doc's "reconcile deltas before promotion"). After 8 sessions
  since the last tidy-up the IDE suggests one once per window (`agent.memory.suggestTidyUp`).
  Not done: multi-agent permissions/versioning beyond the above (one IDE writes the folder), a
  scheduled run (it costs a long local-model call, so the user starts it).
- **Unloaded extensions in the folder**: an agent wrote a hand-made manifest into
  `.ide/extensions/demo-extension` and nothing appeared. The manager now also lists folders under
  `.ide/extensions` that no loaded extension uses ("Not loaded" in the Extensions view, `notLoaded`
  in `ide://extensions`) with the manifest's errors — which now name common mistakes (`"name"`
  instead of `"displayName"`, `"scripts"`) — and a Load button (`extensions.loadFromWorkspace`,
  agent-callable, limited to that folder; permissions are still asked). They're never run without
  that. Found on refresh, when the folder changes, and by a light poll (4 s). The agent prompt says
  to always start with `extensions.create`.
- **Approval cards**: an icon, a heading ("Run a command", the IDE command's title, the MCP tool),
  the exact command or call as a code block, an "Always allow `<prefix>`" checkbox and Deny (Esc) /
  Allow (Enter). The remembered prefix is the program plus a subcommand only ("npm test",
  "git status"; "ls", not "ls .ide/extensions"). A leading `cd <dir inside the folder> &&` is dropped
  and becomes the command's working folder — models add it out of habit, and it made the remembered
  pattern a `cd C:\Users\…`. The working indicator is a small ring spinner instead of three dots.

## Milestone 6.x — Parity and depth (releases ide-m6.N)

### D111 — Cleanup pass; easy gaps from the VS Code / Cursor list
A list of what VS Code and Cursor have that we don't is kept in docs/feature-gaps.md. This pass:
- **Reopen closed tab** (Ctrl+Shift+T): the dock remembers the last 30 closed editor-like tabs
  (view type, state, group); cleared on folder switch.
- **UI zoom** (`window.zoomLevel`, VS Code's 20 % steps; Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+Numpad0) through
  the webview's own zoom (`core:webview:allow-set-webview-zoom`), not CSS zoom, so Monaco and
  xterm measure correctly.
- **Find in terminal** (Ctrl+F while a terminal has focus; `terminal.find {query}` returns
  "n of m"): `@xterm/addon-search` (MIT, xterm's own addon, same release as addon-fit — a
  dependency because matching across wrapped lines and the scrollback is what it's for).
- **Cursor rules** in the agent's prompt: `.cursorrules`, and `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` with
  `alwaysApply: true`; other rules are listed with their description/globs for the agent to read.
- **Custom slash commands**: `/name args` runs `.ide/commands/name.md` (also `.claude/commands`,
  `.cursor/commands`), `$ARGUMENTS` replaced; the prompt goes with the message as context, the
  chat shows what was typed.
- **Export conversation** as Markdown (or copy), from the agent's ⋯ menu.
- **README on first open** (`workbench.openReadme`): a folder opened with no saved layout shows its
  README preview, like VS Code's readme start page. Not in test runs.
- **Markdown preview**: link labels may contain brackets (badges: `[![alt](img)](url)`); https
  images load (CSP `img-src https:`; `markdown.preview.remoteImages` turns it off — they're the
  document's own content, like GitHub and VS Code show them); single newlines in a paragraph are
  spaces in previews (CommonMark/GitHub), still line breaks in agent chat.
- **Browser**: terminal links open the page in the biggest editor group (`browser.open
  {largest}`), not beside the terminal; "Open in system browser" is in the address field; device
  mode moved to DevTools' header (and the ⋯ menu).
- **Small fixes**: Monaco's hover copy button no longer makes one-line hovers scroll; file icons
  sit 1px right in the explorer.
- **Audit fixes** (an independent read of the code): a session claims its turn synchronously (two
  quick sends could both start; compaction and side tasks too); the run_command allowlist no
  longer passes `&`, redirects or newlines outside quotes (`npm test & rm …`); retry/edit put the
  conversation back when the send can't start; Stop cancels a summary; a failed automatic summary
  isn't retried every step; command output buffers keep only their tail; a session keeps the folder
  it was made in (memory tidy-up evidence was mislabeled after a folder switch) and isn't the
  default target in the next folder; a failed folder open no longer looks half-open; Accept all
  applies what it can and records it for undo when one file fails; the Markdown preview's code
  highlight cache evicts instead of clearing (could loop past 500 blocks) and failed image loads
  are retried; the server sweep can't drop a server found meanwhile; extension folder scans
  ignore results for a folder that's no longer open; extension icon blob URLs are revoked;
  diff stats in the agent panel are memoized; attachments survive a send that can't start.
  Left for later: freeing sessions whose tabs closed, the Markdown inline parser's slicing on very
  long paragraphs.

### D112 — Token use and prompt caching; native Anthropic provider
Before plugging hosted models in, the agent's requests were reviewed for what providers can cache.
The main problem was ours: the system prompt was rebuilt for every model call and carried the IDE
state (active editor, cursor line, problems, git) and the plan, so the start of every request
changed and no provider could reuse its cache — not Anthropic's prompt cache, not OpenAI's automatic
prefix cache, not Ollama's KV cache. Now:
- **The system prompt is built once per session** and kept (identity, how to work, AGENTS.md /
  rules, memory index); rebuilt only after a summary and on restart. Its wording no longer depends on
  review/auto-apply mode.
- **The IDE state goes with each user message** (`<ide_state>`), taken when it's sent and stored on
  the message, so earlier messages never change after the fact. The plan isn't in the prompt: the
  update_plan calls are in the conversation, and a summary carries the plan forward.
- **One tool list per turn** (a browser tab opening mid-turn doesn't change the tools).
- **Earlier tool results stay as sent** while the conversation fits (`toMessages {stable}`); they're
  shortened only under budget pressure, and compaction normally comes first.
- **Summaries reuse the cache**: for hosted providers the summary request is the same prompt, tools
  and messages as the turn plus one instruction (read from the cache), falling back to the
  transcript form if the model answers with tool calls. Local models keep the short transcript.
- **Native Anthropic provider** (`kind: "anthropic"`; the preset uses it, and an
  OpenAI-compatible entry pointing at api.anthropic.com is upgraded): Anthropic's compatibility layer
  has no prompt caching and drops thinking, and current models reject `temperature`. The Messages
  API path sets one explicit cache breakpoint after tools + system and the top-level automatic one
  (which follows the conversation's end, so each step reads the previous step's prefix); adaptive
  thinking with summarized display, whose signed blocks are kept on the assistant item and sent back
  unchanged (required with tool use); `output_config.effort` from `agent.effort`; no sampling
  parameters; usage with cache reads/writes; model details (context window, max output, thinking,
  vision) from `/v1/models/{id}`. `agent.cacheTtl` picks 5 min or 1 h (writes cost 1.25× / 2×,
  reads a small fraction of input).
- One-off prompts (editor completions and Edit with AI, the plain summary, memory tidy-up) set
  `noCache`: a cache write that's never read only costs more.
- **OpenRouter** with Anthropic or Gemini models gets `cache_control` on the system prompt and the
  newest user message; OpenAI-compatible providers report `cached_tokens`, shown like Anthropic's.
- **Ollama**: `keep_alive` (`agent.ollama.keepAlive`, 30 min) keeps the model and its prompt cache
  loaded between messages.
- **Hosted context**: `agent.contextLength` (16k) was applied to every model, so Claude got 16k and
  summarized constantly. It's now for local models; hosted ones use their own window capped by
  `agent.cloudContextLength` (200k).
- **Visible**: the context meter's tooltip shows the cached share of the last request and the
  session's totals; `ide://agent/session` has `usage.cached`, `totals` and `promptChars`. With the
  default tools the fixed part is about 2.3k characters of prompt and 6.2k of tool definitions.
- `read_file` cuts lines over 2000 characters (minified files).
- Tests: `tests/scripts/anthropic.jsonc` drives a mock Messages API (in the Ollama mock) and checks
  the breakpoints, an unchanged system prompt across requests, thinking blocks sent back, no
  temperature, the IDE state in the messages, and cache usage; Rust tests cover the request
  conversion (alternating turns, tool results and screenshots in one user turn) and the SSE parser.

Also in this patch: a notification when a terminal command that ran 30 s or more finishes while the
window is in the background (`terminal.notifyAfterSeconds`); a slash-command picker when "/" starts
the message (`agent.slash`, built-ins and the folder's commands); images pasted into the message
box go to vision models (scaled to 1568 px, PNG; not saved with the session); Change language mode
(`editor.setLanguage`, from the status bar); agent sessions whose tabs are closed are saved and
freed after a while (from the audit).

### D113 — Compare, zen mode, Outline, small editor/explorer gaps; linear inline Markdown
From docs/feature-gaps.md, the cheap VS Code items:
- **Compare with saved** (`editor.compareWithSaved`, File menu): the diff tab gets two more kinds —
  saved file ↔ open document (unsaved changes; editable, "Revert to saved") and another file ↔
  this one (`editor.compareFiles`; explorer "Select for compare" / "Compare with …", swap sides).
  Both bases reload on save.
- **Zen mode** (`layout.toggleZenMode`, Ctrl+K Z, View menu): hides the sidebar, activity bar,
  status bar and the bottom/right regions, and restores each as it was. No Esc-Esc chord: a first
  Escape would wait for the second and swallow the next key in editors and widgets.
- **Outline** sidebar view (`outline.view`): the active editor's symbols (the engine's / language
  server's document symbols) as a tree with a filter; the symbol containing the cursor is
  highlighted and revealed; reloads 400 ms after edits and retries while a language service starts.
  Agents get `ide://editors/active/outline` (flattened: name, kind, lines, depth).
- **Explorer**: Duplicate (`explorer.duplicate`, " copy" names, undoable like a paste).
- **Editor**: Copy as Markdown code block (`editor.copyAsMarkdown`: `path:lines` and a fenced block
  in the file's language), in the context menu when there's a selection.
- **Terminal**: double-clicking its tab renames it (`DockView.onTabDoubleClick`; other tabs keep
  "double-click keeps it open").
- **Markdown inline parsing** is linear: patterns match in place (sticky regexes cached by source)
  instead of on a copy of the rest of the paragraph, and an unmatched "[" looks at most 2000
  characters ahead. A long streamed answer was re-parsed quadratically on every token.

### D114 — Editor menu like VS Code's; symbols without a language server; one thinking header
- **Go to / Peek were missing from the editor menu**: Monaco registers Go to definition, type
  definition, implementations, references and their Peek variants as commands (Action2), not as
  editor actions, so `getAction()` returned nothing and the menu filtered them out (only
  F12 worked, through its keybinding). The engine now knows these by the provider each needs
  (`ILanguageFeaturesService…has(model)`) and runs them through the command service on the
  focused editor. The menu follows VS Code's order: Go to definition / type definition /
  implementations / references, a **Peek** submenu, Go to symbol in editor, then Rename, Change all
  occurrences, Format document, Format selection (with a selection), Refactor…, Source action…,
  the clipboard and the palette. Entries without a provider for the file are left out (Monaco's
  TypeScript has no type-definition provider; language servers usually do).
- **Breadcrumbs and Outline for more files**: they come from document-symbol providers, which only
  TypeScript/JavaScript, CSS, HTML, JSON and running language servers had. VS Code adds Markdown
  headings itself; we do too, plus a line-by-line declaration finder for Python, Rust, Go, shell,
  PowerShell, Ruby, PHP, Lua, Java, Kotlin, C#, Swift, C, C++, Zig, SQL, YAML (two key levels), TOML /
  INI sections, Dockerfile stages and Makefile targets, nested by indentation (headings by level).
  When a language server provides symbols for the language, this provider answers with nothing,
  so there are no duplicates. It also feeds "Go to symbol in editor" (Ctrl+Shift+O).
- **Thinking shown twice**: an open work group showed each step's thought under its own
  "Thinking…" toggle, under the group's own "Thinking…" header. Inside a group the thought text is
  now shown directly; the group header is the only toggle.

### D115 — Sidebar on the right; opaque sticky rows; && / || in Windows PowerShell 5.1
- **Sidebar position** (`workbench.sideBar.location`, `layout.toggleSidebarPosition`; View →
  Appearance and the activity bar's right-click menu): the activity bar and sidebar move to the
  right of the window by CSS `order` on the same elements (nothing is re-created, so views keep
  their state), the gap and the activity bar's border mirror, the sash grows the sidebar when
  dragged left, the title bar's sidebar toggle shows the right-panel icon, and "beside" tooltips of
  sidebar rows open toward the editors. The dock (and its bottom/right regions) is unchanged and
  sits to the left; `ide://layout` reports `sidebar.side`.
- **Sticky tree rows** (folders pinned while scrolling) were see-through when selected, focused or
  hovered: those row states are translucent (or "none" for the keyboard cursor) and won over the
  sticky row's opaque background. Every state now draws over the surface color.
- **`&&` / `||` in the terminal on Windows**: Windows PowerShell 5.1 has neither (PowerShell 7
  does), so `cd app && npm run dev` failed — in VS Code too, which picks PowerShell 7 when it's
  installed. Now: PowerShell 7 is found in its install folders and the Store's alias too, not only
  on PATH; and when the shell is 5.1, the shell integration's Enter handler rewrites a line with
  top-level `&&` / `||` to `a; if ($?) { b }` / `a; if (-not $?) { b }` before running it (quotes and
  backtick escapes respected; the rewritten line is what history keeps). Commands the IDE runs
  itself (the agent's run_command) get the same rewrite in Rust (`pty/chain.rs`, tested) when only
  5.1 is there. Pasting several lines runs them one after another, as in VS Code.

### D116 — `clear` typed in the terminal; peek colors; breadcrumbs for every built-in language
- **`clear` / `cls` / `Clear-Host` / `reset` typed at the prompt** left the terminal half-cleared:
  the shell redraws (ConPTY scrolls the screen up instead), while our command tracker kept
  decorations, rulers and the sticky command for lines that were gone. The tracker now recognises
  those commands (shell-integration mark C), records no entry for them, and when the next prompt
  starts (mark A) clears xterm's buffer and its own command list — the same thing the Clear
  button does, so both end in the same state.
- **Peek and other editor widgets** used Monaco's default colors (blue title bar, light result
  list). The theme bridge now maps the peek view (title, editor, gutter, result list, match
  highlights, border), the problems peek, quick input, inlay hints, code lens, ghost text,
  light bulb and badges to semantic tokens; the peek header and reference list use the UI font.
- **Breadcrumbs and Outline**:
  - A `.tsx`/`.jsx` opened before any `.ts`/`.js` never got TypeScript's worker. We created a
    throwaway model of the base language to start it, but Monaco's `onLanguage` (which starts the
    worker) fires on *rich* feature requests — an editor showing the model — not on model creation.
    We now request rich features for the base language directly. This also fixed Go to/Peek
    definition, hover and diagnostics in such projects.
  - TypeScript's navigation tree lists imports and anonymous callbacks (`<function>`); VS Code's
    outline leaves both out, and so do we.
  - Symbols are retried a few times while a language service is starting (it answers "none" first).
  - Opening several files quickly could leave the previous editor "active" (its late focus event
    won), so the outline and breadcrumbs showed the wrong file's symbols. Activity from an editor
    that isn't its group's active tab is ignored now.
  - Coverage matches VS Code's built-ins: TS/JS/TSX/JSX, CSS/SCSS/Less, HTML, JSON/JSONC
    (language services), Markdown headings, plus our heuristic symbols (D114) and any language
    server. `tests/scripts/features-m6-15.jsonc` checks TSX, CSS, HTML and JSON.

### D117 — Agent dev servers; command auto-approval; selectable chat; snippets; path links
- **"npm run dev" looked finished at once, so the agent re-ran it.** `terminal.start` typed the
  command 300 ms after creating the terminal; on Windows PowerShell the first prompt (whose shell
  integration reports "previous command finished, exit 0") arrived after that, so the server was
  reported as ended. Now it waits for the shell's first prompt before typing, and only the end of
  the command it typed counts. Starting the same command again while it runs returns the running
  one (`alreadyRunning`) instead of a second server. The agent's run_command runs recognised dev
  servers and watchers in the background even without `background: true`, and opens the server's
  address in a browser tab (`agent.openServers`, default on; an open tab is reused) so the user
  sees it and the browser tools can check it.
- **Command approval** (`agent.runCommands`: ask | auto; the agent's mode menu). Other agent IDEs:
  Cursor has auto-run with an allowlist/denylist, VS Code's Copilot terminal auto-approve rules
  (allow/deny regexes, plus a global "auto-approve everything"), Windsurf off/allowlist/auto/turbo,
  Claude Code permission modes with allow/deny rules. We keep "ask, unless allowlisted" as the
  default and add "auto": everything runs except a built-in denylist (deleting, moving, killing,
  downloading, running downloaded code, sudo, permissions, history rewrites, publishing; command
  substitution and redirects into files) plus `agent.deniedCommands`. The composer pill shows a
  lightning icon while it's on.
- **Chat**: messages, thoughts, command output and permission details are selectable (the app
  chrome sets `user-select: none`). "Jump to latest" hides after it's clicked (its own scroll was
  ignored by the scroll handler).
- **Icons**: the browser's element picker uses a cursor in a dashed square (as Edge's), DevTools a
  console prompt; the title bar's restore icon is mirrored to Windows' layout (back window top
  right); HTML's "Open preview" uses the browser's globe (viewers can name their icon).
- **Snippets** (VS Code formats): user `snippets/<language>.json` and `*.code-snippets`, project
  `.vscode/*.code-snippets` and `.ide/snippets/`; `scope` picks languages (VS Code ids mapped:
  typescriptreact → tsx). Reloaded on save. Preferences → Snippets creates a commented template.
- **File paths in text are links** (Ctrl+click), like VS Code: relative to the file, then the
  folder; `:line:col` and `(line,col)` suffixes select the position; only existing files are
  underlined (checked through `fs_stat`, cached 10 s, at most 300 checks per pass).

### D118 — Terminal clear on Windows; hex, media and CSV viewers; progress lines
- **Clearing a PowerShell terminal on Windows**, three bugs:
  1. PowerShell reported the command line (E) only at the *next* prompt, from history, and the
     tracker kept it for the next command: a typed `cls` cleared after the *following* command, and
     sticky lines / colors showed the previous command. Now the Enter handler sends E (then C) as the
     line is accepted, the prompt sends just D for it, and a command line never outlives its
     prompt (reset at A). An empty Enter sends no C (it left the IDE thinking a command ran).
  2. After the shell's own clear, xterm skips `clear()` when the cursor is already on the first
     line — leaving the gutter dots and ruler marks. The terminal now disposes every mark it made,
     then clears, then marks the prompt again so the next command is tracked.
  3. The Clear button cleared only xterm, but on Windows ConPTY keeps its own screen: it went on
     drawing at its old cursor row (a pasted line appeared twice) and repainted the old lines on the
     next Enter. At a prompt, Clear now sends Ctrl+L — "clear screen" in PSReadLine, bash, zsh and
     fish, keeping what's typed — and wipes scrollback and marks once the shell has redrawn.
- **Viewers**: a hex viewer (default for common binary types such as .pyc, .class, .wasm, .exe;
  any file through "Reopen with…", and a button on the editor's binary-file notice — VS Code
  shows a notice and offers its Hex Editor extension), a media player for audio and video (VS
  Code's built-in media preview; CSP gains `media-src blob:`), and a table preview for .csv/.tsv
  (VS Code needs an extension for this). PDF was left out: WebKitGTK has no built-in PDF viewer, so
  it wouldn't work the same on every platform.
- **Progress lines** like VS Code's: `ViewRegistry.progress(viewId, title)` shows a 2px line at the
  top of the sidebar view (after 150 ms, so quick work doesn't flash) and a moving mark under its
  activity-bar icon when another view is shown. Driven by commands (`command.started` /
  `command.executed`: file paste/move/duplicate/delete/drop and refresh, closing the folder, undo
  and redo → Explorer; extension installs → Extensions; search → Search), by opening a folder
  (until its tree is listed) and by git's busy state (push, pull, commit… → Source control, which
  drops its own line for this one).

### D119 — Tab close in other groups; title-bar toggles; live agent activity; applied diffs; dark scrollbars
- **× on a tab of an inactive group didn't close it**: pressing the button focused it, which
  focused its group, which re-rendered the tab strip under the pointer — the click then landed on
  a new element and never fired. The close button no longer takes focus on press.
- **Title-bar layout toggles with the sidebar on the right** follow the layout left to right:
  bottom region, right region (an inner-column glyph — it's now the column left of the sidebar),
  sidebar (panel-right, rightmost). Before, the left button toggled the right-hand sidebar.
- **The agent's working header says what it's doing** instead of "Thinking…" for minutes:
  - Providers stream tool calls; a new `toolProgress` stream event (OpenAI-compatible and
    Anthropic; Rust `ToolStreamProgress`) reports the tool, its `path` argument once complete, and
    the size every 2000 characters — "Writing index.html (12k characters)…". The text protocol
    gets the same from a half-written `<tool_call>` (`textToolDraft`). Ollama sends tool calls
    whole, so there it stays as before.
  - While thinking, the latest heading in the model's thoughts ("**Planning the layout**", as
    many models write them) replaces "Thinking".
- **"Open diff" on a change already applied** (auto-apply, or accepted) used to just focus the
  file. The changeset now remembers each file's text before its latest applied change;
  `agent.openAppliedDiff` finds the local-history snapshot with that content (by hash, allowing
  for a BOM or CRLF on disk) and opens that version ↔ the file. A file the agent created opens as
  it is.
- **Dark scrollbars on dark pages** in the browser tab: when a page's background is dark and it
  declares no `color-scheme`, the bridge adds `::-webkit-scrollbar` styles inside a cascade layer
  — any scrollbar rule of the page's own (unlayered) wins, so styled pages keep theirs. Not
  `scrollbar-color`: in Chromium that would switch off a page's `::-webkit-scrollbar` styling.
  Light pages are left alone. The style is hidden from DevTools' Elements.

### D120 — Audit fixes; clone, blame, merge conflicts, terminal tab looks, hot exit; three viewers
- **Audit** (a separate read-only review of m6.13–m6.18), fixed:
  - **Command denylist** (auto-run mode) was easy to step around. Each chained part is now
    normalised before matching — quotes, backslashes and `VAR=1` / `env` / `nohup` / `command`
    prefixes dropped, the program reduced to its name (`/bin/rm`, `rm.exe` → `rm`), git's own
    options skipped (`git -C x push`), the entry's later words matched anywhere (`git reset HEAD
    --hard`), `npx` / `pnpm dlx` packages checked as the program. Always asks: a newline, a
    background `&`, code on an interpreter's command line (`bash -c`, `cmd /c`, `powershell
    -Command`, `node -e`, `python -c`…), `xargs`, `find -exec|-delete`, and every redirect into a
    file (not just the first). More entries: unlink, shred, truncate, rimraf, tee, Set-Content,
    Out-File, Start-Process, scp, rsync, ssh, `git checkout .`, `git stash drop`… Tested with the
    review's bypass list.
  - The agent can't change `agent.runCommands`, `allowedCommands`, `deniedCommands`,
    `mcpServers`, `externalAgents` or `providers` through `settings.set` / `settings.reset`.
  - PowerShell 5.1 `&&` / `||` rewrite had the wrong precedence (`a || b && c` skipped `c`); now
    left to right with a status variable, in both copies (Rust test updated).
  - PowerShell's Enter handler reported a command on unfinished input (`if ($x) {`); it now
    parses first and sends nothing until the input is complete.
  - Clearing: owned timers (no clear on a disposed terminal); a multi-line prompt is no longer cut
    to its last line — at a prompt the shell redraws (Ctrl+L, now on every platform) and the IDE
    then erases scrollback in order with its output (`ESC[3J`) and forgets only the marks made
    before the clear, keeping the redrawn prompt's.
  - Hex view reaches the end of files over ~26 MB (scroll position mapped past 8M px).
  - "Open diff" on applied changes: the diff view gained a content-provider base, and the
    changeset's remembered text is shown directly (empty files included); local history is the
    fallback after a reload.
  - Tool-call progress scanned the whole argument buffer on every delta (quadratic for big
    files); now only the first 4 KB, and the text protocol's draft every ~1000 characters.
  - Smaller: progress lines pair `command.started` / `executed` by an execution id; concurrent
    `terminal.start` of the same command waits for the first, and its bookkeeping is dropped with
    the terminal; CSV preview doesn't rebuild while hidden and drops stale renders; dark
    scrollbars follow a page's theme switch; the path link provider honours cancellation and
    skips files over 1 MB; snippet file names can't be paths; `--version` isn't a server;
    `aria-busy` on busy views.
- **Git clone** (`git.clone`; Git menu, explorer's empty state): URL and parent folder (asked when
  missing), `git clone --progress -- <url>` (an option-like URL is refused), progress in the
  explorer's line and the status bar, then Open. Rust `git_clone`, tested against a local repo.
- **Blame in the status bar** (`git.blame.statusBarItem.enabled`, like VS Code): the cursor line's
  author and age ("Ada, 3 days ago"), the commit in the tooltip, `git.blameLine` for details and
  agents. `git blame --porcelain -L n,n --contents -` with the editor's text, so unsaved edits show
  as "Not committed yet" and line numbers match. Debounced 300 ms; refreshed after git changes.
- **Merge conflicts**: "Accept current | incoming | both" code lenses above each `<<<<<<<` block,
  the two sides tinted (diff3 base too), `editor.resolveConflict` (one, or `all`) as one undoable
  edit. Parser and resolver DOM-free and tested.
- **Terminal tab color and icon** (`terminal.setColor`, `terminal.setIcon`, the terminal's
  right-click menu): six ANSI-based colors (`--file-icon-term-*` tokens) and ten icons, kept with
  the tab across restarts.
- **Hot exit** (`files.hotExit`: onExit, the default, or off): dirty files are backed up with the
  folder's state (debounced after edits, so a crash loses little) and restored — opened, unsaved,
  with a notice — next time; closing the window no longer asks about them (closing or switching
  the folder still does). Files over 2 MB / 10 MB in all aren't backed up.
- **Viewers**: fonts (.ttf .otf .woff .woff2: name, sample sizes, glyphs, via FontFace from the
  bytes), Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb, read-only: Markdown cells, colored code with execution
  counts, stream / result / error / image outputs; HTML outputs aren't rendered — nothing from the
  notebook runs), and ZIP archives (.zip .jar .war .vsix .whl .nupkg .epub .apk: path, sizes,
  dates from the central directory). File icons for archives, notebooks, fonts, audio, video and
  spreadsheets.

### D121 — Codevre Desktop; welcome page; folder-less agent start; Chats sidebar; settings redesign; a bundled extension
- **Name**: `product.json` now says Codevre / Codevre Desktop, the per-project folder is
  `.codevre` (was `.ide`) and the URL scheme `codevre`. The bundle identifier and the extension
  API global (`ide`) stay, so the app data folder (settings, sessions, extensions) carries over.
  Every former `.ide` literal reads `product.workspaceFolderName`. Opening a folder whose `.ide`
  holds our files (and no `.codevre` yet) renames it (`migrateWorkspaceFolder`).
- **Welcome page** like VS Code's / Cursor's: no product name, four cards (Open folder, Clone
  repository, New file, Open file), links (Open recent…, Command palette, Settings), and recent
  projects with a × on hover (`workspace.removeRecent`). `workspace.newFile` and
  `workspace.openFile` work without a folder: they open the file's folder.
- **Servers in the status bar** moved to the right, beside Go Live (VS Code puts port and
  live-server items there).
- **Clone like VS Code's**: `owner/repo` and `github.com/owner/repo` become https URLs — public
  repositories clone with no sign-in; private ones go through git's own credential helper (Git
  Credential Manager on Windows) or SSH. Failures say what to do (sign-in, not found, offline).
  `git.defaultCloneDirectory` (VS Code's setting) starts the folder picker; the last folder is
  remembered.
- **Agent with no folder open**: a request that would make files (`agent.send` without a
  workspace, not a `/command`) shows a card in the chat instead of failing: a folder name
  suggested from the message ("make a snake game in python" → `snake-game-python`), "In
  <folder>" with Change… (a path in the message wins, then `agent.projectsFolder`, then
  `~/Projects`), and Create and start (Enter) / Open folder… / Just chat. One card rather than
  Allow/Decline because the useful answer is often a different name or place.
  `agent.startInFolder` does it for agents and tests; Rust `workspace_create_folder` refuses a
  non-empty existing folder.
- **Chats sidebar** (`agent.chats`, the bot icon; `agent.showChats`): New chat with its key,
  search, this folder's chats by day then other folders, a spinner on running ones, × to delete.
  `agent.openSession` opens a saved one. The palette's "Agent sessions…" stays.
- **Settings** like Cursor's: a category nav with icons on the left (a 48 px icon rail under
  640 px, via a container query), one category per page, rows as cards with title, description
  and control on the right, toggles as switches; search shows matches from every category.
- **A bundled extension** (`src-tauri/bundled-extensions/`): "TODO tree" (TODO / FIXME / HACK /
  XXX / BUG / NOTE comments by file or tag, click to jump; in the spirit of VS Code's Todo Tree).
  An ordinary sandboxed extension, embedded in the binary and copied into the installed
  extensions once, disabled — so the Extensions view always has something to try. The registry's
  `bundled` list remembers the seeding: uninstalled stays uninstalled; a newer shipped version
  replaces an older installed copy.
- **Extension API**: `ide.workspace.findText(query, options)` (`fs.read`) — ripgrep over the
  folder with .gitignore, as a *detached* search that neither cancels nor is cancelled by the
  search view's.

### D122 — Commands that weren't allowed; inputs on cards; a star for the agent; compact folders; stash; Apply in chat
- **Bug: four commands were never allowed.** Tauri only lets the frontend call commands that are
  listed in `build.rs` (which makes their `allow-*` permission) and granted in a capability.
  `git_blame`, `git_clone` (m6.19) and `workspace_create_folder` (m6.20) were registered but not
  listed, so blame, Clone repository and the agent's "Create and start" failed with "not
  allowed" in the app — the UI tests never called them. Fixed, and `scripts/check-commands.mjs`
  (part of `npm run check`) now fails when a registered command isn't listed and granted. The
  UI tests call blame, stash and the folder flow's command.
- **Inputs are never darker than what they sit on** (a standing preference): `--bg-input` is a
  translucent tint of the foreground in dark themes (so a field on a card or panel is a hair
  lighter than it) and white in light themes; `--bg-chip` the same for key chips; checkboxes
  too. DESIGN.md §12.2 and AGENTS.md say so.
- **The agent's icon** is a four-pointed star with a small spark (`agent`, drawn in-repo on the
  Lucide grid) instead of the robot — the activity bar, tabs, menus and the settings nav.
- **Settings names**: `lsp.*` shows as "Language servers", `todoTree.*` as "TODO tree", and
  URL / API / UI / ID / AI are capitalised in titles ("Ollama URL").
- **Folder card fits**: while it waits, the chat shows the request instead of the empty-state
  help, and the card always scrolls into view.
- **Compact folders** (`explorer.compactFolders`, on by default as in VS Code): a chain of
  folders that each hold only one folder is one row, `src/main/java`, standing for the innermost
  folder. One listing of lookahead per subfolder, skipped in folders with more than 100
  subfolders; changes inside the chain refresh the row's parent; the folders in a chain are
  watched. `ide://workspace` lists them (`compactFolders`).
- **Git stash** (`git.stash`, `git.stashIncludeUntracked`, `git.stashList`, `git.stashPop`,
  `git.stashApply`, `git.stashDrop`; Git menu): a message asked from the palette, a picker of
  stashes (message and age) when no index is given, `--index` so staged changes stay staged,
  drop confirmed. Rust `git_stash` / `git_stash_list`, tested on a real repository.
- **Apply on chat code blocks** (like Cursor's): a block whose fence names its file
  (```` ```ts:src/a.ts ````, ```` ```ts src/a.ts ````, `title="…"`, ```` ```src/a.ts ````) gets
  **Apply**, which proposes it as a reviewable change (`agent.applyCode`): the whole file when
  it is new or the block is most of it, else the lines between the block's first and last lines
  — each found once in the file, ignoring indentation; otherwise it says it can't tell rather
  than guessing (no model call). Every finished block also gets **Insert at the cursor**. Code
  block headers show the file name for ```` ```src/main.rs ```` and color by its extension.

### D123 — Faster preview proxy; an idle iframe layer; reload spinner; new logo
- **Reloading a dev-server page was slow** (a Vite + React app felt sluggish next to VS Code's
  and Cursor's browser). Three causes in the preview proxy, all fixed:
  - **Nagle + delayed ACK**: hyper writes a response's headers and body separately; without
    `TCP_NODELAY` each request waited ~40 ms for an ACK. Now set on every proxy socket (and the
    MCP server's). 300 sequential requests through the proxy: 13.6 s → 1.8 s (debug build);
    300 in parallel: 2.3 s → 0.4 s.
  - **A new connection per request** to the dev server: connections are now kept alive and
    reused (up to 16 idle; a stale one is retried once on a fresh connection; WebSocket upgrades
    still get their own).
  - **`localhost` on IPv6 only** (Node 17+ / Vite on Windows bind ::1): every request first tried
    127.0.0.1, which on Windows takes about a second to be refused. The address that answered
    is remembered.
- **The iframe layer's frame loop sleeps**: it followed slots with layout reads on every frame
  for as long as a browser tab existed. Now it runs while something may move (a slot resized,
  window resize, pointer down — drags and sashes —, key presses, transitions, any dock change)
  and stops after 30 quiet frames. Pages keep running when their tab moves, as before (the
  iframe never leaves the layer).
- **Reload spins** while the page loads (at least one turn, so a fast reload still shows; no
  spin with reduced motion — dimmed instead).
- **Agent icon**: just the four-pointed star (the small spark is gone).
- **Empty states wrap** in narrow sidebars (buttons under each other, text wraps), and the
  welcome cards go to one column in a narrow tab.
- **New logo** (`assets/logo.svg`: the white "C" around a violet cube); app icons regenerated
  with `tauri icon` as in D53 (desktop sizes only).

### D124 — Chat titles from the model; rename and clear chats; "Fix with agent"; logo
- **Chat titles** without an extra request: the first message of a chat carries one more line,
  "start your reply with a short title — <title>…</title>" (about 30 tokens, once, on the user
  message so the cached system prompt doesn't change). The loop takes a `<title>` opening a
  reply out of the stream as it arrives (a half-written tag is held back), and the first one
  names the chat; until then, and with models that ignore it, the title is the start of the
  message as before. Cost: ~30 input + ~10 output tokens per chat. A separate "name this chat"
  call to a small model would cost a request (and on Ollama could load a second model); asking
  inside the first reply costs almost nothing. `agent.autoTitle` turns it off.
  `core/agent/title.ts`, tested with streamed pieces.
- **Chats**: `agent.renameSession` (double-click a chat, or its right-click menu),
  `agent.clearChats` (the Chats view's trash button: all chats or this folder's; running chats
  are kept).
- **"Fix with agent"** (`terminal.fixWithAgent`, `terminal.fixWithAgent` setting): when a command
  fails (shell integration's exit code), a chip over the terminal sends the command, its exit
  code and the end of its output (6000 characters) to the agent — the active chat if it's idle,
  else a new one. Also in the terminal's right-click menu. The chip goes away when the next
  command starts.
- **Logo**: the dark cube with the white "C" (`assets/logo.svg`); app icons regenerated.

### D125 — Agent column; Chats: pin, … menu, details tooltip; hiding the shown view
- **One reading column in the agent panel**: messages, cards, the header, plan, changes and the
  prompt share `--agent-column` (680 px) and centre in a wide panel, like Claude's and Cursor's.
- **Chats list**: each row's hover button is now "…" (the same menu as right-click: Open, Pin /
  Unpin, Rename…, Delete); `agent.pinSession` pins a chat to a "Pinned" group at the top
  (saved with the chat); a pin mark when shown elsewhere. The tooltip sits to the right, like
  the explorer's, with the title, when it was last active ("2d ago") and its folder. Renaming
  or pinning doesn't change when a chat counts as last active (`meta.updated` now follows the
  conversation). Groups: Pinned, Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days, months,
  Other folders. The chat commands moved to `chatCommands.ts`.
- **Hiding the sidebar view that is showing** (activity bar right-click) switched nothing: the
  icon stayed because the active view is always listed. Now the sidebar switches to the first
  view still shown (or closes when none is), like VS Code.

### D126 — Untitled files; one page per extension; chats from other folders; empty states higher
- **Untitled files** (File → New text file, Ctrl/Cmd+N, the welcome page's New file):
  `workspace.newUntitledFile` opens "Untitled-1" (`untitled:Untitled-N`, lowest free number),
  dirty while it has text (emptied, it closes without asking). Saving asks where — the name from
  its first line, like VS Code — and the same tab becomes that file (`EditorService.adopt`: the
  model is recreated under the new path, so the language follows the extension); with no folder
  open, the file's folder opens as the workspace first (files are only writable inside it).
  `editor.saveUntitled {untitled, as}` for agents and tests; Save as… on an untitled tab does
  the same. A restored untitled tab comes back empty, and hot exit puts its text back. Not kept
  among closed models.
- **Extension pages**: one tab per extension; a page opened from the list is a preview that the
  next one replaces (VS Code); opening the same extension again focuses its tab.
- **Chats from other folders**: a chat remembers its folder (`session.folder`; a chat started
  before its folder takes the folder of its first message). Opening one from another folder
  shows a strip under the header — "Started in snake-game. Tools work on the open folder." —
  with **Open snake-game** (`agent.openChatFolder`: opens that folder, then the chat) and
  **Continue here** (`agent.moveChatHere`). Also in the Chats row menu ("Open in …") and the
  chat's ⋯ menu (with Rename). A strip rather than a question on click: the chat can still be
  read anywhere, and the choice is there when it matters.
- **Empty states in the sidebar sit near the top** (VS Code's welcome views); the Outline hid
  its empty list, which pushed "No editor is open" to the bottom.
- **Fix**: a message sent the moment an answer appeared could be refused ("still working")
  while the finished turn was still saving; it now waits for that (`AgentSession.settle`).
- `agent.openSession` without a session opens the most recently active saved chat.

### D127 — Agent harness: verify step, observation masking, explore sub-agent; inline blame; file history
From a review of harness techniques (the October 2026 research: Aider's auto-test, JetBrains'
"The Complexity Trap", Claude Code's built-in Explore, Anthropic's harness-design write-up),
three were worth building now; a fresh-context review of the change found nine problems, all
fixed before shipping (listed under "Review").
- **Verify step** (`core/agent/verify.ts`, `session.verify`; settings `agent.verify` auto/off,
  `agent.verifyCommand`, `agent.verifyTimeoutSeconds`): after a message whose work changed files
  **on disk** (auto-apply; held-for-review edits aren't on disk, so nothing runs), the project's
  check runs as a visible run_command ("Checked with npm test") through the agent's own
  permission path (ask / allowlist / auto with denylist), in the foreground. A failure goes back
  to the agent as a harness message (shown as one quiet line, output fenced as data), at most
  twice; then a notice hands over. The check is the setting, else the npm/pnpm/yarn/bun `test`
  script (not npm init's placeholder), else `typecheck` / `check` / `lint`, `cargo check`,
  `go build ./...`; nothing is guessed beyond that. It's skipped when the agent already ran the
  same command after its last change (passed or failed — a failure is only re-checked after new
  changes). Real checks rather than the model reviewing itself: Anthropic found a self-reviewing
  agent "talked itself into approving" bugs. With `agent.runCommands: auto`, a repository's own
  test script runs without asking — like any command in that mode.
- **Observation masking first** (`conversation.ts`): the newest 10 tool results stay whole; older
  ones are shortened (600 characters) before anything is summarized, counting tool steps, not
  user turns (one message with 30 reads was never masked before). The boundary moves in steps
  of 8 so earlier messages stay byte-identical between requests (prompt caching).
  `needsCompaction` measures the masked size, so a summary call happens only when masking isn't
  enough (JetBrains: masking matched or beat LLM summaries in 4 of 5 settings at about half the
  cost). The "call again to see it" hint is only on read-only tools' shortened output.
- **Explore sub-agent** (`exploreTool.ts`, `session.subagent`; setting `agent.explore`): an
  `explore` tool runs a nested agent loop on the same model with only list_dir, find_files,
  search and read_file, its own short prompt (no project rules or memory), 6 / 12 / 24 steps
  (quick / medium / thorough), then — if it used them up — one more call for the report. The main
  conversation gets the report (≤ 4000 characters), not the reads. Its calls don't move the
  context meter. Note: on Ollama the sub-agent's different prompt evicts the main conversation's
  prompt cache once per explore.
- **Review** (fixed): a check after the answer folded the answer into the work group; Retry,
  edit and ArrowUp could pick the harness message as the user's; checkpoint labels counted it;
  it counted as a new turn for masking and compaction; a re-check could nag after an "unrelated
  failure" reply; the masking hint invited re-running side-effecting tools; the step-limit
  report call declared no tools (some APIs reject that); Stop during detection didn't stop the
  check; check output wasn't fenced.
- **Inline blame** (`git.blame.editorDecoration.enabled`, off by default as in VS Code;
  `git.toggleInlineBlame`, Git menu): "Ada Lovelace, 3 days ago • subject" faint after the
  cursor's line (engine `annotateLine`, Monaco injected text the cursor skips).
- **File history** (`git.fileHistory`, Git menu): the file's commits newest first; picking one
  opens that version ↔ the file now (content scheme `git:<hash>`; `git_show` now takes a commit
  hash, 7–40 hex digits). Content schemes ending in ":" answer every scheme with that prefix.
- Chats: the row tooltip moved from the title button to the whole row (beside the list, never
  over "…"), and tooltips keep line breaks.

### D128 — Language configurations; editor defaults and 50 more editor settings; scrollbar sizes; settings reset
- **Bug: no language had a configuration.** Syntax colors come from Shiki, so Monaco's language
  definitions (which carry each language's comments, brackets, auto-closing pairs, indentation
  and folding rules) were never loaded. Ctrl+/ did nothing, bracket pair colorization had no
  brackets to color (the setting was right; the brackets weren't known), auto-closing pairs and
  smart indentation were off. Now each language's configuration is set the first time a file of
  it opens (`monaco/languageConfig.ts`: Monaco's definition modules, configuration only, each its
  own chunk; small ones of our own for JSONC, TOML, Zig and Make; TSX/JSX/C/shell/Vue/Svelte share
  a definition).
- **Defaults**: editor and terminal font size 14; minimap on.
- **More editor settings** (`advancedSettings.ts`, VS Code's names, 50 of them): line height,
  font weight / ligatures / letter spacing, cursor style / blinking / smooth animation / width,
  smooth scrolling, Ctrl+wheel zoom, scrollbar sizes, line highlight, guides (indentation,
  bracket pairs), bracket matching, folding and its controls, minimap side / size / characters /
  width, sticky scroll lines, word wrap column, auto-closing brackets / quotes / surround, format
  on paste / type, linked editing, occurrence and selection highlight, suggestions (quick,
  trigger characters, Enter, Tab), parameter hints, hover and its delay, inlay hints, code
  lenses, color swatches, drag and drop, empty-selection copy, multi-cursor modifier, unicode
  highlight, top padding. A table maps each key to an engine option path; a test checks that
  every one is declared with the same default.
- **Scrollbars**: the editor's 12 px (was 10; `editor.scrollbar.vertical/horizontalScrollbarSize`),
  the terminal's 12 px (`terminal.scrollbarSize`; xterm draws it as wide as its overview
  ruler), everything else 9 px (was 8; `workbench.scrollbarSize`). The global `scrollbar-width`
  / `scrollbar-color` are gone: in Chromium (WebView2) they switch off `::-webkit-scrollbar` and
  the width can't be chosen — that's why the thumbs were thinner on Windows than designed.
- **Settings reset**: resetting a setting whose saved value equalled the default changed no
  value, so nothing was reported and the editor kept the modified bar and reset button until
  rebuilt. The model now also reports keys whose saved value changed.
- **Settings categories**: a setting can name its category (`category` in the manifest); the
  editor's inline edit and inline completion settings show under Agent.
- **MCP stays off by default**: the server needs a client set up with its URL and token, which
  change at every start, so on by default would open a local port and help nobody until then.
  Turning it on is one switch (Settings → MCP), and it asks before anything changes files or
  runs commands.

### D129 — Code actions in the IDE's menu; copying problems; Outline as an Explorer section
- **Bug: "Show code actions" froze the window.** Monaco's action widget draws its list in a
  context view with an invisible full-window layer behind it that swallows every press until the
  list closes. In the IDE the list could come up empty (it closes itself on focus changes it
  doesn't expect, e.g. our dock focusing the editor a frame later), leaving the empty box and that
  layer behind: nothing clickable until Escape. Monaco's `IActionWidgetService` is now our own
  (`monaco/actionMenu.ts`, registered before any service is created): the lightbulb, Ctrl+. and
  the hover's "Quick fix…" open the IDE's menu (same look as every other menu, keyboard and
  dismissal included, groups separated). Nothing stays on screen when it closes. The preview and
  the "disable" bar of VS Code's list aren't there (the standalone editor has no refactor preview).
- **Problems: copy and send to the agent.** A right-click menu on a problem (the Problems tab and
  the per-file list under the editor): Go to problem, Copy, Copy message, Copy problems in this
  file, Copy all problems, Fix with agent, Fix all in this file with agent. Rows show a copy
  button on hover; Ctrl/Cmd+C copies the selected problem(s). Click still goes to the problem
  (the expected action; copying on click would make the most common action two steps). The text
  is compiler style, `src/a.ts:2:1 - error typescript(2304): Cannot find name 'foo'.`, which
  agents and people read without explanation. Commands: `problems.copy` and
  `problems.fixWithAgent` (all, one file's or one problem; the agent gets the list in a fence,
  the active chat if idle, else a new one, like `terminal.fixWithAgent`).
- **Outline under the Explorer.** A sidebar view can name a home view (`sectionOf`): hidden from
  the activity bar, it shows as a collapsible section at the bottom of that view (VS Code's
  layout) with a sash above it while expanded, styled like the Source control and Extensions
  group headers. The Outline's home is the Explorer. Collapsed by default; created on first
  expand; collapsed state and height are kept per folder (`viewSections`); right-click on the
  header → Show in activity bar. `outline.show` (and `view.show`) expand the section instead of
  switching views. `view.toggleSection`; `ide://layout` lists the sections.
- **Dev tools**: `dev.inspectDom` (computed style and HTML of matching elements) and `dev.click`
  (press an element) for UI tests of engine widgets that have no command.

### D130 — Web pages as agent context; settings profiles; column selection; keybinding search
- **@web and `web.fetch`.** Type a web address after @ in the agent's message box (or pick
  "Web page") and the page's text goes with the message, fetched when it's sent. The agent can
  read pages itself with `web.fetch` (network effect: it asks first, once or for the session;
  the system prompt says so). Rust does the GET (`web_fetch`: http/https only, redirects
  followed, 3 MB cap, 30 s) because the webview's fetch is held by CORS; `core/agent/webText.ts`
  turns HTML into Markdown-like text — headings, paragraphs, lists, links made absolute, code
  fences — and leaves out scripts, styles, navigation, footers and forms, preferring `<main>` /
  the one `<article>`. A small tag walker, not a parser: no new dependency. `@docs` (crawling a
  docs site) isn't done; one page at a time covers most of it.
- **Settings profiles.** Preferences → Export profile… / Import profile… (`settings.exportProfile`
  / `settings.importProfile`): user settings.json, keybindings.json and user snippets in one JSON
  file, comments kept, for another machine. API keys stay out. Rust shows the save/open dialog
  and does the write/read itself (`profile_save` / `profile_open`), so the webview never gets to
  name arbitrary paths (debug builds take a path for UI tests). Import confirms what it replaces.
- **Bug: user snippets were out of reach.** `<user data>/snippets` (D117) wasn't in the fs scope,
  so user snippets never loaded and couldn't be created. That folder and the `*.json` /
  `*.code-snippets` files directly in it now are (no subfolders, no symlinks).
- **Column selection mode** (`editor.columnSelection`, Selection menu, status bar item while on —
  click turns it off). Menu toggles for settings (word wrap, minimap, sticky scroll, whitespace,
  column selection) show a check when on.
- **Keyboard shortcuts.** Right-click a row: change / add, show same keybindings, remove, reset,
  copy command id / title / keys. A quoted key (`"Ctrl+K"`) lists exactly the commands bound to
  it; the keyboard button searches by pressing the keys; clicking a conflict mark lists the
  commands sharing the key.

### D131 — Agent composer with attachments; Outline actions; sticky rows aligned
- **Composer layout.** A compact message box — the text and the send button inside it, growing
  with the text (no scrollbar until it stops growing) — with the controls on a row under it: +,
  the edit mode, the context meter, reasoning and the model. In a narrow panel the mode and
  reasoning pills keep only their icons (a container query), the model keeps its name. The send
  button is quiet while there's nothing to send.
- **Attachments.** Cards above the box, one row that scrolls sideways: images as thumbnails,
  files and big pastes as a text preview with a type badge and line count; @-mentions as chips.
  The + menu: Upload from computer… (system picker, any folder), Add project file…, Problems,
  Terminal output, Editor selection, Web page…. Dropping files on the chat attaches them: from
  the system's file manager (Tauri's drop events; the explorer leaves drops over the chat alone,
  `data-os-drop`) and from the explorer (a file drop target in the dock's drag controller,
  `WorkbenchServices.fileDropTarget`). Pasting files or images attaches them; pasting 1500+
  characters or 15+ lines makes a "Pasted" card instead of filling the box. Project files stay
  paths (read when sending); files from elsewhere and images are read when attached (Rust:
  `attach_pick`, `dropped_list`, `dropped_read` — only files the user picked or dropped, 20 MB
  each, at most 10 per message). Text goes to the model as fenced context, images as images.
  Sent messages keep the cards above the bubble (`Item.attachments`; image data isn't saved with
  the chat, as before).
- **Reasoning pill.** Think when the model can / always / never, effort, and Agent settings…;
  the agent's "…" menu also has Agent settings. `settings.open` takes a `category`.
- **Outline.** Collapse all and a "…" menu in its header (also on the Explorer section's header):
  sort by position / name / kind (`outline.sortOrder`), follow cursor (`outline.followCursor`),
  collapse / expand all. Right-click a symbol: go to, select (`editor.select`, new), copy name,
  copy path (`Zed.run`).
- **Bug: sticky rows sat a gutter to the left.** They span the full width, and the gutter was
  their padding, which replaced the row's own: content and indent guides were 8 px left of the
  rows under them. The gutters are now transparent borders, so each tree's own padding applies.

### D132 — TextMate tokens like VS Code (Oniguruma); Shiki themes; file icon themes; small fixes
- **Syntax highlighting.** Monaco 0.57 is current (VS Code ships the same editor), so the
  difference was ours: `@shikijs/monaco` re-registered every language and redefined the theme each
  time a grammar loaded (all open editors re-tokenized), mapped every token's color back to a
  scope by lookup, and Shiki's JavaScript regex engine translated patterns differently in WebKit
  (`//` comments ran into the next line). Now (`monaco/textmate.ts`): the grammars' encoded tokens
  go to Monaco unchanged (`tokenizeEncoded`, the same 32-bit layout VS Code passes — standard token
  types, so brackets in comments and strings aren't paired, and font styles), Monaco's color map
  is the TextMate theme's (`languages.setColorMap`; it grows as tokens use new colors), each
  language registers once, and the regex engine is Oniguruma (WebAssembly, a 0.6 MB lazy chunk —
  the engine grammars are written for and VS Code uses; the JavaScript engine stays as fallback).
  A file's grammar starts loading while the file is read, and the common grammars load when the IDE
  is idle, so files open colored. modern-monaco takes the same route (Shiki grammars and themes,
  lazily); its pre-rendering before Monaco loads is what our plain-text preview already does.
- **Shiki themes.** Shiki's 63 other bundled themes are color themes (Color theme…, source
  "Shiki"), each a lazy chunk: VS Code theme JSON, so they color the UI too. Dark+ and Light+ stay
  the built-in Dark and Light.
- **File icon themes** in VS Code's format (`iconDefinitions`, file names / extensions / language
  ids / folder names, root and expanded folders, light variants, icon fonts). `workbench.iconTheme`
  (VS Code's setting and ids, so a folder's .vscode/settings.json carries over): Material Icon
  Theme by default — the most installed one; MIT; its 1,251 SVGs (1 MB) copied into dist by
  build.mjs from the `material-icon-theme` dev dependency, its manifest a lazy chunk — or Minimal
  (the IDE's own glyphs), or any extension's `contributes.iconThemes` (images read from the
  extension when shown). Icons go through `icon("fi:file:<name>")`, so the explorer, tabs,
  breadcrumbs, quick open, search, source control, problems and agent cards all follow; icons on
  screen are swapped when the theme changes.
- **Explorer:** with folder icons, files no longer get a spacer column (they stay where they
  were). A system drag over the window opens the explorer when the sidebar is closed.
- **Title bar:** the folder name is gone (it's in the status bar).
- **Dock:** a maximized group's button shows inward arrows and restores; the tab strip is as wide
  as its tabs, so the scrollbar under them has a normal cursor (the strip's empty rest is still
  the grab handle).
- **Problems count:** like VS Code, it counts what the language services report, which for
  TypeScript, JSON, CSS and HTML is the open files (VS Code's TypeScript does the same unless
  project-wide diagnostics are turned on); whole-project errors come from a build or check
  command.

### D133 — Quick access like VS Code; workspace symbols; Ctrl+Tab; in-app documentation; About
- **Quick access** is one box whose first character picks what it searches, as in VS Code
  (`quickOpen/quickAccess.ts`): nothing = files (Ctrl/Cmd+P), `>` commands (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and
  F1 — `palette.show` is now `quickOpen.show {query:">"}`), `@` symbols in the active editor
  (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O; it was Monaco's own quick outline), `#` symbols in the workspace (Ctrl/Cmd+T),
  `:` a line (Ctrl+G from the keyboard), `?` the list of prefixes. Typing or deleting the prefix
  switches modes in place; the placeholder says what the box searches. The palette no longer
  needs a folder open. The separate palette list is gone; its "recent first", keybinding chips
  and argument prompts moved over (`quickOpen/input.ts`).
- **Workspace symbols** (`quickOpen/workspaceSymbols.ts`) merge two sources: `workspace/symbol`
  from running language servers that offer it (the client now announces the capability), and a
  declaration search over the folder — one regex (`function` / `class` / `interface` / `type` /
  `enum` / `struct` / `trait` / `def` / `fn` / `func` / `mod`, plus column-0 `const` / `let` /
  `var`) run by the Rust search, name characters in the query's order, then fuzzy-ranked. The
  search needs no server, so every folder gets it; it misses what a line can't show (methods
  declared without a keyword) — servers fill that in. Agents: `quickOpen.findSymbols {query}`.
- **Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab**: open editors, most recently used first, with the previous one
  selected; Tab again moves on while Ctrl is held and releasing Ctrl opens it (QuickInput's
  `activeIndex` / `acceptOnKeyUp`, `moveActive`).
- **Go to line before a file has loaded** clamped to line 1 (the line count was unknown, read as
  1); the reveal now waits for the document.
- **Documentation in the IDE.** VS Code's Help → Documentation opens its website and its
  walkthroughs live on the welcome page; with no website, the user guide ships with the IDE
  (`docs/guide/*.md`, bundled as raw text) and opens as a Documentation tab (Help menu,
  `help.showDocs {page}`) with a page list and `command:` links that run commands. Agents read the
  same pages with `help.readDocs` (so "how do I…" questions are answered from the guide).
- **Help → About** did nothing visible in the webview (the native message box wasn't shown); it
  is now the IDE's own dialog with version, OS, webview engine and data folder, and Copy.
- **OpenRouter** defaults to `openrouter/free` (OpenRouter's router to whatever free model is
  available) when it's linked and the current model isn't available.
- **Flush layout:** no line above the status bar; the sidebar, dock and sash keep a bottom border,
  so the workspace is still separated from it and the activity bar runs into the status bar.
  Section headers (Outline under the explorer) are a row tall with 20 px buttons, and the section
  sash sits above the header so it doesn't cover the buttons.
- **Tests:** steps can run `background` (a picker the next steps answer; errors and, with `print`,
  results are logged), and `dev.type` types into an input and presses or releases keys (with
  `code` and modifiers, so keybindings resolve). The unit-test bundler has the `?raw` plugin.

### D134 — VS Code tasks; preview in place; activity badges; Manage menu; theme dropdowns
- **Tasks, like VS Code's.** A task now runs as its own process in a terminal tab (`pty_spawn`
  with a run spec: the command line through the task's or the default shell — login shells on
  Unix so profile PATHs are there — or `"type": "process"` with its arguments; extra `env`;
  `${env:…}` expanded in Rust), not typed into an interactive shell; " *  Executing task" above,
  the exit code and "press any key to close it" below, and the terminal is reused as
  `presentation.panel` says. Problem matchers (`problemMatchers.ts`): the common built-in names
  ($tsc, $tsc-watch, $eslint-stylish/-compact, $gcc, $msCompile, $go, $rustc, $jshint,
  $lessCompile, $esbuild/-watch), custom regexes, `base`, multi-line patterns with `loop`,
  `fileLocation`, background `beginsPattern`/`endsPattern`. Their problems go to a new
  `ProblemCollections` service: the Problems view lists them for any file (open or not) and open
  files show them as squiggles (Monaco markers with an `external:` owner, kept out of the
  editors' own list so nothing is counted twice). Also `dependsOrder` (VS Code's default,
  parallel, now applies), `${input:…}` (promptString, pickString, command), `${command:…}`,
  `${config:…}`, top-level `options`/`presentation`, `presentation.reveal/focus/panel/close`,
  `hide`, `runOptions.runOn: folderOpen` (trusted folders, `task.allowAutomaticTasks`), user
  tasks, and running tasks: terminate, restart, show (status bar item while one runs),
  `ide://tasks`. `tasks.run` now waits for the task to end (or a background one to be ready) and
  returns its exit code, problem count and output, which is what an agent needs after a build.
  Matchers that come from extensions (`contributes.problemMatchers`) aren't read yet.
- **Preview in place.** Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V and a new eye action swap a Markdown/SVG/CSV file and
  its preview in the same tab (same position; a file with unsaved changes keeps its tab and the
  preview opens beside it). The preview's "Open source" goes to the file when it's open (side by
  side) and swaps back when the preview is alone. Tab actions can name their own tab (`"$tab"`).
- **Activity badges** as in VS Code: the explorer counts unsaved files, source control counts
  pending changes (staged, unstaged, conflicts — `scm.countBadge: all`), and work running in a
  view that isn't shown is a spinning badge (it was a sweeping line). In `ide://layout`.
- **The gear** opens VS Code's Manage menu (command palette, profiles, settings, extensions,
  keyboard shortcuts, snippets, tasks, Themes, Layout density) instead of going straight to
  Settings.
- **Settings:** Color theme and File icon theme are dropdowns of what's installed
  (`SettingsService.registerChoices`: runtime choices for a string setting); Color theme's
  "Built-in" entry follows the Theme setting (Dark/Light). `explorer.folderIcons` (now on by
  default) turns folder icons off with any icon theme, Material included, except themes that
  hide the chevrons (their folder icons are the expand marks).

### D135 — One color theme setting; readable imported themes; the workspace as a rounded frame
- **One setting.** `workbench.colorTheme` is the only theme setting, as in VS Code: "Dark+" (the
  default) and "Light+" are the built-in themes, beside Shiki's and extensions'. The old
  Dark/Light `workbench.theme` is deprecated (hidden in Settings — `SettingSchema.deprecated` —
  still read while `workbench.colorTheme` is empty, and migrated to Dark+/Light+ once). Toggle
  light/dark, the Appearance and Manage menus and `ui.setTheme` write `workbench.colorTheme`;
  VS Code's "Default Dark Modern" / "Dark+" / "Light+"… map to the built-ins, other names pass
  through (an installed theme with that label applies; otherwise the built-in of the kind the
  name suggests). The first paint caches the applied theme's kind.
- **Imported themes stay readable.** The IDE has one text color for every surface, so a VS Code
  theme's surface color that text can't be read on (contrast under 4.5 against the theme's
  foreground) is left to the base theme of the same kind: Slack Ochin (light, with a dark title
  bar, side bar and menus) gets light menus, inputs and title bar instead of dark ones with dark
  text. Accents must be colors (chroma ≥ 0.12; Ochin's near-black focus border isn't). Borders are
  never taken from the theme: `panel.border` is often a loud accent meant for one line (Dracula's
  purple), not for every divider.
- **Explorer folder icons** are off by default again (on: any icon theme).
- **Flush layout frame.** The title bar has no line of its own (like the status bar, D133); the
  workspace — sidebar, splitter and editor area — is one framed region with 8px rounded outer
  corners (`--radius-workspace`) and a 6px gap on the side away from the activity bar
  (`--size-workspace-inset`), so the title bar, activity bar and status bar read as one piece of
  chrome around it. Done in CSS on the existing elements (edge pieces found by sidebar side and
  `[hidden]` siblings). The floating layout's title bar lost a stray line too.

### D136 — No default-theme flash at startup; terminals take a theme that changed while they started
- The first paint now restores the last start's whole look, not just Dark/Light: the color
  theme's token overrides and its syntax theme (VS Code JSON) are cached with the first-paint
  values (localStorage) and applied before anything renders. The appearance effect waits for the
  settings files (`SettingsService.loaded`) instead of applying the defaults first, and an
  extension's theme the last start used is waited for (up to 5 s) while extensions register.
  Together these removed the "default theme, then mine" blink.
- A terminal still starting when the theme changed kept the old colors (the change found no
  terminal to update and later changes were deduplicated against it): the service keeps the
  latest theme and a terminal that comes up with an older one takes it.

### D137 — The everyday git workflow; floating sidebar; drag the sidebar closed
- **Git, as far as a daily workflow goes in VS Code:** a commit's details and its changes (the diff
  tab got a read-only right side, `head`, so a file in a commit is `git:<parent>` ↔
  `git:<commit>`; renamed files read their old path at the parent); a **Commits** section in
  Source control (incoming from the upstream, the branch's history with outgoing commits
  marked, refs as chips; expand a commit to its files) — VS Code's Source Control Graph, without
  the lanes; commit variants behind the Commit button's arrow (staged, all, amend, & push, &
  sync, undo last commit); branches (create from, rename, delete with a confirm for unmerged
