  work, merge, rebase); a merge / rebase / cherry-pick / revert that stops on conflicts shows a
  banner with Continue (disabled until the conflicts are staged) and Abort; tags; remotes;
  .gitignore; Pull offers Rebase or Merge when the branches diverged (it stays fast-forward
  only otherwise); force push with lease; publishing a branch picks origin or the only remote.
  Every operation is a fixed argument list in Rust (`ops::repo_op`), names that look like
  options are refused, and git never waits for an editor (`GIT_EDITOR=true`).
- **Commit message from the model** (Cursor's and Copilot's sparkle): the staged diff (or all
  changes), cut at 24 KB, goes to the user's edit model with a short instruction; the reply
  streams into the message box.
- **Floating layout:** the sidebar is part of the shell (the title bar's color, no card) and the
  editor groups are cards with a hairline border.
- **Sidebar splitter:** dragging it under half the minimum width hides the sidebar (VS Code's
  snap); dragging back out brings it back, in the same drag. Recorded as `layout.toggleSidebar`.

### D138 — Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows; picked themes color the editor fully; audit fixes; chat turns
- **Ctrl+Shift+P** never reached the page in WebView2 (Edge's InPrivate shortcut): the main and
  auxiliary windows turn WebView2's browser accelerator keys off (`accelerators.rs`, through
  `with_webview` and the `webview2-com` / `windows` crates the app already links — nothing new is
  compiled). Every key now reaches the IDE's keybindings; `browserDefaults.ts` still cancels the
  browser's own meaning of the ones nothing claims. Clipboard keys aren't accelerators.
- **Editor colors of a picked theme:** a Shiki or extension theme's own editor colors (scrollbar,
  widgets, selection…) now win over the IDE's token-derived ones inside Monaco, as in VS Code;
  the built-in Dark+ / Light+ keep the tokens. Scrollbars outside the editor (`::-webkit-scrollbar`)
  are repainted after a theme change (Chromium keeps their old colors when only a variable
  changes).
- **Audit fixes:** a task two others depend on starts once (in-flight starts are joined); task
  output is cleaned per complete line (escape codes split across chunks, `\r` progress redraws),
  pending text is capped; problems are published at most every 150 ms; a ready-timer per
  background run no longer piles up in the extension's store; `${input:…}` lists can't be emptied
  by a concurrent load; task squiggles match Windows paths case-insensitively; a failed
  generated commit message restores the box; `git.ignore` skips paths outside the repository;
  the Commits list refreshes when tags or the branch name change; remotes, tags and the
  operation in progress are read only after git-dir changes (not on every save) and again after
  a failed read; Source control's menus replace each other instead of accumulating; the
  first-paint cache isn't rewritten when nothing changed; function keys pass the quick input
  only when they're F1–F24.
- **Chat:** the user's turns sit on the right at up to 85% width (most chat UIs), answers keep
  the full column; the space under the newest message is doubled.

### D139 — Commit graph, interactive rebase, worktrees, GitHub, sign-in prompts; search like VS Code
- **Commit graph:** Commits draws lanes (one small SVG per row; `graph.ts` lays them out from
  the parents, DOM-free and tested). It shows HEAD with its upstream (incoming / outgoing
  marked in the same graph), or every ref with `git.graph.allBranches` (the button on the
  Commits row). Lines continue past an expanded commit's files. `git log --date-order` keeps
  children above parents.
- **Interactive rebase** without an editor: a tab lists the commits after a base, oldest first,
  with pick / reword / edit / squash / fixup / drop, drag or Alt+↑/↓ to reorder, letter keys for
  actions. git takes the list as written: `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR` is `cp "$IDE_REBASE_TODO"`
  (git runs it through its shell, which Git for Windows ships too); a reword is a `pick` plus an
  `exec git commit --amend --only -F` of a message file found with `git rev-parse --git-path`,
  so it also works after a stop and `--continue`. `--autostash`, `--no-autosquash`. Agents pass
  the steps directly. Rejected: starting the IDE binary as the sequence editor (a second
  startup path for no gain) and parsing git's own todo (comments, localized text).
- **Worktrees:** list / create (new branch or existing, default folder next to the repository)
  / delete / prune; open one in this window or a new one. A new window is a second process of
  the IDE (`app_new_window`; also File → New window, Ctrl+Shift+N), since the app has one
  workspace per window.
- **GitHub** through the user's `gh` CLI, like git through `git`: no tokens or OAuth in the IDE.
  Fixed operations with free text in `--flag=value` form; pull requests (list, open in a tab
  with description / checks / comments, checkout, create — publishing first —, merge), issues,
  and the current branch's pull request in the status bar (asked once per branch). Remote
  images in descriptions aren't loaded (alt text), keeping the no-network-by-itself rule.
- **Sign-in prompts (askpass):** with no credential helper answering, git and ssh ask
  `$GIT_ASKPASS` / `$SSH_ASKPASS` (`SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=prefer`); both point at the IDE's binary,
  which (seeing its env) connects to a token-checked listener on 127.0.0.1, and the question
  shows in the quick input, masked for secrets. Nothing is stored. A user's own askpass wins (an
  empty variable counts as unset). Windows keeps Git Credential Manager, which answers first.
- **Search:** `search.exclude` (+ `files.exclude`), `useIgnoreFiles`, `followSymlinks`,
  `smartCase`, `maxResults`, `searchOnType` (+ debounce), `showLineNumbers`, `collapseResults`;
  toggles for "only open editors" and "use exclude settings and ignore files" in the glob fields
  and preserve case in the replace field; a single result's Replace (`lines`); the results menu
  (open to the side, replace, dismiss, copy / copy path / copy all, reveal, find in folder,
  exclude folder, collapse / expand all). Settings are applied in one DOM-free function
  (`effectiveOptions`), so the form keeps what the user typed.
- **Source control box:** two lines tall by default, the AI button clear of the scrollbar, a
  softer divider in the split Commit button.
- **Review fixes before shipping:** the rebase refuses to start while another operation is in
  progress, checks the list against a fresh plan (and runs with
  `rebase.missingCommitsCheck=error`, so nothing is dropped silently), keeps the reword files
  through an `edit` stop (which exits 0), loads the whole message (body, trailers) for a
  reword, and refuses more than 2000 commits instead of cutting the list; "Interactive rebase
  from here" only on commits in HEAD's history; one rebase tab at a time. "New window" passes
  `--new-window`, so an empty window doesn't reopen the last folder (two windows on one folder
  would share its state file). `gh` is found through the login shell and the usual install
  folders when the app's PATH is short (macOS Dock). The status bar's pull request is cached
  per repository and branch for three minutes. Open-editor paths with glob characters
  (`app/[id]/page.tsx`) match only that file. Askpass: prompts close when git stops waiting,
  a reloaded window fails the old prompts at once, ssh's notice-only calls aren't prompts, a
  request line is capped, and `ide <folder>` from a git hook still starts normally. Deleting
  a worktree with changes asks before forcing.

### D140 — Error Lens–style diagnostics, project formatters, accounts; small fixes
- **Inline diagnostics** (the Error Lens extension, which many users install first): the most
  severe problem of a line is written after it in its color, with a faint line tint.
  `editor.inlineDiagnostics`: off / errors / errorsAndWarnings (default) / all. Built on the
  engine's line annotations and line decorations, DOM-free selection tested.
- **Project formatters:** "Format document" (Shift+Alt+F, the menu, `editor.formatDocument`)
  and format on save use the project's own tool when it has one — Biome (with `biome.json`) or
  Prettier from `node_modules/.bin`, Ruff or Black configured in `pyproject.toml` / `ruff.toml`,
  rustfmt in a Cargo project (its edition), gofmt, clang-format with `.clang-format` — found from
  the file up to the workspace root, so nested packages use theirs. Text in on stdin, out on
  stdout (nothing written by the tool); fixed argument lists in Rust; trusted folders only
  (`editor.projectFormatters` turns it off). A formatter error is shown instead of falling back
  to a different style. Edits apply as the changed range only (`replaceText` now keeps the
  common start and end), so the cursor and folds stay. Chosen over registering a Monaco
  formatting provider because Monaco's choice among several providers isn't controllable.
- **Accounts** (VS Code's person icon above the gear): the IDE account is ready on the desktop
  side (OAuth code + PKCE through the browser, loopback redirect, session file; endpoints in
  docs/accounts.md) and switches on with product.json `accountsUrl` (or `accounts.serverUrl`
  while developing the service); until then "Sign in" says it's coming. GitHub sign-in is real
  today through the GitHub CLI (`gh auth login` in a terminal; the menu lists its accounts).
  "Backup and sync settings…" exports / imports a profile until sync exists.
- **AI commit message:** reasoning models' `<think>` text is stripped, the budget allows for
  thinking (an empty answer now says so instead of leaving the box empty), and with nothing
  staged the user is offered "Stage all and continue".
- **Notifications** all hide themselves (paused on hover): 4 s info, 6 s warnings, 8 s errors,
  20 s with buttons; the bell keeps the history.
- The title bar's search box is VS Code's command center: quick open, labelled Ctrl+P. The
  welcome page drops the Open recent / Command palette / Settings links; recent rows are
  vertically centered.

### D141 — Workspace undo you can trust; update imports on rename/move
A report: deleting a project folder and pressing Ctrl+Z brought the folder back looking empty.
The files were back on disk, but the explorer had cached a failed listing from the moment the
folder disappeared. The audit that followed tightened every layer, using VS Code as the
reference.
- **Trash never deletes for good.** Before, a failed move into the app trash (Windows locks
  files that are open elsewhere) fell back to a *permanent* delete. Now that's an error and
  nothing changes. Only a trash on another drive copies the item over first; if removing the
  original then stops half way, what was removed is copied back.
- **All or nothing.** Every undo / redo of a create, delete or move first checks that it can run
  completely: the items are there, nothing sits where they go (no overwriting), and the trashed
  items still exist. It changes nothing otherwise. If a step still fails mid way, the steps
  already done are reversed. Deleting several items where one fails keeps the others
  undoable.
- **A failed step stays on the stack.** Nothing changed, so it can be retried once the obstacle
  is gone. "Skip it" on the warning drops it, so the entries before it can still be undone.
  Before, the entry silently vanished.
- **The tree comes back whole.** A folder whose listing failed (it was gone for a moment) is
  listed again when it reappears. Undoing a delete reloads the restored folders themselves and
  reopens the folders that were expanded.
- **Confirmations like VS Code's `explorer.confirmUndo`.** An undo or redo that deletes files
  (undoing a create or paste, redoing a delete) asks first: "default". "verbose" asks every
  time; "light" never asks.
- **Ctrl+Z in a file that a multi-file operation just wrote** (replace all, accepted agent
  edits, a rename that updated imports) asks "Undo … in all files?": *Undo in N files*,
  *Undo this file*, or *Cancel*. Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z do the same for redo, as in VS Code.
  The editor only asks when its last change *was* that operation's reload, and nothing moved
  in the history since. The check uses a reload mark (model version + time) on the document and
  the entry's `appliedAt`; otherwise Ctrl+Z is the plain text undo, with no delay.
- **Update imports on rename/move** (`editor.updateImportsOnFileMove`: prompt / always / never;
  agents pass `updateImports`):
  - Relative imports that pointed at the moved JS/TS files, or into moved folders, are
    rewritten. So are the moved files' own imports.
  - Each specifier keeps its style: no extension, an extension, `.js` written for `.ts`, or a
    folder `index`.
  - The edits are part of the move's undo entry. Undo reverts the imports first, and only if
    each file still holds what was written; then it moves the files back.
  - Files with unsaved changes are edited in their editor; others are written to disk and their
    editors reload.
  - Path aliases (tsconfig `paths`) aren't rewritten. A language-server rename would cover
    those later.
- **Hardening after an independent audit (19 findings):**
  - **Case-only renames:** allowed only when the target *is* the same file (case-insensitive
    file systems). On Linux, renaming `readme.md` to `README.md` no longer replaces another
    `README.md`.
  - **Symlinks:** delete, rename and move act on the link itself, not on what it points to
    (`resolve_entry`).
  - **Editor keys are per editor.** Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z and Shift+Alt+F are
    editor-scoped actions. Before, Monaco's `addCommand` was global: the newest editor answered
    for all of them, so Ctrl+Z could change another tab.
  - **Cross-drive trash:** undoing a delete copies the item back when the trash is on another
    drive. A failed repair keeps the trash copy and says where it is.
  - **Restore deleted files…** (File menu, `explorer.restoreDeleted`): the app trash keeps
    where each item came from for 30 days. An item can be restored after its undo step is
    gone (restart, skipped, more than 100 steps), beside the original as "name (restored)"
    when something is in the way.
  - **The stacks stay ordered.** Entries have ids, and an undo or redo runs only on the entry
    that was confirmed. A step that runs while a new operation is recorded keeps the order;
    redo is dropped when a new operation came after it.
  - **Replace all:** files over the local-history size limit, or that fail to write, are left
    unchanged and named. Its undo and redo, and the agent's, check every file first and then
    apply all or none. Undoing agent edits that created files asks first.
  - **Import updates:**
    - The move is on the stack at once, and the import edits join it when they're written
      (skipped when the move was undone while the question was open).
    - Undo reverts the imports that still match, then moves the files; redo treats imports
      that can't follow as a warning.
    - Files that aren't valid UTF-8 are left alone, and BOMs are kept.
    - A search cut short updates nothing.
    - Commented-out imports are left alone.
  - **Reload marks** remember the model, so a recreated editor never matches. The
    "undo in all files" offer needs the reload within 15 s of the step.
  - **Workspace Ctrl+Z** answers in the file tree only (`explorerFocus`), not in other sidebar
    views.
  - **Not done yet** (VS Code differences): renaming an open file still starts its text undo
    history over. Tabs of deleted files close and don't come back with the undo.

### D142 — Stuck models are stopped; account picture; instant Accounts menu; show hidden files
- **Degenerate output guard** (`agent/repetition.ts`, tested): free and small models sometimes
  repeat one sentence in their reasoning until the output limit, which can take minutes. Every
  stream (agent turns, sub-requests, Edit with AI, completions, commit messages) is watched.
  Collapsing whitespace, a tail that is one passage of 12–800 characters repeated (at least
  6 copies and 900 characters while reasoning; 8 and 2000 in answers) stops the request. So does
  reasoning over 120k characters. The turn ends with a plain explanation. Rejected:
  provider-side repetition penalties (not every API has them, and they change answers).
- **Accounts menu opens at once.** It used to wait for `gh auth status` (a process start plus a
  network check). Now it shows what's known and refreshes in the background when the data is
  older than 30 s; window focus refreshes at most every 5 minutes.
- **Account picture:** the GitHub (or IDE account) avatar replaces the Accounts icon, as in
  VS Code. Rust fetches it (https, GitHub or the accounts server only, ≤ 2 MB), caches it a day
  in `<data>/avatars/` and serves the cache offline. The page gets bytes, so the CSP stays
  without remote images.
- **Show hidden files** (explorer ⋯ menu and right-click on empty space,
  `explorer.showExcludedFiles`): files.exclude entries are listed, dimmed and italic, and stay
  excluded from search and quick open.

### D143 — Debugger; bookmarks; partial undo of multi-file steps; chat polish; new logo
- **Debugger** (`extensions/debug`), VS Code's workflow and keys: F5 starts (continues when
  paused), F9 or a click in the editor's margin toggles a breakpoint, F10 / F11 / Shift+F11 step,
  F6 pauses, Shift+F5 stops, Ctrl+Shift+F5 restarts, Ctrl+F5 runs without debugging. The "Run and
  debug" view (Ctrl+Shift+D) has the configuration picker, the toolbar, Variables (lazy tree),
  Call stack (runtime internals folded) and Breakpoints (enable, condition, "Uncaught
  exceptions"); the debug console (Ctrl+Shift+Y) evaluates in the selected frame. Configurations
  come from `.vscode/launch.json` and the IDE's own `launch.json` (VS Code's format and
  variables, `preLaunchTask`); with none, the active file runs.
  - **Two transports behind one `DebugSession`.** Debug adapters over stdio speak DAP
    (`session.ts`): debugpy (`python -m debugpy.adapter`), lldb-dap, GDB 14+
    (`--interpreter=dap`) and any `debugAdapter: { command, args }`; their `runInTerminal`
    requests open a terminal tab. Node runs as `node --inspect-brk=127.0.0.1:0` in a terminal
    tab and is debugged through its inspector (Chrome DevTools Protocol, `cdp.ts`). Rejected:
    bundling vscode-js-debug (a large download per platform) and widening the webview's CSP to
    `ws://127.0.0.1:*`. Instead Rust has a minimal WebSocket client (`src-tauri/src/debug`, no new
    crate) that only connects to 127.0.0.1 / localhost / ::1.
  - Breakpoints are kept per workspace, follow their lines while editing (the engine's
    decorations move them) and their files on rename. They are hollow while a session couldn't
    place them. Stepping waits for breakpoint changes already sent, so a fast program can't outrun
    a just-added breakpoint.
  - Not yet: attaching to a running Node process, source maps (TypeScript run through Node's type
    stripping keeps its lines), child processes / workers, logpoints, data breakpoints, hover
    evaluation, several sessions at once.
- **Bookmarks** (`extensions/bookmarks`), like the popular extension: Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+K marks a line
  (a ribbon in the margin's right lane; breakpoints keep the center lane), Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+L / J go
  to the next / previous one across files, "List bookmarks…" (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Shift+K) shows each
  with its label and line text. They follow edits and renames and are kept per workspace.
- **Partial undo of multi-file steps.** VS Code refuses a workspace undo when any file changed
  since and, from the editor, offers "Undo this file" (which we already had). Here, after the
  refusal, the user is asked "Undo in the other N files?": the changed files keep their content
  and leave the step for good (redo skips them too). Agents pass
  `workspace.undo { skipChanged: true }` and get `skipped`. All-or-nothing remains the default:
  a step is never half applied without being asked.
- **Chat:** bold is lighter (550 in the agent's prose, 600 elsewhere), so answers read less like
  a document. A user message over 8 lines or 600 characters folds with "Show more", as modern
  chats do. Code blocks scroll inside 420 px. Text in chat uses the normal arrow cursor, not the
  I-beam, over scrollbars and blank space.
- **Logo:** the new mark replaces the cube everywhere (UI, window and installer icons); the cube
  stays in `assets/logo-cube.svg` and `src-tauri/icons-cube/`.
- **m6.41.1 hotfix:** the D142 avatar rule was inserted into the middle of an existing selector,
  which hid the activity bar's view buttons. The UI test now checks that they are laid out, not
  only that they exist.

### D144 — Clean environment for projects; the agent and PowerShell; scrollbar and chat fixes
- **npm's variables don't leak into projects.** Started with `npm run dev`, the IDE inherited
  npm's script environment (`npm_config_local_prefix` pointing at the IDE's folder,
  `npm_package_json`, `INIT_CWD`, `NODE`, and the IDE's `node_modules/.bin` on `PATH`), and every
  terminal, task and agent command passed it on: a project's `vite` or `tsc` could resolve to the
  IDE's copies. `forget_npm_launcher()` removes them first thing in `main` (only when npm started
  the IDE). The `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` that `npm install` hit in a
  new Vite + React project wasn't reproducible with that environment on Linux; it matches a known
  npm 10 bug with recent packages' peer dependencies (npm/cli#8261, #9787), fixed by npm 11.
- **The agent and PowerShell.** On Windows the prompt now spells out PowerShell's equivalents,
  and the agent's commands get the bash idioms models write anyway rewritten
  (`pty/bash_idioms.rs`, tested): `rm -rf`, `mkdir -p`, `ls -la`, `| head` / `| tail`, `which`,
  `/dev/null` redirections, top-level only and outside quotes. The approval card still shows what
  the model wrote. Rejected: running agent commands in Git Bash when installed (not everyone has
  it, and the terminal the user sees is PowerShell).
- **Loops:** the prompt tells the agent to stop and report after the same error twice, and not
  to work around the folder boundary (npm caches, global installs, folders elsewhere).
- **Path arguments** are cleaned before they're resolved (`agent/pathArg.ts`, tested): quotes, a
  parameter name in front (`path:\C:\…`), a slash before a drive.
- A failed step's long error in the chat truncates instead of scrolling the chat sideways; the
  editor tabs' scrollbar handle brightens on hover and while dragged, and every handle brightens
  under the pointer.

### D145 — Debugger closer to VS Code: breakpoint kinds, watch, hover, source maps, attach
- **Breakpoint kinds.** Conditions, hit counts (`5` = from the fifth hit, `>5`, `==5`, `%3`;
  counted only when the condition holds, as in VS Code) and logpoints (`{expr}` filled in; they
  print instead of stopping), plus caught and uncaught exceptions. Right-click in the editor's
  margin offers VS Code's menu (add conditional breakpoint, add logpoint, edit, disable, run to
  line). DAP adapters get them as `condition` / `hitCondition` / `logMessage` when they say they
  support them. For Node all three compile into one inspector condition (`cdpCondition`,
  tested by evaluating it). Logpoint messages go through a `Runtime.addBinding` function, so
  they reach the debug console without landing in the program's own output.
- **Run to cursor** (Ctrl+F10, margin menu): the inspector's `continueToLocation`; for DAP
  adapters, a temporary breakpoint removed at the next stop.
- **Watch**, kept per folder and re-evaluated at each stop or frame change. **Set value**
  (double-click or F2 in Variables): `Debugger.setVariableValue` for scope variables and an
  assignment through `callFunctionOn` for properties; DAP `setVariable`. As in Chrome DevTools,
  a value V8 has already folded into the expression being returned can't be changed.
- **Hover values while paused**: the identifier under the pointer with its member chain
  (`hoverExpression`, tested), evaluated with V8's `throwOnSideEffect`, so a hover never runs
  code that changes state. Objects show their first 20 properties.
- **Debug console results expand** like Variables, loaded on demand.
- **Source maps** (`sourcemap.ts`, tested: VLQ, sourceRoot, index maps, inline `data:` maps).
  Breakpoints in sources are placed at their generated positions:
  - CommonJS scripts with a map pause first through V8's `beforeScriptWithSourceMapExecution`
    instrumentation.
  - The entry script (already running at --inspect-brk's first stop) is handled at that stop.
  - ES modules get no instrumentation pause in Node 22. For them, each file with breakpoints
    gets a guard breakpoint on its first line, so the module stops before its code runs. Seen
    with tsx: the script's URL is the `.ts` file itself, with an inline map.
  - Maps load lazily; those under node_modules only for a breakpoint there.
  - Stops and call stacks show source lines.
  - Verified with esbuild output and with tsx as both CommonJS and ES modules.
- **Attach** (`"request": "attach"`, `port` / `address` / `websocketAddress`): Rust asks the
  inspector's `/json/list` (local addresses only, reading by Content-Length since Node keeps the
  connection open). Stopping detaches and leaves the program running.
- **Floating toolbar** (`debug.toolBarLocation`: floating by default, docked, hidden): over the
  top of the window, movable by its grip, as in VS Code.
- **Fixed on the way:**
  - Node's "Debugger listening" line could arrive before its listener was assigned (a race
    that threw).
  - `terminal.runCommand` picked a finished task or debug terminal; it now uses the most
    recent live shell.
- **Browser debugging later:** VS Code debugs front-end code by launching Chrome/Edge with a
  debugging port and speaking the same protocol. The inspector client and source maps here are
  what that needs (a "launch browser" type reusing `CdpSession`), and on Windows also
  WebView2's debugging port.

### D146 — Settings open on everything; VS Code's editor metrics; DevTools you can work in
- **Settings** open on **All settings**: every setting, one section per category under its icon,
  scrolling, as in VS Code. Categories in the navigation still show one at a time. Categories that
  had the generic gear got their own icons (Accounts, Debug, Markdown, Outline, Task, GitHub…).
- **Editor and terminal defaults:**
  - Word wrap is on.
  - The terminal's font is 13 px; the editor stays at 14.
  - The editor no longer forces a 1.6 line height (22 px at 14 px). Monaco's own default
    applies, which is VS Code's: 1.35 × the font size on Windows and Linux (19 px), 1.5 on macOS.
    `editor.lineHeight` still overrides it.
- **Browser DevTools:**
  - **Resizable panes:** every two-pane panel (Elements' DOM / Styles, Sources, Application,
    Network's list / details) has a draggable divider (`splitPanes`). Sizes are kept while the
    IDE runs, and double-click resets. Elements stacks DOM over Styles when DevTools is narrow.
  - **Styles like Chrome's:**
    - Rules come in cascade order: the bridge computes each matched selector's specificity.
      Overridden declarations are struck through, with `!important` handled.
    - Each declaration has a checkbox. The bridge remembers a declaration switched off, so it
      comes back in place.
    - Names and values edit in place, applied live as you type. Tab moves on, Escape restores.
      Up/Down step numbers (Shift ×10, Alt ×0.1).
    - Color swatches open the system color picker. A click on a rule's `}` adds a declaration.
      `.cls` toggles classes, and there is a filter.
    - Changes stay in the page. Rejected: writing edits back to the stylesheet files, because
      the page's CSS is often generated (Vite, Tailwind, preprocessors) and a wrong mapping
      would corrupt the source.
  - **Elements:** DOM search by selector or text (Ctrl+F), cycling through matches.
  - **Sources:** find in file, marked with the CSS Custom Highlight API, so the syntax-colored
    code isn't rebuilt.
  - **Performance (new):**
    - Load metrics (TTFB, FCP, LCP, CLS, total blocking time, DOMContentLoaded, load) rated
      against the Web Vitals thresholds.
    - Downloads by type, slowest requests (they open in Network), DOM size and depth, JS
      memory.
    - A recording of frames per second, long tasks and heap. What the engine doesn't report
      (WebKit: LCP, CLS, long tasks, memory) says so.
    - Agents get it as `browser.performance {recordMs}`.
  - **Application:** IndexedDB (databases, stores with counts, their first entries), Cache
    storage (cached requests) and service workers (unregister), next to storage and cookies.
    Databases and caches can be deleted, after a confirmation.
- The color check skips `*.test.ts`, where colors are test data (a page's CSS being parsed).

### D147 — Performance records like Chrome's; DevTools fits small windows
- **Recording:**
  - **Reload and record** (Chrome's "start profiling and reload") reloads the page and records
    from the new document's start until Stop. The bridge restarts the recording in each new
    document with `fromNavigation`, so time 0 is the navigation start. The panel notices the new
    document by the connection dropping and coming back, with a 500 ms check as a fallback.
  - A document that replaces the page mid-recording continues the same way. The old document's
    data is lost with its bridge. Rejected: keeping a copy in the page's storage, because it would
    show up in Application and in the page's own data.
  - On stop, the bridge returns the span's frames (each frame's start, from
    requestAnimationFrame), a sample every 250 ms (fps, heap, DOM nodes), and requests from
    Resource Timing. It also returns long tasks, interactions (Event Timing, ≥ 16 ms) and
    layout shifts. These are watched from the bridge's start, because they reach observers only.
    It adds paint and load markers (FP, FCP, LCP, DCL, L) and the page's own
    `performance.mark` / `measure`.
  - `browser.record {start | reload | stop}` drives it, for agents too. Stop returns the
    statistics and markers. The panel's buttons run the command.
- **Timeline (`timeline.ts`, model and tests in `perfModel.ts`):**
  - An overview of the whole recording (fps, long tasks, load markers). Dragging it zooms;
    double-click shows everything.
  - Under it, a ruler and one track each for frames (late / dropped colored), FPS, main thread,
    network, interactions, timings, layout shifts and memory (heap and nodes). The main-thread
    track shows long tasks with the part over 50 ms hatched. Network requests are packed in
    rows and colored by type. Empty tracks are left out.
  - Paint and load markers draw lines across all tracks.
  - A line follows the pointer, with a readout of the frame, heap and nodes, or of the item
    under the pointer. Clicking a request opens it in Network.
  - Dragging across the tracks selects a range. Ctrl+wheel zooms, Shift+wheel pans.
  - Chrome's Summary below shows the selection or the shown span: fps, dropped frames, long
    tasks and blocking time, requests and bytes, the slowest interaction, layout shift and heap.
  - Drawn as SVG (lines, frames) and positioned elements (blocks), styled by tokens, so themes
    apply.
  - Rejected: Chrome's flame chart of every function call. It needs the CDP profiler, which a
    page bridge can't reach, and WebKit doesn't expose it.
- **Metric cards:** no colored left edge. A rating pill (dot and Good / Needs work / Poor) and,
  for the Web Vitals, a three-part scale with a marker where the value sits (as PageSpeed shows
  them).
- **Elements:** the collapsed "…" opens the element, like its arrow. Both have a pointer cursor
  and a hover background.
- **Small DevTools** (by DevTools' own width, via container queries and a ResizeObserver):
  - The tabs have icons. When they don't fit, they use shorter names (Perf, App), then icons
    only, with the selected tab keeping its name. Past that the strip scrolls like editor tabs
    (wheel, thin scrollbar, the selected tab kept in view).
  - Sources, Application and Network stack their panes when narrow, as Elements already did.
    Stacked panes get their own sizes, a share of the height rather than the side-by-side
    width.
  - Network drops the method, type and waterfall columns, then size.
  - The console's level chips become one "All levels" menu.
  - Buttons with an icon lose their words, filters fill the line, and the Downloads table
    drops its bar.
- Test helpers: `dev.setWindowSize`; `dev.click {hover, x}`.
- **Fixes (m6.47.1):**
  - **Reload and record on Windows (Vite):** WebView2 doesn't always deliver the old document's
    unload message, so the connection never looked dropped and the recording waited at
    "Reloading…". The panel now tells documents apart by `performance.timeOrigin`, which the
    peek returns. It reloads through the view directly (an error in the command path was
    swallowed before), and reloads once more after 4 s if nothing changed.
  - **Network track:** requests that overlapped were stacked on the last of 8 rows, so their
    labels printed over each other. Every request now gets a row, and past 8 rows the track
    scrolls on its own.
  - Clicking a request in the track (or in the slowest list) looked it up by the page's URL, but
    Network lists URLs as the user knows them. It now compares displayed URLs (query-less as a
    fallback), so it opens the request in Network instead of falling back to Sources.
  - Coming back to Performance kept nothing: the timeline was rebuilt and zoom, selection and
    scroll were lost. The recording's section is now kept while the recording is the same; only
    the load metrics are measured again.

### D148 — Source control's Graph like VS Code's; Publish to GitHub
- **Graph, not Commits:** the section is named as in VS Code. It is the history drawn as a graph,
  not a list of commits.
- **Ref badges:** each ref is a pill with an icon, colored by its kind:
  - the current branch: target icon, blue
  - other branches: green
  - remote branches: cloud, purple
  - tags: yellow

  A remote branch on the same commit as the local branch with its name shows as the cloud
  alone, so `main` and `origin/main` together take one name's width. `origin/HEAD` isn't shown.
  When a commit has refs, its row drops author and age (they are in the hover card). In a
  narrow sidebar (a container query), badges other than the current branch keep only their
  icon.
- **Hover card** (new `ui/HoverCard`):
  - What it is: an interactive card, unlike the tooltip, which stays non-interactive. It shows
    after a rest, and the pointer can move into it. Leaving it, Escape, a press elsewhere or the
    wheel hides it.
  - What it shows for a commit:
    - author (initials avatar in a stable color per email), age and full date
    - the whole message
    - files changed, with insertions and deletions. `CommitDetail` gained `insertions` /
      `deletions` from `diff-tree --shortstat`.
    - refs, and incoming / outgoing / HEAD
    - the short hash (click to copy), **Open on GitHub** (or GitLab, Bitbucket…: from the
      remote URLs `git_repo_state` now returns), **Show changes**
  - Rejected: GitHub avatars. Fetching images at runtime goes against the no-network rule, and
    the user's email would be sent to a third party.
- **Graph row actions:**
  - the branch filter (VS Code's "Auto" — current branch and upstream — or All)
  - go to the current commit (`git.revealHeadInGraph`)
  - fetch, pull, push, show commit, refresh
  - **Show more commits** pages 50 more (`git.graphShowMore`)
- **Primary button:** with nothing to commit, it becomes **Publish branch** (no upstream) or
  **Sync changes n↓ m↑** (behind / ahead). Both run `git.sync`.
- **Publish to GitHub** (`git.publish`, `publish.ts`): VS Code's flow, through the GitHub CLI
  as the pull requests already are (no token in the IDE).
  - It asks for a name (the folder's, made valid) and whether the repository is private or
    public.
  - Without a repository it runs `git init`. Without a commit, it commits everything not ignored
    as "Initial commit".
  - It runs `gh repo create <name> --private|--public --source=. --remote=origin --push`. The
    name is checked in Rust as well, so it can't be read as an option.
  - With a remote already, it publishes the branch (`git.push`). `git.sync` (the status bar's
    Publish, the primary button) publishes when there's no remote. If gh isn't signed in, it
    offers to sign in.
  - Different from VS Code: a `node_modules` folder that isn't ignored is added to
    `.gitignore` before the first commit, because uploading it is never wanted.
  - Not done: VS Code's picker of which files to include. The quick input has no multi-select;
    `.gitignore` decides.
- **Fixes:**
  - A recycled tree row kept the previous item's tooltip (the Graph header showed
    ".gitignore · Untracked").
  - A section that appeared later (the Graph after the first commit) counted as collapsed by the
    user and stayed closed. Sections are now tracked from expansion changes, not from rendering.
- **Testing offline:** UI scripts with `"fakeGh": true` run with `tests/fixtures/fake-gh` first on
  PATH. It is a GitHub CLI stand-in that is signed in, and its `repo create` makes a local bare
  repository, adds it as the remote and pushes.

### D149 — A Testing view; a whole-codebase audit; docs that say what the IDE is
- **Testing** (`extensions/testing`), the largest remaining gap against VS Code. It works with
  Vitest, Jest, node:test, pytest, cargo test and go test, without extensions.
  - **Discovery:** tests are found from their files' text before anything runs. A search finds
    the test files, then a light scanner reads each one: JS/TS describe/it/test nested by
    braces, pytest functions and Test classes, Rust `#[test]` with module paths, Go `TestX`.
    Each test belongs to its project: the nearest package.json, pyproject.toml / pytest.ini /
    setup.cfg, Cargo.toml or go.mod. A monorepo's packages run with their own runner, and the
    JS runner comes from the package's dependencies or a `node:test` import.
  - **Runs:** one command per project and framework (node:test file by file), through the same
    `exec` as agent commands, from the project's folder, with names quoted for POSIX shells or
    PowerShell. Results come from each framework's machine-readable output: Jest / Vitest JSON
    (found among other output), pytest `-rA`, cargo test's lines and failure blocks,
    `go test -json`, node:test TAP. A file that fails to load marks its tests failed with the
    reason. When nothing parses and the command fails, the output's tail becomes the message.
  - **UI:** a view by framework, file and suite, with filter, "failed only", Run on every row,
    and the failure message under a failed test. The editor margin shows each test's result as a
    dot, and the status bar shows the counts. Keys are VS Code's chords: Ctrl+; A / F / C / E.
  - **Agents:** `tests.run` returns counts and failures (file, line, name, message), so a fix
    can be checked in one call. `tests.list` and `ide://tests` hold the rest. Running needs a
    trusted folder.
  - Rejected: running each framework's own discovery (`vitest list`, `pytest --collect-only`).
    It is slow, needs the toolchain installed, and runs project code just to list tests. Text
    discovery is instant, and a run adds what it missed (`.each` expansions).
- **Audit** (four reviews: core and workbench, editor and agent, the other extensions, Rust):
  44 verified findings, all fixed. The ones that mattered:
  - **Notifications:** after the bell list was opened once, no toast showed again (its container
    was detached).
  - **Hangs:**
    - `git pull` with a large diffstat deadlocked on a full stdout pipe.
    - `run_command` never returned when the command left a background process.
    - A language server sending a huge Content-Length aborted the app.
    - A login-shell probe had no timeout.
  - **Freezes:**
    - Agent edit near-matching ran unbounded edit distance.
    - The gutter diff allocated up to 128 MB.
    - The text tool protocol rescanned the reply on every streamed chunk.
    - DevTools Console and Network rebuilt every row per message.
    - The Markdown preview re-rendered forever past 500 code blocks.
  - **Data:**
    - Restoring a trash entry with an empty id lost the whole trash.
    - Saving a non-UTF-8 file replaced its characters (such files now open read-only with a
      banner).
    - A copy followed symlinks out of the workspace.
    - The IDE's own save showed "changed on disk" and turned autosave off for the file.
  - **Races:**
    - A session loading from disk overwrote a turn already started.
    - "Save as" onto an open file broke its tab.
    - LSP servers covering two languages (clangd) started twice and killed each other.
    - Stop while a Node debug session launched left it running.
    - Overlapping workspace opens ran twice.
    - Git watchers were duplicated.
    - MCP servers kept running after a folder switch.
  - **Stuck UI:**
    - The debug console froze after 5000 lines.
    - Elements reloaded on every `document.title` change. New documents are now counted by
      their bridge's "ready", which works when WebView2 loses the old one's "leave".
    - A computed signal that threw once stopped notifying.
    - A nested or unclosed brace in `files.exclude` emptied the explorer.
  - **Windows:** stopping a language server or a timed-out formatter that runs through a `.cmd`
    shim now kills the whole process tree, and the `gh` probe no longer flashes a console.
- **Docs:** README.md is now public-facing: what the IDE is for, why it suits agents, what's in
  it, how it compares with VS Code, Cursor and Zed, how to run it. PLAN.md v1.4 records the
  milestones as they happened and the real stack (xterm.js, Oniguruma). AGENTS.md describes the
  release loop and the owner's preferences. DESIGN.md v2.1 adds hover cards, ref badges, rating
  pills, timelines and responsive panels.


### D150 — The terminal pass: ordered input, quiet failure actions, VS Code's terminal habits
An audit of the terminal (structure, Windows ConPTY, keys, rendering limits) and the gaps a
modern terminal shouldn't have. Nothing AI-specific was added: the agent has its own chat.
- **Correctness, most severe first:**
  - **Ordered input.** `pty_write` and `pty_resize` were async Tauri commands, each its own task,
    so keystrokes or an older size could overtake newer ones. They are now synchronous (handled
    in the order sent) and never block: a write queues the bytes for the session's own writer
    thread, which also keeps a big paste from holding up anything else.
  - **Keys that belong to the shell.** Ctrl+W (closed the terminal tab and killed its dev
    server), Ctrl+L (focused the agent instead of clearing) and Ctrl+N now reach the shell while
    a terminal has focus, as in VS Code (macOS's Cmd versions are unchanged). Ctrl+B / Ctrl+J
    stay the IDE's, as in VS Code.
  - **A late first start.** When a shell start timed out and was retried, the first shell
    coming up late (and killed) delivered its output and its exit into the retried terminal:
    "(exited)" on a live shell, which then wasn't killed on close. Each attempt has its own
    handlers now.
  - **Resizes (the Vite banner printed three times, a stale prompt below it on Windows).**
    ConPTY repaints its whole screen on every resize, and Vite clears by the row count it
    knows. VS Code's rule now applies: rows at once, columns after a 100 ms pause once the
    buffer has over 200 lines, hidden terminals when shown. Sizes under 10×3 (a sash dragged
    shut, a minimized window) aren't sent, and the pty gets the view's size again right after
    the shell starts, in case it changed meanwhile.
  - **Unicode 11 widths** (`@xterm/addon-unicode11`, MIT, 31 KB, the same as VS Code). Emoji and
    CJK were measured one cell wide while ConPTY and the shells use two, which shifted the cursor
    and broke PSReadLine's redraws. It is the only new dependency, and it is small and only
    loaded with the terminal chunk.
  - **Clear while a command runs on Windows** only clears the scrollback: xterm's own clear moves
    the cursor line to the top behind ConPTY's back, and ConPTY's next repaint put the old lines
    back around a misplaced prompt. At a prompt, Clear still asks the shell (Ctrl+L), as before.
  - **Shell scripts.**
    - bash and PowerShell hid the command's exit status from the user's own prompt (starship,
      oh-my-posh): it now sees `$?` and `$LASTEXITCODE` as if the integration weren't there.
    - bash and zsh put the prompt marks back when a theme rebuilds the prompt at every prompt
      (powerlevel10k, powerline-go).
    - bash joins a `PROMPT_COMMAND` ending in ";" without a syntax error.
    - PowerShell's script loads in try/catch, so a Restricted execution policy starts a plain
      shell instead of printing an error each time.
    - Marks from a prompt theme's own OSC 133 are ignored once ours (633) are seen, so commands
      are no longer counted twice.
  - **Keys.** Copy and paste go by the physical key (Ctrl+C copied nothing on Cyrillic layouts).
    On Linux, Ctrl+Shift+V pastes and Ctrl+V reaches the program (vim's visual block), as in VS
    Code. Outside Windows, Ctrl+Backspace / Ctrl+Delete delete a word.
  - **Long outputs.** A command whose own line has been trimmed off the scrollback is still known:
    the sticky line shows it, Ctrl+Up goes back to where its output starts, and its output (the
    last 20 000 lines) can still be copied or sent to the agent. Command records in Rust no
    longer turn a UTF-8 character split between two output chunks into U+FFFD.
- **Fix with agent, quieter:** no longer a chip over the top right after every failure (it also
  showed behind the sticky line). A small "Fix" button appears at the right end of a failed
  command's line only while the pointer is on that line, including the sticky copy of it, and
  sits above the sticky line.
- **The command dot** (VS Code's decorations): it is clickable, with a menu to rerun the command,
  copy the command, copy its output, or fix it. The sticky line now carries the command's dot in
  the gutter, like the line itself. Copy last command / output and Fix with agent accept a
  command number, so they work on any command, not just the last one.
- **What modern terminals do that was missing**, all VS Code's names and keys:
  - Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down scroll to the previous / next command.
  - Run recent command (Ctrl+Alt+R) picks from the commands run in any terminal, kept per
    workspace.
  - Several pasted lines are confirmed first when the program didn't ask for bracketed paste
    (`terminal.multiLinePasteWarning`).
  - Settings: `terminal.rightClickBehavior` (menu, or copy/paste as in Windows Terminal),
    `terminal.copyOnSelection`, `terminal.scrollback`, `terminal.cursorStyle`,
    `terminal.cursorBlinking`, `terminal.fontFamily`, `terminal.lineHeight`. All apply live.
  - Files dropped from the system onto a terminal type their paths, quoted for its shell.
- **Workbench:** the activity bar's view buttons scroll when the window is too short to show them
  all. Accounts and Settings stay fixed below, and a hairline marks where the scroll ends.
- **Stress-tested** (`tests/scripts/terminal-m6-49.jsonc`): 200 000 lines of output past a 10 000
  line scrollback (flow control held, the next command ran), wide characters, empty and repeated
  lines, clearing, then the next command.
- Not done, noted in `docs/feature-gaps.md`:
  - The WebGL renderer: faster on huge outputs, but it would be a second dependency and needs
    context-loss handling.
  - Killing a terminal's whole process tree on Windows: closing the console already ends its
    children.
  - A nonce on the marks, so output can't fake them.
  - VS Code's commands-to-skip-shell list.

### D151 — The agent chat reads like a chat; messages sent while it works join its next step
The agent worked well but read like a log: a spinner, "Thinking…" again and again, every thought
shown, code darker than the chat. The owner pointed at Claude's own chat as the model: the work
is there when you want it, the conversation is what you see.
- **The work line** (`view/work.ts`): one quiet line per turn under your message. While working,
  its words shimmer (the spinner is gone); when done, it says what happened ("Read a file, ran a
  command · 4s"). The line is calm on purpose:
  - each phrase stays at least 1.1 s, and the next one fades in;
  - when the agent moves faster, the phrases in between are skipped, straight to the current one;
  - "nothing specific" is never "Thinking": it's one of a few plain phrases ("Working on it",
    "Piecing it together"…), a new one every few seconds. A model's own headings ("**Checking
    the tests**") still show as they come.
- **The steps** (`view/steps.ts`, `workRows` in `turns.ts`, tested): opening the line shows a card
  of rows divided by hairlines, the way Claude shows its work.
  - What the agent said between steps is a row.
  - Each tool call is a row that reads as a sentence: "Read README.md · 4 lines". Its icon, status
    tick and monospace are gone; only a failure shows a red ×.
  - Thinking stays out of the list. The first step's thinking (when it said nothing yet) is the
    first row, under its headline. A later step's thinking opens inside its first tool row, with
    the output (a second click). The answer's thinking is the last row, "Thought process". A turn
    that only thought shows its thinking in the card directly.
- **Nothing darker than the chat:** code blocks, command output, permission code and table
  headers use the raised surface or the chip tint, never the sunken one.
- **Long messages** fold to whole lines with a fade, and "Show more" is plain text, not a link.
- **Tone** (`context.ts`): warm, brief and plain-spoken, "I'll handle it". Lead with the outcome,
  no narration of steps the IDE already shows, jargon only when the user works at that level,
  code only when it helps, at most one next step.
- **Messages sent while the agent works** (like Claude): Enter is never blocked.
  - The message is queued (`session.queued`), shown as your bubble, quieter, with "Take back"
    (`agent.unqueue`).
  - The loop takes it before its next model call (`LoopDeps.takeQueued`, tested). It joins the
    conversation there as a user message that tells the model it came mid-task.
  - A turn that was about to end goes on to answer it.
  - Messages left over when the turn ends are sent as the next message. After Stop or an error
    they go back to the box instead.
  - The send button sends while the box has text, and stops when it's empty.
- **Audit** (the agent's logic), all fixed:
  - **Deleted chats came back.** A chat deleted mid-turn was saved again as the turn unwound.
    Deleted sessions now never save (`markDeleted`).
  - **Stop was dead for seconds.** It did nothing between Send and the model call, while models,
    MCP servers and the IDE state loaded. The message now shows and Stop works at once. A send
    that doesn't start takes the message back off the chat.
  - **A failed send lost what you wrote.** The text, attachments and pasted files now go back to
    the box. A message coming back no longer wipes what you're typing.
  - **Stop couldn't end a tool that ignored it** (an MCP call, an IDE command that waits). The
    step now ends at once, and the tool's late result is dropped.
  - **A permission card could appear after Stop.** Asking after Stop now answers "deny".
  - **Retry and edit lost things.** They dropped the message's images and attachments, and could
    start during another send.
  - **`/compact` summarized too little.** It used the local-model context length for hosted models.
  - **The text protocol stuck.** Once a model without native tools was used, the chat stayed in
    text-protocol mode for good. It's now per model.
  - **Continue failed while loading.** It now waits for the chat to load.
  - **Smaller fixes:**
    - Live output of dropped items is pruned.
    - A side task's Stop isn't an error.
    - `list_dir` caps one huge folder.
    - The "started in another folder" strip isn't rebuilt per token.
    - Composer menus don't pile up.
    - A new permission card takes focus only when the chat has it, so an Enter meant for the
      editor can't approve a command.
  - **New notices:** "Stopped." now offers Continue, and a reply with nothing in it says so
    (with Continue).
- **Build warnings on Windows** (`unused_mut` in `git/github.rs`, `output_within` unused): both
  come from code that only runs outside Windows, and are allowed there precisely.
- **Next** (`docs/feature-gaps.md`): rich blocks in the chat the agent can emit cheaply (a chart
  from a table, link cards, a choice to click), each one fenced data the chat renders, so the
  model writes data, not HTML.

### D152 — The agent doesn't echo the IDE state, and uses the IDE's tools instead of explaining
Two things seen with a hosted free model right after D151:
- **The `<ide_state>` echo.** A reply began with the `<ide_state>` block the IDE puts on each user
  message. The loop now takes such blocks out of replies (`stripEchoedState`, tested), whole or
  half-written, so they never show and aren't sent back to the model. The prompt also says the
  block is for the model and never to repeat it.
- **Explaining instead of doing.** Asked to demo the IDE's debug panel and console, the model wrote
  VS Code steps. Some were wrong for this IDE: no "Launch Chrome against localhost" configuration,
  no "Debug current file" menu item. The prompt now says:
  - when asked to use, try or demo an IDE tool, do it with its commands;
  - this IDE isn't VS Code, so don't describe menus, keys or configurations it hasn't checked
    (`find_commands`, or `help.readDocs`).

  It also names the commands for the debugger (breakpoints, logpoints, start, step, evaluate in the
  console, `ide://debug`), tests, the browser and git. `debug.showView` and `debug.showConsole` can
  now be found by agents.

### D153 — No prompts for what's already in front of you; auto mode means auto
The owner's report after D151/D152:
- toasts for things already on screen;
- a second dev server (Vite on 5174) while the first was running;
- the agent asking about IDE commands with "run commands automatically" on;
- the edit mode forgotten after a restart;
- the Testing icon showing in folders without tests.

What changed:
- **Servers** (`terminal/index.ts`):
  - A detected server already showing in a browser tab gets no "A server is running" toast. Any
    loopback name counts as the same host. This covers `npm run dev` started again after Ctrl+C,
    and a task run on folder open with last session's tab still there.
  - A tab that lost the server while it was down reloads.
  - `terminal.start` (the agent's dev servers) reuses a terminal already serving the same command
    in the same folder, even one the user or a task started, instead of starting a second copy on
    the next port.
- **Auto mode covers IDE commands.** With `agent.runCommands` "auto", the IDE commands the agent
  calls (set a breakpoint, start the debugger, open the browser…) no longer ask.
  - Destructive commands still ask.
  - Commands that type a command line into a terminal (`terminal.sendText`, `runCommand`,
    `start`) go through the same denylist as `run_command`. The policy now receives the validated
    input for that.
  - The setting is read on every call, so changing it mid-chat applies at once.
- **The edit mode is remembered** per workspace. New chats start in the mode last chosen there,
  and a chat saves its mode when it changes. Before, a mode switch with nothing else changed was
  never saved.
- **Testing like VS Code:**
  - VS Code has a built-in Testing view whose icon appears once a test extension finds tests. Ours
    appears once tests are found in the folder (`ViewRegistry.setAvailable`); `testing.alwaysShow`
    keeps it always.
  - A failed run's toast isn't shown while the Testing view is open.
- **The agent's "needs your answer" toast** shows only when that chat isn't on screen. The card
  in the chat is the question.
- **Browser debug configurations** (`chrome`, `msedge`, `pwa-*`) say plainly that browser
  debugging isn't supported yet and point to the IDE's browser DevTools. Before, the error was
  about a missing `debugAdapter`. Debugging browser code from the IDE's debugger goes on the gaps
  list.

### D154 — A turn's file changes as one card; the plan kept current
With Claude in the IDE, a long build showed two problems:
- **Stacked cards.** Every file the turn wrote got its own diff card, so a dozen "reviewed" cards
  stacked under the work line.
- **A stale plan.** The plan stayed at 0/8 while the model wrote file after file.

What changed:
- **One changes card per turn** (`view/changes.ts`).
  - The header says what happened: "Changed 10 files +412 −8", "3 files to review", or "Changed
    7 files · 3 to review".
  - While files wait for review, the header holds Accept all / Reject all for that turn's files
    (`agent.acceptAll` / `rejectAll` take `paths`).
  - Opening it shows one quiet row per file: name, folder, "new" / "deleted", line counts. Clicking
    a row opens the diff. Pending rows have Accept / Reject.
  - It starts open only when up to 3 files wait for review; the user's open / closed choice is
    kept. Long lists scroll inside the card.
  - Applied files show their real counts: the changeset keeps each file's text before the turn's
    first write and after its last (`appliedStat`). Before, they only said "reviewed".
- **The plan, kept current.**
  - Models often forget to tick their plan off while busy. As in Claude Code, after 6 tool calls
    without `update_plan` while a step is unfinished, the next tool result carries one line asking
    the model to update the plan (`planNudge`).
  - The prompt also asks for `update_plan` as each step finishes. The plan card itself was always
    live: it only shows what the model sends.
- **Out of steps, said out loud.** The same build ended with no summary. It had used up
  `agent.maxSteps` (30 model calls) mid-work, the loop stopped silently, and the project check
  ran as if it were done.
  - The default is now 150 (at most 1000).
  - Running out of steps with a tool call last adds "Paused after N steps: the work isn't
    finished", with Continue, and skips the check on half-written work.

### D155 — The turn's screenshots on its work line
Agents that test their work (Claude especially) take many screenshots. They were only inside the
open work group, one per tool row. Like Claude's chat:
- **Thumbnails on the work line.** The newest three show at the right of the line, with "+N" for
  earlier ones, and update live as more are taken (`view/shots.ts`, `WorkGroupState.shots`).
- **A viewer over the window.** Clicking a thumbnail opens it full size, with "1 of N", ← / →
  (keys too), and Esc, ✕ or a click outside to close.
- The thumbnails inside the steps stay as they were.

### D156 — A large preview on hover; chats keep small copies of their images
- **Hover preview.** Resting on a work line's thumbnail shows the screenshot large in a hover
  card, with what took it ("Took screenshot · IDE") and which one it is ("2 of 5"), like Claude's
  chat. The viewer also shows the caption (`shotPreview`, `Shot.caption`).
- **Images survive a restart, for the person only.**
  - Screenshots and pasted images were kept in memory only. A chat opened the next day showed
    none of them, and the agent's work line lost its thumbnails.
  - Each now gets a compressed copy saved with the chat (`previews.ts`): WebP, or JPEG where the
    engine can't encode WebP, at most 1280 px wide. They're made when the chat saves.
  - The newest 40 per chat are kept; older ones are dropped. A typical screenshot is 60–150 KB
    this way, against 0.5–2 MB as a PNG.
  - The model never sees them: `toMessages` only sends `images`, the full ones of this session.
    After a restart the model has the text of what it saw, as before, and the person still has
    the pictures.
  - Rejected: keeping the full PNGs (transcripts of tens of MB), and sending previews back to the
    model (tokens, and cache-breaking for no gain on an old screenshot).

### D157 — Replies cut off at the output limit carry on; thinking-only turns never sent back
With Claude in the IDE, a turn stopped by itself while planning a layout. Continue then failed with
Anthropic's 400 "The final block in an assistant message cannot be `thinking`".
- **The cause.** The reply hit the output limit (`stop_reason: max_tokens`): the model's thinking
  and the start of a large file used up the 32k budget. The unfinished tool call was dropped, and
  the step ended with nothing but thinking, so the loop took it for the end of the turn. On
  Continue, that thinking-only message was sent back, which the Messages API refuses.
- **What changed:**
  - **Carry on.** A reply cut off at the limit with nothing to run carries on by itself. The loop
    adds a harness message asking the model to go on in smaller pieces (a large file as
    `write_file` and then `edit_file`, short thinking). It does this at most twice in a row
    (`LIMIT_NOTE`, `auto: "limit"`, tested). The message isn't shown, and the work stays in the
    same group. It works the same for OpenAI-compatible and Ollama models (`length`).
  - **Never send a thinking-only assistant turn.** `anthropic.rs` drops an assistant message that
    has only thinking (no text, no tool call); it has nothing for the model anyway (tested).
  - **A bigger budget.** Claude gets up to 64k output tokens, when the model reports that much,
    instead of 32k.

### D158 — Attachments open in the viewer
The screenshot viewer (D155) now opens attachments too: a sent message's cards and the cards
waiting above the message box.
- **Navigation.** Clicking a card opens the viewer on it; ← / → page through that message's other
  attachments in order (`openableCards`, `viewerItem`).
- **Images** show as images, saved compressed copies after a restart included (D156).
- **Pasted text and files** show as a readable page: name, line count, monospace, selectable,
  scrolling. Sent attachments now keep their text for this (`SentAttachment.text`, at most 50 000
  characters per attachment, saved with the chat; the model's copy is unchanged).
- **Elsewhere:**
  - Project files waiting in the box open in the editor instead.
  - @-mentions (Problems, Terminal output…) have nothing to show and stay plain chips.
  - Cards are keyboard-reachable (Enter / Space).

### D159 — Notes between steps in the conversation; retry after a restart; the chat's buttons audited
- **Layout like Claude's chat** (`layoutTurn`, tested):
  - What the agent says between steps now shows in the conversation, and the steps between two
    such texts collapse into their own line ("Ran 3 commands").
  - Before, every note went into the one closed group per turn, and a long task read only
    "Working on it…".
  - A note's thinking opens its group as its first row. Only the turn's latest group can say
    "Working…". The turn's changes card sits under its last group.
  - The prompt already keeps notes to one short line.
- **Retry and edit after a restart resend the images.** Full images aren't saved (D156), so a
  message's saved previews are re-encoded to PNG and sent again (`imagesToResend`). Every
  provider takes PNG. Pasted text and files were already kept, as the message's context.
- **Audit of every button in the chat** (16 findings). Fixed:
  - **Retry / Continue only on the latest notice.** On an older notice, Retry redid the newest
    turn.
  - **Continue never sends a conversation ending with the agent's own reply.** That is a prefill
    for Claude and a repeat for other models. A hidden harness message asks it to go on.
  - **Accept is safe with a busy agent.** Accepting removes the accepted proposal by identity,
    so one the agent made meanwhile stays. A double click accepts once, and a per-change accept
    refuses if the file changed again (tested).
  - **Rejected files say "rejected"** in the changes card, with no misleading diff link. They
    don't count as changed.
  - **Line counts survive a restart.** The changes card's counts are saved with the chat
    (`appliedJSON`).
  - **A chat interrupted by quitting** reopens with "Interrupted when the IDE closed" and
    Continue. Running tool rows say "interrupted", and closing a chat saves it.
  - **Small fixes:**
    - Restore checkpoint is refused while the agent works.
    - An edit whose resend can't start goes back to the box.
    - The folder card starts once on a double click, and Cancel keeps the message.
    - The model choice is saved with the chat.
    - A deleted chat's diff tabs close.
    - Messages can be queued from the very start of a turn.
    - Retry / Continue clicked again while running do nothing, instead of showing an error.
  - **Left for later** (`docs/feature-gaps.md`):
    - an older turn's card acting on a newer proposal of the same file;
    - queued messages losing their attachment cards on Stop / Take back;
    - external (ACP) agents and attachments;
    - Retry on a memory tidy-up;
    - checkpoint labels after a retry.

### D160 — The leftovers fixed, a second audit, the owner's reports
- **The five leftovers from D159:**
  - **User messages record their turn.** Each work group knows its turn, so a changes card only
    acts on its own turn's proposals. A file a later turn changed again says "changed again
    later" and opens the current proposal. Line counts are kept per turn and file
    (`appliedStat(path, turn)`), so an older card doesn't show a newer turn's counts.
  - **Checkpoint labels** come from the message that started each turn, so they're right after
    retries and edits. Chats saved before this fall back to the old labels.
  - **Queued messages keep their cards.** The original uploads and project files go back to the
    box on Take back, Stop, or a failed send (`returnQueued`).
  - **External (ACP) agents get the message's context** (attached files and pastes, as text) and
    its images, when the agent says it takes images (`promptCapabilities`). After a retry or an
    edit, the agent's session starts over with a recap of the conversation, since it still
    remembered the dropped turns.
  - **A memory tidy-up is a one-off task** (`sideTask`): no Retry or Edit on it.
- **The owner's reports:**
  - **The card's "Accept all" did nothing.** The card was updated in place (`morph`), which keeps
    the first render's click handlers, and they held only the files known then. Cards are now
    rebuilt when they change. A UI test covers six files proposed one by one, then Accept all.
  - **Its chevron didn't open the list.** Same cause. Its hover now reaches the card's edge.
  - **A finished plan came back** as a 3/3 card when the next message started a task. A new
    message now clears a finished plan, and the plan reminder counts from zero.
  - **New files said "Changed".** They now read "Created 5 files", or "Created 2 files, changed 3".
  - **A title in a bare tag** (`<Landing Page Ready>`) showed in the chat. It is now taken as the
    title (tested; HTML tags aren't).
  - **The browser showed the old page** after the agent changed files, on a server without live
    reload. After a turn that wrote files, or after accepting changes, tabs on a local server
    reload (`agent.reloadBrowser`).
  - **Notes between steps had a copy button.** While the agent works, its latest text may be a
    note, so actions now show only on finished answers.
  - **The changes bar's top corners** are rounded like the message box under it.
- **Second audit** (11 findings), fixed:
  - **Sending only attachments did nothing.** The message had to be non-empty; now it can be
    empty when something is attached.
  - **Retry, Edit and Continue change the conversation only once the session is claimed,** and
    put it back if the turn can't start. Before, a message sent meanwhile could be cut out, or a
    notice lost.
  - **Plan reminders** go only to the turn's own model, not the explore sub-agent's.
  - **Memory:** change texts of older turns are dropped (their counts are kept), and finished
    tool rows drop their live output.
  - **Rejections** are per turn and saved with the chat.
  - **A step that went on only for a queued message** ends if the message was taken back.
  - **The text-protocol fallback** removes the right item.
  - **The Send button** doesn't offer queuing to external agents.
  - **The work line's duration** runs on after Continue.
  - **The `<ide_state>` echo filter** only takes a block at the start of a reply. It used to cut
    replies that mentioned the tag (tested).
  - **Stop** reaches a sub-agent's tool call too.
  - **Saved chats** are checked item by item on load.
### D161 — Agent audit: the world changing under a turn
The generic "audit everything" prompt the owner brought was reworked into `docs/agent-audit.md`.
It is about half the size and aimed at this agent's own risks: the folder, files, tabs or the IDE
changing during a turn; tools and the changeset; and the conversation. Three read-only passes and
a mock-model probe found these, all fixed:
- **Stop now stops side effects, not only the step.** A tool still finishing after Stop (an edit
  waiting on the language service, a terminal waiting for its prompt) used to write the file or
  start the dev server anyway. Each call now has its own stop flag, which the next turn doesn't
  clear. Auto-apply leaves a stopped edit as a proposal. A background command typed after Stop
  has its terminal killed. A foreground command never starts. In Rust, a cancel that arrives
  before the process is registered is remembered.
- **Accepting a proposal kept the agent's text over anything changed since.** That included the
  user's typing, `npm install`'s edit to package.json, or another chat's change. Accept (and hunk
  accept) now applies the agent's changes on top of the file as it is now (`rebase` in
  `core/diff`, a small three-way merge). When both sides changed the same lines, it refuses and
  the proposal stays.
- **Files that editing would corrupt are refused** (`editableText`): non-UTF-8 files (UTF-16 from
  PowerShell 5.1's `>`, legacy code pages), binary files, and files over 4 MB. Before, they were
  decoded lossily and written back full of U+FFFD.
- **Auto mode's denylist could be bypassed** with `( rm … )`, `{ …; }`, `if …; then rm`,
  `% { ri $_ }` and `[IO.Directory]::Delete`. **The allowlist could be bypassed** with
  `npm test (Remove-Item …)`, since PowerShell evaluates `(…)` inside arguments. Groups, script
  blocks, .NET calls and shell keywords now ask. `sc`, `ac`, `icm`, `Invoke-Command` and
  `Clear-Item` are denied.
- **Closing the folder** stops its chats with "Stopped: the folder was closed." and Continue.
  - **External (ACP) agents:** one started in the old folder is restarted, with a recap, when
    the chat goes on elsewhere. One that doesn't answer Stop is ended after 3 s instead of
    leaving the chat "running".
  - **The system prompt** (folder path, AGENTS.md, memory) is rebuilt for the new folder.
- **Quitting the IDE kills running agent commands.** Exec processes used to outlive the app with
  no timeout.
- **Windows paths:**
  - **Absolute paths are normalized:** `..` is collapsed, and a path inside the root takes the
    root's spelling. Pending changes compare paths case-insensitively, so one file gets one
    proposal.
  - **`cd /d dir &&`** is understood.
  - **A `cwd` that doesn't exist** is an error. Before, it ran in the root, so `rm -rf *` meant
    for `build/` would have hit the project.
  - **UNC paths are refused before any file access,** and so are UNC links in the chat. Windows
    would connect to the host, offering the user's credentials.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - `list_dir` survives links to folders outside the project.
  - Restoring a checkpoint moves created files to the trash, keeps a BOM, and names files it
    couldn't restore.
  - An auto-applied edit to a file with unsaved editor changes tells the agent it isn't on disk.
  - **Code block buttons:** a block that closed while streaming kept the Copy handler on its
    Apply button. Its header is now keyed.
  - **Deeply nested Markdown** (3000 `>`) overflowed the stack and blanked the chat. Nesting stops
    at 40.
  - **Reopened chats:** a turn that ended with its check no longer reopens as "Interrupted", and
    interrupted tools tell the model so instead of "(no output)".
  - **Retry and Edit** rebuild the plan from what's left.
  - **Saving while output streams** happens at least every 10 s.
  - **Chat links:** `#anchors` are ignored, and `path#L42` opens at the line.
  - **Stop during a provider retry wait** says "Stopped", not an error.
  - **`/compact` after a Stop** works.
- **Left, with reasons:**
  - **The model stream after a reload,** if Rust doesn't stop on a closed channel. Not traced.
  - **Streaming cost for 10 000-line answers** (the whole message is re-parsed each frame), and
    slow inline parsing of adversarial input (`![` × 30 000). Neither has been measured in the
    real DOM yet.
  - **Saved transcripts** keep full results before a summary.
  - **"Always allow"** remembers `node`/`cmd` as a program.
  - **A fuzzy `edit_file` match** isn't reported as fuzzy.

### D162 — Welcome bento, readable disabled menu items, menu icons, Testing toggle
- **The welcome page's four cards** sit in a quiet bento instead of a 2 × 2 table: five columns,
  split 3/2 then 2/3, with the first row a little taller and the labels at the bottom of the
  cards. When the tab is narrower than 340 px, they become one column (a container query on
  `.welcome`).
- **Disabled menu items** were `--fg-disabled`, which is hard to read on dark overlays and on
  imported themes. They now mix `--fg-subtle` (70 %) with `--fg-disabled`: still clearly off,
  but readable on every theme. Their icon and key hint follow the same color.
- **Menu icons:** DESIGN.md §12.5 now has a table of which icon goes with which action, so one
  action has one icon everywhere (rename → `pencil`, copy path → `clipboard-copy`, push →
  `cloud-upload`…). The menu bar, file and folder menus, tab and group menus, the editor's
  context menu and the view header menus fill in their icons from it. Lists of data (models,
  themes, recent folders, branches) and on/off items, which show a check, stay without. 28 Lucide
  icons were added to the sprite.
- **Testing was missing from the activity bar while the menu showed it checked.** It's kept off
  the bar until the folder has tests, as in VS Code, so the menu now leaves it unchecked.
  Checking it turns on `testing.alwaysShow` and it appears. Views declare this with
  `alwaysShowSetting`.

### D163 — Full access, a quiet reply shows it's working, `<result>` tags, D161's leftovers, base layout
- **Full access (never ask):** a third command mode next to "Ask before commands" and "Run
  commands automatically" (`agent.runCommands: "full"`). Nothing asks: not risky commands, IDE
  and browser commands, MCP tools, or external agents' permission requests. `session.ask`
  answers "once" at once. Choosing it also turns on auto-apply, since nothing should wait on a
  review either. Checkpoints still undo file changes. The composer shows "Full access".
- **Auto mode asks less:** `curl` / `wget` / `iwr` against localhost (checking the project's own
  server, which free models do constantly) count as reading, unless they save, upload or post.
  Output piped into a shell (`| sh`, `| iex`) always asks.
- **A reply that goes quiet mid-turn** used to show only its caret: the model writing a whole
  file in a tool call it doesn't stream, or a slow provider. After 1.5 s without growth, the work
  line shows under it ("Working…", or "Writing index.html…" when the call is known).
- **`<result>…</result>` wrappers** that some free models add are left out of answers and notes
  (`withoutWrapperTags`, not inside code blocks). If Markdown rendering ever throws, the reply
  shows as plain text instead of the chat freezing.
- **D161's leftovers, fixed:**
  - **Reload mid-turn:** Rust records which window started each model request and agent command.
    A page that loads (`page_loaded`) cancels its window's leftovers, so nothing streams or runs
    for a page that's gone.
  - **A long streaming reply** (more than 20 000 characters) re-renders at most every 250 ms.
  - **Adversarial inline input** (`![` × 30 000) is bounded and stays fast.
  - **Saved chats:** before the newest summary they drop what only the model used (context,
    IDE state, attachment text, reasoning; tool results cut to 2 000 characters).
  - **"Always allow" for an interpreter** remembers the exact line, so `node x.js` doesn't allow
    `node -e …`.
  - **An approximate `edit_file` match** tells the model where, so it can check.
  - **The text-protocol fallback** takes a fenced JSON call only at the end of a reply, not an
    example in the middle.
  - **Deleting a proposed new file** drops the proposal.
- **Base layout** (`applyBaseLayout`): explorer at 260 px, the welcome tab, and the agent at
  about 380 px on the right. There's no terminal without a folder, and one for a folder opened for
  the first time. It's the same at startup without a folder, after Close folder, and for a fresh
  folder. The explorer is shown without taking focus, so a palette opened meanwhile stays open.

### D164 — AI setup: the "AI models" page, a first-run card, Copilot through its CLI; the agent column keeps its width
- **The agent column keeps its pixel width** when the dock changes size (window maximized or
  resized, sidebar shown or hidden), like VS Code's secondary side bar (`keepRightWidth`, on a
  top-level row whose last column holds the agent). Before, a window opened small and then
  maximized gave the agent 40 % of the screen.
- **With no folder, the sidebar shows Chats** instead of an empty Explorer, since the welcome tab
  already offers Open folder. Opening a folder switches to the Explorer.
- **The "AI models" page** (`agent.showSetup`, a tab rather than a settings form) has four
  sections:
  - **Connected providers:** a status dot, the model count, Change key and Remove.
  - **Add a provider:** tiles for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI, OpenRouter (free
    models), Groq, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and any other server. Each tile opens a key form in
    place.
  - **Ollama:** shown as running, installed, or not installed, with the matching action
    (download a starter model, start it, or get it).
  - **Agent CLIs:** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot, as installed (Use) or not
    (Install, which runs the install and sign-in in a terminal).

  A default-model pill sits at the top. The page has room for routing and custom agents later.
- **Connect checks first** (`agent.connectProvider`): the key is stored under a scratch id and
  the models are listed. Only if that works is the provider saved and the key stored for real. A
  wrong key never replaces a working one, and errors read as reasons ("The key was rejected").
  The first provider's model becomes the default (OpenRouter's free router for OpenRouter).
