- **The first-run card:** with no model, an empty chat shows "Set up the agent" with three
  choices, one open at a time: Run models on this computer, Use an API key, Use an agent you
  already have. `agent.showSetup { firstRun: true }` ("Models and providers" in the palette,
  first run) previews it in a new chat, so it can be tried without deleting anything.
- **No hosted providers are added before a key:** they're tiles, so a new install shows no red
  "unreachable" entries.
- **GitHub:** GitHub Models (the inference API) was retired on 30 July 2026. A Copilot plan is
  used through the Copilot CLI's ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), now an agent preset.
- **New commands:** `agent.removeProvider`, `agent.detectTools` (Rust `programs_installed`),
  `agent.pullStarterModel`, `agent.installAgent`, `agent.closeSetupPreview`.
- **Trying the onboarding:** "AI: Preview first-run setup" (`agent.previewSetup`) in the palette,
  and `npm run dev:fresh`, which runs the IDE with a new temporary profile. It also gives that
  run its own empty GitHub CLI config (`GH_CONFIG_DIR`), because the GitHub login comes from `gh`
  and is machine-wide, not per profile. It points Ollama at an address where nothing answers, so
  the setup card shows; `npm run dev:fresh-ollama` keeps Ollama visible. The profile folder can
  also be set with the `IDE_USER_DATA_DIR` environment variable, because PowerShell eats the
  `--` that passing `--user-data-dir` through npm and tauri dev needs.
- **Entry points:** the model menu's "Manage models and providers…" and the Accounts menu's
  "AI models and providers…". They replace the old quick-pick flow, which is still available as
  `agent.addProvider`.

### D165 — The AI models page from Settings and the gear menu
- **Settings → Agent** opens with a "Models and providers" row that leads to the AI models page.
  Settings categories can list pages like this (`CATEGORY_LINKS` in the settings view): they
  come first in the card, are found by search, and are left out of "@modified".
- **The gear menu** has "AI models and providers" next to Settings and Extensions.

### D166 — Simpler setup prompt, provider-safe resets, the models link stands out
- **An empty chat without a model** now shows one button, "Set up AI models", which opens the AI
  models page. It replaces D164's three-choice card, since the page already handles every path.
  "AI: Preview first-run setup" shows the button (with Close preview) even when models are set
  up.
- **Settings → Agent:** "Models and providers" is its own card above the settings, in the info
  color, like the agent's "Started in" banner.
- **Resetting all settings, or the Agent settings, keeps connected model providers and their
  keys.** The prompt has an option, unchecked by default, to remove them too; most services show
  a key only once. To support this, dialogs can carry an option (`confirmWithOption`),
  `settings.reset` takes an `except` list, and `agent.forgetProviders` removes every provider
  and key.
- **The "Started in" banner's buttons** wrap together, aligned right, when the panel is narrow.

### D167 — Provider tiles in their own colors; official logos when added
- **Provider and agent tiles have character without logos:** each gets a letter badge in its own
  color (`--brand-*` tokens) and a soft wash of that color from the top, stronger on hover.
- **Agent and Ollama rows** use the same badges, with the status dot on the badge's corner.
- **Official logos (optional):** most of these companies allow their logos in integration
  listings under their brand guidelines. The IDE doesn't draw them; an official SVG put in
  `src/assets/brands/<brand>.svg` replaces the letters. `scripts/gen.mjs` turns those files into
  `brandLogos.ts`, which is git-ignored. It skips files with scripts or event handlers and loads
  the rest as `<img>`, on a light chip so dark logos read in dark themes.
- **Logos added at the owner's request:** the files come from `@lobehub/icons-static-svg` 1.95.1
  (MIT), copied unaltered; the folder's README lists the sources. The agents (Claude Code, Codex,

  keeps its letter badge.
- **The chat's "Set up AI models" button** has its icon at the top left, next to the two lines of
  text, and the chevron stays centered.

### D168 — Logos on their brand colors
- **Colored logos** (Gemini, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) stand on their own, with no chip.
- **One-color logos** are drawn in white (a CSS mask) on a chip in the brand's color:
  - terracotta for Anthropic;
  - indigo for OpenRouter;
  - orange-red for Groq;
  - violet for LM Studio;
  - near-black for OpenAI, xAI and GitHub Copilot.

### D169 — Small things all over: model menu speed, providers by address, folder opening, header actions, activity bar
- **The model menu opens at once.** It used to wait up to 400 ms for every provider to list its
  models again (OpenRouter has hundreds, and a dead key times out); now it refreshes in the

- **A provider added by hand matches its preset by address** (`presetFor`): for example
  `openrouter-ai` with a trailing slash. It gets its logo and name, and its tile isn't offered

- **The AI models page** has "Edit in settings.json" next to the default model.
- **Opening a folder shows progress** (`workspace.opening`):
  - A moving line under the title bar until the workspace is ready.
  - On the welcome page, the folder's recent row shimmers and the rest steps back.
  - A start card shows a press, and a line along its foot while its command runs (a dialog, a
    clone).
- **`workbench.view.alwaysShowHeaderActions`** (off by default, as in VS Code) keeps header
  buttons visible: sidebar views and sections, editor groups, and the title bar's layout toggles.
- **Activity bar:**
  - Icons keep their size and the list scrolls, with the tab strip's thin always-visible
    scrollbar, turned vertical.
  - Icons can be dragged to reorder them (`view.move`, saved in `workbench.activityBar.order`).
  - The right-click menu follows that order.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - **Git graph:** the subject truncates before the ref badges, which always stay visible.

### D170 — Rich blocks in the chat
- **The model writes fenced data and the chat draws it.** That's few tokens, it works with any
  model, and there's no HTML:
  - ```` ```chart bar|line Title ```` takes a small table (a header row, then a label and numbers
    per row) or JSON.
  - ```` ```choices ```` takes an optional question, then options. Clicking one sends it as your
    answer; it stays marked and the others dim. Only the latest answer's choices can be clicked,
    and only while the agent waits.
  - ```` ```links ```` and ```` ```files ```` become cards; files open in the editor.
  - ```` ```steps ```` becomes a checklist.
  - ```` ```colors ```` becomes swatches; a click copies the color.
- **Drawing:**
  - **Parsing** is DOM-free and tested (`core/agent/richBlocks.ts`).
  - **Charts** are HTML around an SVG line (non-scaling stroke) or bars of divs, so text stays
    crisp at any width. They have a legend for two or more series, hover values on every mark,
    and "Show data" for a table.
  - **The palette** is `--chart-1…6`: the dataviz reference palette's first six slots, validated
    for color-vision deficiency in both themes. The light theme's low-contrast slots are relieved
    by the table and the tooltips.
  - **While a block streams** it shows as "Drawing a chart…"; a block that doesn't parse shows as
    code.
- **The system prompt** says when to use them, in five lines. `agent.richBlocks: false` leaves
  them out of the prompt.
- **The Markdown renderer** got a `richBlock` hook for this; other previews don't use it.
- **Remote windows were weighed and deferred.** VS Code's model needs a remote build of the
  backend plus a transport (weeks). "Open a WSL folder" goes on the gap list as the cheap first
  step.

### D171 — Rich output through display tools, the way the big chat apps do it
- **What they do:** Claude's chat widgets (charts, quizzes, maps), Claude Code's AskUserQuestion,
  ChatGPT's Apps SDK (`structuredContent` plus a template) and MCP Apps (`_meta.ui.resourceUri`,
  supported by Claude, ChatGPT, Goose and VS Code) all work the same way: the model makes a
  **tool call with JSON arguments**, and the app draws that call as a card beside the text. The
  answer's text never contains the card, so copying a message gives plain Markdown. Fenced
  blocks are standard only for formats with wide adoption (```` ```mermaid ````, math, GFM task
  lists, `> [!NOTE]`). D170's ```` ```chart ```` / ```` ```choices ```` fences were our own
  invention: they leaked raw data into copied answers, and every model had to learn them from
  the prompt.
- **Now** the agent has three display tools (`displayTools.ts`), with JSON schemas shaped like the
  big apps' widgets:
  - `show_chart`: `{ type, title, unit, labels, series: [{ name, values }] }`.
  - `show_links`: items with a `url` (https) or a `path` (and `line`); files open in the editor.
  - `ask_user`: `{ question, options }`. **It waits**, like AskUserQuestion: a click, or a message
    typed while it asks (`agent.send` answers instead of queueing), is the tool's result. Stop
    answers it as "didn't answer"; full access (D163) doesn't wait, and the model is told to pick
    and say which. The session is "waiting" meanwhile, so the away-notification fires (D107).
    `agent.answer` is the command behind a click.
- **Results:** the model gets one line ("Shown to the user as a bar chart (2 series × 4 points)"),
  like the Apps SDK's short `content`.
- **Layout:** a display call's card sits in the conversation where it happened, like text said
  between steps, not inside the work group (`turns.ts`). A call that failed is a normal row.
- **Cards** are the D170 renderers: the chart got "Copy as table" (Markdown), and choices show a
  typed answer as chosen.
- **What stays:** ```` ```steps ```` and ```` ```colors ```` aren't tools (`update_plan` and
  Markdown cover them); the fences are still drawn when a reply has them (chats from m6.71, a
  model that writes them anyway) but the system prompt no longer asks for them.
  `agent.richBlocks: false` leaves the display tools out (three fewer tools for small local
  models).

### D172 — Mermaid and math everywhere Markdown shows, Ctrl+K inline edit per hunk, search history and tree, AI opt-in
- **Diagrams: pele, not our own charts.** The only widely used fenced format for pictures is
  ```` ```mermaid ```` (GitHub, Obsidian, ChatGPT and Claude all draw it), and pele (Obsidian's
  renderer, MIT, `pele` 1.7.0, zero dependencies, by Obsidian's own team) draws every Mermaid
  diagram type, including XY bar / line charts, pie, sankey and radar. It also takes well under a
  millisecond per diagram (0.19 ms for a sequence diagram here). So D170's ```` ```chart ```` and
  the m6.72 `show_chart` tool are gone, along with our chart renderer. The agent's system prompt
  says in one line that ```` ```mermaid ```` and `$math$` are drawn. Copying an answer gives the
  Mermaid source, which is standard Markdown anywhere.
- **Where:** `ui/markdown/visuals.ts`, so every Markdown surface gets diagrams and math: the chat,
  file previews, the guide, extension pages and GitHub texts. `RenderOptions.visuals: false`
  turns them off.
  - **Loading:** each library is a lazy chunk. pele is 680 KB (252 KB gzipped) and KaTeX 268 KB
    (77 KB gzipped); neither is in the startup shell. Once loaded, rendering is synchronous and
    cached by source, so a streamed answer doesn't flicker.
  - **Width:** each diagram is laid out for its card's width (`maxWidth`, in 40 px steps, one
    shared `ResizeObserver`). A wide flowchart turns vertical in the narrow chat instead of
    shrinking to unreadable text. The font is the UI's at 14 px.
  - **Colors:** tokens, through pele's CSS variables; series colors are `--chart-1…6`. A theme
    switch recolors without drawing again.
  - **Safety:** pele escapes labels and allows only http(s) / mailto / tel links. On top of that,
    the SVG is cleaned before it's inserted (no scripts, foreignObject or `on*` attributes, and
    only http(s), mailto or `#` links), and link clicks go through the host.
  - **Errors:** a diagram that doesn't parse says which line and shows its source.
- **Math: KaTeX 0.19.0 (MIT) as MathML.** The webviews (WebView2 and WebKitGTK) draw MathML
  natively, so there are no fonts or CSS to ship. 0.19 is past the 0.18 trust-bypass advisory,
  and `trust` is off anyway.
  - **Syntax:** `$…$` inline by GitHub's rules: no space just inside the dollars, and a closing `$`
    followed by a digit doesn't count, so "$5 and $10" stays text. `\$` escapes. `$$…$$` and
    ```` ```math ```` are blocks.
- **Inline edit on Ctrl+K (Cursor's key), reviewed per hunk.** D106's Edit with AI moves off
  Ctrl+I.
  - **Hunks:** `ai/hunks.ts` (DOM-free, tested) splits the rewrite into hunks against the
    original. The editor always holds `compose()`: unchanged lines, then each hunk's new lines, or
    its old ones once rejected.
  - **Review:** each hunk has its old lines struck through above its new ones and its own Accept /
    Reject (`editor.inlineEdit.acceptHunk` / `.rejectHunk`). Ctrl+Enter keeps the rest; Esc undoes
    everything (back to the clean file when nothing else changed it). The edit closes once every
    hunk is reviewed.
  - **Chords:** Ctrl+K is VS Code's chord prefix, so the resolver learned "soft" chords. A key
    that is both a command (where its `when` holds) and a chord prefix runs the command at once
    and keeps the chord open. A next key with Ctrl / Alt / Cmd finishes a chord (Ctrl+K Ctrl+O,
    Ctrl+K Ctrl+S), and the prompt nobody typed in closes (`keyboard.chordAfterCommand`). A plain
    key is typing in the prompt, not Ctrl+K V; that one still works outside the editor or with
    Edit with AI off.
- **AI is opt-in outside the chat** (the owner's rule, now AGENTS.md hard rule 8). Inline edit
  and completions were already off by default. Generate commit message now is too:
  `git.aiCommitMessage.enabled`, and the button, menu item and command appear only when it's on.
- **Search:**
  - **History:** Up / Down walk what each box held before (query, replace, include, exclude;
    `InputHistory`, saved per folder), like VS Code. A query is remembered on Enter, on leaving
    the box, on opening a result, and for every `search.run` that waits. The view's
    search-as-you-type doesn't fill history with half-typed words.
  - **View as tree:** `search.toggleViewMode` (a header button) groups results by folder.
    `folderTree` puts folders first, sorted, and compacts single-child chains like VS Code. The
    choice is saved per folder; `search.defaultViewMode` sets the start.
- **Background agents on worktrees** move to feature-gaps' new "Proposed ideas" section.

### D173 — Missing packages install themselves, commit messages stay on, readable terminal colors
- **`npm run dev` after a release with new packages failed** with "Could not resolve "pele"",
  because `npm install` hadn't run. Now `scripts/gen.mjs`, which runs before dev, build and
  check, installs anything package.json lists that node_modules lacks, then goes on. It skips
  this during npm's own postinstall. On Windows it goes through the shell, since npm is
  `npm.cmd`.
- **Generate commit message is on by default** (`git.aiCommitMessage.enabled: true`). It runs only
  when pressed, and every IDE has it. This is the owner's one exception to D172's opt-in rule
  (AGENTS.md hard rule 8 says so). Inline edit and completions stay off.
- **`terminal.minimumContrastRatio`, default 4.5,** is VS Code's
  `terminal.integrated.minimumContrastRatio`. xterm.js lightens or darkens text that would fall
  under that contrast with its background. PowerShell's progress bar is yellow text on cyan, and
  our cyan made it unreadable. 1 keeps the program's colors, and it applies live.

### D174 — Commit messages that are messages, a model per AI feature, the repository map
- **Commit messages (`git/commitMessage.ts`, tested), done the way the commit-message tools
  do it.** Qwen answered "The diff you've provided shows… ### ✅ Key features" with the old
  prompt.
  - **The request** names the branch, then the changed files with +/- counts, then a few recent
    subjects to match the repository's style. Then comes the diff, at most 2,500 characters per
    file and 14,000 in all, so one big file can't crowd out the rest; lockfiles, maps and
    minified files are listed but not shown. It ends with "Write the commit message now. Output
    only the message", since small models follow the last line best.
  - **The style** is a summary line plus `- ` bullets, one per change. The owner preferred that
    over Conventional Commits' `feat:`; a repository whose recent commits use another style
    keeps its own.
  - **A reply that reviews the diff** gets a second, format-only request: it turns the review into
    a message and costs little, because the diff isn't sent again. `looksLikeCommitMessage`
    catches headings, bullets, chatter ("Here's…", "The diff…") and emoji.
    `cleanCommitMessage` takes off Markdown and emoji and keeps the subject to 72 characters.
  - **Streaming:** the message box only shows text while it reads like a message.
- **Stop:** while it writes, the button is a stop button (`git.cancelCommitMessage`, an
  AbortController on both requests). The box gets back what it had before.
- **A model per AI feature.** The purposes are now `edit`, `completion` and `commit`, each with
  its own setting (`git.aiCommitMessage.model` is new). The AI models page has "Models for each
  feature": each feature on or off, and its model, where empty means the chat's model
  (`agent.selectFeatureModel`).
- **Scrollbars show the arrow cursor:** a styled scrollbar took its element's cursor, the text
  cursor in the commit box. Now `cursor: default` is set on every `::-webkit-scrollbar` part.
- **Repository map (Aider's idea, our own code, no parser dependency).**
  - **What it is:** a new chat's system prompt holds the files that matter most and their
    functions, classes and types as signature lines, with members indented under their class.
  - **Symbols** come from per-language patterns: TS/JS, Python, Rust, Go, Java, Kotlin, C#,
    Swift, Ruby, PHP and C/C++. Comments, keywords and very common names are skipped.
  - **Ranking:** PageRank over "this file uses a name that file defines", within one language.
    Before that rule, a Rust `type Error` ranked first because every TS file says `Error`. Names
    defined in many files, and short lowercase ones, count less. The ranking is personalized
    toward the open editors, like Aider's chat files.
  - **Size:** cut to `agent.repoMap.maxChars` (4,000, about 1k tokens, Aider's default size).
    `agent.repoMap.enabled` is on: it's part of the chat.
  - **Building it** (`agent/repoMap.ts`): files come from the workspace index, which honors
    .gitignore; `index_query` now lists up to 50,000 paths for an empty query. Dependency,
    build and generated folders, tests and files over 300 KB are left out, up to 2,000 files,
    shallow first, read 12 at a time.
  - **Freshness:** symbols are cached per file by size and modification time. The map is warmed
    4 s after a folder opens, rebuilt after the IDE writes files or after two minutes, and a
    chat that starts before it's ready waits up to 2.5 s.
  - **Caching:** it lives in the frozen system prompt (D112), so prompt caching still works.
  - **Cost and inspection:** on this repository (455 files) parsing takes about 200 ms and
    ranking about 110 ms. `ide://agent/repoMap` and `agent.showRepoMap` show it.

### D175 — Audit of m6.60–m6.75 (the code since D161's)
Three reviewers, each new to the code, read one area each (agent and chat; editor, search and
git; workbench, scripts and Rust) for leaks, races, hangs, Windows paths, huge inputs and logic
bugs. They reported only what they verified by reading the code path. Everything verified is
fixed, with tests where a test can show it.
- **Inline edit:**
  - **Lines that moved (high).** The range was plain line numbers, so typing elsewhere while the
    model answered made the result overwrite other lines. Now a change the edit didn't make ends
    it: during review the text is kept as it stands, while it runs the request is dropped (with a
    notice), and with only the prompt open the next request asks again. A UI test types during
    review.
  - **Esc during a follow-up** now undoes the earlier rewrite too ("rejecting always restores").
  - **A trailing blank line** in the range is kept (exact line text, no stripping).
  - **Esc and Ctrl+Enter** apply only with the editor focused (`&& editorFocus`), not in the
    terminal, chat or dialogs. An edit whose tab closes goes with it.
  - **The first Esc after Ctrl+K** closes the prompt: after a soft chord, a plain key is resolved
    on its own.
- **Commit messages:** one at a time, and not during another git operation. It's claimed before
  the first await, so the Stop button can't be lost and two streams can't share the box. The
  quadratic regexes on model output became plain trims.
- **Search:** the history doesn't carry over to another folder, and the open view reads the
  current folder's history (`InputHistory.replace` in place).
- **Diagram SVG:** an element allowlist (shapes, text, gradients, markers) replaces the blocklist.
  `style`, `animate` / `set`, `image` and foreign content go; style attributes that load or run
  anything go, and `<use>` may only point inside the diagram.
- **Repository map:**
  - **Calls aren't definitions:** a member needs its body's brace, so code without semicolons
    (`  setup(app)`) no longer counts.
  - **No values:** constants are shown without them, so `export const API_KEY = "…"` doesn't put a
    secret in every chat's prompt.
  - **A still-filling index** isn't stored as the project's map; it retries.
  - **A folder switch** waits out the old build, then starts the new folder's.
  - **The index lists the project's own files** before dependency and build folders, so a folder
    without a .gitignore doesn't fill the list with node_modules.
- **Agent:**
  - **No false "Working…"** with a running clock while it waits for your answer.
  - **Stop at the start of a step:** pressed before Rust registered the request, it's sent again
    once the request streams.
  - **Attachments while it asks:** a message with only attachments is refused with "type your
    answer first" instead of waiting forever.
  - **Installing an agent CLI** runs its install and sign-in as two commands, since a `;` breaks
    in cmd.exe.
- **Workbench:**
  - **Reload:** a command registered to a window but not started yet is cancelled on reload
    (`cancel_owner` through `cancel`).
  - **Activity bar drag:** it ends when the window loses focus or is hidden, so the next click
    can't drop the icon.
  - **The agent column's width** is remembered in pixels through a window too narrow for it,
    and the base layout's share isn't scaled a second time (`assumeDockWidth`). NaN sizes never
    come out.
  - **dev:fresh** removes its throwaway profile and treats a kill as a failure.
  - **gen.mjs** doesn't expect dev packages that were left out on purpose.
- **Checked and fine:** gen.mjs can't recurse through postinstall. The new Rust code has no
  panics. The ask_user and permission promises are always resolved (on stop, delete and
  dispose). The map's regexes stay under 2 ms on worst-case lines.

### D176 — Extensions that can change the IDE, and the agent building them
The owner wants the IDE to be a playground for their agent: when asked, it should be able to
upgrade the editor and build tools with their own windows and viewers, close to what a VS Code
extension can do. Others, Anthropic included, should be able to bring their own agent. This
release widens the extension API, gives the extension page what VS Code's has, and makes the
agent ask before it changes the IDE.
- **The editor:**
  - `ide.editor.open / text / replace / select / decorate / clearDecorations`.
  - `ide.languages.setDiagnostics / registerHoverProvider / registerCompletionProvider`.
  - The pieces live in a DOM-free registry, `services.extensionFeatures`, which the editor's
    lazily loaded Monaco part reads (`monaco/extensionFeatures.ts`), so extensions can start
    before the editor exists.
  - Providers answer through the worker within 1.5 s, or nothing shows. Their Markdown is
    untrusted (no command links, no HTML).
  - Decorations are a fixed set of styles drawn in theme colors (highlight, underline, error,
    warning, info, faded, strong), so an extension can't make text unreadable in some theme.
  - Agents get the same edits as commands: `editor.getText` and `editor.replaceRange`, one
    undoable edit when the file is open, otherwise on disk.
- **The workbench:**
  - **Status bar items:** `ui.createStatusBarItem`, at most 10, text only with `$(icon)`. A new
    command or position replaces the item.
  - **Menu items** in `explorer/context`, `editor/context`, `editor/title` and `view/title`. The
    manifest accepts VS Code's object form or a list. `when` clauses see `resourceExtname`,
    `resourceFilename`, `resourceLangId`, `explorerResourceIsFolder` and `view`.
  - **Pages** (`"location": "editor"`): webview views in the editor area.
  - **Windows:** every extension page can move into a window of its own
    (`webview.openInWindow`, `layout.moveToNewWindow`). The frame leaves the iframe layer for
    the view's element, and messages are taken from the new window.
  - **File viewers** (`contributes.viewers`, VS Code's custom editors): a page registered with
    `services.viewers`, so it opens files directly or from "Open preview" / "Reopen with…".
    The page gets `{ file: { path, name, text, canSave } }`, again whenever the file changes,
    and saves with `{ save: text }` when the extension has `fs.write`.
- **Safety:**
  - Menu items, status bar items and keybindings may only run the extension's own commands.
  - Everything an extension registers goes when it stops.
  - Limits: 20 providers, 5,000 ranges per decoration set, 1,000 problems per file, 50 menu
    items.
- **Bringing an agent** (and Anthropic's or anyone's): `contributes.agents` (Agent Client
  Protocol over stdio, like the built-in Claude Code and Codex entries), `mcpServers` and
  `modelProviders`.
  - Agents and MCP servers start programs, so they need both `shell` and `agent`.
  - Providers need `agent` and https (or http on localhost), and can't take a built-in
    provider's name. They appear as tiles marked "Extension" with the server's host, and the
    user still adds them with a key.
  - The user's own settings of the same name win, and an extension can't replace Claude Code or
    Codex.
- **Activation:** `onStartupFinished` (2 s after startup) and `workspaceContains:<glob>` were
  added. Commands, views and viewers still start the worker on first use.
- **The extension page:**
  - **Details:** the README drawn like the Markdown preview (diagrams, math, the extension's
    own images) beside a side panel. The panel shows identifier, version, source (installed,
    comes with the IDE, development, this folder's), state, last updated, license, location,
    categories and keywords, repository and homepage links, and a marketplace section.
  - **The marketplace section** says plainly that nothing is published yet. Showing invented
    ratings would be dishonest.
  - **Tabs:**
    - Features: also lists viewers, menus, agents, servers and providers.
    - Settings: the settings editor's own rows, live.
    - Files: the folder's files with a preview, opened in the editor, read-only for installed
      extensions. Rust `ext_files` lists only known extension roots.
    - Changelog: when `CHANGELOG.md` exists.
    - Permissions and Log, as before.
  - **Header:** Install permanently, and Edit with agent… (`agent.compose`: the panel opens with
    a drafted message, not sent).
  - **Avatar:** `"icon": "<name>"` draws an icon of the IDE's set (`extensions.listIcons` lists
    them all), tinted like the initials tile.
- **Development to installed:**
  - `extensions.installPermanently` copies a development extension into the installed ones. It
    keeps its permissions, and the folder stays where it is but is no longer loaded.
  - In the explorer, an extension folder's context menu has Run as development extension,
    Install extension permanently and Extension details. A quick `extensions.folderStatus`
    check runs before the menu opens.
- **The agent:**
  - `extensions.guide` returns docs/extensions.md and the API types.
  - The system prompt says what extensions can do and how to build one.
  - Installed extensions live outside the folder, so `read_file` and `list_dir` take their
    paths, read-only, through the extension store's scoped reader. So do `extensions.listFiles`
    and `extensions.readFile`. The owner saw "outside the workspace" when the agent tried to
    compare with the bundled TODO tree.
  - `ide://extensions` shows each extension's live contributions.
- **The agent changing the IDE asks, even with full access.** It's the owner's call: the agent
  rearranging panels is surprising whatever it may do to files.
  - Commands under `layout.`, `view.`, `workbench.`, `ui.`, `settings.`, `keybindings.`,
    `extensions.`, `window.` and similar ask in the chat, except reading and showing a view
    (`core/permissions/ideControl.ts`).
  - "Always allow this chat" covers all of them for that chat. Destructive ones still ask every
    time.
  - Opening files, the browser, terminals and the debugger keep their usual rules.

**Audit (three reviewers new to the code: security, lifecycle and UI, docs vs. code).** Every
verified finding is fixed:
- **Agents can't write through `editor.replaceRange`.** It skipped the changeset review, so
  agents now edit with their reviewed tools. It and `editor.getText` work only inside the open
  folder.
- **Read-effect commands need `fs.read`.** Before this, an extension without it could read any
  file through `editor.getText` or `viewer.open`. A viewer still reads the file the user opened
  in it, which needs no permission, as VS Code's custom editors do.
- **Extensions can't install themselves permanently.** `extensions.installPermanently` refuses
  extension and MCP callers.
- **Pages close with their extension.** Panel, page and viewer tabs close when it stops, so a
  page left open can't start it again, and a stopped runtime refuses to start its worker. They
  reopen within 15 s when it comes back, since a development extension reloads on every save.
  A viewer checks `fs.write` again at each save.
- **IDE-control asks cover more:** `notifications.*`, `explorer.toggleExcludedFiles` and
  `git.toggleInlineBlame` now ask too. Extensions and MCP clients can't change the settings that
  decide what the agent may do, which already held for agents.
- **Extensions only see the open folder:** the active editor's path and hover / completion
  requests stay inside it.
- **More limits:** 500 files with problems, 200 decoration sets, and ranges cut before parsing.
  Agents don't get hidden files from extension folders. A provider name that starts with a
  built-in provider's name is refused.
- **The extension page:**
  - It redraws only when what it shows changed. A development extension's poll every 1.5 s
    redrew it and broke typing in the Settings tab.
  - Blob URLs are revoked when replaced and on close.
  - The Changelog tab doesn't bounce the reader back to Details on an edit.
  - The Files list and preview use separate counters.
- **MCP:** a server is stopped only when its extension's config changed, not on every reload.
  A user's `"enabled": false` does turn an extension's server off.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - A stale folder check can't open a menu after a newer right-click.
  - Editor title buttons appear when an extension starts.
  - Provider timers are cleared, the engine disposes extension features, and decorations of
    closed models are forgotten.
  - A failed permanent install restarts the development copy.
  - `folderStatus` recognizes VS Code `package.json` extensions.
- **Docs vs. code:**
  - The docs' sample manifest asks for the permissions it uses.
  - `notify`, `showInput` and `settings.get` give `undefined`, as typed.
  - Unknown status bar icons fall back to a dot.
  - Explorer menus get `resourceLangId`.
  - Command descriptions say "<workspace folder>", and the prompt names the real one.

### D177 — The workspace folder: the project's own .vscode when it has one
The IDE kept a project's settings, tasks, launch configurations, snippets, agent memory and
commands, extensions and screenshots in `.codevre`, even in projects that already have a
`.vscode`. The owner asked that a project's existing folder be used for all of it.
- **Which folder:** product.json now lists `workspaceFolderAliases` (`[".vscode"]`).
  - When a folder opens, the first that exists wins: the IDE's own (`workspaceFolderName`),
    then the aliases. With none, the IDE's own is created when something is first saved.
  - `workbench/workspaceFolder.ts` holds the choice, and every path goes through
    `workspaceFolderName()` / `workspaceFolderPath()`.
  - The name stays in product.json, so renaming the app means changing that one file. Another
    accepted name is one more alias.
- **When .vscode is the workspace folder:**
  - `.vscode/settings.json` is both the workspace settings file (written with
    `setJsoncProperty`, so comments survive) and the VS Code layer. That layer still translates
    VS Code keys, and a key the IDE knows shows as "workspace".
  - `tasks.json` and `launch.json` are read once, not twice.
- **Legacy and limits:** a legacy `.ide` folder is still renamed to the IDE's own first. A folder
  created while the project is open counts from the next time it opens.

### D178 — Deleting a folder on another drive than the trash: whole or not at all
The owner deleted an extension's folder in a project on another drive than the app's data (the
trash). Its files went, but the empty folder stayed, with "The system cannot find the file
specified (os error 2)", and it only vanished after the folder was closed and reopened.
- **Cause:** across drives the trash can't rename, so it copied the folder and then deleted it in
  place. On Windows a folder that a program has open (a terminal or a server running inside it,
  often one the agent started) can't be removed. The delete emptied it and failed on the folder
  itself, which Windows then kept as a "delete pending" shell until that program closed.
- **Fix:**
  - **Rename aside first.** The item is renamed beside itself first
    (`.<name>.deleting`, same drive). That works whole or not at all: a folder in use can't be
    renamed, so nothing is touched. Only then is it copied to the trash and removed.
  - **Any failure puts it back** under its own name.
  - **The message says it's in use** (Windows codes 5, 32, 145) and what to close. The explorer
    names the open terminals whose working directory is inside it.
  - A Rust test covers both the success path and a failed copy.

### D179 — Settings like Cursor's (pages, sections), the agent's settings, closing what it opened
The owner sent Cursor's settings pages to compare with ours. They asked for the agent options
that make sense, a clearer layout (sections under a page like a docs site, a side panel with
dividers, arrows on entries that open elsewhere), and a way to close things the agent opens.
- **Pages** (`settings/pages.ts`, DOM-free, tested):
  - **Groups** with dividers:
    - General: Appearance, Editor, Files and explorer, Search, Terminal, Keyboard shortcuts ↗
    - AI: Agent, AI in the editor, Models and providers ↗, MCP server
    - Tools: Source control, Browser and network, Run and debug, Testing, Language servers
    - More: Accounts, extensions' own pages, Extensions ↗
  - **A page gathers categories:** Appearance holds Workbench and Window.
  - **Sections:** a page's settings are grouped by a schema's new `section`, else their
    category. Each section is a card with a small label above, like Cursor's.
  - **The navigation lists the open page's sections** so a click jumps there.
  - **Titles:** schemas may set a `title` when the derived one reads badly ("Prompt cache TTL",
    not "Cache ttl").
  - **New placement:** AI settings in the editor (Edit with AI, suggestions as you type, commit
    messages) moved from the Agent page to "AI in the editor".
- **Look** (the owner's notes on ours vs. Cursor's), within DESIGN.md:
  - Search sits at the top of the navigation.
  - Navigation text is smaller (`--text-sm`), with group dividers.
  - The page title has User · Workspace, reset and settings.json beside it.
  - Row dividers are inset from the card's edges.
  - A changed setting gets a small dot in a quiet color instead of the 2 px accent bar.
  - Under 640 px the navigation is an icon rail and search moves above the page.
  - `settings.reset` takes `keys` (a section's reset).
- **The agent's settings**, now sectioned: Models and context, Conversation, Context and tools,
  Memory, Execution and approvals, Applying changes, Integrations. Added where Cursor has a
  useful equivalent we lacked:

  | Setting | What it does |
  |---|---|
  | `agent.textSize` | Small, default or large chat text (the conversation is scaled) |
  | `agent.submitWithCtrlEnter` | Ctrl+Enter sends and Enter makes a new line |
  | `agent.whileWorking` | A message sent while it works queues (as before) or interrupts |
  | `agent.codeBlockWordWrap` | Long lines in chat code blocks wrap |
  | `agent.webFetch.enabled` | Turn off the agent's web reading |
  | `agent.webFetch.autoApprove` | Read web pages without asking |
  | `agent.thirdPartyConfigs` | CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, .cursor/rules, Copilot instructions, .claude and .cursor commands; on by default (AGENTS.md is always read) |
  | `agent.ideControl` | D176's ask before changing the IDE; on |
  | `agent.closeOpenedOnStop` | Stop closes what that chat opened |
  | `agent.browserProtection` | Browser page actions always ask; off |
  | `agent.mcpProtection` | Every MCP tool call asks, read-only ones too; off |
  | `agent.deleteProtection` | Command lines that may delete files ask; off, like Cursor's |
  | `agent.formatOnFinish` | Run the project's formatter on the files the turn wrote; off |

  - "Even with full access" applies to the three protections, so they ask in full access too.
  - The delete check is cautious: a line the denylist checks can't see through asks too.
  - Formatting skips open files with unsaved edits.
  - `workbench.statusBar.visible` and View → Toggle status bar are new.
  - **Left out on purpose:**
    - Voice: we had no voice input then (added in D180).
    - Agent autocomplete and agent review on commit: AI is opt-in outside the chat (rule 8),
      and they'd need the owner's say.
    - Inline diffs: our review is per hunk already.
    - Worktree limits: no worktrees yet.
    - Network diagnostics: no service of ours to check.
    - Commit attribution and branch prefix: the agent doesn't make commits or branches by
      itself.
- **What the agent opened** (`agent/opened.ts`): tabs that appear while one of the IDE's own
  agent's commands runs are recorded per chat.
  - **Credit is cautious:** a command that runs long (over 3 s) or overlaps another agent
    command isn't credited, since the user or another chat may have opened the tab meanwhile.
    Leaving one of the agent's tabs open beats closing one of yours.
  - **External agents' tabs aren't tracked:** they reach the IDE through its MCP server.
  - **Closing:** `agent.closeOpened` (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+W, the chat's ⋯ menu) closes them, and
    windows go with their tabs. `ide://agent` reports how many are open.
  - **Windows:** `layout.returnAllWindows` brings every window's tab back. Windows already open
    beside the main window, so "can't see it" is mostly tabs and views it opened unnoticed.

**Review (an independent reader, verified findings, all fixed):**
- **The agent can't switch its protections off.** The new settings join the agent-guarded keys:
  `settings.set` / `settings.reset` from agents, extensions and MCP clients refuse them, even
  after "Always allow this chat".
- **Browser protection covers all page actions.** Back, reload and scroll are declared without
  effects, and an earlier chat grant used to let them through. The policy's new
  `agentAlwaysAsks` sends them to the ask.
- **Format when done goes through the changeset.** Only the files this turn wrote are formatted
  (`changeset.writtenIn`), as a proposal accepted at once: checkpointed, one undo entry, merged
  with any typing. Before, undo of the agent's edit failed and a held proposal's original could
  be formatted.
- **Credit for opened tabs is cautious** (see above). Closing them isn't forced, so an editor
  with unsaved changes asks Save / Don't save, and a kept tab stays listed. Stop's close is quiet
  when there's nothing to close.
- **The status bar's row goes when it's hidden,** in zen mode too. The toggle writes to the scope
  that sets the value. Settings search focuses the visible box in the narrow layout.
- **Deletion protection covers external agents' delete requests and terminals,** plus `rimraf`
  and `--delete` flags. Web reading turned off is refused before asking, and the prompt stops
  suggesting it.

### Sizes and startup after M3 (Linux x86-64, release)
| | M2 | M3 |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend total (`dist/`) | 16.70 MB (3.77 MB gzip) | 16.77 MB (3.80 MB gzip) |
| Initial shell (index.html + main.js + main.css) | 338 KB | 398 KB (≈ 125 KB gzip) |
| Release binary | 24.7 MB | 25.6 MB |
| `.deb` / `.rpm` | 9.06 / 9.06 MB | 9.27 / 9.27 MB |

The shell grew by the git and LSP extensions, the line diff and the LSP client, which load at
startup (they are small; the source control view itself is created on first show). Startup, same
VM and method as M2, 3 runs: shell visible +100–121 ms after the webview starts (M2: 96–101 ms),
extensions active +140–163 ms, folder restored +277–298 ms, editor ready +982–1020 ms.

| | M3 | M4 |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend total (`dist/`) | 16.77 MB (3.80 MB gzip) | 17.70 MB (3.98 MB gzip) |
| Initial shell (index.html + main.js + main.css) | 398 KB (≈ 125 KB gzip) | 522 KB (≈ 155 KB gzip) |

The shell grew by the agent extension (panel, commands, Markdown renderer), the MCP/ACP clients
and the menu rework, all in main.js. Startup, same VM and method, 3 runs (the first cold): shell visible +108–151 ms after
the webview starts, extensions active +145–211 ms, folder restored +266–460 ms, editor ready
+926–1065 ms. Warm runs are within ~10 ms of M3 for the shell.

### D180 — Agent modes, voice input, the setup card, menu polish, and children that end with the IDE
The owner asked for a batch of polish, Cursor's chat and plan modes, and Cursor-like voice input.
They also sent a Task Manager screenshot with dozens of busy "Console Window Host" processes.
- **Modes** (`session.chatMode`, `agent.setChatMode`, `agent.build`, the composer's first pill,
  Shift+Tab):
  - **Agent** is as before.
  - **Ask** offers read-only tools only (`readOnly`) and answers.
  - **Plan** offers read-only tools plus `update_plan`. It ends with a "Plan ready" notice and
    **Build**, which switches to Agent and sends "Build it: carry out the plan above."
  - The mode's rules go in the user message's context, not the system prompt, so prompt caching
    holds when you switch.
  - The message keeps a `mode` (a chip on it). The mode is saved with the chat, and
    `ide://agent/session` has `chatMode`.
  - The tool list is fixed per turn (`turnMode`), so switching mid-turn applies from the next
    message.
  - Retry and Edit & resend use the current mode's rules, not the ones saved with the message.
  - External agents (Claude Code, Codex…) get the mode's rules as instructions. Their tools
    can't be narrowed, so their own permission prompts still guard changes.
  - Build refuses a plan that later messages have moved past. If the agent is busy, the mode
    stays as it was.
- **Voice** (`view/voice.ts`, `core/agent/voice.ts`, `ai/transcribe.rs`):
  - **Why not the browser's speech API:** WebView2's `SpeechRecognition` is unreliable
    (Microsoft Q&A 2054895, Chromium 41172064), and WebKitGTK has none. Instead the composer
    records with `MediaRecorder` and the Rust side posts the audio to an OpenAI-compatible
    `/audio/transcriptions`. The key never reaches the page.
  - **Provider:** Groq (whisper-large-v3-turbo) if it has a key, else OpenAI
    (gpt-4o-mini-transcribe). `agent.voice.provider` / `model` pick any OpenAI-compatible one,
    a local Whisper server too. Anthropic and Ollama have no speech endpoint.
  - **Like Cursor's:** the microphone takes the send button's place while the box is empty, and
    with only an attachment, Enter still sends.
  - **While recording,** the box shows a live waveform (an AnalyserNode's loudness, one bar every
    60 ms, in a theme color), a timer and ×. Enter / ✓ transcribes, and Esc / × cancels.
  - **The text** is added to the box. Ending with a word from `agent.voice.submitWords` ("submit")
    sends it.
  - **Limits:** 5 minutes, and 25 MB for the request.
  - **Settings** (Agent → Voice): `enabled`, `provider`, `model`, `language`, `submitWords`.
  - **Rule 8:** voice runs only when you press the microphone, inside the agent's chat, so it
    isn't a new AI-outside-the-chat exception.
  - **macOS:** `src-tauri/Info.plist` adds `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, which the bundler
    merges in; without it macOS ends the app when the microphone opens. A notarized build with
    the hardened runtime also needs the `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement,
    to add when macOS signing is set up.
  - **No provider, no recording:** the microphone checks for a speech provider before it records,
    so you don't talk for a minute only to get an error. A cancel (Esc, ×) while it transcribes
    drops the text, and a newer recording is never touched by an older one's result. A request
    times out after 2 minutes.
  - **Submit words** match in any alphabet ("…, отправить").
- **Setup card:** "Set up AI models" shows an overlapping row of brand marks (logos where we
  have them, else letters in the brand's color) and "and more", instead of a sentence. The names
  are its tooltip and label.
- **Menus** (`ui/Menu.ts`):
  - A press on the button that opened a menu closes it, and the click that follows doesn't
    reopen it. Every menu opened from a button toggles this way.
  - A menu that replaces an open one (the menu bar's hover switch, ←/→) skips the fade
    (`.menu.is-instant`), so it doesn't blink.
  - A submenu opens scrolled to, and focused on, its checked item. The model menu marks the
    provider holding the current model, so its list opens on that model.
- **Small fixes:**
  - Chats view tooltips show the chat's project folder.
  - Run and debug had two gears that did the same thing. The title bar's is gone, and the one
    beside the configuration list stays.
  - The extension details' side panel is sticky in wide layouts.
- **Console hosts** (`src-tauri/src/job.rs`):
  - **Cause:** on Windows, a child outlives the IDE when the IDE ends abruptly (crash, Task
    Manager, `tauri dev` rebuilding it). Shells, language / MCP / agent servers and formatters
    kept running, each with a conhost, some spinning on a closed pipe. A page reload also left
    the old page's terminals and stdio language servers running.
  - **Fix:** every child the IDE spawns for itself (PTYs, `exec`, formatters, language servers)
    joins one job object with `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`. Windows closes the handle when the IDE's
    process ends, however it ends, and that kills them.
  - Things launched *for* the user (their browser, another window) aren't added.
  - **Trade-off:** programs started from the integrated terminal are in the job too, so they end
    with the IDE (a dev server, or a GUI app started from a shell). A grandchild that a launcher
    starts before `adopt` runs (microseconds) can escape. Putting the IDE itself in the job
    would close that gap, but it would also take the user's browser and other windows down.
  - When the main window's page loads again, its terminals and language servers are ended.
  - This is a no-op elsewhere: Unix children get a hangup.
  - Orphans from before this build must be ended by hand once.

### D181 — A canvas the user and the agent share (bundled, off by default)
The owner asked for a canvas the agent can work on, like other agents have, as an extension
that ships disabled, like the TODO tree.
- **What others do:**
  - **Cursor's canvases** (3.1, cursor.com/blog/canvas) are interactive pages the agent
    generates: dashboards, PR reviews, eval analysis. They're built from a React component kit and
    kept as durable artifacts beside the terminal and browser.
  - **tldraw's MCP app** (tldraw.dev/blog/tldraw-mcp-app) gives the agent three tools (create,
    edit and delete shapes) and passes the canvas state back into the chat, so you iterate
    between sketch and text.
  - **ChatGPT Canvas and Claude's artifacts** are about documents and code, not boards.
  - **What we built:** a whiteboard of cards and arrows, the part a developer uses by hand too
    (architecture sketches, feature plans, codebase maps), with tools shaped like tldraw's.
- **Format:** JSON Canvas 1.0 (jsoncanvas.org, Obsidian's open format).
  - Nodes are `text` (Markdown), `file`, `link` or `group`, and edges have sides, ends, labels and
    colors (six presets or hex).
  - The files open in Obsidian and other tools. Unknown fields and node types are kept as they
    are.
  - The project's main canvas is `<workspace folder>/canvas/main.canvas`. `ide://workspace` now
    has `workspaceFolder` so extensions can find it.
- **No library:**
  - tldraw needs React and its license requires a watermark unless you buy a business license.
  - Excalidraw is MIT but also React, and several MB.
  - The rules are vanilla TS with no new runtime dependency, and a JSON Canvas board is small. So
    it's our own: about 1000 lines of plain JS in a sandboxed extension, plus a 150-line safe
    Markdown renderer. The extension page can't use the IDE's renderer.
- **The extension** (`src-tauri/bundled-extensions/canvas/`):
  - Seeded disabled like the TODO tree (D121).
  - Permissions: `fs.read` and `fs.write` for its canvases, and `browser` to open link cards.
  - The viewer (`viewer.js`):
    - **Moving around:** pan with the wheel, Space+drag or the middle button. Ctrl+wheel zooms at
      the pointer. Box select.
    - **Cards:** double-click adds a card (Markdown with tickable tasks). Drag cards; groups carry
      their cards. Resize from the corner.
    - **Arrows:** drag an edge dot onto a card for an arrow, or onto empty space for a new
      connected card. Arrows get labels.
    - **Shortcuts and tools:** colors, Group (Ctrl+G), Arrange (along the arrows, else a grid),
      copy/cut/paste, duplicate, nudge, undo/redo, fit.
    - **Small windows:** the toolbar drops undo and zoom steps under 460 px.
  - **Saving:** edits save to the file after 300 ms.
- **The agent:**
  - The commands are ordinary discoverable ones, found with `find_commands canvas`:
    - `canvas.read`: cards, arrows, the user's selection, and whether it's open.
    - `canvas.edit`: one call with a list of ops: `add` (with `ref` names that later ops in the
      call can use, and `near`/`side` placement), `update`, `remove`, `connect`, `disconnect`,
      `group`, `layout` (tree / grid / row / column), `clear`.
    - Also `canvas.focus`, `canvas.open`, `canvas.new` and `canvas.list`.
  - **One call, one approval:** a whole diagram is one write command, so one approval (or
    "allow for this chat") covers it. The call is all or nothing, and an error names the op
    ("ops[3] (connect): no card \"x\"").
  - **Placement:** cards without a position go in free space below what's there, and cards without
    a size are fitted to their text. So the agent rarely needs coordinates.
  - **Edits go to the file.** The open page sees the change, merges its own unsaved edits on top
    (by id), lights up what changed, and makes the change one undo step. So Ctrl+Z takes back the
    agent's edit. Not narrowing this through the open page keeps one path, and the agent can
    work on a closed canvas too.
  - This isn't AI outside the chat (rule 8): the canvas never calls a model, and the agent
    uses it only from the chat.
- **A review before shipping (16 findings, all fixed):**
  - **Card Markdown could inject script.** The page's CSP allows inline script, and a crafted
    link or URL broke out of an attribute. Now links and code are built from the raw text into
    placeholders, with each part escaped on its own, and only then is the rest escaped. Unit
    tests try the known break-outs.
  - **File previews:** the page may only preview files that are on a card of its canvas, so a
    compromised page still can't read `.env`.
  - **Saving:**
    - Typing is saved when the card is committed, and anything pending is saved when focus
      leaves the page. Closing a tab used to drop the last edit.
    - Saves are remembered until they come back from the file. If the agent's `canvas.edit` read
      the file before our save landed, our cards are put back on top of its version.
    - The IDE delivers file versions in order (`WebviewFrame.sendFile` is queued).
    - A file change during a drag waits for the drag to end.
    - A canvas that first loads broken can't be saved empty after it's fixed.
  - **Which canvases are open** comes from the IDE: viewers get `{ ide: "viewerOpened" }` and
    `{ ide: "viewerClosed" }` (documented in extensions.md). The page's own goodbye dies with it,
    and a page reloads when its tab changes window.
  - **Smaller:**
    - Paths normalize `.` and `..`.
    - `canvas.new` takes a folder only when it is one.
    - A file card without a file renders.
    - Tasks inside quotes tick the right line.
    - Removing an empty new card drops its own undo step, not the agent's.
    - Nested groups move with their group.
    - Removing a group with its contents can also name those contents.
    - A cancelled gesture is finished cleanly.
    - Long card text in `canvas.read` says it was cut.
- **Theme tokens for extension pages:** the message now carries surfaces, borders, text sizes,
  radii, shadows and `--label-1..6`. These are new tokens for colors a user gives things, tuned
  for both themes.
- **Lint:** the page's CSS adds 13 `noDescendingSpecificity` warnings, the same kind as the
  existing 80.
- **Also:** the "Set up AI models" card drops its left icon, and the brand marks lose the ring
  they had on hover.
- **Later, if it's used:**
  - Image cards. The page's origin can't load project files, so images would need a data-URL
    read.
  - A minimap, and Mermaid in cards.
  - Cursor-style generated pages: charts and tables as cards.

### D182 — Finding what extensions add: View → Tools, an Open button, New tab
The owner turned Canvas on and couldn't find how to open it: "Canvas: Open" lived only in the
command palette. They asked that a tool someone builds never ends with "how do I open this?".
- **The Canvas extension now has a sidebar view, Canvases** (activity bar icon):
  - It lists the project's canvases, with the main one first, then by name.
  - **How it finds them:** the canvas folder, plus a search for `*.canvas` files. The search
    skips hidden and .gitignored folders, so the canvas folder is listed on its own.
  - **Title buttons:** + new canvas, and refresh.
  - **Keeping it current:** a canvas the extension writes for the first time refreshes the list.
    So does a created, deleted or renamed file.
- **Every tool is listed in three places, with no work for the extension's author:**
  - **View → Tools:** the IDE's own tools (Explorer, Search, Source control, Run and debug,
    Testing, Outline, Extensions, Agent, Chats, Terminal, Problems, Browser, Settings, Keyboard
    shortcuts), then each extension's views, grouped by extension. It's searchable, like other
    long submenus.
  - **The Open button on an extension's page:** with one tool it reads "Open <name>"; with
    several it opens a menu. The list row's ⋯ menu starts with the same entries.
  - **New tab** (a group's ⋯ menu and `layout.newTab`'s picker): the extensions' tools come after
    the IDE's own. `layout.newTab { tool, toolInput }` runs one in that group.
- **Where the list comes from:** `ExtensionFeatures.openers` holds each extension's views
  (sidebar ones open with `view.show`, panel and editor pages with `<view>.show`).
  `allOpeners()` adds commands an extension puts in the new menu location `menubar/view`, for a
  tool that opens with a command rather than a view. Canvas puts Main canvas there.
- **Why not one "Extensions" menu, or VS Code's "Open view…":** listing the IDE's tools beside
  the extensions' answers "where is X" without knowing who made X. A sidebar view also gets the
  activity bar icon it already had.

### D183 — Canvas, round two: file search, images, its own menus and settings; viewer tabs stay
The owner tried the canvas, and these were their notes:
- "Add file…" made them type a whole path, with no search.
- An image card said "(an image: double-click to open it)".
- A right-click showed the web view's Inspect menu.
- The canvas had no settings of its own.
- They wanted several canvases.
- Opening anything else closed the canvas, because its tab was an italic preview tab.

They took back dragging files in from the desktop (that would clash with the dock's split drop
targets).

**File search for extensions:** `quickOpen.pickFile { placeholder?, extensions? }` is quick
open's fuzzy file search returning the pick: recent files first, the Rust index, .gitignore
respected.
- **Who calls it:** extensions with `fs.read` (the canvas's Add file… and Add image…, which
  limits it to image endings).
- **Hidden from the palette:** it only returns a path.
- **Not hidden from agents:** it's a read and it only asks the user, and the extension host
  refuses `hidden` commands.

**Images:** `ide.workspace.fs.readBase64(path)` (`fs.read`, 8 MB at most) gives an extension a
file's bytes.
- The canvas sends image cards to its page as `data:` URLs, because the page's origin can't load
  project files. The CSP already allows `data:` images, and an SVG in an `<img>` runs no script.
- The preview gate from D181 applies: only files on a card of that canvas.
- `canvas.showImages` turns previews off.

**The page's own context menus** (`menus.js`, split from `viewer.js` behind a `page` object):
- **The board:** add a card, file, image, link or group at that point; paste; select all;
  arrange; fit; 100%; find; settings.
- **A card or the selection:**
  - **By type:** edit; open, show in explorer and copy the path of a file; open and copy a link;
    rename, select inside and ungroup a group.
  - **For any card:** a color row, duplicate, group, bring to front, send to back, fit to text,
    copy, cut, delete.
- **An arrow:** edit the label, an arrow at the end or start, reverse it, color, delete.
- The web view's menu is suppressed everywhere in the page except text fields.
- Keyboard: arrow keys move through the menu and Esc closes it.

**Find** (Ctrl+F, toolbar): matches card text, files, links and group names. Enter and
Shift+Enter step through them and zoom to each. F2 renames or edits.

**Settings:**
- `canvas.folder`: where new canvases go, and where the list looks first.
- `canvas.cardWidth`.
- `canvas.arrowStyle`: curved, straight, or elbow with right angles.
- `canvas.showImages`.
- These come alongside the grid and snapping settings, and the toolbar's gear opens them.

**Several canvases:** `canvas.newNamed` asks for a name. The Canvases view's +, the explorer's
folder menu (in that folder) and the palette use it; agents keep `canvas.new` with a path.

**Tabs:**
- A viewer page that saves pins its tab (`ctx.pin()`), as typing does in a preview editor, so
  editing a canvas keeps it open.
- The canvas's own commands open it with `preview: false`.

**Review fixes** (10 findings):
- **Settings button:** `settings.open` is now `discoverable`, so an extension's button can open
  settings. An agent running it is still asked, because `settings.*` counts as changing the IDE.
- **`quickOpen.pickFile`:** refuses agent, ACP and MCP callers (only a person can pick), and an
  empty box says to type.
- **`readBase64`:** checks the size before reading.
- **Previews:**
  - They go only to the canvas that asked, and are fetched again when their file changes.
  - `canvas.showImages` is checked by the worker too, and changing it re-asks for previews.
- **Menus:**
  - Copy and Cut go through the system clipboard, like Ctrl+C.
  - A menu closes when the file changes under it.
  - Duplicate skips cards that are gone.
- **Find bar:** it no longer covers the selection bar in narrow pages.
- **New canvas from a folder:** a name with a / stays inside the folder you clicked.

**Bundled extensions really update, and come back (m6.83):**
- **What went wrong:** after m6.82 the owner still had m6.80's canvas.
  - Seeding (D121) replaced an installed bundled extension only when the shipped *version*
    changed, and Canvas stayed 1.0.0.
  - Uninstalling then kept it uninstalled, by design, with no way back.
- **Now:**
  - An installed bundled extension is rewritten whenever any shipped file differs. Installed
    copies are read-only to the user, so nothing of theirs is lost.
  - **Restore bundled extensions** (`extensions.restoreBundled`): right-click the Extensions
    list, or the Extensions icon in the activity bar, or run it from the palette. It re-seeds
    the bundled extensions that were uninstalled. They come back disabled, as on first start.
  - Canvas is 1.2.0.
  - **Uninstalling moves the folder aside in one rename before deleting it** (to `.removing`,
    cleared on the next uninstall). The UI tests showed that the list's seeding could write a
    file back into a half-deleted folder ("Directory not empty").

**Size:** `viewer.js` is still about 1650 lines after the split. Its gestures, rendering and
saving share one closure's state, so splitting further would mean exposing most of it. It's left
as a known exception for now.

### D184 — Canvas, round three: Obsidian's features, editor-colored file cards, export
The owner asked for Obsidian Canvas's features "within reason" (obsidian.md/canvas and
/help/plugins/canvas), file cards that use the IDE's syntax colors and file icons, and a settings
page that refreshes when an extension with settings is turned on or off.

**Settings page:** registering or dropping an extension's settings now bumps `settings.version`,
so an open settings tab rebuilds.

**What we took from Obsidian:**
- **Moving and resizing:**
  - Alt-drag duplicates and Shift-drag stays on one axis.
  - Holding Space turns snapping off.
  - Cards resize from every edge and the corner, and Shift keeps the shape.
  - The selected card draws on top.
  - **Snap to objects** (`canvas.snapToObjects`): edges and centres line up with other cards, with
    dashed guides (`geometry.js`).
- **Arrows:**
  - Drag a selected arrow's end onto another card to reconnect it, or off any card to remove it.
  - Its menu has "Follow to the other end", Direction (none, one way, both, reverse), add or
    remove the label, and color.
- **Align** (selection bar and context menu): left, centre or right; top, middle or bottom; row,
  column or grid; spread out evenly; same width or height.
- **Groups:** a background image (cover, keep ratio, repeat). Go to group from the board menu.
- **Files:**
  - Markdown cards render the note, narrowed to a heading if you choose one.
  - Convert to file turns a text card into a note.
  - Swap file, Change link, and a nested canvas's summary.
  - The explorer's **Add to canvas** adds a file or a folder's files. It stands in for dragging,
    which the owner ruled out because the dock's drop targets would take the drag.
  - **Pasting an image** saves it under `attachments/` beside the canvas and makes a card.
- **View:**
  - Shift+2 zooms to the selection.
  - **Read-only** (lock) applies to this view only.
  - Custom colors (any hex).
  - Help (`?`) lists the shortcuts.
- **Export as image:** PNG at 1–3× or SVG; the whole canvas or the view; privacy mode draws bars
  instead of text.
  - `export.js` builds a standalone SVG: theme colors resolved, text wrapped and clipped, images
    inlined. A PNG is that SVG drawn on a canvas.
  - The file is saved beside the canvas. `canvas.export` does the same for agents and tests, and
    returns the path.

**Left out:** web pages and YouTube embedded in cards (the page's CSP forbids frames), PDFs,
audio and video, and Obsidian's Bases and vault links.

**File cards look like the editor:**
- `editor.renderFile { path, maxLines?, iconOnly? }` returns a file's first lines colored by the
  editor's engine, and its icon from the active file icon theme, as self-contained markup.
- **Colors:** turned into inline `color` styles from `getComputedStyle`, and every text node is
  escaped there.
- **Icons:**
  - A sprite `<use>` is replaced by the symbol's drawing.
  - Theme images are inlined as data (sniffed SVG or PNG, or drawn at 32 px when the asset can't
    be fetched).
  - Scripts, event attributes and outside links are stripped.
- Extensions with `fs.read` may call it for files inside the folder.
- The canvas refetches previews when the theme changes.

**APIs:**
- `ide.workspace.fs.writeBase64` (`fs.write`, 16 MB), for pasted images and PNG exports.
- `canvas.addFiles` and `canvas.export`.
- Canvas settings: `canvas.snapToObjects`.

**Review fixes** (15 findings):
- **`editor.renderFile`:**
  - It caps each line (400 characters) and the total (24 KB) before coloring. A minified file's
    one huge line used to stall the IDE.
  - The engine's HTML is parsed inert and rebuilt from text and token classes only.
  - Font-glyph icon themes are drawn to an image.
  - A code card asks once, not twice.
- **Gestures:**
  - Shift-drag on a selected card moves it; Shift-click without a drag deselects.
  - Alt-drag copies on the first movement, not on a bare Alt-click. It copies a group's cards and
    the arrows among them, and moves only the copies.
  - A small wobble on an arrow's end no longer deletes the arrow.
  - Snapping is per axis: aligned on one axis, on the grid on the other.
  - Align and arrange carry a group's cards along with it.
- **Menus:** → opens only submenus (it used to run the focused item).
- **Groups:** a background image shows as soon as it arrives.
- **Read-only lock:** it stops edits, not saves; typing is saved before it locks.
- **`canvas.export`:**
  - It waits for the page to have loaded its file.
  - A late page no longer exports by surprise.
  - Errors return to the caller.
  - If the canvas is open twice, only one picture is kept.
  - It never swaps PNG for SVG.
  - An over-large PNG is reported as an error.
- **Saving files from the page:** exports and pasted images are written only beside an open
  `.canvas`. Free-name searches throw instead of overwriting.
- **Convert to file:**
  - `\` means a folder, as `/` does.
  - Names are relative to the canvas.
  - Windows' reserved names are refused.

**Sizes:** the page is split by responsibility:
- `viewer.js`: state, rendering, gestures. Still over 1200 lines, for the reason in D183.
- `menus.js`: menus, find, help.
- `geometry.js`: snapping, align, distribute, arrange and resize maths. Unit-tested in
  `src/core/canvas/canvas.test.ts`.
- `export.js` and `markdown.js`.

### D185 — Extensions from git repositories; authors; New tab lists every page; pages stacked one by one (m6.86)

**Context:** official extensions will live in a git repository, and people will want to install
one straight from GitHub. Extensions had one `author` string. New tab listed only some pages.
During a group drag the whole iframe layer was raised above the drag overlays, so a canvas page
covered the drop preview.

**Decision:**
- **From a repository:** `extensions.installFromRepo {repo, ref?, path?}`.
  - Rust `ext_download_git` runs `git clone --depth 1 [--branch ref] -- <url>` into
    `<data>/extensions/.downloads/<stamp>`, removes `.git` and lists the extension folders (an
    extension.json, or a VS Code package.json; three levels deep).
  - Refused before git sees them: input starting with `-`, `::` transports (`ext::` runs commands),
    refs outside `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`.
  - One extension installs directly; several give a picker (a catalog repository).
  - The registry's `sources` remembers repo, ref and path: the page says "From owner/name", its ⋯
    menu has Update from repository (`extensions.updateFromRepo`). Installing from a folder forgets it.
  - The download is always discarded; ones a crash leaves are cleared after a day.
  - `owner/name` means GitHub over https; `./path` is relative to the open folder.
- **Official repository:** product.json `extensionsRepo` (empty for now), overridable with the
  `extensions.officialRepo` setting to try one. `extensions.browseOfficial` is the same picker
  over it. With none, it says so.
- **Authors:** manifest `authors: [{name, github?, url?, avatar?: "brand:<id>"}]`, else npm's
  `author` / `contributors`. Shown as overlapping pictures with "A and B" in the page header, a list
  with profile links in the side panel, and the names in the Extensions list.
  - Pictures: a GitHub user's (Rust `ext_github_avatar`, 64 px, cached a week, old copy used
    offline), a brand mark the IDE ships, else initials on a label color. Nothing else is loaded.
  - `extensions.create` writes `authors`: the agent (from its model: Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, or
    the ACP program) when an agent makes it, plus the user when signed in to GitHub (`gh`).
  - The bundled extensions are by Claude and Tezumie.
- **New tab** lists every page that opens in a tab: also AI models, Documentation and Debug console
  (entries whose view isn't registered are left out), then extensions' tools; searchable above 10.
  View → Tools has the same pages.
- **Iframe stacking:** the layer has no z-index of its own (absolute, no stacking context); each
  page frame is `z-index: var(--z-sticky)` and a lifted group's frames are above the drag layer.
  So drop previews, menus and the lifted group are above every other page, for any future page
  that uses the layer. The drop preview and the lifted group's old slot are rounded and outlined.
- Smaller: the extension page is one width on every tab (and keeps the scrollbar's room); Agent
  settings button on the AI models page; menu icons for Profiles, Tasks, Layout density, Open
  running server and the logo for Welcome; the setup card's brand row has no tooltip.

### D186 — The explorer follows any tab that shows a file; the drag preview keeps round corners (m6.87)

**Context:** the explorer's auto-reveal only knew editor tabs, and skipped a file it had revealed
last. With a canvas open it kept app.ts selected; back on app.ts after the selection moved, it
didn't select it again. The dragged group's corners were drawn before its scale, so a group
shrunk to a third had 3 px corners, and its editor and page weren't clipped to them.

**Decision:**
- Auto-reveal uses the tab view's `resource` (the file it shows: editors, extension viewers such as
  the canvas, previews, diffs, a browser on a local file) and runs on every change of active tab
  or focused group. A tab without a file (agent, terminal) is remembered as "nothing", so coming
  back to a file tab selects its file again. Files outside the open folder aren't revealed.
- The lifted group sets `--lift-scale`; its radius is `--radius-md / scale`, it clips its content,
  and its pages' bottom corners are clipped the same way.

### D187 — Pages render Markdown like the preview; web pages in canvas cards; dragging out of cards (m6.88)

**Context:** the canvas drew notes with its own small Markdown renderer, so they didn't look like
the user's preview; zoomed out, card text was hidden; a note scrolled only once selected; file
code didn't look like Markdown code blocks; Obsidian shows web pages in link cards and lets you
drag links and headings out of notes.

**Decision:**
- `editor.renderMarkdown {text | path, base?, css?}` (palette false, `read`): the preview's
  renderer, returning self-contained HTML — code colored with inline styles (as renderFile),
  the open folder's *pictures* inlined as data: URLs (other files never), the original path in
  `data-src`; scripts, handlers, javascript: URLs and the IDE-only copy buttons removed — and the
  preview's CSS: every IDE rule naming a `.md…` class, with each `var(--token)` it uses resolved
  for the current theme on `.ide-md`. Any extension page can read like the preview this way.
- The canvas: note file cards use it (the worker narrows to the heading, checks the file is on the
  canvas); text cards keep the page's own renderer (fast, tickable tasks) but emit the IDE's
  markup (`md-pre`, `md-code`, `md-table-wrap`) and sit in `.md-document`, so both look the same.
  The CSS is asked for at load and on theme changes.
- **Permission `web.embed`:** an extension's pages are served with `frame-src https:` instead of
  `'none'`. The canvas asks for it: link cards show the page (YouTube/Vimeo as players) in a
  sandboxed frame (scripts, same-origin, forms; no popups, no top navigation), usable once the
  card is selected. Sites that refuse framing show their refusal; the card's menu has Show as a
  link (`embed: false` on the node) and `canvas.embedPages` turns it off.
- **Dragging out:** in a selected card, links, images and (in notes) headings are draggable; a drop
  on the board makes a link card, a file card, or the note narrowed to that heading. Dragged text
  becomes a text card. Files from the computer are still not taken (the IDE's own drop handling).
- Zoomed out, text stays (only below 16% do cards keep just their first line); cards scroll
  whenever they overflow (wheel and scrollbar, selected or not); file code looks like a Markdown
  code block; the settings button is a gear. Canvas 1.3.0.
- Tabs follow a renamed or moved file whatever shows it (`workbench/followRenames.ts`): a viewer
  tab (an image, a preview, the canvas) is reopened on the new path in its place. Moving a canvas
  out of the canvas folder used to leave its tab on the old path, and opening it made a second.

### D188 — Jupyter notebooks you edit and run (m6.89)

**Context:** .ipynb files opened read-only. VS Code's notebooks are the bar: edit cells, run them on
a Jupyter kernel, rich outputs, keyboard model, kernel picker, variables.

**Decision:**
- **Editor** (`src/extensions/editor/notebook`, the `notebook` dock view, replacing the read-only
  viewer):
  - Code cells in embedded engine editors. The engine gained `createEditor(container,
    {embedded})`: no minimap, margin or scrollbars, and as tall as its text (`contentHeight`).
    Editors are created as cells near the screen.
  - Markdown cells render until edited. Raw cells.
  - Jupyter's keys: command and edit modes, Shift / Ctrl / Alt+Enter, A, B, D D, M, Y, R, Z, O,
    I I, 0 0, C / X / V, arrows across cells, Ctrl+Shift+- to split.
  - Undo for cell operations, a variables panel, an inline input() box.
  - A banner when the file changes on disk while edited; save asks on close and on window close.
- **Format:** nbformat 4 round-trips. Unknown fields are kept, keys sorted, one-space indents and
  text as lists of lines, like Jupyter's writer, so unchanged notebooks diff cleanly. Cell ids are
  repaired and the minor version raised to 4.5.
- **Running:** one host process per notebook (`src-tauri/notebook/kernel_host.py`, written to the
  data folder by `notebook_host_path`), over the stdio host as ndjson. It runs either:
  - **Jupyter:** a real kernel through `jupyter_client`, so any kernelspec works (ipykernel, R,
    Julia…), with streams, display updates, input and interrupt;
  - **Plain Python (better than VS Code, which needs ipykernel):** with no packages, cells run in
    one namespace. It keeps the last expression's value, display(), rich reprs, matplotlib figures
    as images, input(), `!cmd`, `%pip`, `%cd`, `%time`; interrupt through `interrupt_main`;
    restart is a new process.
- **Kernels:**
  - Every Python found is probed with `--list`: `notebook.pythonPath`, the folder's `.venv`,
    `venv`, `env`, `debug.pythonPath`, PATH (`py -3` on Windows).
  - Default choice: the kernelspec the notebook names, else the language's, else plain Python.
  - The choice is remembered per notebook in the workspace state.
  - Running asks for workspace trust once.
- **Outputs:**
  - Streams and errors keep their ANSI colors (terminal palette tokens) and carriage-return
    progress bars.
  - PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG (as an image); Markdown; LaTeX (KaTeX); JSON; text.
  - HTML goes through the Markdown renderer's allowlist, so pandas tables render. Script-driven
    HTML and ipywidgets say so and show their fallback.
  - Long outputs scroll (`notebook.output.scrolling`).
- **Kernel help in cells:** completions and hovers from the kernel through a built-in language
  feature on the cells' `notebook-cell` documents.
- **Commands for everything, agents included:** `notebook.read`, `editCell`, `insertCell`,
  `deleteCell`, `runCell` (returns the output text), `runAll` (returns the failing cell),
  `variables`, `restart`… They open the notebook when given a path. `ide://notebook` gives the
  active notebook. Also File → New Jupyter notebook, Ctrl+S (`activeNotebook`), and Export as
  script (`# %%` cells).
- **Not yet:** ipywidgets and script-driven outputs (plotly, bokeh) need a sandboxed output page;
  notebook-wide find and replace; notebook diffs.
- **After the audit (22 findings, all fixed):**
  - Kernel host:
    - A dead Jupyter kernel answers runs at once and restarts on the next run.
    - Restart holds every socket's lock.
    - Interrupts only land in user code, and a cell's end is always reported.
    - Real SIGINT on POSIX, so blocking calls stop (Windows: the flag only).
    - Kernels' and child programs' stdio never touch the protocol pipes; fd-level output (os.system)
      shows in the cell.
    - Magics inside multi-line strings are left alone.
    - NaN is sent as text, and notebooks containing NaN open.
    - Shutdown waits for the host to exit, so R and Julia kernels stop too.
  - IDE:
    - Each start is its own process id, and a host that dies before hello fails at once.
    - Finding kernels asks for trust first.
    - Undo restores cells without reverting typing (an agent's text edit comes back) and keeps
      live cell views, so running cells keep streaming.
    - A renamed notebook keeps its view, edits and kernel (`renamed`; follow-renames never reopens
      dirty views).
    - Kernel completions and hovers work in cells (features declare `schemes`).
    - Agents' commands don't take the focus.
    - Export and New don't overwrite files.
    - Outputs redraw incrementally and long text shows its last 200 000 characters.
    - Kernels stop only once the folder really closes.
    - Escape and the arrows go to the editor's popups first.
    - Paths are normalized.
    - A failed notebook refuses edits.
    - Picture URLs are revoked.
