    - `editor.renderMarkdown` reads Markdown files only.

### D189 — Jonna, its workspace folders, and m6.90 (notebook outputs, extension updates, UI fixes)

**Context:** The product is named Jonna. Projects may already have a `.vscode` (VS Code) or a
`.codevre` (the IDE's earlier name) folder; the IDE used whichever it found first and wrote there,
so it sometimes created `.vscode`. A list of issues from daily use came with it.

**Decision:**
- **Name:** product.json is Jonna (window, account, the agent's prompt read it from there); the
  bundle identifier stays, so installs keep their data.
- **Workspace folders** (`workbench/workspaceFolder.ts`):
  - The IDE writes only to `.jonna`, created on first save; `.vscode` and `.codevre` are read
    when the project has them, never created. Precedence `.jonna` > `.vscode` > `.codevre`:
    settings are layered that way (the lower folders are one layer under `.jonna`'s), tasks and
    launch configurations by label/name, memory, commands, snippets, extensions and canvases are
    listed from all of them, the higher one winning a name.
  - The explorer marks a lower folder that something in a higher one overrides (a "!" with what,
    the overridden files dimmed), and offers "Merge into .jonna…" (`workspace.mergeFolder`):
    files only it has are copied, settings / tasks / launch configurations / memory notes only it
    has are added, `.jonna`'s are kept; it can then go to the trash (default for `.codevre`, not
    for `.vscode`, which VS Code still reads).
- **Extensions:** a development copy with an installed extension's id replaces it while loaded
  ("Replaces 1.3.0"); `extensions.copyForDevelopment` makes one (or a fork with its own id).
  Installing it permanently asks: replace the installed one (a version that isn't newer is
  pointed out; a bundled one becomes "customized" — the IDE's updates skip it, and "Use the IDE's
  version" goes back; a repository link is dropped, as updating would undo the changes) or install
  beside it under a new id. Extension webview proxies survive closing the folder (the canvas said
  "127.0.0.1 refused to connect" after a folder switch: its cached origin had been stopped).
- **Notebooks:**
  - Outputs that run code (HTML with scripts, JavaScript, Plotly, Bokeh, ipywidgets) run in a
    sandboxed frame: a page of the IDE's on a local origin of its own (`notebook_output_origin`),
    sandboxed without same-origin. It talks to the notebook by messages only.
  - Widgets are live: the kernel host passes comm messages both ways, a `WidgetStore` keeps each
    widget's state so every frame can be given it, Output widgets capture outputs as Jupyter Lab
    does, and the state is saved in the notebook's metadata (shown, not live, when reopened).
    Libraries come from `notebook.output.cdn` (jsDelivr; a mirror where it's blocked); Bokeh's
    INLINE resources work offline. Bokeh's element and script outputs share a frame.
  - Diffs of .ipynb (source control, history, the agent's proposals, compare) show cells: paired by
    id, else by text, with line changes, changed outputs and metadata; "Show JSON" switches.
  - "New Jupyter notebook" left the File menu (New file… makes one); the clear buttons use the
    circle-slash icon everywhere and the eraser is gone from the icon set; the output buttons sit
    side by side (they overlapped the next cell's run button).
- **Views of deleted files close** (`registerCloseDeleted`): every view that names its file, an
  extension's too, when the file is deleted through the IDE or by anything else (checked while
  the window is used). The text editor keeps its "deleted" banner; diffs stay; unsaved views stay.
- **UI:** menus use the window's height before scrolling (searchable lists stay capped); author
  pictures stack properly; every scrollbar is 10px by default and extension webviews get the IDE's
  (Chromium's native overlay bars grew on hover); a setting changed back to what it inherits is
  removed from settings.json; the lifted group has a border and the larger radius; the bottom panel
  opens at a quarter of the height and the test output opens there; above the dock and over a top
  tab strip a dragged tab reorders (only the dock's top 4px splits the whole dock); off-screen
  setting rows skip layout (resizing lagged with the settings open); `editor.scrollBeyondLastLine`
  is on by default.
- **Agent:** a message sent while the agent works is never refused: the IDE's own agent reads it at
  its next step; when the turn can't take it (an external agent, a summary) it's held and sent as
  the next message when that ends.

### D190 — m6.91: files from outside, drops of many files, remembered positions, extension pictures
- **Files from outside the open folder** open like in VS Code: when the user opens one (a path
  typed, clicked or dropped; test callers too), Rust adds that one file to the workspace scope
  (`workspace_allow_file`); agents and extensions stay inside the folder. Restored tabs ask again,
  only for files the user opened (`editor.outsideFiles` in the workspace state: a tab an agent
  opened through `layout.openView` never widens the scope). Opening or closing a folder forgets
  them; network and relative paths are never let in (D161).
  Quick open lists the project's recent files first, then the outside ones.
- **Several explorer rows dragged onto the dock** (the selection, when the dragged row is in it)
  open together in the group they're dropped on (`editor.openPaths`); a **folder** opens as a
  folder browser tab (`folder` view type): an "up a level" row inside the open folder, folders
  first; a folder goes in, a file opens in that group and the browser closes.
- **Positions are remembered.** A text file opened again — after its tab closed, or after a
  restart — comes back to its scroll position and cursor (per workspace, the 500 most recent
  files; an explicit line wins). Every other view keeps its scroll offsets too
  (`workbench/scrollMemory.ts`): put back when its tab moves to another group or window (Chromium
  drops them when an element is re-parented), and after it's closed and opened again or the app
  restarts (by view type and state, 150 views per workspace). Monaco, terminals and iframes scroll
  themselves and are skipped. Saves wait 2 s after scrolling stops.
- **Extension pictures.** `icon` may be any image file of the extension (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP,
  SVG) or an icon name; `screenshots` (at most 12, files of the extension, optional captions) are
  shown above the README. Development copies change them from their menu or page
  (`extensions.setIcon`, `extensions.addScreenshot` — a picture of the IDE as it is, or a file —
  and `extensions.removeScreenshot`); installed ones say to copy for development first.
- **Paste in the explorer:** text or a picture copied elsewhere since the explorer's own Copy
  becomes a new file named inline (image.png, pasted.md/json/svg/txt, the name part selected). The
  explorer's Copy also puts the paths on the system clipboard, and that's how Paste tells the two
  apart. (The canvas already pasted pictures and text.)
- **Smaller fixes:** link hovers in chat and Markdown show where a link goes; Ctrl+click on a link
  in an editor hover opens it in the browser and its copy button copies the link; cut/copy/paste
  and Select all in the Markdown preview and chat (paste goes to the prompt); a side panel's header
  has a VS Code-like context menu (its actions, Hide, Move side bar), extension views included; a
  missing or outdated ACP agent shows an install card (and Windows' own Copilot app, a Store
  alias named `copilot`, no longer counts as the GitHub Copilot CLI); the terminal's sticky command line falls
  back to the command's text; one color theme picker ("Color theme…"); text on accent buttons
  picks black or white for contrast when an imported theme's doesn't; the active tab's bold label
  no longer changes its width; Open to the side works the same for images; consistent gaps in the
  search, source control, testing and debug forms; Mermaid diagrams zoom and pan; a file viewer
  (the canvas) follows changes to its file made outside it; deleting a folder whose files are
  watched releases the watches first (Windows: "in use"); Find's widget has its corners rounded;
  Replace / Replace all use the IDE's icons.
- **Voice input** only picks a speech-to-text service whose API key is set (an OpenAI entry
  without one was used before), and says that Win+H works without any setup.

### D191 — m6.92: what an agent wants (wishlist 1–19), UI fixes
- **Tool results read better.**
  - Strings come back as text. Documents keep their beginning and say which `offset` to read on
    from (`call_command`, `get_state`); logs keep their end.
  - Unknown commands and state paths get "did you mean".
  - Errors are `Error [code]: message` plus a hint (`core/agent/toolText.ts`).
  - `find_commands` is ranked (the namespace, then the id, the title, the description) and gives
    one line per command: id, effects, whether it asks now, first sentence. `{}` lists the
    namespaces, `{ namespace }` lists one, `{ ids }` gives the full schemas.
  - State paths take a query (`ide://x?a=1`).
- **Building extensions.**
  - `extensions.guide` is a table of contents; `{ section }` returns one part, and `"api"` the
    types. `part` still works.
  - `extensions.validate` checks the JSON, the loader's errors, unknown fields and the files the
    manifest names.
  - `extensions.manifestSchema`: the editor validates and completes extension.json in any
    extensions folder with it.
  - `extensions.try` runs one of the extension's commands and returns the result and the log
    lines it wrote.
  - `extensions.examples` has six small complete extensions, and a unit test checks that each one
    loads.
  - `ide://extensions` is brief (one line each) past 8 extensions; `?id=` or `?brief=0` give the
    full form.
- **Seeing and polling.**
  - `screenshot` and `workbench.screenshot` take `view` (a tab, a view type, a side bar view) or
    `selector`, for a smaller image.
  - `ide://events?since=n` is a numbered change feed: files, documents, tabs, the user's
    commands; the last 500 are kept.
- **Memory across projects.** A user-level memory in the user config folder (`<config>/memory`,
  `.md` only, let into the file scope like snippets). `remember { scope: "user" }` writes there
  after the user says yes to that note, even with full access, because one folder's prompt
  injection mustn't follow them into every project;
  the prompt shows its index in every project; `recall` searches both, and with no input lists
  the topics.
- **Small models.**
  - `agent.smallModelProfile` ("auto": a context under 8k tokens, e.g. a 4k local model; the mock test model's 8k keeps the full set) gives a short prompt with the
    commands to try first, and drops explore, rich cards and the browser tools (the screenshot
    stays).
  - `ide://agent/usage` reports tokens per session and in all (cache reads and writes, the
    context used), plus the cost from `agent.prices`.
  - Item 20, parallel helpers in worktrees, is planned (feature-gaps "Next", B6).
- **UI fixes.**
  - Scrollbars no longer grow under the pointer: the hover rules set `background`, which reset
    `background-clip` and filled the thumb's transparent border. They use `background-color`
    now, extension pages too.
  - The editor's and the terminal's scrollbars are 12px again.
  - A setting set back to what it inherits is reset through `settings.reset`; D189's
    `settings.set` without a value failed with "value: required", so it stayed modified.
  - Text on the accent is checked on the colors as the browser resolved them, for any theme
    format and colorCustomizations, and switched to black or white below 3:1.
  - A compact folder row names each folder in its own span: right-clicking one acts on that
    folder, and Rename edits its name in place (`explorer.compactFolders` turns compact rows
    off).
  - The Git menu groups Branch, Stash, History and GitHub in submenus.
  - A dragged group is rounded with a visible edge: the flush style's `border-radius: 0` outranked
    the lifted rule, and the edge is now a layer above the contents.
  - Panning a Mermaid diagram no longer selects its text.

### D192 — m6.93: the terminal buttoned up, agent sign-in, updates and signing, WSL
- **The terminal says it is this IDE, not the editor that started it.**
  - Started from a VS Code terminal (`npm run dev`), the app inherited `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`,
    `VSCODE_*` and Claude Code's own variables. Claude Code in our terminal then believed it ran
    inside VS Code ("Welcome to Claude Code for VS Code"), tried that window's extension and
    asked to log in again.
  - `forget_parent_editor()` (lib.rs, called from main) drops these when inherited:
    - `VSCODE_*`, `TERM_PROGRAM*`, `CURSOR_*`, `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`, `CLAUDECODE`,
      `CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `ENABLE_IDE_INTEGRATION`
    - `WT_SESSION`, `WT_PROFILE_ID`, `TERMINAL_EMULATOR`, `COLORTERM`
    - the editor's `GIT_ASKPASS`, and a `NODE_OPTIONS` that loads its debugger bootloader
  - Our terminals set `TERM_PROGRAM` to product.json's short name and `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`.
- **Resizes don't smear full-screen programs.** The shell starts after its panel has a size
  (no 80×24 first frame), and resizes are debounced while a program runs. The pty applies them
  on a latest-wins thread, so a burst becomes one. Ink programs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) used
  to repaint their banner once per resize step.
- **Robustness:**
  - Shell-integration marks carry a per-terminal nonce (`IDE_SHELL_NONCE`, unset by the
    scripts), so output that prints `ESC]633;E` can't fake a command line. Every terminal has
    one, so a terminal without the scripts (cmd.exe, WSL) accepts no command lines at all.
  - Killing a terminal on Windows kills its whole tree (`taskkill /T /F`), so a dev server
    started from it doesn't survive.
  - Flow control has patience: a missed ack can't stall output for good. After 5 s the count
    resets.
  - A pty started for a terminal whose creation then failed is killed.
- **Keys for the program, not the IDE.**
  - While a program runs (or the alternate screen is on), Ctrl+letter, Ctrl+\ [ ] ; / go to the
    terminal instead of IDE shortcuts, so nano, vim and Claude Code get Ctrl+R, Ctrl+G and so on.
  - `terminal.sendKeybindingsToShell` does it always. Ctrl+P stays with the IDE (quick open).
  - A terminal without shell integration counts as running a program, as there are no marks
    to tell.
  - Shift+Enter sends ESC CR (a newline in Claude Code and other TUIs).
- **Links:**
  - OSC 8 hyperlinks open with Ctrl+click.
  - A URL wrapped over several rows is one link.
- **Sticky command line:** hidden in the alternate screen and while the running command's output
  is still at the bottom. Its layout is measured only when it changes.
- **ConPTY:** bundling a newer conpty.dll and OpenConsole.exe (as VS Code and Windows Terminal do,
  for Windows 10's older ConPTY) is deferred. It can't be tested from here, and Windows 11's
  ConPTY handles these programs.
- **Agent CLIs:**
  - The Claude Code adapter moved to `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` (Zed's
    `@zed-industries/claude-code-acp` is deprecated, and its old SDK didn't see current logins:
    "Authentication required").
  - Codex moved to `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`; Gemini is `gemini --acp`.
- **Agent setup feels like VS Code's and Zed's:**
  - Detection re-runs when the AI models page opens, when the window regains focus (if something
    was missing) and after an install, so "Install" turns into "Use" without a restart.
  - On Windows, detection reads the PATH from the registry too, so a CLI installed while the IDE
    runs is found.
  - "Authentication required" (and "not logged in", "/login") shows a "Sign in to <agent>" card:
    Sign in runs the CLI's login in a terminal (`agent.signInAgent`), then Retry.
- **Updates (`src-tauri/src/update`, `workbench/updates.ts`):**
  - The release workflow gives the update signing key to the build step only, not to `npm ci`.
  - tauri-plugin-updater, registered only when the build has a public key (product.json
    `updates` or `IDE_UPDATE_*` at build time), so source builds never connect.
  - `update.check` and Help → Check for updates…; `update.mode` is default / manual / none.
  - Install confirms unsaved files like closing does, verifies the signature and restarts.
- **Signed installers:** `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds Windows, macOS and Linux on a tag
  and drafts a release with `latest.json`. With Azure Artifact Signing secrets, Tauri signs every
  binary through `bundle.windows.signCommand` (set by gen.mjs). docs/releasing.md has the setup
  and why Artifact Signing rather than EV (EV no longer skips SmartScreen).
- **WSL folders (`src-tauri/src/wsl.rs`):**
  - File → Open WSL folder… picks a distribution and starts the folder dialog at its home.
  - Files go through `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\…`.
  - Terminals, tasks, the agent's commands and git run inside the distribution
    (`wsl.exe -d <distro> --cd <linux path> --exec …`: `--exec`, not `--`, so arguments aren't
    read by the user's shell a second time); git's Linux paths are mapped back.
  - Variables the IDE sets (git's `GIT_EDITOR`, `TERM`, a task's `env`) are listed in `WSLENV`,
    the only way they reach Linux. git's password prompt doesn't cross (it is a Windows
    program): in WSL, git uses the distribution's credential setup.
  - Watching polls there (every 2 s), since change notifications don't cross 9P.
  - The browser preview works unchanged: WSL 2 forwards localhost.
  - A status bar item shows "WSL: <distro>".
  - Not yet: language servers and debuggers run on Windows against the UNC path.
- **SSH folders and dev containers: designed, not built.**
  - Both need the backend's fs, pty, exec, git and watch services behind one transport.
  - The plan:
    1. A small `ide-server` binary (the same Rust services, no UI), copied over SSH to
       `~/.ide-server/<version>` and started there.
    2. Requests travel over the SSH channel as the same JSON the IPC uses.
    3. Paths become `ssh://host/path` in the frontend, and the services route them as `wsl.rs`
       routes WSL paths.
    4. Dev containers reuse it: `devcontainer up` (or `docker exec`) instead of SSH.
    5. Ports are forwarded for the browser preview.
  - WSL came first because Windows already shares its files, so only program launching needed
    routing.
- **Small gaps closed:**
  - Pinned folders in the recent list (`workspace.pinRecent`, a pin button on the welcome page,
    first in File → Open recent).
  - `search.seedWithNearestWord`.
  - Centered layout (`layout.toggleCenteredLayout`, `workbench.editor.centeredLayout`).
  - Auto-closed tags (`editor.autoClosingTags`: typing the `>` of `<div …>` inserts `</div>` in
    HTML, XML, JSX/TSX, Vue, Svelte and Astro; not for void elements, `/>` or TypeScript
    generics).
  - Sticky headings in the Markdown preview.
- **Process:** a full audit and the full UI suite run every two or three versions and before
  each release (docs/releasing.md). In between, each version's own changes get a targeted
  test script (m6-93.jsonc) and a review of the diff.

### D193 — m6.94: moving from VS Code, MCP to the current standard, parallel agents, reviews
- **Small UI fixes.**
  - The "Where should this project live?" card lines its fields up (Name; Location as a
    read-only field with a folder button), shows the folder it will create, and puts the main
    button on the right with the other choices quieter on the left.
  - The Graph header in Source control keeps the branch filter, Pull and Push. Fetch, Go to the
    current commit, Show commit and Refresh moved to a "…" menu, so the title keeps its room.
- **External agents' own models.**
  - Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot report their models over ACP. The newer session
    config options (`configOptions`, category model / thought_level, changed with
    `session/set_config_option`) are used, and the older `models` + `session/set_model` when
    that's all there is.
  - The agent starts when it's picked in the model menu, so its models are listed before the
    first message. They appear at the top of the menu, with Reasoning as a submenu. The pill
    reads "Claude Code · Sonnet 4.5".
  - The choice is remembered per agent (`agent.externalAgentChoices`) and applied on its next
    start. `agent.setAgentModel` sets it from the palette or a script.
  - It is still one chat, not a separate Claude panel.
- **Import from VS Code** (Preferences, the welcome page, a one-time notification when VS Code is
  found).
  - The page covers VS Code, Insiders, Cursor, VSCodium and Windsurf, or a chosen User folder.
    It has a row per part with counts and details:
    - **Settings:** the theme included; the user's own values are kept unless "use theirs".
    - **Keyboard shortcuts:** VS Code command ids mapped to ours, `editor.action.*` run through
      Monaco, `when` contexts renamed, and the ones that can't apply listed.
    - **Snippets.**
    - **MCP servers:** into the user's `mcp.json`, inputs kept.
    - **Extensions:** what each becomes here (built in, a setting that Import turns on, or not
      available yet).
  - Nothing changes until Import. `settings.importFromEditor` does the same (with `dryRun`).
- **MCP to the current standard** (`core/mcp/config.ts`, `agent/mcp.ts`).
  - **Where servers come from:**
    - `agent.mcpServers` and the user's `mcp.json`
    - the folder's `.vscode/mcp.json`, `<IDE folder>/mcp.json` and `.mcp.json`: trusted folders
      only, and each server is approved once in the chat ("always for this folder")
    - with `agent.mcp.discovery`, Claude Desktop's, Claude Code's (`~/.claude.json`), Cursor's
      and VS Code's user configs
    - extensions
  - **Variables:** `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}`, `${env:NAME}`, `envFile`.
  - **`${input:id}`:** asked once. A password input goes to Rust's secret store and is put into
    the process's arguments, environment or headers there (`${secret:mcp.…}`, `mcp.` ids only),
    so neither the webview nor the agent ever holds it.
  - **Remote servers (`url`):** use the Streamable HTTP transport (Rust POSTs and reads JSON or
    SSE: `mcp/remote.rs`; https or localhost only). OAuth isn't supported yet; a 401 says to use
    a token header.
  - **`agent.addMcpServer`:** the agent can add a server to the folder's mcp.json after the user
    approves it.
    - Keys go through password inputs: a value that looks like a key is refused, so "install X
      for me" never asks the user to paste a key into the chat.
  - **Status:** `agent.mcpServers` shows the servers' status and can restart one or forget its
    inputs. `ide://agent/mcp` is the state.
- **Agents in worktrees** (`agent/worktreeAgents.ts`).
  - "New agent in a worktree…" gives a task a branch (`agent/<task words>`) and a folder next to
    the repository, and opens a window there whose chat starts on the task.
  - The task travels through the global state (`agentHandoffs`): ten-minute expiry, taken once by
    chat id.
  - "Agent worktrees" lists them with how far each is ahead, and can open, review (another
    model), merge or delete one.
  - Each worktree has its own window, chats and state. Ports aren't separated yet.
- **Reviews (`agent.reviewChanges`)** give a second opinion on any of these:
  - uncommitted changes, staged changes, the branch against its base, or a chat's pending edits
  - or a range, using a chosen model or external agent
  - A new chat in Ask mode gets the diff and reports problems, most severe first.
- **Memory:** `agent.memory.autoTidyUp` (off by default, rule 8) runs the tidy-up by itself, in the
  background, at most once a day after five sessions. It says when the result is ready to review.
  The tidy-up now looks for the user's corrections and "remember this".
- **Next-edit suggestions** (`editor.nextEdit.enabled`, off by default).
  - After a change and a pause, the suggestions model predicts the edit that follows.
  - It's shown tinted with its new text below: Tab goes there, Tab applies, Esc dismisses. It
    never edits by itself.
  - Applying one asks again, so renames ripple.
- **Fixed after an independent review of these changes:**
  - **Secrets per server:**
    - A server's `${secret:…}` reaches only its own inputs (`mcp.input.<server>::<input>`; Rust
      checks it against the process id or the POST's server).
    - Only MCP processes get `${env:}` / `${secret:}` filled in.
    - A config naming `${secret:…}` itself is refused.
    - The approval card shows env and headers, and changing them asks again.
  - **Remote servers:** no redirects (they could carry the headers elsewhere). Event streams are
    decoded whole lines at a time, a stream that ends without the answer is an error, and the
    old `/sse` transport is named as unsupported.
  - **Startup:** servers start before the turn's first step (awaited, never twice), and the ACP
    agent's start is shared by the menu, the pick and the message.
  - **Small fixes:**
    - Custom agents aren't restarted on every message.
    - Dismissed inputs aren't asked again until Restart.
    - Only the real config files trigger a restart.
    - `agent.addMcpServer` asks for anyone but the user.
  - **Files:**
    - Import and Add MCP server refuse to write into a file with a syntax error.
    - Discovery returns only Claude Code's servers from `~/.claude.json`, never the rest of it.
  - **Worktree handoffs:** read from disk before writing, and taken once per window.
  - **Next edit:** Tab is left to ghost text and snippets, and `>>>` inside code doesn't end
    the block.
  - **Review:** "uncommitted" includes new files, and "branch" compares with the default
    branch.
- **Not done this round:**
  - settings sync and accounts, the extension store
  - MCP OAuth, sampling, MCP Apps, per-server sandboxing, and renewing an expired remote session
  - diff-gutter review comments; per-worktree ports

### D194 — m6.95: follow-ups to D193
- **Import from VS Code:**
  - The startup notification is gone. It's in Help → Import from VS Code…, and on the welcome
    page as a link whose × hides it for good (`hideImportLink` in the global state).
  - The extensions list keeps each row's height (the scrolling flex column squeezed them).
- **External agents' models:**
  - The model menu has External agents → each agent → its models (and Reasoning). The agent in
    use is also at the top. Models come from what the agent reported last time (cached per agent
    in the page's storage), so they're there before it starts. Picking one selects the agent with
    that model (`agent.selectModel` `agentModel` / `agentLevel`).
  - "(recommended)" is dropped from choice names.
  - Copilot's ACP mode has no model choice: its docs say the server's settings are chosen by
    whoever launches it. Agents with `modelFlag` (Copilot: `--model`) get a Model setting built
    from the choices their `--help` lists, plus "Other model…". Changing it restarts the agent
    with the flag, and the chat is recapped to it.
- **MCP:** the "no servers" message names the IDE's own folder (`<IDE folder>/mcp.json`); `.vscode`
  and `.mcp.json` are read too.
- **Models for each feature** has Next-edit suggestions (`editor.nextEdit.model`) and Memory tidy-up
  (`agent.memory.model`).
- **Memory tidy-up:** the automatic tidy-up (`agent.memory.autoTidyUp`) is on by default. It's the
  owner's second exception to AGENTS rule 8: it's the agent's own upkeep and only proposes
  changes for review.
- **Agent panel "…" menu:** "New agent in a worktree…" and "Agent worktrees…" are always listed,
  disabled outside a git repository, so they're findable.

### D195 — m6.96: model roles, subagents and the Agents page
Researched against Claude Code (the reference): a model per role (its `opusplan`: Opus plans,
Sonnet builds), subagents defined as Markdown files with their own prompt, tools and model, and
background subagents whose results come back later. Ours had one model per chat plus the explore
helper. Now:
- **Plan and build models:** `agent.planModel` answers in Plan mode and `agent.buildModel` carries
  out a plan when Build is pressed (`nextTurnModel`). Empty means the chat's model. A role model
  doesn't replace the chat's own model.
- **Subagents** (`src/core/agent/subagents.ts`, DOM-free and tested; `src/extensions/agent/subagents.ts`):
  - Built in: explore (its own tool, as before), plan and reviewer (read-only), and general (the
    agent's tools, no delegating again).
  - Custom: Markdown files with a header (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`,
    `permissionMode: plan`, `maxTurns`), read from `<IDE folder>/agents`, `.claude/agents` and the
    user's agents folder, in that order of precedence. Claude Code's files work unchanged: its tool
    names map to ours (Read → read_file, Bash → run_command…), `model: sonnet/opus/haiku` matches
    the newest model with that name, `inherit` uses the chat's.
  - The agent uses them through the `delegate` tool (`agent.delegate`, on). Each runs in its own
    context with its own model and hands back only a report. Transient model errors are retried
    twice.
  - `background: true` runs one while the conversation goes on, with read-only tools only. Its
    report joins the running turn at its next step, or starts a turn. Stop stops them;
    `agent.stopSubagents` (also in the "…" menu while any run) does too.
  - A small model (the small-model profile) gets no delegate tool, like explore.
- **Automatic review** (`agent.autoReview`, off): after a turn that changed files, the reviewer looks
  at them in the background. A turn started by a report isn't reviewed again, so it can't loop.
  It's off by default under AGENTS rule 8 (it spends model calls on its own).
- **Agents page** (`agent.showAgentConfig`): the agent as a tree.
  - The main agent, Modes (plan and build), Subagents (switch, model, source, edit, "New
    subagent…"), External agents (the model each starts with), and AI features (switch and model).
  - Every control is a command: `agent.chooseModel {for: main | mode:plan | mode:build |
    subagent:<name> | feature:<x> | external:<agent>, model}`, `agent.setSubagent`,
    `settings.set`. `ide://agent/subagents` is the same tree as data.
  - Reached from Settings → Agent ("Configure agents"), the AI models page ("Models for each
    feature" → Configure agents…), the settings sidebar's AI group, and the agent panel's "…" menu.
- **Review changes** offers the reviewer subagent's model first.
- **Menus:** a submenu that opened to the left keeps opening its own submenus to the left while
  they fit.
- **WSL** (fix from D192): "Open WSL folder…" is registered on every platform (usable on Windows
  only) and left out of the File menu elsewhere. Before, the explorer reported that it failed to
  start on macOS and Linux.
- `docs/agent-architecture.md` maps the whole agent in diagrams.

### D196 — m6.97: the main agent and presets, browser debugging, search editors, Timeline, Vim
- **The main agent can be an external agent.** Picking one (the chat's model menu, or the Agents
  page) also makes it `agent.model`, so new chats start with it; the Agents page shows the chat in
  use (an external agent with its own model) instead of the default IDE model. Connecting a
  provider no longer replaces an external agent as the default.
- **Agent presets** (`agent.presets`, `core/agent/presets.ts`): a named snapshot of the main agent,
  plan and build models, subagents, external agents' models and each feature's model. Applying
  one writes every key it covers (absent parts go back to their defaults, so nothing from the
  previous setup stays) and switches the active chat. The Agents page shows which preset the
  setup matches; the chat's model menu lists them, for when one provider's credits run out.
  Changing the model in the chat still changes the setup (it shows as "Unsaved"); presets don't
  lock anything.
- **Debugging pages in Chrome and Edge** (`debug/browser.ts`): the user's own browser, started with
  a debugging port and a profile of its own in the IDE's folder (git-ignored), or attached on a
  port. The page is opened only after breakpoints are set. `CdpSession` gained a `page` host part
  (URL ↔ file mapping, source maps over local HTTP, console to the debug console, navigations
  don't end it). Rust: `debug_local_get` reads http:// on local addresses only (chunked bodies
  too), for dev servers' source maps. Launching through the IDE's own browser pane was left out:
  WebView2 / WKWebView / WebKitGTK don't share one protocol, and the user's Chrome is what
  VS Code's js-debug uses too.
- **Search editors** (VS Code's): results as a document in a tab, context lines, `.code-search`
  files in VS Code's format (they open in it and search again).
- **Timeline** under the Explorer: local history and git commits per file, by day.
- **Vim mode** (`editor.vimMode`, off): monaco-vim 0.4.4 (MIT, CodeMirror's Vim keymap; a 200 KB
  chunk loaded only when turned on). Nothing in the platform does modal editing, and writing a
  Vim emulation is weeks of work. Its "browser" export is a UMD bundle with a second copy of parts
  of Monaco, so the build resolves the ES module instead.
- **Chat:** the image viewer opens beside the chat it came from when there's room (Slack's way),
  so the chat stays usable; "Add to project" on attachment cards (`agent.addAttachmentToProject`).
- **Header actions** (`workbench.view.alwaysShowHeaderActions`) are on by default; VS Code's
  default is off, but the owner prefers seeing them.
- **Docs:** Athas is gone from the docs (it was never a reference); AGENTS rule 5 now says no code
  from GPL/AGPL projects; feature gaps reviewed against VS Code 1.119, Copilot's September 2026
  updates, Cursor's July 2026 releases and Zed 1.15, with a list of what testers will expect.

### D197 — m6.98: DOMPurify pinned to a fixed version
`npm audit` reported DOMPurify ≤ 3.4.16 (critical: several XSS bypasses, GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p and
others), pulled in by monaco-editor 0.57 for its Markdown hovers. `npm audit fix --force` would
downgrade Monaco to 0.56, a breaking change. Instead `package.json` `overrides` pins DOMPurify to
3.4.17 (the fixed release, same major); the Monaco advisory was only that dependency, so audit is
clean. Drop the override once Monaco ships with a fixed DOMPurify.

### D198 — m6.99: Timeline off the activity bar; the docs brought up to date
- **Timeline** is hidden from the activity bar by default (`workbench.activityBar.hidden` defaults
  to `["timeline.view"]`): it sits as a collapsed section at the bottom of the Explorer, as in
  VS Code. Right-click the activity bar to give it its own icon again.
- **The name:** the root `README.md` (the public page) now says Jonna; AGENTS rule 1 says the name
  lives only in `product.json` and stays out of code, comments and the in-app docs (which still
  say "the IDE"), so a rename is a one-line change.
- **`docs/feature-gaps.md` rewritten** from a review of every area against VS Code 1.119, Copilot's
  September 2026 updates, Cursor 2.4–3.x and Zed 1.15: what alpha testers will hit first, existing
  features below par (by area), missing features, agent ideas, a watch list, and a condensed Done.
- **This log** got milestone headings for M4–M6.x, one heading level for every decision, and an
  index; the old "proposed scope for M2" moved back to the M1.5 section it belongs to.
- Area READMEs, the guide and the agent docs were checked against the code and corrected.

## Milestone 7 — Alpha readiness (releases ide-m7.N)

The "Before the alpha" list in `docs/feature-gaps.md`: what testers coming from VS Code or Cursor
hit in their first hour.

### D199 — m7.0: language servers on demand, project-wide TypeScript, Emmet, encodings
- **Language servers on demand.** `builtin.language-servers` now has 17 servers (TypeScript, Python,
  Rust, Go, C/C++, C#, Java, PHP, Ruby, Lua, Bash, YAML, TOML, Dockerfile, Svelte, Zig, Kotlin),
  each with `install` methods (`{ tool, package, platforms? }`). Opening a file whose server is
  missing offers Install / Don't ask again; Install runs the package manager in a terminal (npm,
  pip, go, rustup, dotnet, gem, brew or winget, the first one on PATH) so the user sees what runs,
  and starts the server when it exits 0. Servers aren't bundled: they're large (jdtls about 50 MB,
  clangd 30 MB), versioned with the user's toolchain, and VS Code's extensions fetch them too.
  The status bar shows the active file's server (running, starting with its progress, "Install X",
  failed). Known limit: winget changes PATH for new processes only, so a server it installs may
  need an IDE restart (windows-pending).
- **TypeScript across the project** through typescript-language-server (tsserver), offered like the
  others. While it runs, Monaco's own TypeScript service is switched off for TS/JS
  (`setModeConfiguration` all off, diagnostics off, the TSX/JSX variant providers disposed), and
  back on when it stops: two services would double every completion and problem. Without it the
  built-in service keeps working for open files, as before.
- **Language-server protocol depth:** `workspace/applyEdit`, `workspace/executeCommand`, code
  actions with resolve (the lightbulb, auto-import), code lens with resolve, inlay hints, semantic
  tokens (full), folding and selection ranges, declaration, document links, `prepareRename`, rename
  edits that open closed files first, `didChangeWatchedFiles` from the file events, `$/progress`,
  `window/showMessageRequest` as a notification with the server's buttons. `lsp.codeActions` for
  agents and tests.
- **Emmet** through emmet-monaco-es 5.7.0 (MIT, about 224 KB, self-contained, loaded only when an
  Emmet language is first opened): HTML, Vue, Svelte, PHP, Astro, CSS, SCSS, Less, Sass, JSX, TSX.
  It uses its "standard" tokenizer because our colors come from Shiki, not Monaco's Monarch.
  `emmet.enabled` (on), `emmet.excludeLanguages`. Writing Emmet ourselves would be weeks.
- **Line endings and encodings** from the status bar: `editor.changeEol`, `editor.selectEncoding`,
  `editor.reopenWithEncoding`, `editor.saveWithEncoding`. Decoding is `TextDecoder`; saving writes
  UTF-8 (with or without BOM), UTF-16 LE / BE (with BOM) and the single-byte code pages, whose
  tables are built from `TextDecoder` itself (no table data shipped). Shift JIS, EUC-JP, GBK,
  GB 18030, Big5 and EUC-KR read only: browsers have no encoder for them and their tables are
  large. Characters an encoding can't hold stop the save with a message.
- **Explorer:** Outline is a collapsed Explorer section by default like Timeline
  (`workbench.activityBar.hidden` default `["outline.view", "timeline.view"]`), above Timeline
  (new `ViewDescriptor.sectionOrder`). With no folder open the sections could be dragged over the
  "No folder open" content: the view's main part now scrolls instead. Git's "M" is VS Code's
  yellow (`--git-modified-fg`: `#e2c08d` dark, `#895503` light; themes map
  `gitDecoration.modifiedResourceForeground`), not the diff blue.
- **Outline follows previews:** with a Markdown preview (or another viewer of a file) focused, the
  Outline shows that file's symbols, not the last text editor's.
- **Welcome:** a recent folder's pin shows on hover, like its X (a pinned one keeps it).
- **Vim:** `:wq` and `:x` wait for the save before closing the tab they were typed in.
- **Agent edits land on disk at once** (Cursor, Claude Code). In Review mode the agent's edits are
  written (after a checkpoint) and stay in the changeset for review (`PendingFile.onDisk`), so its
  commands and tests see them. Accept only clears the review (records an undo entry). Reject puts
  back what the file held before the turn, applied on top of the file as it is now with the
  three-way `rebase`: if the user changed the same lines since, reject refuses ("same lines") and
  nothing is written. A created file is deleted on reject (if unchanged since); a deleted file is
  written back. Auto-apply still means "no review". The verify step now runs in both modes.
  Proposals made with `{ staged: true }` (the memory tidy-up) keep the old way: nothing is written
  until accepted. Review diffs compare `agentBase:<session>` (the original) with the live file.
  The system prompt says edits are written at once and may be reverted.
- **Inline review** (`inlineReview.ts`), built only from services: decorations (tint, hover,
  an after-line hint), gutter marks, editor title and context menus under the context key
  `agentReviewActive`. Commands: `agent.acceptHunk`, `agent.rejectHunk` (`path` + `index` or
  `line`, default the cursor's), `agent.nextHunk`, `agent.previousHunk`, `agent.acceptFile`,
  `agent.rejectFile`, plus `agent.openReviewDiff`. Keys (when `agentReviewActive &&
  editorTextFocus`): Ctrl+Alt+Y keep, Ctrl+Alt+N undo, Alt+F5 / Shift+Alt+F5 next / previous.
  A partial keep moves that change into the review's original (no undo record of its own); a
  partial undo writes those lines back. State: `ide://agent/review`.
- **Agent ignore file**: `.aiignore` and `.cursorignore` (gitignore syntax: last match wins, `!`,
  dir-only `/`, anchored patterns) at the folder root and in the IDE's own folder, plus
  `agent.ignoreFiles` and, with `agent.ignoreDefaults` (default on), `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`,
  `*.key`, `id_rsa*` and credentials files. read_file / edit_file / write_file refuse, list_dir
  marks entries "(excluded from the agent)" and doesn't descend, find_files and search skip them,
  @-mentions refuse, and files attached in the composer are named without their content.
  **run_command is not blocked**: the shell can read anything, so the ignore file is a guard
  against accidents, not a security boundary. State: `ide://agent/ignore`. Matcher in
  `core/agent/ignore.ts` (DOM-free, tested). Hardened after the release review: matching ignores
  case and Windows' other spellings of a name (`.ENV`, `.env.`, `.env::$DATA`); the agent can't
  write `.aiignore` / `.cursorignore` (it could lift its own limits); `call_command` refuses
  commands whose `path` input is excluded (`editor.getText`, `git.fileHistory`…) and drops
  excluded files from search results; an excluded file's selection stays out of the prompt and
  `get_state`; the defaults apply at once while the rule files load.
- **Cost**: prices are `agent.prices` (wins), else the provider's listing (OpenRouter `/models`
  `pricing`, parsed in Rust to dollars per million), else a built-in list of common hosted models
  (Claude, GPT-5 / 4.1 / 4o, o3, o4-mini; longest id prefix; approximate, dated October 2026).
  Each request is priced as it's made, so a chat that switches models is summed correctly. The
  cost of a turn shows under its last answer; the chat's cost shows beside the context meter
  (and in its tooltip); `ide://agent/usage` has per-session `cost` and `budget` and the total.
  `agent.budget.perChat` (dollars, 0 = off) adds a notice at 80 % and, past 100 %, asks once
  before the next request (even with full access); "deny" stops the turn.
- **Fixes from the release review** (an independent read of the whole change):
  - Review mode: Stop while the language service checks leaves the edit a proposal, unwritten
    (D161 again); the inline review shows only the agent's lines (the agent's change replayed on
    the file as it is now), so undoing a change never undoes the user's typing; rejecting a
    deletion looks at the disk, not an open tab; what an open file's save trims or formats is
    what's recorded; reject and per-change actions wait for an agent write to the same changeset.
  - The agent refuses files open in a non-UTF-8 encoding, as it does on disk (a revert would read
    them back as UTF-8).
  - With typescript-language-server on, the built-in TS checker the agent's edit check uses is off:
    the check returns at once instead of waiting 2 s; the switch is counted per server.
  - `workspace/applyEdit` is all or nothing and refuses edits for an older document version.
  - The chat's cost is saved with it (the budget holds across restarts); built-in prices match an
    id or a dated one only (`o3-pro` isn't priced as `o3`).
  - Explorer sections move only when out of order (scroll and focus stay); a server's question
    goes away with its timeout; pip is looked for as `py` / `python3`.
  - Left as is: `session.ts` (about 2370 lines) and `commands.ts` (1525) were over the size rule
    before this release and grew a little; splitting them is its own change.

### D200 — m7.1: Explorer targeting and find, drag out, the small gaps closed
The rest of feature-gaps' small items (S and S–M), in four parts built side by side.

**Workbench, editor, language servers and git**

- **Explorer: the root is a target** (VS Code). A click on the space below the rows or on the
  root header clears the selection, Escape too; a right-click there opens the root's menu with
  nothing selected, and its New file / New folder go to the root (they used to go to the folder
  still selected). The header buttons follow the selection, as in VS Code.
- **Explorer find** (Ctrl+Alt+F, `explorer.find {query?, filter?}`, `explorer.closeFind`) and
  type-ahead (typing a name's first letters moves to it) in every tree (`ui/treeFind.ts`, tested;
  `TreeDataSource.label`). Like VS Code it searches the shown rows (expanded folders); quick open
  finds files anywhere. Highlight or filter (a toggle); Enter / ↓ next, Shift+Enter / ↑ previous.
- **Drag files out** of the explorer into other apps (Zed 1.15, VS Code): when an explorer drag
  leaves the window with the button down, the OS drag starts (`explorer.dragOut` → Rust
  `fs_start_drag`, the `drag` crate 2.1.1: MIT/Apache-2.0, CrabNebula, the Tauri team; OLE
  DoDragDrop / NSDraggingSession / GTK drag behind one call, about 1,100 lines of Rust; its
  Windows build pulls a second `windows` crate version). Starting the OS drag only at the edge keeps every drag inside
  the window ours (tabs, the tree, the chat). Files are copied by the target app.
- **Sidebar sections:** a collapsed section's top edge resizes the open section below it (VS
  Code: drag above a collapsed Outline to make Timeline taller). The settings page's category list
  has the activity bar's thin scrollbar.
- **Editor:**
  - `files.encoding` (for files that aren't valid UTF-8; a read-only legacy encoding stays
    read-only) and `files.autoGuessEncoding` (UTF-16 without a BOM, else Windows 1252). VS Code
    reads every file in `files.encoding`; we keep valid UTF-8 as UTF-8 (a stray setting can't
    turn UTF-8 text into mojibake). `ide://editors/active` has `encoding`.
  - `editor.codeActionsOnSave` (`"source.organizeImports": "explicit"`, `"source.fixAll"`, any
    `source.*` kind; "explicit" / "always" / "never" / booleans / the list form): asked of the
    document's language servers and applied before the write (awaited: Monaco's own action returns
    before its edit lands, which saved the old text).
  - Diff views: `diffEditor.renderSideBySide`, `diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace` (now on by
    default, as in VS Code), `diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.enabled`; the toggles in each diff
    toolbar's ⋯ menu (`diffEditor.toggleInline`, `.toggleWhitespace`, `.toggleCollapseUnchanged`).
  - Language configuration from extensions (`contributes.languages[].configuration`, VS Code's
    `language-configuration.json`, `languageConfiguration.ts`, tested): comments (Ctrl+/),
    brackets, auto-closing and surrounding pairs, folding markers, word pattern, indentation rules.
- **Language servers:** pull diagnostics (`textDocument/diagnostic`, after each change a server
  got), linked editing ranges (renaming a tag renames its partner, `editor.linkedEditing`),
  `workspace/didChangeConfiguration` when the IDE's settings for a server change. On Windows,
  PATH is read again from the system after an install (`app_refresh_path`), so a server winget
  installed starts without a restart.
- **Python interpreter** for Pyright (VS Code's "Select interpreter", `lsp/python.ts`, tested):
  `python.defaultInterpreterPath`, else the folder's `.venv` / `venv` / `env`, given to Pyright as
  `python.pythonPath`; a status bar item on Python files and `python.selectInterpreter`.
- **Git:** `git.autofetch` (off, as in VS Code) and `git.autofetchPeriod` (quiet; stops after a
  failed fetch until the refs move); `git.stageSelectedRanges` (stage only the selected lines,
  `core/diff` `applySelectedLines`, tested; also in the change bar's menu); `git.quickDiffBase`
  (`index` default, `head`, `mergeBase`: the change bars against where the branch left the
  default branch, what a pull request shows; Rust `git_merge_base`); `git.enableCommitSigning`
  (`-S`) and `git.alwaysSignOff` (`--signoff`); git's own `commit.gpgsign` already worked.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` is clean again (two test modules moved to
  the end of their files).

**Agent chat**

- **Restore checkpoint on a message** (Cursor's "Restore checkpoint", Claude Code's rewind).
  - Each of your messages has a Restore button (`agent.restoreToMessage { session?, item?,
    files? }`; `item` defaults to your latest message). It removes that message and everything
    after it, puts the message's text back in the box, and (unless `files: false`) puts the files
    the agent changed since back from the checkpoints (D71). Destructive: the user confirms it.
  - The restore is shared with `agent.restoreCheckpoint` (`session.restoreFiles`), and both now
    update the review: `changeset.afterRestore` drops a change put back to its original text and
    staged proposals from those turns; a file still changed by an earlier turn stays under review
    with its restored text. Before, a restore left stale entries in the review list.
  - The turn counter keeps counting after a restore (later turns' checkpoints are dropped from the
    chat), so a new turn never adds files to an old turn's snapshot (Rust keeps a file's first
    snapshot per turn).
  - Editing or retrying a message whose turn (or a later one) changed files asks first: "Undo and
    send / Keep changes / Cancel" (`askUndoFiles`). Scripts and agents pass `files: "undo" |
    "keep"` to `agent.editMessage` / `agent.retry` (default keep, as before).
  - Limits: a message sent while the agent worked (steered into the turn) shares its turn's
    checkpoint, so restoring to it also undoes what the turn did before it. Chats saved before
    turns were recorded on messages (D160) have no Restore button. Images pasted into the message
    don't come back to the box, only its text. If an edited message's send fails after "Undo", the
    files stay restored (the conversation comes back).
- **Rules: every file, attached when it applies** (Claude Code's nested CLAUDE.md, Cursor's
  auto-attached rules, Copilot's `applyTo`). `rules.ts` + `core/agent/rules.ts`.
  - All rules files are read, not only the first of AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / copilot-instructions:
    root `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`,
    `.cursorrules`, `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, subfolders'
    `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (found through the workspace index, so ignored folders such as
    node_modules are skipped; at most 60 each), and the user's own rules.
  - The user's own rules file is `<config>/AGENTS.md` (next to settings.json), in every project,
    also with no folder open; with `agent.thirdPartyConfigs`, Claude Code's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`
    too. Rust lets the frontend reach exactly these (`ipc/settings.rs`: `AGENTS.md` joins
    USER_FILES; `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and plain `.md` files directly in `~/.claude/commands` and
    `<config>/commands`, no symlinks for the commands).
  - How each applies: always (root files, `.mdc` with `alwaysApply: true`, `applyTo: "**"`, user
    files) — in a new chat's prompt, each file at most 8 000 characters and 24 000 in all, a file
    whose text repeats another (CLAUDE.md that only imports AGENTS.md, a symlink) once; for a
    folder (a subfolder's AGENTS.md) or for matching files (`.mdc` `globs`, `applyTo`) — listed in
    the prompt and attached to the result of the first read_file / edit_file / write_file of a
    file it covers, once per chat (a summary or a cut of the conversation lets it come again);
    by description (`.mdc` with only `description`) — listed for the agent to read; manual (no
    front matter) — only with @rules. A glob without a `/` matches the name in any folder.
  - Attaching to the tool result rather than the system prompt keeps the prompt cache (D112):
    the prompt stays the same all chat.
  - CLAUDE.md `@path` imports (outside code; a path with `/` or an extension, so `@someone`
    isn't one), relative to the file, `~/` the home folder, 5 levels deep, each file once; only
    files inside the folder (or the home folder for the user's file).
  - `agent.listRules` ("Rules…" in the chat's ⋯ menu; picking one opens it) and
    `ide://agent/rules` list each file with its kind, when it applies and why, and in which turn
    the active chat got it.
  - Limits: `.cursor/rules` and `.github/instructions` are read at the root only (not nested
    `.cursor/rules` folders); external (ACP) agents read their own rules; subagents (explore,
    delegate) don't get the attached rules; the rules are cached for 30 s or until a rules file
    is saved through the IDE.
- **@-mentions: @git, @commit, @branch, @chat, @rules, @symbol** (`mentions.ts` +
  `core/agent/mentions.ts`).
  - `@git`: the uncommitted changes (`git diff HEAD`, plus new files as additions, files excluded
    from the agent left out); `@commit`: pick a commit (the last 60), its message, files and diff;
    `@branch`: this branch against the default branch (origin/main, origin/master, main, master —
    as `agent.reviewChanges`); `@chat`: pick another chat (this folder's first), its transcript
    (tool calls one line each), the start and the end within 24 000 characters — not a model-made
    summary (a compacted chat's own summary is part of it); `@rules`: every rules file in full;
    `@symbol`: a function, class or type found by name in the repository map's symbols (D174,
    no language server needed), its code from its line to the next definition (at most 120
    lines). Diffs are cut at 60 000 characters.
  - The @ picker offers symbols after the files as you type (2+ characters); the + menu has Git
    (Uncommitted changes, A commit…, This branch's changes), Past chat…, Symbol…, Rules.
  - Values are kept as `@commit <hash> <subject>`, `@chat <id> <title>`, `@symbol <path>:<line>
    <name>`, so scripts and agents can pass them to `agent.mention`; without the argument they ask
    only when a person runs it.
  - Symbols come from the repository map rather than `lsp.symbols` because the map covers the
    whole project with no server running (`lsp.symbols` is per file and starts a server).
- **Slash commands** (`slashCommands.ts` + `core/agent/slash.ts`; Claude Code's format).
  - Built-ins: `/compact`, `/clear` (a new chat in this one's place; the old one stays in Chats),
    `/model [provider/model]` (without a name, the picker), `/review [focus]` (`agent.reviewChanges`
    on the uncommitted changes with this chat's model, in a new Ask chat), `/init` (the agent
    looks at the project and writes or improves AGENTS.md; in Review edits mode it's a change
    under review, in Auto-apply mode it's applied at once like any edit).
  - Command files from the project (`<IDE folder>/commands`, `.claude/commands`,
    `.cursor/commands`) then the user's (`<config>/commands`, `~/.claude/commands`), the first
    wins a name; built-ins win over files.
  - Front matter: `description` and `argument-hint` (the / picker), `model` (that message runs on
    it, like Build's model; a name the IDE doesn't know falls back to the chat's), `allowed-tools`.
  - Body: `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1`…`$9` (shell-style words, quotes group), the arguments added at the
    end when neither appears (as before); `!`command`` lines run in the folder before sending and
    their output takes their place (30 s timeout, 8 000 characters); `@path` files add their text
    (20 000 characters, files excluded from the agent are named only).
  - Shell lines are approved the way run_command is: `agent.runCommands` (auto / full), the
    allowlist and the denylist, deletion protection; `allowed-tools` `Bash(prefix:*)` /
    `Bash(exact line)` / `Bash` pre-approves (a line with `;`, `&`, `|`, `$`, backticks or
    redirects always asks). Otherwise an approval card in the chat (`session.askBeforeSend`:
    an earlier Stop doesn't answer it); "deny" sends the prompt with "(not run: the user said
    no)".
  - Limit: `allowed-tools` doesn't narrow the turn's tools (Claude Code's semantics are
    permissions); the model is told which tools the command names. Commands in subfolders
    (`/frontend:test`) are not done (MCP prompts as commands are, below).
- **Files:** session.ts (about 2500 lines) and commands.ts (about 1550) were already over the
  size rule (D199); the new parts went into their own modules (rules, slashCommands, mentions,
  checkpointCommands), and the old slash code moved out of commands.ts.

**MCP, external agents and web search**

- **MCP client to the 2025-06-18 spec** (`core/mcp/client.ts`, `elicitation.ts`, `prompts.ts`,
  tested; `agent/mcpFeatures.ts`).
  - `notifications/tools|prompts|resources/list_changed` re-list. A burst of notifications
    re-lists once more after the listing in flight, not once each. The next step of a turn has
    the new tools; `ide://agent/mcp` and **MCP servers…** show tool, prompt and resource counts.
  - **Prompts** (`prompts/list`, `prompts/get`) are slash commands named
    `/mcp__<server>__<prompt>` (Claude Code's naming; VS Code's `/mcp.server.prompt` would clash
    with the `[\w-]+` command names). Typed arguments: `name=value`, then words in order, the
    last argument taking the rest; one-argument prompts take the whole text; a missing required
    one is asked in a quick input. The messages go as the message's context. `agent.mcpPrompts`
    (hidden from agents: prompts are user-controlled per the spec).
  - **Resources** (`resources/list`, `resources/read`) are @-mentions (`@mcp <server> <uri>`,
    read when the message is sent; binary contents are named, not sent). `agent.mcpResources`
    is agent-discoverable (read effect); with `agent.mcpProtection` it asks like read-only tools.
  - **Elicitation** (`elicitation/create`; the capability is advertised): answered in quick
    inputs, not a chat card: they work while a tool call waits, outside any chat, and are
    drivable by the UI tests (`dev.type`). The server's question with **Answer…** / **Decline**;
    Esc anywhere is cancel; then one input per field (string with min/max length and the
    email / uri / date / date-time formats, number / integer with bounds, boolean, enum with
    `enumNames` or `oneOf` const/title), validated as typed. One elicitation at a time (a second
    quick input would close the first). A schema we can't show (nested, arrays) is declined with
    a notification; URL mode (2025-11-25) is declined.
  - **Remote servers:** Rust's `mcp_remote_post` now takes a Channel; the server's own requests
    and notifications inside an SSE reply go to the page as they arrive (an elicitation the
    server waits on before it answers a `tools/call` would otherwise deadlock until timeout).
    No standalone GET stream is opened, so a remote server's notifications arrive only during a
    request.
  - Not done: sampling, OAuth, roots list_changed, `resources/subscribe`, resource templates,
    starting servers just to list prompts in the "/" picker (they start with the first message).
- **External agents (ACP):**
  - `session/load` when the agent's `initialize` says `loadSession`: the agent's session id is
    saved with the chat (`acpResume`: agent, id, folder) and loaded when the agent starts again
    (after a restart, or after its process exited). The replayed `session/update`s are dropped
    (the transcript already has them), except `config_option_update`. A failed load falls back to
    `session/new`.
  - Without `loadSession` (or when the load fails), the first message after the start carries a
    recap of the chat (20 000 characters), as a retry or edit already did (D160). Before, a
    restarted external agent silently forgot the chat.
  - A retry / edit clears `acpResume` (the old session remembers dropped turns).
  - `available_commands_update` → the agent's own commands in the "/" list (with their input
    hint), only while the chat uses that agent; they're sent to the agent as typed.
- **Web search** (`core/agent/webSearch.ts`, `agent/webSearch.ts`, Rust `ai/search.rs`):
  - `web.search` (read + network effects: agents ask like `web.fetch`), the agent's `web_search`
    tool (read-only, so Ask and Plan modes have it; left out when `agent.webFetch.enabled` is
    off), `agent.setupWebSearch`, `@web search <words>` mentions (and "@web <words>" typed in the
    picker offers a search).
  - Providers: Brave Search API (`X-Subscription-Token`), Tavily (Bearer), Exa (`x-api-key`,
    highlights), SearXNG (`<url>/search?format=json`, no key; a 403 or HTML answer says to turn
    on its json format). Setting `agent.webSearch.provider` (default `off`), plus
    `agent.webSearch.searxngUrl` and `agent.webSearch.maxResults` (8, at most 20). The provider
    and address are guarded settings (agents and extensions can't change them).
  - Keys are stored where provider API keys are (the secrets file, `websearch.<provider>`), asked
    in a password box by `agent.setupWebSearch`, never an input of a command; Rust reads them for
    the request. The request goes through Rust (no CORS, no key in the webview).
  - Off: the tool answers with how to set it up (without asking for approval first); a missing
    key or address says which. Results: title, URL, snippet (400 characters), markup stripped,
    http(s) only, deduplicated, marked as untrusted text in the tool result.
  - `agent.webFetch.autoApprove` ("Fetch without asking") covers searches too; one setting for
    the agent's web access.

**Search, quick access, settings, trust, extensions, tasks**

- **Multi-line search.** A query that can match a line break (a regex with a `\n` escape that
  isn't `\\n`, or text holding a newline) searches in grep-searcher's multi-line mode with no line
  terminator on the matcher (`search::is_multi_line`). Each match is reported on the line it starts
  on, its range running to the match's end or that line's end, whichever comes first (VS Code
  shows the first line too); matches sharing lines are merged per line. `\n` outside a character
  class becomes `\r?\n` (`crlf_tolerant`), so a pattern written with `\n` also finds CRLF files, as
  in VS Code. Replace uses the same pattern (the `regex` crate already matched `\n`), so a
  multi-line replace works; its preview in the Search view still shows the line unchanged (the
  preview is per line). Single-line searches are untouched.
- **Quick access providers** (`quickOpen/providers.ts`): `%` text (a detached Rust search with
  the search settings' excludes and smart case, the first 100 lines, 200 ms debounce), `view `
  (side bar views, panels, extensions' openers), `task ` (`tasks.list` → `tasks.run`), `debug `
  (`debug.listConfigurations` → `debug.start`, the active file, "Add configuration…"), `term `
  (`ide://terminals` → `terminal.focus`, "Create new terminal"), `edt ` (open editors by group),
  `@:` (symbols grouped by kind, VS Code's group names and order, `groupByKind`). Each lists what an
  existing command or state path knows and a pick runs that command: the box adds no behaviour.
  `QuickPickItem.separator` draws VS Code's group line and name. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter opens the picked
  file (files, `@`, `#`, `%`, `edt `) to the side and closes the box; → at the end of the text
  opens it in the background and keeps the box open (VS Code's behaviour for →). New commands
  `quickOpen.openView`, `quickOpen.quickTextSearch`, `quickOpen.showEditors` (no default keys yet;
  VS Code binds Open view to Ctrl+Q, which would need checking against Quit on Linux).
- **Settings search filters** (`settings/searchQuery.ts`): `@modified`, `@id:a,b`, `@ext:<id>`
  (full id or its last part), `@tag:<tag>`, `@lang:<language>`, combinable with words. Setting
  schemas now carry `extension` (set by `toSettingSchemas`) and may declare `tags` (also in the
  manifest schema). Derived tag: `ai` for the agent's and AI features' settings. `@lang:` lists the
  language's own settings plus the editor's and says they apply to every language: there are no
  per-language values yet (feature-gaps §2 "Per-language settings").
- **Keyboard shortcuts reference** (Help menu, `keybindings.showReference`): VS Code links a PDF
  per platform; the IDE renders the same sections from its effective keybinding table (so the
  user's own keys show), plus a fixed list of Monaco's own editing keys, which aren't in the
  table (move line, multi-cursor, comment, format, F12…). Print copies the sheet into a
  page-level container that is all `@media print` shows, in the system's light colors
  (`Canvas` / `CanvasText`) whatever the theme. `keybindings.printReference` opens the print dialog.
- **Workspace trust asked when a folder opens** (`security.workspace.trust.startupPrompt`:
  `once` default, `never`; user-only). A moment after a folder the user hasn't decided about opens,
  the existing dialog shows, now with "Trust the authors of all files in the parent folder" (a
  checkbox). Trusting the parent stores the parent's key as trusted; a folder's own decision wins,
  else the nearest trusted parent (`workbench/trustModel.ts`). Same trust store
  (`globalState.trust`), same restricted mode. Dismissing (Escape) decides nothing: no second
  prompt this session, and the first task / debug / test run asks as before (one dialog at a
  time; a run started while the open-time dialog shows waits for it). Trust set another way
  (`workspace.setTrust`) or the folder closing closes the dialog (`showDialog({ signal })`). Test
  runs never get the open-time prompt (scripts set trust themselves). `ide://workspace/trust` has
  `inheritedFrom`; `workspace.setTrust` takes `parent`.
- **Install from VSIX** (`extensions.installFromVsix {file?}`, Extensions view ⋯ and right-click
  menus): Rust unpacks the file into the extensions' scratch downloads folder
  (`extensions/vsix.rs`, `ext_unpack_vsix`), the frontend installs its `extension/` folder like a
  folder (`manager.installFrom`, permissions asked) and the scratch folder goes. Our own ZIP reader
  (central directory, stored and deflated entries) with `flate2` for inflating: flate2 1.1 is
  already compiled into the app (png, the updater), so nothing new is built or shipped; the `zip`
  crate in the lock file is built without deflate and only on Windows. Refused: names that would
  leave the folder (`..`, absolute, drive letters), encrypted entries, Zip64; capped at 256 MB
  packed, 1 GB unpacked, 50 000 files; sizes and CRC-32 checked. As for any VS Code extension, only
  declarative parts work.
- **Configure default build / test task** (`tasks.configureDefaultBuild`,
  `tasks.configureDefaultTest {label?}`, Terminal menu): a picker of every task (the group's first,
  the current default marked); the picked one gets `"group": { "kind", "isDefault": true }` in the
  tasks.json it comes from, and other tasks of the group keep `"group": "<kind>"`, in every one of
  the folder's tasks.json files (so an older default elsewhere can't still win). A package.json
  script gets its own entry: `"type": "npm"` with `script`, or a shell task with the detected
  label for pnpm / yarn / bun (so the tasks.json entry replaces the detected one). Where: the
  project's tasks.json that exists, else `.vscode/tasks.json` when the folder has `.vscode` (VS
  Code's file), else the IDE's own folder (as `tasks.configure` does). Comments outside the
  `tasks` array are kept; the array itself is rewritten as JSON (comments inside it are lost: a
  known limit). The file opens afterwards for the user, as in VS Code.

**Fixes from the release review** (an independent read of the whole change):
- A project's command file (`.claude/commands`, the IDE folder's `commands`) can't approve its
  own `!` shell lines with `allowed-tools`, and in an untrusted folder every one of its lines asks;
  the denylist and delete protection come before any allow rule. Only the user's own command
  folders honour `allowed-tools`.
- Pyright's interpreter (`python.defaultInterpreterPath`, a committed `.venv`) is used only in a
  trusted folder: Pyright runs it. `python.selectInterpreter` asks for trust first.
- Stage selected lines takes a change of as many new lines as old ones line for line (it used to
  stage the unselected old lines as deleted).
- A project's CLAUDE.md can't import `~/` files (only the user's own can); Claude Code's files in
  `~/.claude` are read, never written (`resolve_write_path`).
- Code actions on save drop an edit when the text changed meanwhile or the save went ahead
  (version and deadline checks); pulled diagnostics keep the latest answer per document.
- Restore and edit-with-undo keep a turn's checkpoints when a file couldn't be put back, and an
  edit drops them only once the new message is on its way.
- @git / @branch / @commit leave out excluded files' diffs and name them.
- Windows PATH refresh reads PowerShell's output as UTF-8 and only appends new entries.
- VSIX: Windows device names and names ending in a dot or space are refused; inflating doesn't
  pre-allocate the declared size.
- Autofetch: no timer after dispose; after a failure it waits for a fetch, pull or push of your
  own (not any change in .git, which brought sign-in prompts back).
- MCP elicitation: one question per server at a time; what still waits is declined when the agent
  goes.
- A quick input prompt shows its question until you type or press Enter (an empty required field
  opened with its error instead).


### D201 — m7.2: change bars open the diff, commit messages, settings per language, file nesting, task detection, continuous runs, background commands, usage

**Change bars** (the editor's git gutter)
- The bars show a pointer and a click opens our own diff tab (`editor.openDiff {path, line}`,
  preview) scrolled to that line, rather than VS Code's inline peek. We already have a full diff
  view with staging, navigation and the toggles; a second, smaller one to keep in step would cost
  more than it gives, and the tab shows the change in context. `EngineEditor.onChangeBarClick`
  (mousedown on a quick-diff line decoration), `EngineDiffEditor.revealModifiedLine`; a diff tab
  that's already open reveals the line; a new one reveals it after its first diff computes.

**Commit messages**
- The prompt follows VS Code's (Copilot's) shape: a summary line naming the main themes (two may
  be joined with ";"), a blank line, then up to 12 past-tense bullets of concrete changes; no
  bullets that only repeat file names. The diff budget grew to 20 000 characters, shared evenly
  between files (4 000 at most, 700 at least each), and each file line carries its hunks'
  contexts (`— in: function foo, class Bar`) so the model knows where a change sits even when the
  file's diff was cut. `hunkContext` is tested.

**Welcome page**
- A recent folder's path fills the row; the pin and remove buttons appear only on hover or focus
  (a pinned folder's pin always shows) and the path truncates then.

**Chat attachment viewer**
- The viewer sits at the modal layer, so hover previews (tooltip layer) show above it; it fades
  and scales in (the motion tokens, off with reduced motion); beside the chat its backdrop is the
  new `--media-scrim-soft` (0.42); it leaves 6 px next to the chat so the dock's sash stays
  grabbable.

**Tree**
- A node that becomes a nest parent after a refresh starts expanded when the source says so
  (`becameParent`), and revealing a file inside a folded nest expands it.

**Settings per language, files.associations, file nesting**
- **Settings per language** (VS Code's `"[python]": { "editor.tabSize": 4 }`, also
  `"[javascript][typescript]": {…}`), in user, workspace and the other folder's (`.vscode`)
  settings.json. `core/settings/languageOverrides.ts` (tested) names the blocks and the languages
  they cover (`typescriptreact` / `javascriptreact` are the editor's `tsx` / `jsx`); a later block
  wins over an earlier one. Order, VS Code's: workspace block > `.vscode` block > user block > the
  plain value of the highest layer (a user block beats a plain workspace value). Invalid values in
  a block fall through (and are listed in `problems`); a user-only setting in a workspace block is
  ignored. A change inside a block is reported as a change of its own key, so everything keyed on
  `editor.*` refreshes.
- **What reads them per document:** every editor option (`editorSettings(settings, language)`:
  font, word wrap, rulers, minimap, the D128 advanced options, auto-closing tags…), tab size and
  spaces, `editor.formatOnSave`, `editor.codeActionsOnSave`, and the `files.*` that act on one
  file (`trimTrailingWhitespace`, `insertFinalNewline`, `eol` for new files, `encoding`,
  `autoGuessEncoding`). Not per language: auto save, hot exit, Vim mode (user-only), the AI
  features, diff views (`diffEditor.*` stay plain).
- **Tab size on the model, not the editor:** Monaco's `editor.updateOptions({ tabSize })` sets a
  global default for every model, so editors get the plain values and each model its language's
  through `model.detectIndentation(insertSpaces, tabSize)` — the same call Monaco makes with the
  plain ones (the file's own indentation still wins when it has one). Applied only when the plain or
  language values change, so a tab size picked in the status bar stays. Fixed on the way: showing a
  document forced `quickSuggestions` on for every non-prose file, overriding
  `editor.quickSuggestions: false`; now Markdown and plain text get it off (unless their own block
  sets it) and other files follow the setting.
- **Settings editor:** `@lang:python` now edits the `[python]` block of the scope shown (rows show
  the language's value, the dot means "set in this scope's block", reset removes it from the block;
  title "N settings found for python files"). It lists VS Code's language-overridable kind of
  settings: `editor.*` without the IDE-wide ones (file status bar, AI features, project formatters,
  Vim, import updates) plus the per-file `files.*` above — no longer the language's own settings
  (`markdown.preview.*` aren't read per language). `settings.set` / `settings.reset` take
  `language`; `SettingsService.updateForLanguage` edits one key inside the block keeping comments
  (`setJsoncNestedProperty`), making the block when needed and removing it once empty.
  `settings.json`'s schema gives blocks the same keys (completions and checks inside them).
- **Import from VS Code** keeps the blocks (their settings that apply here; the others reported as
  `[python] key`), merged into the user's block of the same name (theirs win unless "replace").
  `.vscode/settings.json` blocks are read as a layer; `.codevre`-style folders keep them too.
- **`files.associations`** (`{ "*.mdx": "markdown", "Dockerfile.*": "dockerfile" }`, VS Code's
  matching: a pattern with `/` against the path in any folder, else the file name, ignoring case; a
  name without wildcards beats a pattern, then the longer pattern) is checked first by
  `languageForPath`, so syntax colors, settings per language, language servers (they start by
  language), file icons and `resourceLangId` follow it. Changing it switches open files whose
  language came from detection (not one set with Change language mode) and announces them like a
  newly opened file, so their server starts; a model whose language changes now joins or leaves a
  running server (`monaco/lsp.ts`, also for Change language mode, which didn't before).
- **Explorer file nesting** (`explorer.fileNesting.enabled` off by default, `.expand` on,
  `.patterns` with VS Code's default list): `explorer/nesting.ts` (tested) applies a folder's
  patterns — a parent name with at most one `*` (`${capture}`), children with `*`, `${capture}`,
  `${basename}`, `${extname}`, `${dirname}` — ignoring case, one level deep (a child's children go
  under the same top file), a file named by several parents under the shortest name, files in a
  cycle left at the top. A nest parent has its own chevron before its icon; a click on the row opens
  the file and only the chevron toggles (VS Code's `expandOnlyOnTwistieClick` for nests); Enter
  opens. New in `Tree`: `TreeDataSource.opensWithChildren` and `startsExpanded`; a node that moved
  under another parent isn't forgotten by its old parent's refresh.
- **Limits:** a language block applies to settings the IDE reads per document only (the list
  above); extensions' `configurationDefaults` per language aren't read; language servers'
  `workspace/configuration` answers stay plain (no `scopeUri` language); delete, move, cut and
  copy of a collapsed nest parent act on that file only (VS Code takes the nested files along);
  git decorations of nested files don't show on a collapsed parent; the explorer's expanded ids
  (`ide://workspace` `expandedFolders`, saved state) include expanded nest parents.

**Task detection** (feature-gaps §2 "Task detection")
- Besides package.json scripts, tasks come from build files (VS Code's task providers, built in):
  `tsc: build - <tsconfig>` / `tsc: watch - <tsconfig>` per `tsconfig*.json` (`$tsc` /
  `$tsc-watch`), `make: <target>` per Makefile target (`$gcc`), `cargo: build / check / test /
  run` (`$rustc`; `run` only for a package with `src/main.rs` or `[[bin]]`), `gradle: build /
  test / run` (`run` only with the application plugin), `maven: compile / test / package`,
  `gulp: <task>` and `grunt: <task>` read from their files. Build and test groups follow VS Code
  (tsc build and watch, `make all/build`, `cargo build`, `gradle build`, `maven compile` are
  build; `make test/check`, `cargo test`, `gradle test`, `maven test` are test).
- Looked for in the root and its first-level folders (not hidden, git-ignored, node_modules,
  target, build, dist, out, vendor, venv…; at most 40). A subfolder's task is labelled
  `make: test - native` (`tsc: build - web/tsconfig.json`) and runs in that folder; its problem
  matcher reads paths from that folder (`{ base, fileLocation: ["relative" | "autoDetect",
  "${workspaceFolder}/<dir>"] }`). A Cargo / Gradle / Maven root hides its subfolders' own (the
  root builds its members). VS Code's npm detection looks through the whole tree; one level is a
  cheap middle that finds the usual `frontend/` + `backend/` layouts without walking big trees.
- The project's own programs win: `node_modules/.bin/tsc` (`.\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd` on
  Windows), the same for gulp and grunt, `./gradlew` / `.\gradlew.bat`, `./mvnw` / `.\mvnw.cmd`;
  else the program from PATH.
- Makefile targets: rule names, not assignments (`X := 1`, `X = a:b`, `?=`, `::=`), pattern rules,
  special targets (`.PHONY`), names with `$(…)`, `define` blocks or recipe lines; a name with a
