#### Terminal splits, folder profiles, the automation profile

- **Splits inside one tab** (VS Code's terminal groups). A terminal tab holds one or more
  terminals: `TerminalView` (view.ts) is the tab, `TerminalPane` (pane.ts) one shell with its find
  bar, Fix button, menu and suggestions; `split.ts` (DOM-free, tested) has the sizes, sash math,
  orientation, focus order, the group's title and the tab-state shape. `terminal.split`
  (Ctrl+Shift+5 / Cmd+\, toolbar, context menu) adds a terminal after the focused one (same folder
  and profile) with a hairline sash (drag; double-click = equal; `terminal.resizePane`); side by
  side in a wide tab, stacked in a tall one. `terminal.focusNextPane` / `focusPreviousPane` on
  Alt+arrows (Cmd+Alt on macOS) only while `terminalSplitPaneActive`, so an unsplit shell still
  gets Alt+arrows. `terminal.kill` closes only that pane; `terminal.unsplit` moves a pane, shell
  still running, into its own tab; `terminal.splitToNewGroup` keeps the old behaviour. The tab is
  titled "a, b". Tab state: one pane keeps the pre-D209 shape, a group is `{ panes, active, sizes }`
  with each pane's restored output under its own key, so a split tab comes back split.
  `ide://terminals` adds `pane`, `panes`, `activePane`, `tabTitle`. A task pane sharing a tab is
  neither reused nor closed with it. *Also fixed:* closed terminal tabs left their element in the
  page. *Limits:* no dragging a pane between tabs or "join terminals"; no nested splits;
  orientation follows the tab's shape, not a setting.
- **Restricted settings** (VS Code's): a schema flag `restricted` (`core/settings/model.ts`); a
  folder's layers set such a key only once `SettingsModel.setTrusted(true)` (following
  `services.trust`), else the user's value applies and `problems()` says why; extensions never
  write one. `terminal.profiles.*` and `terminal.defaultProfile.*` moved from user-only to
  restricted, so a trusted folder's profiles apply.
- **Automation profile:** `terminal.automationProfile.<platform>` (`{ path, args, env }`,
  restricted; VS Code's `terminal.integrated.automationProfile.*` is read from `.vscode`) is the
  shell of shell tasks without `options.shell` and of debug launches' `runInTerminal` commands,
  with the run flag added (`-c`, `-Command`, `/d /c`). Tasks and the debugger quote for that shell
  (`automationShell()`, `parseTasksJson(..., defaultShell)`, `shellLine(..., kind)`). *Limits:* a
  profile's `env: null` can't unset a variable for a task; WSL folders' tasks still run in the
  distribution's bash.

#### Debug console per session

- `consoleSessions.ts` (tested): each line carries its console (`sessionId`) and the session that
  answered (`source`, so an expandable result is read from the right one). A Node child process or
  worker writes into its parent's console (js-debug's merge-with-parent); every other session (a
  compound's, a serverReadyAction browser) has its own. The console shows the selected one plus
  session-less lines and follows the focused session; a picker (two consoles or more) and
  `debug.selectConsole` switch it. Ended sessions stay pickable "(ended)" until their lines go.
  `debug.evaluate { session? }` runs in the shown console's session; `debug.clearConsole { all? }`.
  `ide://debug` adds `consoleSession`, `consoles`. *Limits:* a Node program's own `console.log`
  still goes to its terminal; one input history for all consoles.

#### Command line and windows

- **Command line** (`cli.rs`, `instances/client.rs`): `<cli> file:line[:col]` (a position only
  when the part before it exists, or with `--goto`/`-g`; `C:\x.ts:3:4` works), `--diff a b`,
  `--wait`/`-w`, `--verbose`; relative paths against the shell's folder. Files go to the running
  window whose folder holds them (deepest), else the last focused one, else this process becomes
  the window. `--wait` returns once all the tabs it opened are closed (`ide://windows` `waiting`);
  with no window running it starts one, waits up to 45 s for it to register and blocks, so it
  works as git's `core.editor`. Started from a shell, a new window is detached so the prompt
  comes back.
- **Install shell command in PATH** (`instances/shell_command.rs`,
  `workbench.installShellCommand` / `uninstallShellCommand`, `{ dryRun }`) shows the steps and asks.
  Windows: a `<name>.cmd` shim (sets `IDE_CLI`, runs the exe with `%*`; relative to a per-user
  install's `bin`, else absolute, `%` doubled, UTF-8 code page for a non-ASCII path) and its folder
  appended to the **user** PATH through PowerShell's `Microsoft.Win32.Registry` (kept
  REG_EXPAND_SZ, unexpanded, the value passed in an environment variable), then a user variable
  set and removed so .NET broadcasts WM_SETTINGCHANGE; the system PATH is never touched. macOS /
  Linux: a symlink in `~/.local/bin` (or `~/bin` when only that is on PATH; the AppImage when
  `$APPIMAGE` is set); an existing non-link file is never replaced. *Limits:* the Windows release
  exe is a GUI program: it doesn't block from PowerShell without the shim and prints no `--help` /
  `--version`; `--diff` needs a folder in the target window; a missing file opens as an error, not
  an untitled file; macOS uses `~/.local/bin`, not `/usr/local/bin`.
- **A folder already open is focused; windows are restored** (`instances/`). Each window
  registers in `<data>/windows/<pid>.json` (port, random token, folder, last focus; 0600) and
  listens on 127.0.0.1 (token-checked; `ping` answers with the pid, so a reused pid or port isn't
  taken for a window). `<cli> folder`, Open folder, Open recent and `workbench.newWindow { folder }`
  bring the window with that folder forward (`AllowSetForegroundWindow` on Windows) and return
  `focused`. `window.restoreWindows` ("all" default, "one", "none"): the last window to quit keeps
  its entry; the next plain start reads the leftovers (crashed windows' too), takes the last folder
  and starts a window for each other (`restoreWindows.ts`, tested). *Why:* VS Code does both, and
  a second window on the same folder shared and overwrote its state. *Limits:* still one process
  per window; empty windows and per-folder bounds aren't restored; windows closed at the same
  moment (OS shutdown) may each drop their entry.

#### Notebooks, keyboard shortcuts

- **Several cells at once** (`core/notebook/selection.ts`, DOM-free, tested: focused cell, anchor,
  selection). Shift+click outside a cell's editor selects a range, Ctrl/Cmd+click toggles,
  Shift+Up/Down (Shift+K/J) extend, Ctrl/Cmd+A selects all. Run, delete, move (Alt+Up/Down, each
  past its unselected neighbour, nothing when one is at the edge), copy / cut / paste, clear
  outputs and change type act on every selected cell as one undo step; **Join selected cells**
  (not across kinds) and Run selected cells in the "…" menu. Cell commands take `cellIds`;
  `notebook.selectCells` is the selection as a command; `ide://notebook` adds `selection`. In a
  cell's editor Shift+click and Ctrl+click stay the editor's, as in VS Code.
- **Sticky cell toolbar:** a zero-height `position: sticky` dock at the top of the cell's column
  keeps the toolbar in view in a cell taller than the screen.
- **Change when expression in the row:** an input in the When column (Enter saves, Escape
  cancels, leaving it saves); an agent's call or a binding not in the open tab still prompts.
- **Keys the IDE and the editor share** (VS Code's single keybinding service): an IDE default on a
  key Monaco also binds runs only after `engine.handlesKey` (Monaco's `softDispatch`, its `when`
  against the focused editor, nothing run) says the editor's doesn't apply, so Ctrl+PageDown
  pages an open suggestion list and switches tabs otherwise; a user's binding wins over both.
  Monaco's standalone F1, Ctrl+Shift+O and Ctrl+G are taken from the editor, so the IDE's palette,
  go to symbol and go to line run there. Such keys show as *resolved* (an ⓘ; `resolved` in
  `ide://keybindings`), not ⚠; bindings whose `when` clauses can't both hold aren't flagged
  (`whensCanOverlap`, tested). *Limits:* only single keys are checked against Monaco (a two-key
  chord goes the IDE's way); regex and `in` clauses are assumed to overlap.

#### Testing, output channels and logs

- **Results kept** (`testing.keepResults`, default on): the run history, each test's last result
  and the last coverage report survive a reload, a restart and a folder reopen, as git-ignored JSON
  in the folder's IDE folder: `testing/results.json` (at most 5000 results, 20 kB of text each) and
  `coverage/last.json` (Clear coverage deletes it). `persist.ts` (tested) validates what it reads;
  a damaged file is ignored. *Why the folder:* a big suite's results are megabytes and the
  workspace state file is rewritten on every UI change.
- **A test's own output** beside the runs in Test results (`tests.showTestOutput`): Go's `-json`
  output events, pytest's `-rA` sections, cargo's stdout block, node:test's diagnostics, Jest /
  Vitest failure messages with stacks; otherwise the failure message. Up to 20 kB per test and
  1 MB per run, failures first. *Limits:* nothing per test from Mocha and Playwright, node:test's
  `console.log`, Jest / Vitest console lines or passing cargo tests; plain text, not a terminal.
- **Output channels:** Window, Extension host (`[id]` first), Git (each git call, its time and
  failure; frequent calls at trace), Tasks, Agent (each command the IDE's agent, ACP agents and MCP
  clients ran) and one per language server. The Output tab (`output.show { channel? }`) follows
  new lines, clears, sets the level and opens the logs folder; `output.read` and `ide://output`
  for agents. `core/diagnostics/output.ts` (tested) keeps 5000 records per channel.
- **`log.level`** (trace … error, default info; `log.setLevel`) applies to the session log and
  every channel. Debug adds every command run to Window, trace git's frequent calls; both have
  their own flood limit (1000 a minute) and stay out of the problem report's recent errors.
- **Channel files:** each channel but Window is written to
  `<logs>/sessions/session-<time>-<pid>/<channel>.log` (`SessionLog::write_channel`, `log_write`'s
  optional `channel`), redacted, 4 MB each, at most 64, rotated with the session. No new Tauri
  command. *Limits:* one level for all channels; extensions can't create channels; no filter box
  or word wrap in the tab.

#### Merge editor

- A sash between the inputs and the result (double-click: half each); the input widths and that
  split are kept with the tab (`mergeLayout.ts`, tested; `git.mergeEditor.setLayout`). Word
  highlights in the result too, in the color of the side each change came from. A delete / modify
  conflict opens with the changed side and Keep the file / Delete the file
  (`git.mergeEditor.resolveDeleted`: stages the choice and closes the tab).
  `ide://git/mergeEditors` adds `inputsShare` and `deleted`. *Limits:* no word highlights in the
  base; add / add without a base, delete / delete and renames go through Source control; sizes are
  per tab, not per file.

#### The browser keeps links, redirects, forms and popups in the IDE

- **What VS Code and Cursor do:** VS Code's integrated browser navigates any origin in place,
  opens `target=_blank` / a gesture's `window.open` as a new browser tab in the same group (the
  child keeps `window.opener`) and sends other links outside only when asked; Cursor's is the
  same kind of web view. The owner's report: a link from one local port to another
  (`127.0.0.1:8787/account`) and a `window.open` button opened the system browser.
- **Now:** a navigation the frame can't make itself is cancelled by the bridge (`links.js`: the
  Navigation API's `navigate` event where the engine has it, WebView2 and current WebKitGTK, else
  click / submit listeners) and handed to the IDE:
  - another local server (localhost, 127.x, ::1, 0.0.0.0, *.localhost, any port) loads through its
    own proxy in the same tab by the page's own navigation, so history works across ports and a
    form POST keeps its body;
  - a page load redirected (3xx) to another origin goes through `/__ide/goto?url=…` (navigations
    only), which `location.replace`s, so Back doesn't bounce;
  - `target=_blank`, named targets that aren't the page's frames, Ctrl/Cmd/Shift/middle-click and
    `window.open` open a new browser tab in the opener's group; `window.open` needs a user gesture
    (an agent's `browser.click` counts), at most 5 tabs per tab per 10 s. It returns a stand-in
    window (`postMessage`, `close`, `closed`, `focus`, `location.href =`) and the popup gets a
    `window.opener` relayed through the IDE, with the sender's origin and `targetOrigin` checked;
    `window.close()` closes the popup's tab;
  - other sites follow the new `browser.externalLinks`: `ide` (default; in the tab's site window,
    Back returning to the local page, or a new tab for `_blank`) or `system`. Site windows hand a
    navigation back to a local server (the OAuth callback) to the tab's frame and turn their own
    `_blank` / `window.open` into IDE tabs (WebView2 dropped them silently before).
- **Cookies in the frame:** the frame is cross-site to the IDE's page. WebKitGTK refused every
  cookie there, so the main webview's cookie policy is now Always; WebView2 drops SameSite=Lax
  (and unmarked) cookies in a cross-site frame, so on Windows the proxy rewrites `Set-Cookie` to
  `SameSite=None; Secure`, while on WebKit it drops SameSite. `Domain=localhost` is dropped. All
  proxies share 127.0.0.1, so cookies are shared across local ports, as browsers do.
- **Smaller fixes:** the proxy's Location rewrite no longer matches an origin as a prefix
  (`:5173` rewrote `:51730`); an embedded iframe's cross-origin links are no longer swallowed;
  the frame accepts bridge messages from any of this window's proxies; `browser.back` / `forward`
  go through the tab; a popup tab closes with its site window.
- *Limits:* other sites still show in a separate native window the tab controls (a child webview
  over the tab needs Tauri's unstable multi-webview); site-window popups relay JSON only, and
  `popup.document`, `opener.location` and `rel=opener` there aren't emulated; without the
  Navigation API (older WebKitGTK, macOS) a script's `location.href` to another port loads it
  directly in the frame; macOS ITP isn't changed; Back in a frame steps the window's joint history;
  a POST form with `target=_blank` submits in the same tab; popped-out state isn't restored;
  downloads have no IDE UI; `file://` links do nothing.

#### Also

- **Stashes:** the Git tools Stashes header has **Stash changes…** again (`git.stashChanges` in the
  bundled extension asks for the message, runs the IDE's `git.stash` and refreshes the section),
  lifting D208's limit. **Sync changes** shows the behind / ahead counts with arrow icons (VS
  Code's), not text arrows that read like digits.
- **Tests:** `split`, `profiles`, `consoleSessions`, `restoreWindows`, `settings` (restricted
  keys), `notebook/selection`, `keybindings/effective`, `persist`, `diagnostics/output`,
  `mergeLayout`, `browser/links` and `opening` tests; Rust `cli`, `instances`, `browser`; UI
  `parA-m7-6`, `parB-m7-6`, `browser-m7-6` (an "accounts server" in
  `tests/fixtures/mock-devserver.mjs`) and `git-m7-5` (the Stashes button).


### D210 — m7.6.3: Markdown HTML, preview find, the Graph section

**What.** The Markdown preview renders the HTML READMEs use (sanitized) and its https images,
loses sticky headings and gains find; Source control's Graph becomes a resizable section with
VS Code's Outgoing / Incoming rows and lane colors; activity badges count to 9999; the folder
picker after Clone keeps the pointer.

#### Markdown preview

- **Raw HTML in Markdown renders, sanitized** (VS Code's markdown-it `html: true` + sanitizer,
  GitHub's README rendering). Inline tags anywhere in a paragraph or heading (`# <img src=…
  height="64"> <img …>`, `<a href>…</a>`, `<sub>`, `<kbd>`, `<br>`) and CommonMark HTML blocks
  (condition 1: `<pre>`/`<script>`/`<style>`/`<textarea>` to their end tag; 6: the block tags;
  7: a line that is one complete tag) go through `src/ui/markdown/sanitize.ts`: a CommonMark tag
  tokenizer (the browser's HTML parser is never used on the text), an allowlist of tags (a, img,
  picture/source, br, details/summary, sub/sup, kbd, p/div/span, center → div align=center,
  h1–h6, lists, tables, code/pre, b/i/em/strong/s/u/ins/del/mark/small, abbr, q, ruby…) and of
  attributes per tag, each validated (align/valign/dir enumerations, width/height numbers or %,
  colspan/rowspan/start ranges, img src/alt/width/height/srcset, a href, details open). Dropped
  with their content: script, style, iframe/frame, object/embed, form and its fields, svg, math,
  template, noscript, meta/link/base, audio/video/canvas. Unknown tags keep their text (in prose
  they show as written: "Vec<T>"). URLs: http(s), mailto (links), `#anchor`, data:image/…
  (images), relative files; decoded first (numeric references with or without ";", `&colon;`,
  `&Tab;`…), tabs/newlines removed and controls / zero-width characters ignored when reading the
  scheme; UNC and protocol-relative paths (`\\host`, `//host`, also percent-encoded) and drive
  paths refused. `id`/`name` become `data-anchor` (no clobbering the app's ids; `#anchor` links
  find them). The safe tree is rebuilt as fresh elements by render.ts: hrefs never reach the DOM
  (clicks go to `openLink`), images go through the preview's `image()` — the same rule as
  Markdown images (workspace files as blob: URLs inside the folder, https only while
  `markdown.preview.remoteImages` is on). `<picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">`
  follows the IDE's theme. An image that fails to load shows its alt text (or URL).
  Also: `&amp;`/`&copy;`/`&#169;` in Markdown text decode (CommonMark), `\&` escapes.
  Limits: Markdown inside an HTML block (`<details>` + blank line + Markdown) still shows as
  text; HTML block layout follows our simple implied-end-tag rules, not the full HTML parser.
- **No sticky headings in the Markdown preview** (reverts D192's sticky h1–h3): VS Code's
  preview has none, and a heading stuck over the text hid what was being read.
- **Find in the Markdown preview** (VS Code's preview find widget): Ctrl/Cmd+F with the
  preview focused opens a bar at its top right (seeded with a one-line selection): the query,
  match case / whole word / regex toggles, "n of m" ("No results", "Bad pattern"),
  previous / next, close. Enter / Shift+Enter in the field and F3 / Shift+F3 (Cmd+G /
  Shift+Cmd+G) step with wrap-around, Escape closes and returns focus to the document. All
  matches are CSS highlights, the current one stronger, scrolled into view (a closed `<details>`
  opens). Matches may span inline markup ("foo **bar**") but never two blocks; code blocks'
  headers and buttons aren't searched. It follows the document as it's edited. Commands
  `markdown.find` (`query`, `caseSensitive`, `wholeWord`, `regex`, `focus`, `path`),
  `markdown.findNext`, `markdown.findPrevious`, `markdown.closeFind`; keys bound with the context
  keys `markdownPreviewFocus`, `markdownFindVisible`, `markdownFindInputFocus` (so they don't
  touch the editor's, notebook's or terminal's find); state `ide://markdownPreview`.
  Limits: no replace (it's a preview); matches cap at 5000.
- **https images in Markdown, fetched by the backend** (lifts the gap the sanitizer bullet
  above names): the window's CSP keeps `img-src 'self' data: blob:` (no remote loads by any page),
  so README logos and badges go through a new IPC command `remote_image`
  (`src-tauri/src/ipc/remote_image.rs`): https only; the host must be a name or a public IP
  (no localhost / `.local` / private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT or IPv4-mapped private
  addresses), and names are resolved through a resolver that drops private answers (DNS
  rebinding); at most 3 redirects, each checked the same way; 15 s; 10 MB; `Accept: image/*`, an
  `image/*` / octet-stream / missing content type. The page reads the type from the bytes
  (`src/core/ipc/remoteImage.ts` `sniffImage`: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, ICO, SVG) and
  shows a blob: URL, cached for the window (64 MB, oldest out first; at most 6 fetches at once; a
  failed one retried after a minute; the preview re-renders once they arrive, so a `<picture>`'s
  https `<source>` for the dark theme is used). Embedded IPv4 (IPv4-compatible, NAT64, 6to4),
  0.0.0.0/8, multicast and reserved addresses are refused too (audit).
  Used by the Markdown preview, notebook Markdown cells and `editor.renderMarkdown` (data: URLs
  there, for extension pages). `markdown.preview.remoteImages` (default on) still turns them off.
  *Limits:* with a system proxy the proxy resolves the name (the rebinding check applies to direct
  connections); SVG badges show without their scripts (as in `<img>` anywhere); fetching tells the
  image's host the IDE opened the file (as VS Code's preview does).

#### Source control

##### The Graph is its own resizable section of Source control
- **What:** the Graph moved out of the Changes tree into a view of its own, `scm.graph`
  (`src/extensions/git/graphCommands.ts`, `graphView.ts`), docked under Source control with the
  same section and sash the Git tools extension's sections use (D129, D208). Order: Changes, then
  Graph (`sectionOrder` 0), then Stashes / Line history / Compare / GitHub notifications (10–13);
  with Git tools off, the Graph is the only section. Open by default at 300 px; its height and
  collapsed state are kept per workspace like every section's. The section header carries VS Code's
  Graph buttons: the branch filter (`git.graphFilter`, a menu of Auto / All branches), Go to the
  current commit, Fetch, Pull, Push, Refresh.
- **Why:** VS Code lets the Graph be resized against Changes; ours was one tree, so a long history
  pushed the changes away.
- **Workbench, general:** a view descriptor's `sectionOnly` keeps it a section whatever
  `workbench.activityBar.hidden` says (no activity bar icon, no "Show in activity bar"; users with
  their own hidden list would otherwise have got a Graph icon), `sectionDefault` is its state
  until changed, and a new command `view.resizeSection { id, height }` sets a section's height —
  the sash's drag and double-click run it (they wrote the state directly before).
- **State:** `ide://git/graph` — shown, `allBranches`, commits listed, `outgoing` / `incoming`
  counts (null without the row), `more`.
- **Limits:** the Graph can't be dragged to another container or onto the activity bar (VS Code
  allows moving views); the filter button doesn't show "Auto"/"All" as text in the header (it's
  an icon with a menu; the menu checks the current one).

##### Outgoing / Incoming changes rows
- **What:** VS Code's rows in the Graph: **Outgoing changes** (a dashed node in the current
  branch's color) right above HEAD when the branch has commits its upstream doesn't, and
  **Incoming changes** (dashed, in the upstream's color) right above where the branch and its
  upstream forked when the upstream has commits the branch doesn't — the upstream's lane runs into
  it, as in VS Code. Each shows its count and the upstream's name, a tooltip, and expands to the
  files the commits change together (merge base ↔ HEAD / upstream); a file opens that diff.
  Right-click: Open changes…, Pull / Push, Sync changes. Commands (agent-discoverable):
  `git.showOutgoingChanges` / `git.showIncomingChanges` return the commits and files; `path` opens a
  file's diff; from the palette, a file picker.
- **Pure logic:** `withSyncChanges` (graph.ts) inserts the rows as synthetic commits
  (`#outgoing` with HEAD as parent; `#incoming` with the fork as parent, the upstream's commits
  that sat on the fork re-pointed to it) so the lane layout draws them; tested.
- **Limits:** VS Code opens a multi-file diff editor on click; we have no multi-diff editor, so
  the row expands to its files instead (each a diff tab). No rows without an upstream (an
  unpublished branch), or when the fork isn't among the listed commits (Show more brings it). The
  incoming row reflects the last fetch (autofetch or Fetch).

##### Graph colors like VS Code's scmGraph
- **What:** lanes are colored as VS Code does: a commit carrying the current branch's ref colors
  its lane blue from there down, one carrying its upstream's ref purple; a lane without such a
  label keeps the color it came in with (the line joining a commit from above stays the color it
  had), and a new lane takes the next of five rotating colors (VS Code's scmGraph.foreground1–5).
  So unpushed history reads blue down to where the remote is, purple below. Dots take the lane's
  color below them (VS Code's circle color); HEAD is a ring. Ref chips by kind: local branches
  blue (the current one filled), remote branches purple (filled), tags yellow (tinted).
- **Tokens (dark and light):** `--scm-graph-ref`, `--scm-graph-remote`, `--scm-graph-tag`,
  `--scm-graph-lane-0…4`; VS Code color themes' `scmGraph.historyItemRefColor`,
  `scmGraph.historyItemRemoteRefColor`, `scmGraph.foreground1–5` (and `charts.*`) map onto them.
  The old `--scm-graph-0…5` stay for the hover card's author avatars.
- **Limits:** no "base" ref color (VS Code's orange for the branch the current one came from);
  in All branches mode other branches' chips are blue by kind, not in their lane's color as VS
  Code does. The old bold / accent text for outgoing / incoming commit subjects is gone (the rows
  and colors say it now); without lanes (`git.graph.enabled` off) the rows still head each part,
  with arrow icons.

##### Activity bar badges up to 9999
- **What:** badges show up to four digits, then "9999+" (was "99+"); four or five characters get
  a tighter badge that stays inside the 36 px icon. `badgeText` in `workbench/activityOrder.ts`,
  tested.

##### Clone repository: the pointer over the folder picker (Windows)
- **Found:** nothing in the page sets a cursor, an overlay, `inert` or pointer capture around the
  dialog: the welcome card only shows its progress line (no cursor), the quick input is closed and
  the progress / status bar item start after the dialog. The difference from Open folder: Clone
  opens the native folder picker straight from the **Enter** that confirmed the URL in the quick
  input (Open folder is a click). On Windows, "hide pointer while typing" hides the pointer in the
  webview while typing, and with the modal dialog taking the mouse the webview never sees the move
  that would show it again — the likely cause; not reproducible on Linux.
- **Fix (every native file dialog, Open folder too, for consistency):** `dialogIpc.pickFolder`,
  `pickFile` and `pickSavePath` first leave the focused text field, let the key's events finish (a
  16 ms timer) and call the new Rust command `app_show_cursor` (Windows: raises the cursor display
  count to visible on the main thread — the window that owns the dialog — and sets the arrow
  pointer; elsewhere nothing).
- **Limits:** unverified on Windows (can't be reproduced here) — see windows-pending.

#### Also

- **Editor theme after a start with another cached theme:** the first paint uses the theme
  cached from the last start; when the settings then pick another one while the Monaco engine is
  still loading, the change found no engine to re-theme and the code editor kept the old theme
  inside the new chrome (a light editor in a dark window). `loadEditorEngine` now re-applies the
  current theme once the engine is created if it changed meanwhile (seen in screenshots; checked
  over repeated starts, no UI script: it needs a different cached theme at start).
- **Tests:** `remoteImage` (type sniffing), Rust `remote_image` (allowed hosts), graph lanes / rows
  and badge text; UI `md-m7-6`, `scm-m7-6`.


### D211 — m7.6.4: external agents get the IDE's tools, terminal output for any agent, two Windows fixes

- **External agents get the IDE's tools.** ACP sessions started with no MCP servers, so Codex,
  Claude Code or Gemini CLI saw only their own shell: they couldn't read the user's terminals,
  open editors or diagnostics. Now a session gets the IDE's built-in MCP server (the one
  `claude mcp add` connects to), as an HTTP server with its token, when the agent advertises
  `mcpCapabilities.http` (Codex's ACP adapter and Claude Code's do).
  - The server is **lent**: it starts if needed without turning `mcp.enabled` on, and stops when
    the last borrowing chat ends and the setting is off (`core/mcp/agentAccess.ts`; deliberately
    not a command, since the result carries the token).
  - Calls run as caller `mcp` under the permission policy, so changes still ask.
  - The setting `agent.externalAgents.ideTools` (default on) turns it off.
  - `ide://agent/session` shows `ideTools`: on, off, or unsupported.
  - *Limit:* agents that only take stdio MCP servers get nothing yet (a stdio proxy through the
    IDE's executable would cover them).
- **What a terminal shows** (`terminal.readOutput`, read-only and agent-visible, and
  `ide://terminals/<id>/output`): the last lines of the scrollback and screen as plain text, for
  any program, with or without shell integration (a dev server's log, cmd.exe). Before, only
  shell-integration command records had output, so a running server's log wasn't readable.
- **The command dot and the sticky line on Windows:** ConPTY's redraws can leave the command's
  mark on a blank row next to the prompt. The dot then sat under the command, and the sticky line
  found a blank row and showed only the command text (`● npm install` instead of the whole
  `PS …> npm install` line). When the marked row is blank, the nearest row within 3 holding the
  command is used (`terminal/commandLine.ts`, tested); a row with text is trusted, so a two-line
  prompt keeps its dot. The dot moves when the command finishes; the sticky line checks once per
  finished command.
- **Explorer right-click on a file showed the root's menu** when something other than the row
  element caught the event (an overlay, a row between renders, often after no left-click first):
  the tree mapped it to "no item". It now falls back to the row geometrically under the pointer;
  below the last row is still the root.
- **Tests:** `commandLine` (unit); UI `acp-tools-m7-6` (the mock ACP agent reads the terminal
  through the lent MCP server, and gets nothing with the setting off) and `explorer-m7-6`.

### D212 — m7.6.5: more provider presets with logos, name suggestions, a server's own image

- **What:** the AI models page's "Add a provider" keeps its first rows (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini,
  xAI, OpenRouter, Groq, LM Studio, llama.cpp) and gets **View more (13)** under them: Mistral AI,
  DeepSeek, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Cerebras, Hugging Face (router), NVIDIA NIM, Kimi (Moonshot
  AI), Qwen (Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, international endpoint), Z.ai (GLM), Azure OpenAI, Amazon
  Bedrock (its OpenAI-compatible `bedrock-mantle` endpoint) and vLLM. Each has its documented
  OpenAI-compatible base URL, key link, key placeholder and logo. Azure and Bedrock ask for the
  address along with the key (it's the user's resource or region).
- **Logos:** 13 new one-color SVGs from `@lobehub/icons-static-svg` 1.95.1 (MIT, copied
  unaltered; license text and file list in `src/assets/brands/README.md`). One-color files only:
  they're drawn as a CSS mask in `--brand-on` (or `--brand-ink` on light brands) on the brand's
  `--brand-<key>` token, so no color lives outside tokens.css.
- **Other server suggests presets:** typing a name ("groqai", "together", "deepsek", "kimi",
  "zhipu", "hf") shows matching presets in a list under the box (logo, name, host). Click, or
  ArrowDown/Up + Enter, turns the form into that preset's (its URL, key link, logo; a key already
  typed is kept); Escape hides the list; a name of your own shows nothing and stays custom.
  Matching (`providerMatch.ts`) normalizes, strips filler words (ai, api, cloud…), uses prefixes,
  aliases and a small edit distance; presets already connected aren't offered.
- **Logos for hand-added providers:** a provider at a preset's host (any id or path, subdomains
  count: `my-res.openai.azure.com`, `bedrock-mantle.eu-west-1.api.aws`) or whose name clearly is a
  preset ("Groq") shows that logo. Local addresses never match by host.
- **A custom server's own image:** "Choose image…" in the form (and "Set image" / "Remove image"
  on a connected provider without a known logo) opens the native file dialog; PNG, SVG, JPEG or
  WebP up to 256 KB, checked by its bytes (an SVG with script or event handlers is refused), kept
  as a data URL in this computer's global state (`providerImages`, beside recent folders), never in
  settings or the workspace; removing the provider forgets it. Shown as an `<img>` (no script
  runs); nothing is fetched from a URL.
- **Native:** `openai_api` (Rust, `ai/mod.rs`) adds "/v1" only when the base names no API version
  of its own, so Gemini's `/v1beta/openai` and Z.ai's `/api/paas/v4` work for chat, models, FIM and
  transcription (before, Z.ai got `/v4/v1/...`).
- **Commands:** `agent.matchProviderPresets` (name → presets with scores; `baseUrl` → the preset
  that address is), `agent.chooseProviderImage` (dialog or `path` → data URL, saves nothing),
  `agent.setProviderImage` (`id`, `path` / `clear`), `agent.connectProvider` takes `image`; state
  `ide://agent/providerPresets`. `agent.addProvider`'s quick pick lists the new presets and asks
  Azure/Bedrock for their address. Keys still go only to the native side.
- **Limits:** Bedrock is reached only through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a Bedrock API
  key (no SigV4/IAM profiles). Azure needs the v1 OpenAI endpoint (`…/openai/v1`); deployment-style
  URLs with `api-version` aren't built for the user. Qwen defaults to the international DashScope
  host (mainland China users edit the address via Other server or a hand-added entry). No preset
  for Perplexity (its API isn't a full OpenAI-compatible models list) or Ollama Cloud. Extension-
  contributed provider names are now also barred from posing as the new presets.
- **Tests:** `providerMatch` (unit); UI `providers-m7-6`.

### D213 — m7.6.5: risky folders (Downloads and the like), agents stay out of Downloads, protected agent config files

- **What.** A public warning says never to start Codex or Claude Code in `~/Downloads`: a browser
  saves files there without asking, plain text included, so a downloaded `AGENTS.md` /
  `CLAUDE.md` / `.claude/settings.json` (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed elsewhere steals the sign-in
  token) / `.codex/config.toml` (an MCP server, approvals bypassed) is read by an agent started
  there. The IDE now treats a few folders as **risky**: the Downloads folder and every folder
  inside it (an extracted zip), plus `security.riskyFolders`; and — only as themselves — the home
  folder, the Desktop, the temp folder and a drive / file system root (`C:\`, `D:\`, `/`,
  `\\server\share`). Projects *under* the home folder, the Desktop, temp or a drive root are
  ordinary (test runs live under temp).
- **Where they are (Rust, `user_folders.rs`).** Windows: the Known Folders FOLDERID_Downloads and
  FOLDERID_Desktop (`SHGetKnownFolderPath`, through Tauri's path resolver / the `dirs` crate),
  so a Downloads folder moved to another drive is found, plus `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads` where
  browsers fall back to; temp = `GetTempPath`. macOS `~/Downloads`, `~/Desktop`. Linux
  `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` / `XDG_DESKTOP_DIR` from `user-dirs.dirs` (parsed and tested: `$HOME/…`,
  absolute, `\` escapes, comments, `$HOME` alone = turned off) plus `~/Downloads`; temp also
  `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`. Each folder as found and canonical (links resolved, `\\?\` removed), sent
  with `app_info` (`userFolders`); worked out once per process. No new Tauri command, no new
  dependency.
- **Opening one (the caution).** Every open (Open folder, recent, the command line, a drop) goes
  through `workspace.setOpenGuard`. For a risky folder a dialog says what's risky in plain words
  and offers **Open in restricted mode** (the default button), **Open and trust**, **Cancel**,
  with "Don't ask again for this folder". The choice is saved as the folder's trust decision
  *before* it opens, so git, language servers and the agent never see it undecided. A link into
  Downloads is asked about as the folder it resolves to. A folder already restricted by its own
  decision opens without asking. `security.warnRiskyFolders` (default on) turns the caution off
  (the agent's questions stay). A risky folder **never inherits a trusted parent's trust**
  (`trustOf(…, inherit=false)`): trusting `~` doesn't trust `~/Downloads`.
- **The agents stay out unless the user says so.** The built-in agent's tool gate (first in the
  new gate list, `toolGate.addToolGate`) asks — even with full access, a refusal told to the model
  as "don't work around it" — before: the first tool working in a risky open folder; any
  `path`, `cwd`, command input path or command line (`~/Downloads`, `$HOME/Downloads`,
  `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads`, `$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads`, `Downloads/…` from the home folder) in
  a Downloads folder. "Allow" counts for that chat and folder until the folder closes; "Deny"
  isn't remembered. find_files, search (also through call_command) and list_dir leave out files
  in a Downloads folder the chat wasn't allowed into (list_dir names the folder with "in
  Downloads: ask the user first"). Asking rather than refusing-unless-named was chosen because a
  question is visible and can't be talked around by text in a file, while matching the user's
  wording ("fix the downloads page") would open it by accident.
- **External agents (ACP).** Before an external agent starts in a risky open folder the user is
  asked (it reads AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md itself); its `fs/read_text_file`, `fs/write_text_file`
  and terminal requests into Downloads ask the same way; a permission request whose locations or
  title touch a protected config file loses "Always", is marked dangerous and asks even with full
  access.
- **Instruction files aren't loaded from a risky folder** (nor in restricted mode): the folder's
  rules (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules…), skills, subagents and its MCP server lists
  (`.mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, the IDE folder's mcp.json — also not when the risky folder is
  trusted). A rules file inside a Downloads folder below the open one (the home folder open) is
  skipped too. The Rules page says why; `@`-mentioning a file still attaches it.
- **Protected config files always ask** (`core/security/agentConfigFiles.ts`, tested): other
  agents' configuration (`.codex/…`, `.claude/settings(.local).json`, `.claude/**/hooks`,
  `~/.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/*.json`, `.vscode|.gemini|.amazonq|.roo/mcp.json`, the
  IDE folder's `mcp.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `.continue/config.*`), shell / tool startup
  files (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, `.profile`, `.npmrc`, PowerShell profiles, fish config), git config
  and hooks, `~/.ssh/`, login startup folders (Windows Startup, `~/.config/autostart`,
  `~/Library/LaunchAgents`). write_file / edit_file, write commands through call_command, and
  command lines that name one of these or run `codex|claude|gemini… mcp add|remove|import` or
  `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` / `--dangerously-skip-permissions` / `--yolo` /
  `-c approval_policy=…` ask every time, even with full access, with the reason. Windows'
  trailing-dot / trailing-space file names count as the plain name.
- **Commands and state.** `workspace.resetRiskyFolderWarnings`; the test hook
  `security.setTestDownloadsFolder { path?, open? }` (caller `test` only; relative paths resolve
  in the open folder). `ide://security/riskyFolders` (folders, `warn`, `dismissed`, `open`),
  `ide://agent/riskyFolders` (`open`, `instructionsBlocked`, `allowed` per chat),
  `ide://agent/rules` `projectBlocked`; `ide://workspace` and `ide://workspace/trust` have
  `risky`. Settings: `security.warnRiskyFolders` (default true), `security.riskyFolders`.
- **Behaviour change to note:** restricted mode now also stops the folder's own rules, skills and
  subagents loading (MCP lists and project slash commands already needed trust). Folders in the
  "unknown" state still load them.
- **Limits.** A shell can reach anything: the command-line checks are heuristics (a variable,
  `cd ..` chains or a script file that names Downloads aren't seen). External agents' *own*
  file tools (Claude Code / Codex reading files directly rather than through ACP's fs requests)
  aren't seen by the IDE — the question before they start in a risky folder is the guard there.
  The IDE's lent MCP server (D211) runs commands as caller `mcp` under the permission policy
  (writes ask), but its reads into Downloads aren't asked about. Terminal commands the user types
  aren't checked (on purpose).
- **Tests:** `riskyFolders`, `agentConfigFiles`, `trustModel` (unit), `user_folders` (Rust); UI `risky-folder-m7-6`.

### D214 — m7.6.5: earlier attachments for the agent, download and add to project, 20 attachments

- **The agent can look at earlier attachments.** Saved chats keep only small previews of images
  (the full images are memory-only), so after a restart the user still saw the pictures but the
  model's history had none, and it said it couldn't see them. Two parts:

    returns the text, or the image for vision models: the full one while it's in memory, else

  - Text attachments with nothing kept (older saves) show no buttons.
- **The viewer's spacing:** the arrows moved over the image's edges (hidden when there's nothing
  to go to) instead of taking a column each side, so the image is closer to the chat; the

- **Up to 20 attachments per message** (was 10).

### D215 — m7.6.6: external agents from the ACP agent registry

The IDE had four hard-coded ACP presets (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot). Other
editors (Athas, Zed, JetBrains, Devin Desktop) offer the official ACP agent registry's agents
(github.com/agentclientprotocol/registry, Apache-2.0); we do the same.

external agents of the official ACP agent registry (github.com/agentclientprotocol/registry,
Apache-2.0), with an icon, description, version and details, and install them. We do the same.

- **What:** a gallery of the registry's agents under "Use an agent you already have" on
  Customize → Models (cards: icon, name, version, license, description, Install / Use / Update /
  Remove / Details with repository, website, license link, authors and distribution; a search
  box). An installed agent is `acp/<name>` in the model menu like the presets, gets a row above
  the gallery, and is listed on the Agents page; that page's External agents branch has
  Browse agents…. Commands `agent.registry.list / refresh / install / uninstall / cancelInstall /
  details / browse`; state `ide://agent/registry`.
- **List:** a bundled snapshot (`src/assets/acp-registry/registry.json`, 36 agents, made by
  `scripts/gen-acp-registry.mjs` from a clone; README there with source, commit and license),
  then the copy fetched last time (`<data>/acp-agents/registry.json`), then the CDN
  (`cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json`) fetched through Rust when the
  gallery opens (once per window) or on Refresh. Left out: the registry's quarantined agents and
  agents whose own license is GPL/LGPL/AGPL (corust-agent, minion-code) — also in a live
  refresh.
- **Checks (`core/acp/registry.ts`):** the file is parsed strictly and an agent failing a check is
  skipped with its reason: plain ids and versions, https links (no credentials), npm / PyPI
  package names, a binary's `cmd` relative and inside its archive, known platforms only, SHA-256
  format, no installer formats, env vars that load code refused (PATH, LD_*, DYLD_*,
  NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHON*…). Icons are SVG checked for scripts, handlers, `javascript:`, external
  references (`href`, `url(`, `@import`), `<style>`, `<image>`, `<use>`, `foreignObject` and
  DOCTYPE/ENTITY; shown as an image (a CSS mask in the text color for one-color icons, which all
  registry icons are, so they read in light and dark; `<img>` for colored ones). The published
  registry links icons: those not in the bundle are fetched by Rust (https, public hosts, 64 KB,
  cached a week) and checked again; the webview never loads a remote image.
- **Install:** npx and uvx agents run as `npx -y <package> …` / `uvx <package> …` (pinned versions
  from the registry; Node.js / uv named when missing; nothing downloaded until the first start).
  Binary agents: Rust downloads the archive for this platform (https to public hosts, each
  redirect checked, 2 GB cap, stall timeout, progress over a Channel, cancellable) into a scratch
  folder, checks the SHA-256 when the registry lists one (a mismatch installs nothing), unpacks
  it (`acp_agents/archive.rs`: .zip with the in-house reader of `extensions/vsix.rs`, .tar.gz,
  .tar.bz2, raw binaries; zip slip, absolute names, drives, Windows device names refused; nothing
  written through a symlink; symlinks only with a relative target that stays inside; hard links
  copied; only the executable bit kept; 4 GB / 200 000 entries caps), moves it to
  `<data>/acp-agents/<id>/<version>/` and removes older versions. The command's path is resolved
  and must stay inside that folder. Remove deletes the folder. A binary agent whose program is on
  PATH (`cursor-agent`, `kimi`, `goose`, `opencode`, `kilo`…) is offered "Found on your PATH" and
  uses it instead (`from: "path"`).
- **Asking:** every install shows who it comes from, the license, the URL / command and whether
  it's checksum-verified ("Not checksum-verified: the registry lists no SHA-256" for Cursor,
  Devin, Junie, Cortex, Stakpak). The user's click → a dialog; an agent's call (built-in or an
  external one through the lent MCP server) → a card in its chat that full access doesn't skip;
  the agent can't install silently. Remove asks too.
- **Kept:** the four presets stay as they were and map to their registry ids (claude-acp,
  codex-acp, gemini, github-copilot-cli); their cards say "Built in" and use the presets' Install
  (agent.installAgent) and `acp/<preset>` names, so existing `acp/Claude Code` chats and
  `agent.externalAgents` settings keep working (the user's settings still win over everything).
  Installed agents are kept in the global state (`acpAgents`, checked on load), listed by
  `externalAgents()` after the presets and extensions' agents; their menu name is the registry's
  unless taken (then `Name (id)`; GitHub's two "Copilot" entries become "Copilot" and
  "Copilot (github-copilot)"). They go through the same AcpBackend, so the D213 risky-folder
  question and config-file protection and the D211 lent MCP server apply unchanged.
- **Dependencies:** `bzip2` 0.6.1 (MIT/Apache-2.0) with its default `libbz2-rs-sys` 0.2.5
  backend (pure Rust, bzip2-1.0.6 license — BSD-style permissive, added to deny.toml; ~50 KB
  crate, a small pure-Rust decoder) for goose's .tar.bz2; `tar` 0.4.46 (MIT/Apache-2.0) was already
  built for the updater. No new npm packages. Bundle: +125 KB JSON (the snapshot with icons).
- **Limits:** zip64 archives are refused (the vsix reader; none seen in the registry); symlinks in
  archives are skipped on Windows; no automatic update of installed agents (an Update button when
  the registry has a newer version); npx/uvx agents aren't pre-fetched (the first start
  downloads them, as the presets already do); no proxy/registry URL setting (the CDN is fixed;
  test builds take a local registry); the registry's `preview` channel isn't offered; the
  agent's own sign-in (auth methods) is whatever ACP `authenticate` does, as for the presets.
- **Tests:** `core/acp/registry` (unit), `acp_agents` archive and install (Rust); UI `acp-registry-m7-6`.

### D225 — m7.7: the program is named after the product (Jonna.exe, not ide.exe)

- **Why:** Windows showed `ide.exe` (the Cargo package's name) in the UAC prompt, Task Manager,
  the installed folder and the shortcut's target. `scripts/gen.mjs` now sets Tauri's
  `mainBinaryName` from product.json's `nameShort`, so release and dev builds produce
  `Jonna.exe` (`Jonna` on Linux and macOS). The Cargo package stays `ide` (internal; no product
  name in code).
- **Test builds keep `ide`** (`tauri.test.conf.json` sets `mainBinaryName: "ide"`), so the UI test
  harness and CI paths don't change. `scripts/size.mjs` finds either name.
- **The IDE's MCP server** introduces itself with the product's short name (lowercase, like
  TERM_PROGRAM) instead of "ide".
- **Note for installs:** an earlier build installed `ide.exe`; installing this one adds
  `Jonna.exe` beside it in the same folder (the NSIS installer replaces the shortcut). Uninstalling
  the old build first leaves nothing stale. Before the alpha ships this doesn't affect anyone else.

### D217 — m7.7: hidden terminals, the terminal's own split icon, the command dot and sticky line on Windows

The owner asked for VS Code's way of
putting a terminal away without ending it: an × in the terminal's actions that hides the tab
while its process keeps running, and the ▾ menu able to show hidden ones again. And since the
editor's split and the terminal's split do different things, they shouldn't share an icon.

- **What VS Code does (the reference):** the panel's × hides the panel, terminals keep running;
  "Detach session" (`workbench.action.terminal.detachSession`) takes one terminal out of the
  tabs list with its process alive and "Attach to session" lists the detached ones to bring one
  back; the trash kills. Our terminals are dock tabs (no panel to hide), so the × hides the tab:
  the closest fit for both.
- **Hide:** `terminal.hide { id? }` (the × at the end of the terminal toolbar, titled "Hide
  terminal (keeps running)"; "Hide terminal" in the terminal's context menu; the palette) takes
  the whole tab — a split group too — out of the dock: `TerminalView.detachAll()` keeps the panes
  (their xterm canvases detached from the page, their ptys untouched), `HiddenTerminals`
  (`hidden.ts`, DOM-free, tested) keeps them with their sizes, active pane and the tab's dock
  group and index, and the empty tab closes. Hidden panes report `hidden:<key>` as their tab, so
  no dock lookup finds them; their resize is skipped while detached (no 0×0 reaches ConPTY).
- **Agents and tools:** every terminal command that takes an id works on a hidden terminal
  (`terminal.readOutput`, `sendText`, `runCommand`, `find`, `rename`, `setColor`, `commands`,
  `ide://terminals/<id>/output` and `/commands`); `terminal.kill { id }` ends it where it is;
  `terminal.focus { id }` shows it first; `split` / `unsplit` say to show it first. Commands
  without an id still default to the most recent visible terminal. Task terminals that are
  hidden aren't reused by a new task run (their tab can't be replaced).
- **Show:** `terminal.showHidden { id? , all? }` ("Show hidden terminal…" in the palette; the
  ▾ menu's "Hidden terminals (n)" submenu lists each by title and icon, plus "Show all hidden
  terminals"). With neither argument: the only hidden one, or a picker. The new tab adopts the
  same panes (the hand-off "Unsplit" already used, generalised to a group: `handOffPanes`), at
  the tab's old place when its dock group still exists, else beside the most recent terminal,
  else at the bottom; a collapsed group is revealed. A tab that doesn't open within 10 s puts
  the panes back among the hidden ones.
- **State:** `ide://terminals` gives each terminal `hidden` (and `tabId: null` while hidden; its
  `pane`, `panes`, `activePane`, `tabTitle` from the hidden group) and a top-level `hidden` list
  (`ids`, `title`, `hiddenAt`).
- **Limits:** hidden terminals end when the folder closes and aren't restored after a restart
  (their output isn't saved either; visible tabs keep D204's restored output). The dock tab's own
  × still kills, as before; the trash stays. No "hide" for one pane of a split (the whole tab
  hides).
- **Split icon:** `terminal-split`, an in-repo glyph in `scripts/build-icons.mjs` (Lucide's
  square-terminal on the 24-unit grid with a second pane on its right: a divider at x=15, the
  prompt moved left), used for the terminal's split only — the toolbar button, the context menu
  and the ▾ menu. The editor's split keeps `columns-2`.

- **The command's dot and the sticky line for a long-running command (Windows, PowerShell,
  `npm run dev`):** D211's correction ran only for finished commands, and only when the marked
  row was blank. A dev server never finishes, and ConPTY's mark can sit on the row below the
  command that the command's output fills later (npm prints a blank line, then `> app dev`), so
  the dot stayed under the command and the sticky line found a blank row and showed only
  `● npm run dev -w apps/site` without the `PS …>` prompt. Now `correctedCommandLine` takes the
  command's row just above the mark (a prompt's mark never comes after its command line) unless
  the marked row holds the command or is the first line of a two-line prompt (the command on the
  next row); a blank mark still looks below. Running commands are checked each time the sticky
  line updates (a few rows read), and the dot is placed again 0, 150, 600 and 2000 ms after the
  command starts, besides when it finishes.
- **The sticky line stays while the command runs** (VS Code's terminal sticky scroll): scrolled to
  the bottom of a running command's output, its line stays at the top. D192 hid it there for
  programs that draw their own screen; the alternate buffer (vim, less, htop) still hides it, but
  a program drawing in the normal buffer (Claude Code's own UI) now gets the sticky line over its
  top row, as in VS Code. `stickyApplies` (tested) decides.
- **Test scripts can save a result** (`"save": "t"`, then `"${t.id}"` in a later step's input,
  state path or expectation; `core/testing/script.ts`, tested): terminal ids aren't predictable
  in the UI tests (the window opens a terminal of its own).


### D218 — m7.7: language-server leftovers, a UTF-8 rewrite makes a file writable, Markdown inside HTML

- **Timed workspace pulls** (VS Code's client): after each `workspace/diagnostic` answer the
  workspace is pulled again 2 s later, besides edits and `workspace/diagnostic/refresh`, so
  problems that change without an edit here (a build's, another tool's) show up. Failures back off
  (4 s, 8 s… up to 60 s); a server without the method (MethodNotFound), or `ServerCancelled` with
  `retriggerRequest: false`, stops the timed pulls (edits and refreshes still pull);
  `ContentModified` / `ServerCancelled` retry at 2 s. A hidden window waits. One request at a time
  as before; result ids keep repeat answers cheap. `core/lsp/workspaceDiagnostics.ts`
  `nextWorkspacePull`, `workspacePullOutcome` (tested). *Limit:* no per-server interval setting
  (VS Code has none either).
- **`didSave` with `includeText`:** when the server's `textDocumentSync.save.includeText` is true,
  `didSave` carries the saved text. The editor binding (`LanguageClient.flushDocument`) sends a
  pending (debounced) `didChange` first, so `didSave` always follows the last edit (it could
  arrive before it until now, whether or not the server wanted the text). *Limit:* a notebook's
  save sends no text (its cell documents aren't one file).
- **Closed files kept for undo are closed for language servers:** the model of a closed file
  (kept so undo survives a reopen, D86) now gets `didClose` and, on reopen, `didOpen` (VS Code
  disposes the model, so the server sees it closed). What the server reports for the closed file
  — its workspace report, a push after `didClose` (pyright's workspace mode, rust-analyzer's cargo
  check) — is listed in Problems, where before the file's problems were hidden altogether. The
  built-in checkers (TS/JS, JSON, CSS, HTML workers) keep checking the kept model, so their
  markers on it stay out of Problems (`engine.diagnostics()` leaves them out). Push markers stay
  after close until the server clears them, as in VS Code (and as for a disposed model before).
  `editor/monaco/keptClosed.ts`, `EngineDocument.setKeptClosed`.
- **Pushes for files that aren't open are listed:** `publishDiagnostics` for a file with no model
  went nowhere (setModelMarkers needs a model); now they're set through the marker service by URI
  and listed in Problems (VS Code lists them); cleared when the server stops. An empty push also
  clears a closed file's markers now (they used to stay).
- **Server settings for 12 servers** (was 7): intelephense (PHP version, max file size,
  diagnostics, format, brace style, fully qualified globals), bash-language-server (ShellCheck
  path and arguments, glob pattern, background analysis limit, all workspace symbols), taplo
  (schemas, align entries, reorder keys, trailing commas, column width), ruby-lsp (formatter,
  linters, enabled features — initialization options), zls (build on save, semantic tokens, style
  warnings, zig path). From the servers' documentation / their VS Code extensions' settings; LSP
  has no schema request, so the rest stay JSON-only (csharp-ls, jdtls, docker-langserver,
  svelteserver, kotlin-language-server).
- **The stdio host's blocking calls are off the async threads:** `lsp_start`, `lsp_send`,
  `lsp_stop`, `lsp_close_stdin` (and `stop_all` from `page_loaded` / `workspace_close`) run on
  `spawn_blocking` threads (`LspHost` is now a cheap clone, `LspHost::blocking`). A server that
  stops reading (a full stdin pipe) or a slow `taskkill` of a tree on Windows no longer holds a
  runtime worker (which every other IPC command shares). Messages keep their order: the webview
  sends each after the one before it returns (`core/ipc/ordered.ts`). `stop_all` no longer holds
  the servers' lock while killing. `lsp_interrupt` stays inline (one `kill(2)`).
- **Encodings: rewritten as UTF-8, writable again.** A file that opened read-only (not valid
  UTF-8, or in an encoding that can't be written) and is then rewritten as UTF-8 (or UTF-16 with
  a BOM) elsewhere is read as UTF-8 on the watcher's report (or Reload from disk) and becomes
  writable: a new model, the banner goes, the status bar shows UTF-8. `diskText.ts` `utf8Again`
  (tested), `EditorService.becameUtf8`. *Limits:* a file reopened by hand in a read-only encoding
  (Shift JIS…) whose bytes are pure ASCII also switches to UTF-8 on the next change on disk (same
  text); the read-only model had no undo history to lose.
- **Markdown inside HTML blocks (GitHub's way):** HTML blocks follow CommonMark (a `<details>`
  block ends at the blank line too; block tags like `</details>` end a paragraph), and an HTML
  block that leaves elements open takes in the Markdown blocks after it up to the block that
  closes them: `<details>` + `<summary>` + blank line + Markdown + `</details>` shows the Markdown
  rendered inside the details, as on GitHub (it showed as text).
- **HTML's full tree rules, through the browser's own parser, safely:** HTML blocks are rewritten
  by `SafeHtmlWriter` (sanitize.ts) as clean HTML — only allowlisted tags, each with its checked
  attributes escaped, text escaped, dropped tags gone with their content, unknown tags unwrapped,
  Markdown blocks as `data-md-slot` placeholders (an attribute the source can't produce) — and
  only that text goes to an inert `DOMParser` document (no browsing context: nothing runs or
  loads). Its tree is checked again (`htmlTree.ts`: every element through `cleanTag`, ids back
  from `data-anchor`, depth capped at 48) and rebuilt as fresh elements as before. So implied end
  tags, foster parenting (text misplaced in a table goes before it), misnested formatting and
  `<p>` closing follow the HTML standard, as markdown-it's output does in VS Code. The source
  HTML itself still never reaches a parser. Notebook HTML outputs (`sanitizeHtml`) use the same
  path. Without a DOMParser (unit tests) the old tree builder stands in.
- **Preview find stays "as drawn"** (decided): diagrams and math are searched in the text they
  draw (labels, MathML glyphs), not their source — VS Code's preview uses the webview's
  find-in-page, which does the same, and a match in the TeX source would have nothing visible to
  highlight. Find has no replace (it's a preview), as in VS Code.
- **Range semantic tokens:** unchanged — a large file still also asks for the full tokens, as VS
  Code does.


### D219 — m7.7: keyboard shortcut rules and merge editor gaps

#### Keyboard shortcuts

- **Two-key chords the IDE and the editor share** (D209 covered single keys only). An IDE default
  or an extension's binding on a Monaco chord (Ctrl+K Ctrl+C…) now runs the editor's command in an
  editor when the editor's binding holds there, and the IDE's anywhere else. The IDE takes the
  first key, so Monaco never sees it. The keyboard service keeps the first key's event, and the
  engine looks up both keys on Monaco's resolver (`engineChordCommand` in
  `monaco/keybindings.ts`, using the internal `_getResolver` / `_contextKeyService`; it fails
  safe to the IDE's command). The IDE then runs the editor's command itself (`EngineKeys.chordCommand`).
  The user's own keybinding still wins. *Limits:* chords of three keys or more aren't checked
  (Monaco binds two at most). No IDE default sits on a Monaco chord today, so this matters for
  extensions' keys and future defaults.
- **When-clause logic** moved to `core/keybindings/whenLogic.ts` (DOM-free, tested). Overlap now
  understands `!=`, `=~` regex (against `==` values, `!key` and its own negation), `in` /
  `not in`, numeric ranges (`n < 2` / `n >= 5`), and `!( … )` around groups (De Morgan). A clause
  that contradicts itself overlaps nothing. *Limits:* `!(n < 2)` and regex against regex stay
  "could overlap". No constant substitution (`isMac`) when comparing clauses.
- **Removals honour `when`** (VS Code's rule): a `-command` rule with a `when` removes only the
  binding of that command (and key, if given) whose clause is the same. `whensEqual` ignores
  operand order, nesting, spaces and quote style. A removal with a `when` never removes a binding
  that has none. This applies in the resolver, the shortcuts table and the keyboard service's pass-through table for Monaco keys
  (Monaco applies the rule on its own side). Removals written by the shortcuts editor already
  carry the binding's own clause, so they keep removing exactly that row.
- **The Ctrl+K chord edit with synthetic keys, checked:** with synthetic keys, Ctrl+K Ctrl+X
  resolves to `editor.action.trimTrailingWhitespace`, and the IDE runs `editor.runAction` for it
  (the window log at debug level shows "ok"). The edit still doesn't land. The same
  `editor.runAction` called from the test does trim the line. So the IDE's routing is right, and
  what fails is Monaco running the action inside a synthetic keydown. The UI script checks the
  routing and the direct run; the edit with real keys stays a manual test.

#### Merge editor

- **Word highlights in the base**: the words each side changed, in that side's color
  (`merge-word-<side> merge-word-in-base`).
- **Add / add** (both sides added the file, no stage 1). It opened before, but as one conflict
  covering the whole file. Now the lines both versions share are common text, and each stretch
  where they differ is a conflict, even where only one side has lines, since both added the file.
  This matches git's own markers (`computeMergeChanges` with an empty base). The base pane says
  "none (both sides added the file)". `bothAdded` is in `ide://git/mergeEditors` and the commands'
  summary.
- **Final newline**: merged three-way. The side that changed it from the base wins, so a newline
  only the incoming side added (or removed) isn't lost. Reset brings back the merged value after
  a hand edit changed it.
- **Sizes per file**: each file's last layout is kept in the folder's state (`editor.mergeLayouts`,
  the 100 most recent files). A new merge tab for the file opens with those sizes. A tab's own
  saved sizes still win.
- **Not done:** an explicit "Accept all non-conflicting changes". Those changes are always in the
  result already: the only way to lose one is a hand edit, and Reset brings it back. VS Code has
  no such action either. Delete / delete and renames still go through Source control (see
  feature gaps).

**Tests:** unit tests `core/keybindings/whenLogic.test.ts` (overlap, equality, removals in the
table and the resolver), `workbench/keyboard.test.ts` (shared two-key chords, the user's binding
winning, removals with a `when` on Monaco's keys), `core/diff/merge.test.ts` (add / add, final
newline), `editor/mergeLayout.test.ts` (per-file memory). UI test `keys-merge-m7-7`.


### D220 — m7.7: Source control: status from the file watcher, "multiple" repositories, a repository picker, Graph colors

- **Status from the file watcher (VS Code watches files).** The file index's watcher (Rust
  `src-tauri/src/index`, already watching the folder for quick open) now also reports every batch
  of changed files (create / modify / remove / rename; `.git` and access events left out; at most
  1000 paths, else `overflow`) to one listener per window: new IPC `index_watch` (Channel
  `IndexChanges`), TS `indexIpc.watch`. `GitRepositories` routes each batch to the repositories
  the paths are in (`repositoriesTouched`, the deepest root; overflow: all) and each runs
  `git status` once the changes have been quiet for 1 s (VS Code's debounce), so a build or a
  checkout costs one read. The 5 s poll while focused is now a fallback: 60 s while the folder
  is watched (catches what a watcher misses: network drives, WSL paths), 5 s when it isn't
  (`statusPollMs`). `ide://git/status` gains `watched`. *Why:* every repository ran
  `git status` every 5 s while the window was focused. *Limits:* on Windows / macOS the watch is
  recursive, so writes in ignored folders (node_modules, target) also start a (debounced) status
  read, as in VS Code; on Linux only indexed (non-ignored) folders are watched, so a brand-new
  folder's files are seen after the index rebuild picks it up, or by the fallback poll.
- **Autofetch** restarts only when `git.autofetch` or `git.autofetchPeriod` change
  (`restartsAutofetch`); any settings change used to push the next fetch back.
- **"multiple" repositories mode** — `scm.repositories.selectionMode` ("single" default,
  "multiple"; VS Code's setting name). With several repositories, "multiple" lists every
  repository's changes in the one Changes tree, each under a row of its own (icon, name, branch,
  ahead/behind, pending count, Refresh); a click on a repository's row selects it, and the message
  box / Commit act on the selected one (bold; `git.selectRepository` gains `show: false` so
  selecting from the tree doesn't re-show the view). Group actions (Stage all, Unstage all, Discard all)
  pass their own repository; file actions already route by path. The separate Repositories list
  is hidden in this mode. *Limits:* one message box (VS Code has one per repository in this
  mode); no multi-select of which repositories to show (VS Code's "multiple" lets you choose a
  subset in the Repositories view) — all are shown.
- **A repository picker for the remaining commands** (VS Code's "Choose a repository"): the branch,
  tag, remote, commit-variant, operation (continue / abort), cherry-pick / revert / checkout
  commit, show commit, undo last commit commands (`workflow.ts`), `git.rebaseInteractive`, the
  worktree commands and the GitHub commands (pull requests, open / checkout / create / merge pull
  request, issues) take `repository`. Without it, with several repositories, the user gets a
  picker (the selected repository first); agents and other callers get the selected one. Views
  pass their repository, so buttons and menus never ask (the Graph, the Source control form,
  the pull request tab, the rebase tab, the status bar's pull request item). The rebase and pull
  request tabs remember their repository. `git.sync` takes `repository` too (Commit & sync on a
  picked repository syncs that one); without a remote it publishes only the folder's own
  repository. Worktree agents pass `repository: "."` (the folder's own).
- **Review commands with only a number** (`github.openPullRequestFile`,
  `github.replyToReviewThread`, `github.resolveReviewThread`, `github.addReviewComment`): take
  `repository`; without it they use the repository of the pull request under review (the one the
  user is looking at), else the selected one — they used the selected one.
- **Graph:**
  - *Base branch, orange* (VS Code's `scmGraph.historyItemBaseRefColor`): `RepoState.baseBranch`
    (Rust `default_branch`: origin's HEAD, else main / master). A commit carrying it colors its
    lane "base" unless it is the current branch or its upstream; its chip is orange. Auto mode
    now lists the base branch too (VS Code's Auto: current, upstream, base), so a feature branch
    shows where it left main. Token `--scm-graph-base` (dark #ea5c00, light #c94f00); VS Code
    themes map `scmGraph.historyItemBaseRefColor` / `charts.orange` onto it.
  - *Chips by lane in All branches mode* (`refChipColor`): every ref other than the current
    branch, its upstream and the base takes its commit's lane color (filled, as VS Code's
    labels); in Auto mode they stay colored by kind.
  - *The filter shows its choice:* the Graph header's filter button reads "Auto" / "All" beside
    its icon (new `ViewAction.label`, reactive; the button's aria-label carries it too).
  - *Not done:* a multi-file diff editor for the Incoming / Outgoing rows — the IDE has no
    multi-diff editor yet (they keep expanding to their files, each a diff tab); building one is
    a feature of its own (M). Moving the Graph to another view container: skipped, the view
    system has no movable views (VS Code's view drag and drop) and it isn't cheap.
- **Size rule:** `git/view.ts` was already split in D210 (the Graph went to `graphView.ts`); it's
  about 800 lines now with "multiple" mode, under the limit. Nothing else in the area is over.
- **Tests:** unit — `repositoriesTouched`, `statusPollMs`, `pickerOrder` (repoPaths.test.ts),
  `restartsAutofetch`, `refLabelColor` base, `refChipColor` (graph.test.ts); Rust
  `changed_paths_skip_git_access_and_repeats`. UI — `tests/scripts/git-m7-7.jsonc`.


### D221 — m7.7: skills and slash commands at Claude Code's level, approvals and saved state, session.ts / commands.ts split

- **The split (first commit, no behaviour change).** `session.ts` (2711 lines) is the session's
  state, permission questions, the message queue, retry / edit / restore, checkpoints and saving
  (now ~1150); a turn of the IDE's own agent is `sessionTurn.ts`, an external agent's turn
  `sessionExternal.ts`, subagents / background runs / the automatic review `sessionSubagents.ts`,
  summaries and one-off tasks `sessionSummaries.ts`, request options / usage / budget
  `sessionUsage.ts`, the saved form and the two-window check `sessionStore.ts`, shared types
  `sessionTypes.ts` (re-exported from `session.ts`, so imports elsewhere are unchanged). Members
  those modules share are marked `@internal` instead of `private` (functions in other files can't
  reach TS privates; a host interface per module would have doubled the code for no safety
  gain). `commands.ts` (1608) keeps the session commands (~760), with `sendCommands.ts`
  (`agent.send`, `agent.startInFolder`), `reviewCommands.ts` (accept / reject, review diffs,
  restore checkpoint), `modelCommands.ts` (models, providers, keys) and `mentionContext.ts`
  (@-mention context; `MENTIONS`, `mentionLabel` re-exported).
- **Patterns on other tools** (`core/agent/toolRules.ts`, tested): in a command's or a skill's
  `allowed-tools` / `disallowed-tools`, `Read(…)` (read_file, list_dir), `Edit(…)` (edit_file,
  write_file), `Write(…)` (write_file) take gitignore-style path patterns as Claude Code reads
  them — no `/`: the name in any folder; `/x` or `./x` or `x/y`: from the open folder; `//x`: an
  absolute path; `~/x`: the home folder; a folder's pattern covers what's inside; Windows paths
  match without case and with either slash. `WebFetch` / `WebFetch(domain:docs.rs)` stand for
  web.fetch through call_command (the domain and its subdomains). Pre-approval (`preApprovedCall`)
  takes those calls only; `disallowed-tools` refuses them (`callDisallowed`, before the tool
  gates) with "doesn't allow this (its disallowed-tools)". A pattern doesn't take a whole tool
  away; a disallowed `WebFetch` doesn't take call_command away (only web.fetch is refused). The
  IDE-command permission handler asks the session (`preApproves`) so `WebFetch(domain:…)` in a
  user's own command lets those pages load without asking (after Ask patterns, browser
  protection and IDE-control questions, which still ask). Narrowing: `WebFetch` in `allowed-tools`
  keeps call_command in the turn (any IDE command can then be called; it asks as usual).
- **Skills' `allowed-tools` pre-approve** — for a **user's own** skill only (the IDE's, Claude
  Code's, Cursor's and `.agents` user folders): for its `/name` turn (merged into
  `nextTurnTools`, `mergeTurnTools`), or for the rest of the turn when the agent loads it with
  use_skill (`ToolHost.preApprove` → `session.preApproveForTurn`). As full access for those calls
  only: Ask patterns, delete protection, destructive calls and the denylist still ask. A
  project's skill still only shows them (a cloned repository mustn't approve its own commands,
  D206); use_skill's result says which. Skills don't narrow the turn's tools (commands do, D203:
  a skill listing `Bash(git:*)` would otherwise lose edit_file).
- **`paths` decide when a skill is offered** (Claude Code's reading): a skill with `paths` isn't
  in the prompt up front (`upFrontSkills`); the first read_file / edit_file / write_file result
  of a file it matches carries "Skills for <file>; load one with use_skill…" with its name and
  description (`skillsForFile`, `renderFileSkills`), once per chat (`session.toldSkills`, saved
  with the chat, cut with retry / edit / restore, cleared by a summary).
- **Nested skills**: `<folder>/.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` (and the IDE folder's /
  `.cursor` / `.agents` labels) in the folders between a file and the root are read when the
  agent works on a file there (`nestedSkillDirs`, each folder once until a change) and offered
  the same way; with `paths` too, relative to that folder or the root. use_skill and `/name` find
  them once found; a root or user skill of the same name wins (no `folder:name` names). Not in
  restricted mode or a risky folder (D213); `node_modules`, `.git` and skills folders aren't
  looked into; the agent's ignore rules apply to each SKILL.md.
- **`context: fork`** (+ `agent`, default general): use_skill runs the skill's instructions
  (with `arguments` as `$ARGUMENTS`) as that subagent's task with its tools, rules and model (the
  skill's `model` first), and returns only the report; `/name args` of a forked skill tells the
  agent to call use_skill with those arguments (the IDE can't put a tool call in the
  conversation itself without faking the model's turn). Unknown `context` values are a warning.
- **`model` / `effort`**: a skill's `model` (not `inherit`) is its `/name` turn's model, as a
  command's (D200); `effort` (low, medium, high, xhigh, max; others are a warning) is that turn's
  reasoning effort (`nextTurnEffort` → `turnEffort` → `requestOptions`; Anthropic only, as
  `agent.effort`). Loaded mid-turn with use_skill neither changes (one model per turn).
- **A skill as a session-long mode: decided against.** A skill's instructions stay in the
  conversation once loaded (as in Claude Code); Cursor's custom modes are a mode picker, which
  the IDE has (Agent / Ask / Plan, D180) and which a skill doesn't need. What was missing was a
  summary dropping them: a summary now names the skills used before it (`skillsUsedIn`) and asks
  the agent to load them again before following them.
- **Live watching of the user folders**: Rust's watcher gets a recursive mode
  (`Watcher::recursive()`), and `skills_watcher` (`skills_watch_start`,
  `skills_watch_set_dirs`) watches the user skills folders themselves (only those; anything else
  is refused) with what's inside. Any change reads the skills again; the 30 s re-read is kept only
  when the watcher couldn't start. A folder that doesn't exist can't be watched: on focus and
  after any re-read the folders are looked at again (one that appeared is watched and read). The
  open folder's skills folders are *not* watched this way: on Windows a watched folder is an open
  handle, and git or a script deleting `.claude/skills` would find it "in use"; the workspace's
  file events cover the IDE's own edits. `release_watches` lets the skills watcher go too.
- **Always on a destructive browser command: decided, no change.** No browser command is
  destructive today (`browser.*` are read / write / network); if one becomes so, it asks every
  time without Always, like every destructive command (the policy, D70) — Always saves the site
  as Allow, which would also let that site's *other* actions run without asking.
- **get_state and protected files**: the editor's selection in a file `agent.autoApprove` asks
  before reading is asked about ("Read the selection in <file>", even with full access) before
  get_state returns it; Deny returns the state with the selection replaced
  (`stateSelection.ts`). Excluded files keep D199's "(excluded from the agent)".
- **write_file's freshness check survives a restart**: the changeset keeps a fingerprint per
  file (length + two 32-bit FNV-1a hashes, `textFingerprint`) instead of the text, saved with the
  chat (`seen`, the newest 400 files) and read back; write_file still refuses "changed since you
  last read it" after the IDE restarts. No text of the files is saved.
- **The same chat open in two windows**: the saved transcript has a version (modified time in ns
  + size, `agent_session_version`, a stat); a window remembers the version it loaded or last
  wrote and saves with `expect` (`agent_session_save`). Another window's write in between makes
  the save a conflict: nothing is written, the chat stops saving and shows an error notice with
  **Keep this version** (saves this window's chat over the other) and **Reload the other** (loads
  the saved chat in its place; not while the agent works) → `agent.resolveChatConflict { keep:
  here | other }`; `ide://agent/session` has `savedElsewhere`. Saves of one session are queued so
  they never race each other's version. Renaming / pinning a chat that isn't open in this window
  (Chats list) writes without `expect`, so a window that has it open sees a conflict on its next
  save (correct: the title changed elsewhere).
- **Subagent rules cap**: left at 16 000 characters (D204), not a setting: no one has asked, and
  rules beyond that belong in folder or matching-files rules, which subagents get per file.
- **Commands / state / settings.** New: `agent.resolveChatConflict`; Tauri `agent_session_version`,
  `skills_watch_start`, `skills_watch_set_dirs` (+ `expect` on `agent_session_save`).
  `ide://agent/skills` gains `watching` and per skill `model`, `effort`, `fork`, `agent`,
  `nested`, `preApproves`. No new settings, no new dependency.
- **Limits.** Pattern tools beyond Read / Edit / Write / WebFetch (`Grep(…)`, `Glob(…)`,
  `WebSearch(…)`) aren't read (no match: a pattern entry for them pre-approves nothing and
