  refuses nothing); Claude Code's `/x` means "relative to the settings file", read here as the
  open folder. Nested skills are found only when the agent reads / edits / writes a file there
  (not by search or list_dir, and not by `/name` before that). Linked skill folders inside a
  watched user folder: Windows doesn't report changes inside the link's target (adding or
  removing the link is seen). A user skills folder created outside while the window isn't
  focused is noticed on the next focus. The conflict check compares versions, it doesn't merge;
  a window that crashes mid-conflict loses its unsaved part.
- **Tests:** `core/agent/toolRules.test.ts`, `slash.test.ts` (patterns, disallowed calls,
  merged turn tools), `skills.test.ts` (fork / agent / effort, offering by paths and nested
  folders, nested folder candidates, fork texts, skills used before a summary),
  `changeset.test.ts` (fingerprints saved and restored), Rust `agent::tests` (a stale window's
  save is a conflict); UI `agent-skills-m7-7`.


### D222 — m7.7: worktree windows after a restart, a cheaper overview, executeCode images, Send selection to Claude Code

- **Worktree windows after a restart.** `app_windows_alive(tags, folders)`: a tag this process
  started is answered as before (D207, `try_wait`). One it doesn't know (this window restarted,
  or another window started it) is now answered from the window registry (D209): open when a
  running window, one that answers a ping with its own pid and token, has the worktree's folder
  open, else closed. So after a restart a window closed mid-turn shows **Stopped**, and an open
  one isn't marked stopped after 10 quiet minutes. No new marker file: each window already
  registers its folder and answers pings (`instances::open_with_folder`, tested). The folder is
  made canonical before it's compared (symlinked temp folders, `\\?\` on Windows via
  `store::simplify`). Limit: a window that has the worktree folder open counts even when the user
  opened it by hand, which is right, since the agent's chat lives in that folder's window.
- **The overview stops reading every chat every 2 s.** Windows are separate processes with no
  push channel between them, so every tick does a stat per chat (`agent_session_stamps`: size and
  modification time; saves are atomic renames, so each save moves it) and reads and parses only
  the chats that moved. It keeps a small copy (meta, changed paths) instead of the transcript.
  The diff (a git process) follows the chat (at most every 6 s) and otherwise runs every 30 s,
  for edits the chat doesn't record, such as a command the agent ran (`planWorktreeRead`,
  `slimChat`, tested). Before, a 2 s tick read every agent's full transcript and ran git every
  6 s. Why not a file watcher: the sessions folder is outside the workspace watcher's scope and
  needs a second notify watcher plus a Channel. The stat costs about the same as the watcher's
  bookkeeping and also works when watchers are short (network drives, WSL).
- **Claude Code `/ide` executeCode images.** The cell's PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP outputs come back
  as MCP image content after its text (`{ type: "image", data, mimeType }`, at most 4 and 4 MB
  of base64). The text no longer says `[image/png]` when the image is there. SVG and HTML stay as
  text. `notebook.runCell` takes `images: true` for this (`outputImages` in
  `core/notebook/nbformat.ts`, `executeCodeResult` in `core/mcp/ideTools.ts`, tested).
- **executeCode's new cell: kept.** VS Code's Claude Code extension also runs each call in a new
  code cell after a per-cell confirmation ("execute a new code cell in the notebook", issue #1568).
  So the IDE keeps one cell per run at the notebook's end, with what ran visible and undoable.
- **Send selection to Claude Code in the editor.** The editor's context menu has **Send selection
  to Claude Code** and the key is **Ctrl+K Alt+K** (macOS Cmd+K Alt+K), only while the
  integration runs (context key `claudeCodeIdeRunning`; the key also needs `editorTextFocus`).
  The extension's own Ctrl+Alt+K (Cmd+Option+K) is bookmarks.toggle here, and Ctrl+Alt
  chords are AltGr characters on many Windows layouts, hence the chord. Given the active editor's
  file with no lines (what the menu passes), the command sends that editor's selection, not
  line 1.
- Tests: Rust `instances::tests::a_folder_is_open_when_another_live_window_has_it`,
  `agent::tests::a_chat_stamp_moves_when_it_is_saved_again`; TS `worktrees.test.ts` (read plan,
  slim chat), `ideTools.test.ts` (images, executeCode answers); UI
  `tests/scripts/agent-worktrees-m7-7.jsonc` (an agent with no window reads Stopped from the
  registry, a repeated read keeps it, the overview row; the editor menu without and with the
  integration, the menu's file sends its selection, the key has no conflict).


### D223 — m7.7: stdio-only agents get the IDE's tools, MCP and sampling hardening, external agents' changes step by step

- **The IDE's executable as a stdio MCP server (D211's gap).** Agents that don't advertise
  `mcpCapabilities.http` (every ACP agent takes stdio servers) now get the lent server too, as
  `{ command: <the IDE's binary>, args: ["--mcp-stdio-proxy", <url>], env: [IDE_MCP_PROXY_TOKEN] }`.
  The binary checks the flag in `main.rs` before anything of the app starts (like git's askpass),
  reads newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin, POSTs each message to the lent Streamable HTTP server
  (bearer token, `Mcp-Session-Id` and the protocol version from initialize), and writes each
  message of the answer (JSON or server-sent events) to stdout on one line. Requests run side by
  side (a tool call waiting for permission doesn't hold up the rest); initialize and
  notifications keep their order; a request the server refuses or can't be reached for gets a
  JSON-RPC error answer ("the IDE's MCP server isn't running"); stdin closing ends the session
  (DELETE). *Why the environment:* any program can read another's command line (`ps`, Task
  Manager); the environment needs the agent's own rights. *Why loopback only:* the proxy can't be
  pointed at another host to leak the token. Rust `mcp/stdio_proxy.rs` (tested against a local
  server), `mcp_stdio_proxy` command (the binary's path), `ideMcpServer` in
  `core/mcp/agentAccess.ts`, state `ide://agent/ideTools` (`http` / `stdio` by chat).
  `agent.externalAgents.ideTools: false` still turns both off. *Limits:* the server's own GET
  stream isn't opened (the IDE's server sends no requests or notifications of its own); one proxy
  process per agent session.
- **External agents' changes step by step (D208's gaps).** A step that finishes (`tool_call_update`
  completed / failed) has the files it named compared at once; the change goes under review and
  shows on that step's card while the turn goes on. The end of the turn compares them again (a
  later step may change more, or put the file back: then it leaves the review). A file a step names
  before it runs is read then — so a git-ignored file that existed (`build/…`, `.env.local`) is an
  edit, not "created", and a file git would give with other line endings (autocrlf on Windows)
  isn't a whole-file diff. A diff's `oldText` is no longer taken as the whole file while the step is
  pending (Claude Code's is the edited snippet). A file the user saves in the IDE during the turn
  (`files.didSave`, not one the IDE itself wrote through ACP) is compared from that save on, and
  the "Changed files" step says so. Caps raised: up to 1000 dirty files / 64 MB read at the start
  (was 200), 1000 compared at the end (was 300), the files the steps named first; what's left out
  is counted on the "Changed files" step.
- **A turn's tokens by model.** `_meta.quota.model_usage` (Claude Code and Codex send it in the
  `session/prompt` answer; it is a per-model token count, *not* plan limits — the brief's "Codex's
  plan limits (`_meta.quota`)" was read from the agents' sources: codex-acp's `_meta.quota` is
  `{ token_count, model_usage: [{ model, token_count }] }`, and its plan limits only appear as text
  in its `/status` command) → one usage-log record per model when there are two or more: the
  current model's carries the request and the agent's cost, the others are `part` records (tokens,
  no request, no cost of their own). Claude Code's rows include its subagents and compaction, so
  they're the fuller count and replace `usage` then. `promptModelUsage` (`core/acp/display.ts`).
- **The `--help` model probe** (agents with a launch `modelFlag`, e.g. Copilot) quotes a program
  path with spaces: `& 'C:\Program Files\…\copilot.exe' --help` in PowerShell, `'…' --help` in sh.
- **Password inputs keyed by the server's identity.** `mcp.input.<name>::<input>@<hash>`, the hash
  (SHA-256, 12 hex) of what the server is: its address without query/fragment/trailing slash, or the
  program's name and its arguments without version pins (`@1.2.3`, `==1.2`, `:1.2`). A folder's
  mcp.json naming a server "github" that points elsewhere no longer gets the key stored for the
  user's own "github": it's asked for again (and stored apart). Keys stored before under the name
  alone keep working for the user's own servers (settings, user mcp.json); servers from a folder
  or another tool ask once more. "Forget its stored inputs" removes both. Rust's per-server prefix
  check is unchanged (the id still starts `mcp.input.<name>::`).
- **Secrets file across processes.** Every change to `secrets.json` happens under an exclusive OS
  lock on `secrets.json.lock` (`File::lock`: `LockFileEx` on Windows, `flock` elsewhere) besides the
  in-process mutex, and reads the file again inside it: two windows saving keys at once keep both.
  The lock file stays (removing it would race). No lock (a read-only folder): the old in-process
  lock only.
- **Model streams time out.** Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and Ollama reply streams give up after
  five minutes without a byte ("the reply timed out: nothing came from the model for 300
  seconds"), which the agent's retry treats as transient. Five minutes, not less: reasoning models
  can think silently for minutes on chat completions, and a local model loads after the headers.
- **Sampling hardening.**
  - Size cap: more than 200 000 characters of text (system prompt included) or ~15 MB of images and
    audio is refused before anyone is asked.
  - Model hints under "allow" (or "always" for the window): a hint only picks a model that costs no
    more than the one the request would get — a local one, or one whose input and output prices are
    both known and no higher; never a paid model in place of a local one, nor an unpriced one.
    Asked, the user sees the model in the question, so the hint stands.
  - A server that stops or exits takes its requests with it: the question closes, the model call is
    cancelled (`ai_cancel`), a pending answer review is rejected.
  - Audio in user messages (WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, WebM, FLAC) is transcribed by voice input's
    speech-to-text service (the provider in `agent.voice.provider`, or Groq / OpenAI with a key) and
    sent as `[audio, transcribed]: …`; without one the request is refused saying what to set up.
    The question says the audio goes to the speech-to-text service first.
- **Step-up sign-in progress.** A tool call that hits a 403 `insufficient_scope` shows "<server>
  needs more access (scope): waiting for you to sign in again…" on its row, then "Signed in: sending
  the call again." or "Not signed in: the call fails."; `ide://agent/mcp` has `signingIn` for the
  server meanwhile.
- **Registry entries checked.** `runnerRisks` (`core/mcp/registry.ts`): refused — `docker run
  --privileged`, `--pid/--network/--ipc/--uts/--userns/--cgroupns host`, `--cap-add`, `--device`,
  `--security-opt`, mounts (`-v`, `--volume`, `--mount source=`) of `/`, a drive root, the home
  folder, system folders (`/etc`, `/var`, `/usr`, `/root`, `/home`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`,
  `C:\Windows`, `C:\Users`…) or docker's socket; `npx -c / --call / --node-options /
  --script-shell`. Shown in the install question (and `warnings` in `agent.searchMcpRegistry`) —
  other host mounts, `--network <name>`, `-p` ports, `-u root`, `--env-file`, `--add-host`,
  `npx --registry / -p`, `uvx --index-url / --extra-index-url / --from / --with / --python`.
  Mount paths that are inputs (the user types them) aren't judged. Refused entries are left out of
  the search with `refused: [{ name, reason }]`.
- **server.json fields.** A remote's address with `{variables}` (`https://{region}.acme.dev/mcp`)
  becomes inputs asked at start. Arguments and variables with `choices` become VS Code's
  `pickString` inputs (written to mcp.json with `options` and `default`; mcp.json `pickString`
  inputs, strings or `{ label, value }`, are now read, asked as a pick); `promptString` `default`
  fills the box.
- **Claude Code's pending diffs end with its connection.** Rust tracks each WebSocket connection's
  calls; when it closes, they fail and the webview gets `{ kind: "cancel", id }`: the diff tab
  closes without writing and a notification says Claude Code disconnected.
- **The keychain as a choice — decided: not offered.** Secrets go to the OS keychain whenever one
  answers (D207) and to the secrets file otherwise, as VS Code's SecretStorage does with no setting.
  A "file instead of keychain" switch would only weaken storage; a "keychain only" switch would
  break headless Linux. Nothing changed.
- **Tests:** Rust `stdio_proxy_tests.rs` (loopback-only, session and protocol headers, SSE over two
  data lines, out-of-order answers, error answers, DELETE on close), `secrets` (a write waits for
  another process's lock and keeps its key), `ide_ws` (a call in flight is dropped and the webview
  told), `ai::tests` (a silent stream times out); TS `core/mcp/hardening.test.ts` (runner risks,
  refused / warned registry entries, address variables, choices → pickString, mcp.json pickString,
  server identity and secret ids, the lent server for HTTP and stdio), `sampling.test.ts` (audio
  transcripts, size cap, hint pricing), `core/acp/modelUsage.test.ts` (per-model rows, `part`
  records), `acpHelp.test.ts` (the `--help` line). UI `mcp-acp-m7-7` (a stdio-only mock agent reads
  the terminal through the proxy; a step's ignored-file edit shows before the turn ends; the
  user's save isn't credited; the second model's tokens are logged).


### D224 — m7.7: Ghost text: suggestion cache, import-graph context, a token estimate per model family

**Suggestion cache (`editor/ai/cache.ts`)**
- What: `GhostTextCache`, an LRU (64 entries, 10 minutes) of suggestions keyed by file, completion
  model, the last 1000 characters before the cursor and the first 400 after it. While the user
  types what the ghost text shows, the rest of it comes from the cache: the engine's
  `InlineCompletionSource.cached` is asked before the debounce, so it shows at once and no request
  goes out. Coming back to a spot (backspace over a divergent character, undo after accepting)
  shows the suggestion made there; a spot where the model had nothing is remembered as nothing.
  Alt+\ (`editor.inlineSuggest.trigger`, explicit) always asks the model. Partial accepts (word,
  line) also hit the cache. Cleared when the feature is turned off. `ide://editor/inlineCompletions`
  gains `requests` (model requests made) and `cache: { size, hits, misses }`.
- Why: Copilot / Cursor Tab don't re-ask on every key that matches the shown suggestion; before,
  each key after the pause asked the model again (latency, cost, a suggestion that could change
  under the user's fingers).
- Limits: the code after the cursor must be unchanged (auto-closed brackets typed inside a
  suggestion change it: that's a new request); the anchor is the prefix's end, so an identical
  1000-character tail elsewhere in the same file could match (harmless: the same code before the
  cursor); suggestions don't expire when other files change (only after 10 minutes); FIM vs chat
  mode isn't part of the key.

**Next-edit suggestions share the cache module (`editor/ai/nextEdit.ts`)**
- What: predictions kept in an `LruMap` (32, 10 minutes) keyed by model + path + the exact prompt
  (the numbered window, the change and the cursor line). The same change in the same lines (undo /
  redo, a change reverted and made again, the pause after re-applying) shows the remembered
  prediction without a request; `editor.nextEdit.suggest` (explicit) asks anew. Failed requests
  aren't cached. New state `ide://editor/nextEdit` (enabled, model, showing, requests, cache).
- Why not the ghost-text cache itself: next edits aren't typed through character by character;
  their key is the whole change, so a plain LRU by prompt is the right shape.

**Import-graph context (`editor/ai/imports.ts`)**
- What: the current file's local imports — TS / JS (`import … from`, `export … from`,
  side-effect imports, `require`; "./x.js" tries x.ts first, then extensions and index files),
  Python (`from .x import a, b`, project modules next to the file / from the folder root / src),
  Rust `mod x;`, C / C++ `#include "x.h"` — are resolved to files of the folder and read through the
  backend (stat, ≤ 400 KB, not binary; an open editor's unsaved text first; cached until a
  save / change / rename / delete event, a minute at most; missing candidates until a file is
  created). From each (≤ 8 files): the declarations of the imported names (signature and up to 12
  lines; `default`; namespace imports by the members the file uses), else an outline of top-level
  declarations; ≤ 1500 characters per file. They are `kind: "import"` snippets ("Imported from
  src/util.ts:" in the FIM prompt, "(imported)" in the chat one), scored 0.6 when the code near the
  cursor uses one of the names, else 0.3, ranked with open-file windows and recent edits (now up to
  six) inside the same 30 % snippet budget; skipped when an open-file window of that file already
  holds the text. Agent-ignored files (.aiignore, secrets) are neither read nor sent. Covered by
  `editor.inlineCompletions.context`.
- Limits: no tsconfig `paths` / package aliases, no node_modules / site-packages / crates; Rust
  `use crate::…` and Go packages aren't followed; declarations are found by a regex (no language
  server); only direct imports (one level of the graph).

**Token budget (`editor/ai/tokens.ts`)**
- What: no tokenizer is bundled. `tokenizerProfile(model)` picks a family — "large-bpe" (GPT
  cl100k / o200k, Llama 3, Claude, newer Codestral), "large-bpe-digits" (Qwen, DeepSeek,
  StarCoder, Granite, Gemma: single-digit numbers), "sentencepiece" (Code Llama, Llama 2, Mistral
  7B: 32k vocabularies), "default" — and `estimateTokens` follows a BPE pre-tokenizer (words split
  into camelCase / snake parts, digit groups, punctuation runs, indentation, newlines). The prompt
  budget (`editor.inlineCompletions.contextTokens`) is turned into characters with the ratio the
  estimate gives for the code around the cursor, instead of a flat 4 characters a token.
  `last.promptTokens` and `last.charsPerToken` show it; `tokenizer` names the family.
- Why not a real tokenizer: cl100k's ranks are ~1.7 MB (gpt-tokenizer, MIT, 28 MB unpacked with
  all encodings), Qwen's / Llama's tokenizer.json 7–9 MB each, and the user's model can be any of
  dozens; a budget only has to be about right. Calibrated against cl100k / o200k (gpt-tokenizer in
  a scratch folder, not a dependency) on this repo's TS, Rust, JS and Python: within ~5 % on code
  (3 % over in total), ~12 % low on JSON / Markdown. The SentencePiece family's parameters come
  from published averages, not measured (Hugging Face was unreachable from the sandbox).

**Skipped: a model trained on edit histories.** Cursor Tab's model is Cursor's own, trained on
their users' edits; the IDE uses the user's models (Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible server, the
providers), and training or hosting one would need the product's own service. Not a placeholder:
out of scope by design. FIM-trained code models (qwen2.5-coder etc., D204) are the substitute.

- How: `editor/ai/cache.ts`, `imports.ts`, `tokens.ts` (DOM-free; `cache.test.ts`,
  `imports.test.ts`, `tokens.test.ts`); `completions.ts` (cache, import graph, ratio, state);
  `nextEdit.ts` (prediction cache, state); `engine.ts` (`InlineCompletionSource.cached`),
  `monaco/zones.ts` (asked before the pause). Mock Ollama: ", imports" in the FIM answer when the
  prompt carried an imported file; answers numbered ("// #N") for `src/counted.ts`.
- UI: `tests/scripts/ghost-text-m7-7.jsonc`.

### D226 — m7.7: explorer real-mouse fixes, local writes refresh the tree, chat scroll, Providers tab

- **Ctrl/Shift+click lost the selection, and a right-click on a name could open the root's
  menu.** Found with real mouse input (xdotool under xvfb): the list's own mousedown handler
  selects the row and re-renders it, so by the time later handlers ran, the event's target (the
  name's `<span>`) was detached. `target.closest(".vlist-row")` then found nothing: the tree's
  "click below the rows" handler cleared the selection (twice, with the explorer's body
  handler), and the explorer's body `contextmenu` handler took a right-click for empty space and
  showed the root's menu over the item's (which is also why the item sometimes kept a focus
  ring). Synthetic clicks hit the row element itself, so tests never saw it. These checks now use
  the event's dispatch path (`eventClosest` in `ui/treeParts.ts`, `composedPath()`), which keeps
  the elements the event went through even after a re-render; the same for compact folder
  segments (`folder/folder` rows: the segment under the pointer still decides the menu's folder)
  and the sticky rows. Covered by `explorer-m7-7` with real mouse input.
- **Files this window writes show at once.** `fsIpc` reports the paths it changed (`fsChanges`:
  write, create, rename, delete, trash, untrash, move, copy) and the explorer lists their folders
  (and each folder up to the root) again after 80 ms, instead of waiting for the OS watcher, which
  could miss or delay an agent's writes or Accept all / Reject all.
- **Opening a changes card no longer scrolls the chat to the top.** The transcript replaced all
  its children when one changed (a card re-renders when opened), and emptying the column for a
  moment clamped the scroll position to 0. It now inserts and removes only what changed.
- **Customize → Models is now "Providers"** (the page's tab title: "Model providers"): the page
  is about connecting providers and agents; which model does what lives on the Agents page.
- **`dev.elementsAt`** (test builds): the elements under a point and the last mouse events the
  document saw, for tests and debugging with real input.
- **m7.7 spot audit fixes:**
  - *Registry runner check (D223):* options are read the way docker and npx read them (`-v/:/h`,
    `-itv /:/h`, `-v=…`, `--mount` as CSV with case-insensitive, quoted keys, npx `-c=…`), host
    paths are normalized (`/.`, `/tmp/..`, `\\?\C:\`), `/run`, `/mnt`, `/media`, `/snap`,
    `/Volumes` and `C:\ProgramData` count as system folders, and inputs are judged with their
    defaults and choices and with the fixed text around a typed value (`/:/host/${input:x}` still
    mounts `/`).
  - *Tool path patterns (D221):* a call's path has `.` / `..` folded before matching
    (`Edit(src/**)` no longer pre-approves `src/../package.json`), and `disallowed-tools` entries
    ignore case (`Read(.env)` also stops `.ENV` on macOS).
  - *A server's stored keys (D223):* the identity keeps a relative program path whole
    (`./tools/npx` isn't the user's `npx`) and includes the server's environment, env file and
    working folder.
  - *Two-window chats (D221):* "Reload the other" keeps saving blocked until the other version is
    loaded. The version check is still check-then-write (two saves in the same instant: the last
    wins).
  - *Stdio proxy (D223):* a line of exactly the size limit no longer swallows the next message.
  - *Models after the Ollama address changes:* `agent.refreshModels` during a refresh of the old
    provider list waits for it and lists the new ones.
  - *Notebook cells (D218):* problems a server reports for a notebook's combined document go to
    the cells only, not also to Problems as a file of their own (the cells' last-line "unused
    expression" showed again).

### D227 — m7.7: model picker with a provider rail, composer toolbar order, zip attachments, external agents ask first, "This project"

- **Model picker** (`view/modelPicker.ts`, like T3 Chat's): a rail on the left with Favorites and
  recent (a star), then one tab per provider the user added and per external agent they have
  (installed, added by them or from an extension, or in use), each its logo with the name in the
  tooltip; beside it a search box over every tab, the tab's models, a star per model, and a
  footer with Presets and Refresh. It replaces the nested model menu (`menus.ts` `showModelMenu`,
  `agentSubmenu`). Favorites and recents are settings (`agent.favoriteModels`,
  `agent.recentModels`) so agents and Settings see them; an external agent's own model is one key
  (`acp/<agent>#<model>`, `modelPicks.ts`). `agent.selectModel` keeps Recent;
  `agent.toggleFavoriteModel` stars. Listeners are delegated on the rail and the list, which are
  rebuilt when the models, statuses, the agent's settings or the favorites change.
- **Composer toolbar order:** + and the chat mode on the left; on the right the cost and context
  meter, then the model (with its provider's or agent's logo), its effort (a word, no brain icon;
  an external agent's own reasoning levels when it has them; "Default" when nothing is set, not
  "Auto", which people now read as a permission mode), and last the permissions, the order
  Claude's and Cursor's composers use. The permission button says Review, Accept edits (was
  Auto-apply) or Auto (full access, was "Full access"), as other tools name them. Words only: no
  chevrons and no icons except the provider's logo (the chat mode lost its icon too); the model
  and permission read in the default color, the effort dimmer, the permission a little apart. The logos are the AI models
  page's badges, moved to `view/brandMark.ts`. More provider logos are a follow-up: the picker
  only shows providers the user added, which all come from presets that have logos or letter
  badges.
- **Logos everywhere a provider or agent is named:** Ollama (built in, not a preset) and agents
  installed from the ACP registry (their registry icon) had letter badges in the picker and the
  model button. The "Add a provider" tiles are flat now (`--bg-surface-raised`, hover
  `--bg-hover`): with a logo on each, the brand-color wash looked cheap.
- **Zip attachments** (`core/agent/zip.ts`): a `.zip` becomes one text card: where it is (so the
  agent can extract it with a command), its file list, and its text files' contents up to the
  usual 100,000 characters. Read with the platform's `DecompressionStream("deflate-raw")`, no
  dependency; zip64 and encrypted entries are listed, not read. A zip inside the folder is read
  too (as a path the agent couldn't read it). The limit was already 20 attachments per message.
- **External agents ask before writing** (`core/acp/modes.ts`): Codex and Claude Code write files
  themselves, so "Review edits" only showed their changes afterwards (with Accept all), which
  looked like they ignored the setting. Each turn now starts with `session/set_mode` to the mode
  that matches the IDE's settings: Review edits or Ask before commands → Claude Code's `default`,
  Codex's `read-only` (both ask before a write, through the IDE's approval card); Auto-apply with
  commands automatic → `acceptEdits` / `auto`; full access → `bypassPermissions` / `full-access`.
  Ids are matched before names (Codex calls its `auto` mode "Default"). An agent without modes,
  or one whose modes match nothing, is left as it is; its changes are still reviewed after the
  fact as before (D208).
- **Chats: "This project"** (`chatGroups.ts`): with a folder open, its chats come right after
  Pinned under "This project", newest first; every other chat is grouped by day (Today,
  Yesterday…) with its folder's name, replacing "Other folders".
- **`terminal.runCommand` with a long timeout:** an agent asked for more than 600,000 ms (an
  install) and the schema refused it ("must be <= 600000"), shown to the user as a failed
  command. There's no schema maximum now; the wait is capped at an hour, like the agent's own run
  tool.

#### D227, second part: agent hooks, custom modes, codebase index, pull requests from a chat, read-only paths, ten smaller gaps

The owner asked for the next upgrades from the gap list and ten more of the smaller ones. Built in
one batch (the smaller ones by helper agents in parallel), then audited (two read-only reviews of
the whole diff) and fixed.

**Agent**
- **External agents' modes, checked against the real ones.** `claude-agent-acp` reports
  `default` ("Manual"), `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `bypassPermissions`; `codex-acp` reports
  `read-only`, `workspace-write`, `agent` ("Auto review", its default: it never asked before a
  write) and `agent-full-access`. The mapping picks `default` / `read-only` for "ask",
  `acceptEdits` / `agent` for edits applied automatically, `bypassPermissions` /
  `agent-full-access` for full access (ids before names, so Codex's "Auto review" can't pass for
  Claude's `auto`). An agent with no mode that asks gets a one-time notice in the chat that its
  changes show for review after each step.
- **Hooks** (`core/agent/hooks.ts`, `hooks.ts`), in Claude Code's format so one configuration
  works for both: `PreToolUse` (blocks a call; the reason goes to the agent), `PostToolUse` (its
  words follow the result), `UserPromptSubmit` (blocks the message, which goes back to the box, or
  adds context) and `Stop` (sends the agent back once per message, Claude Code's
  `stop_hook_active`). Matchers take the IDE's tool names and Claude Code's (`Bash`, `Edit|Write`,
  `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`). The event is JSON on stdin; exit code 2 blocks with the output as the
  reason; exit 0 may print JSON (`decision`, `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision`,
  `additionalContext`), and the last JSON line counts, so a warning before it doesn't hide a deny.
  Sources: `agent.hooks` (user settings only: a folder's IDE settings can't add commands) and a
  trusted folder's `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json`, approved per content
  (SHA-256; the card shows every command, and offers no "always" when it had to cut them).
  `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is set. Subagents' tools are hooked too. Stop ends running hooks. Hooks
  run through the agent's command runner (`exec_run` gained `stdin`, and `env` limited to
  `CLAUDE_*`); with no folder open they don't run. State: `ide://agent/hooks`.
- **Exit codes on Windows.** PowerShell's `-Command` turned every failure into exit code 1, so a
  hook's 2 never blocked and the agent saw 1 for any failing program. The runner now ends with
  `if (-not $?) { exit $LASTEXITCODE or 1 }` (on its own line: a trailing comment can't swallow
  it).
- **Custom chat modes** (`core/agent/chatModes.ts`, `customModes.ts`): `agent.customModes` and a
  trusted folder's `.github/chatmodes/*.chatmode.md` / `.github/agents/*.agent.md` (Copilot's
  files: front matter `description`, `tools`, `model`, the body is the instructions). `tools`
  takes tool names and groups (`read`, `edit`, `run`, `mcp`, `mcp__<server>`, and Copilot's and
  Claude Code's names); none listed: every tool. They follow Agent, Plan and Ask in the mode menu
  and Shift+Tab; "Create chat mode…" (`agent.createChatMode`) writes a template and opens it.
  `agent.setChatMode` takes `custom:<name>`. A mode that's gone (renamed, deleted, folder no
  longer trusted) sends the next message in Agent mode with a notice; until then the chat gets
  read-only tools. State: `ide://agent/chatModes`. Trust changes reload them.
- **Codebase index** (`core/agent/codeIndex.ts`, `codeIndex.ts`, `ai/embed.rs`), Cursor's
  `codebase_search`: off by default (`agent.codebaseIndex.enabled`, rule 8: the code goes to the
  embedding model's provider) with an embedding model (`agent.codebaseIndex.model`, any
  OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings`; Ollama's too). Source files (by extension, not dependencies or
  generated files, not files the agent ignores) are cut into ~60-line overlapping chunks that end
  at a blank line when one is near, embedded in batches of 64, stored as int8 vectors (a quarter
  of float32) in the app's data folder, one index per folder (up to 4000 files, 20,000 chunks).
  A file goes into the index only once all its chunks are embedded, so a failed run leaves
  nothing half done; saves re-embed only the changed files. The agent's `codebase_search` tool
  appears only with the index on; `agent.codebaseSearch` and `agent.rebuildCodebaseIndex`
  (shown only when on, `aiCodebaseIndex`); state `ide://agent/codebaseIndex`. A search before the
  first build says so at once instead of waiting for it.
- **Pull requests from a chat** (`chatPullRequests.ts`): "Open pull request" in the chat's "…"
  menu (`agent.createPullRequest`) asks the chat's agent to commit the conversation's work on a
  branch and open the pull request with `github.createPullRequest` (or `gh` for an external
  agent), title and description from the conversation. `github.didCreatePullRequest` links it to
  the chat that opened it (an external agent calling through MCP: the chat that asked, within 30
  minutes): a card in the chat, `pullRequest` in `ide://agent/session`, kept with the chat; the
  menu item then opens it.
- **Read-only paths** (`agent.readOnlyPaths`, default `/.git/**`, `/.vscode/settings.json`,
  `/.idea/**`, plus the IDE's own folder settings always): the agent's file tools and IDE
  commands that write files are refused without a question and told not to try another way.
  Windows spellings (`.git./hooks`, trailing spaces, `::$DATA`) count as the file. Commands it
  runs aren't parsed for these paths (D213 still asks for git hooks and agent config files).
- **Model picker polish:** each model's price (`$3 / $15 per M`, "free") on its row,
  Ctrl+1…9 picks a favorite, ↑/↓ move along the rail, and arrow keys in the search box no longer
  moved two rows (both the box and the picker handled them).
- **20 more provider presets** (42 in all, plus Ollama and custom servers), each OpenAI-compatible
  with a `/models` list: SambaNova, Novita, DeepInfra, Hyperbolic, Nebius, SiliconFlow,
  Volcengine Ark, StepFun, ModelScope, Friendli, Featherless, Chutes, Venice, kluster.ai,
  Inference.net, PPIO, Vercel AI Gateway, AIHubMix, CometAPI, Xinference, Jan. Logos from the
  same MIT package (Jan has none there: a letter badge).

**Ten smaller gaps** (helper agents; their notes in the area READMEs)
- **Logs:** per-channel log levels (`log.channelLevels`; `log.level` stays the default), the
  Output tab's filter box (`text, !exclude`), level picker and word-wrap toggle
  (`output.setFilter`, `output.toggleWordWrap`), and the Git channel listing the git command lines
  (`> git status -z [12 ms]`; Rust keeps the last 1000 in `git/journal.rs`, home shown as `~`, at
  most 200 arguments a call, fetched with `log_git_commands` after a burst of git calls; a reload
  doesn't list them twice).
- **Command line:** a file that doesn't exist opens as an untitled editor named after it that
  saves there without a dialog, inside or outside the folder: only for the user's own (command
  line) editors, kept in a set; an `untitled:<path>` document an agent opens saves through the
  dialog. A file that appeared meanwhile is replaced only when the user says so. `--diff a b`
  works without a folder. `allow_file` accepts a not-yet-existing file whose folder exists (that
  path only).
- **Tasks:** Makefile targets from `make -p -n -q -r .DEFAULT` (trusted folders, make on PATH,
  5 s, 8 MB; `$(foreach)`/`$(eval)` and included makefiles' targets); otherwise the text is read.
- **Terminal:** `~/…` links (and `~\…` on Windows) open the file in the home folder (the click
  lets that one file in); `terminal.splitDirection` (auto / horizontal / vertical); a profile's
  `env: { "X": null }` unsets X for tasks too.
- **Notebooks:** hot exit (unsaved notebooks come back unsaved, one undo step; the backup text is
  kept per edit version, not serialized on every state save) and dragging cells by their gutter,
  several selected ones together (`notebook.moveCellsTo`).
- **Debug console:** one input history per console (kept across restarts of a configuration), and
  Node's `"console": "internalConsole"` / `"outputCapture": "std"` copying the program's output
  to the debug console (a pause shows an unfinished line without breaking it).
- **Extension API:** tree items' context menus (`menus["view/item/context"]`, `viewItem`, groups,
  inline buttons; the command gets `{ item }`) and `ide.ui.createOutputChannel(name)` (its channel
  is `ext.<id>~<name>`: `~` can't be in an extension id, so one extension's channels never look
  like another's).
- **MCP:** server icons from `serverInfo.icons` and the registry's server.json (data: images after
  the SVG check, https through the backend's image fetch) on the MCP page and in the registry
  search (12 rows, 400 ms at most); a named argument with nothing to fill in is passed as a flag,
  an optional boolean one only when its value says "true" (anyone can publish to the registry).

**Audit fixes in this batch** (from the two reviews): hook approval keyed by SHA-256, not a weak
hash; the approval card no longer cuts commands silently; "allow once" lasts for the chat; Stop
while asking isn't a decline; declines reset with the folder; a zip entry is inflated only up to
its limit (a declared size can lie: zip bomb); the code index respects `.aiignore` and friends;
read-only paths and Windows spellings; a blocked message no longer left the chat "running";
the untitled-for-path escalation (an agent opening `untitled:<startup folder>\run.cmd`); optional
boolean registry flags; `~/` links outside the folder; the registry search waiting on icons; Git
journal paths and size; duplicated Git lines after a reload; notebook backups; the debug console's
line splits; output channel ids. Pre-existing clippy errors from the newer toolchain
(`wsl.rs` `as_chunks`, an unused test variable on Windows) and a dead `git/fileBlame.ts` (its
feature moved to the bundled git tools extension) went too, and real ISO 8859-1 decoding (WHATWG
decodes the label as Windows-1252).

**Left:** `notebook/view.ts` is 1230 lines (over the ~1200 rule by a little); the debug console
can't tell stderr from stdout (one terminal stream); `~` in a WSL terminal is the Windows home;
the agent's commands aren't parsed for read-only paths; the codebase index has no rate limiting
beyond batches of 64 and stops at 4000 files.

### D228 — m7.7: the UI suite on Windows, and the audit of D227

**Why:** the command-script suite had never run green on Windows (CI stops before it; it was
written in the Linux VM). On the owner's machine 60 of 135 scripts failed. Most failures were the
tests, not the IDE, but a few were real Windows bugs the suite had been hiding.

**The runner (`scripts/ui-test.mjs`):**
- On Windows, the scripts' terminals open **Git Bash** (a `terminal.defaultProfile.windows` in
  the test profile): their setup lines are bash (`printf`, `mkdir -p`, `&&`). Tasks and the
  agent's commands keep the default shell, so PowerShell is still what those tests exercise.
- **Git as on a fresh machine:** `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` (a per-run file: a test identity, `main`,
  `core.autocrlf=false`, no signing) and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`. Git for Windows' own config turns
  on autocrlf and names the first branch master; a user's may sign commits or add hooks.
- The mock servers must be listening before a script starts: a port still held (a mock from a
  stopped run) ends the run with that reason instead of failing every browser test far from it.
- `"platforms": ["linux"]` in a script: run only there (the zsh and fish profiles from
  `/etc/shells`); skipped scripts are counted apart.
- Scripts made portable: paths next to the test folder instead of `/tmp` (with a saved
  `ide://workspace` root), `python3` or `python`, a fake prettier with a `.cmd` shim, the debug
  launch file written by a setup script (the CI image's Chromium only where it exists), `pkill`
  through a small node helper. A leftover debugging step (copying screenshots to `/tmp`) went, and
  `agent-m6-71` (D170's fenced rich blocks, replaced by D171's display tools, which `agent-m6-72`
  tests) was removed.

**Real bugs it found (fixed):**
- PowerShell terminals reported the **line that loads shell integration** as the first finished
  command: a `terminal.runCommand` sent as the terminal opened got that result (exit 0, its own
  command line) instead of its own. The first prompt now only notes the history position.
- **Task exit codes** through PowerShell were always 1 (`-Command`): tsc's 2 is now the task's,
  as D227 did for the agent's commands; and a rewritten `a && b` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 kept
  its exit code (it ended in an `if`, so `$?` was true).
- Windows PowerShell 5.1's `>` / `>>` wrote **UTF-16** (`echo x >> notes.txt` from the agent or a
  worktree setup script made a file git calls binary): UTF-8 now, as PowerShell 7 does.
- An image attachment read from disk could fail to decode in WebView2 (`createImageBitmap` on a
  blob typed `image/*`): the right MIME type from the name, and an `<img>` fallback.
- Inline completions reported **`c:\…` paths** (Monaco's `fsPath` lowercases the drive): the
  path wasn't made relative and edits tracked under `C:\…` never matched. `upperDrive` in
  `core/paths`.
- A browser click on a link that navigates waited out the timeout: WebView2 doesn't always
  deliver the unloading page's "leave"; a load or a new document's hello ends the old one's calls.
- **`gh` on Windows** was looked up as `gh.exe` only (Rust's search): a `gh.cmd` earlier on PATH
  (a wrapper, the tests' offline stand-in) was passed over. It's found as a command prompt finds
  it now (PATHEXT). With the runner adding `PATH` beside Windows' `Path`, this let
  `features-m6-47` reach the real GitHub CLI and **publish the sample as a private repository on
  the signed-in account**. The runner now sets the existing key and gives tests a fake
  `GH_TOKEN`, so the real CLI can't sign in either.
- Notebook cells got CRLF at the first Enter on Windows (Monaco's default for a one-line model):
  LF always, as Jupyter writes them.
- `editor.openFile` with `..` in an absolute path allowed one spelling and read another
  ("outside the open workspace"): the path is collapsed first.

**The audit of D227 (three independent reviews; the verified findings fixed):**
- Hooks: the JSON answer is found in pretty-printed output after other text, and the **end** of a
  long output is kept (it's where the answer is); `"continue": false` stops the agent (it no
  longer sent a Stop hook's agent back to work); plain output of tool hooks isn't sent to the
  agent (only UserPromptSubmit's, as in Claude Code); `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` works in PowerShell;
  a folder's approval is tied to that folder; messages sent into a running turn go through
  UserPromptSubmit; a tool doesn't start after Stop during its PreToolUse hook; a cancel that came
  while a command's shell was starting is no longer lost.
- External agents: with Review edits on, a failed switch to the asking mode **refuses the turn**
  (it ran in whatever mode the agent was in, possibly bypass); an agent moving itself to a mode
  that writes unasked mid-turn is put back; changing Review edits or the command setting mid-turn
  re-syncs the mode. A gone custom mode resets for external agents too.
- Read-only paths: 8.3 short names (`GIT~1`) are refused; `.git` and `.idea` themselves are
  read-only (a worktree's `.git` is a file); a move's or paste's destination and a rename's new
  name are checked.
- Codebase index: a size limit that fits app data's 32 MB (1536-dimension vectors overflowed it
  after all the embedding was paid for); saved as it goes and on an error, so a failure late in a
  first run keeps what was done; waits for the file list and for `.aiignore`; stats before
  reading (a 1 GB dump isn't read); the same folder in another case is one index on Windows;
  renames, external changes and folder deletions update it; another folder's pending changes
  don't narrow the scan; turning it off during the last batch saves nothing.
- Model picker: closes with its chat (Ctrl+W while open), and its keys are its own while open
  (Ctrl+PageDown switched dock tabs under it). Pull requests from an external agent link only
  when exactly one chat waits for one.

**Left in the suite on this machine:** 116 of 143 scripts pass (1 skipped), up from 75 of 135
(the first run stopped halfway). Of the rest:
- **Tools this machine lacks:** `debugpy` (`debug-m6-42`), Go (`testing-m6-48`), Chrome
  (`debug-browser-m6-97`: Edge only), a Python with venv (`editor-m7-1`, `notebooks-m7-5`).
- **How Windows draws:** line heights and scroll positions with Windows fonts (`features-m6-45`,
  `m6-91`); `dev.type` can't focus an editor while another window is in front (`editor-m7-5`,
  `gaps10-m7-6`, `keys-merge-m7-7`).
- **Checks spelled for Linux:** paths with `/` (`extensions-api`, `notebook-m6-89`'s move), a zsh
  folder profile under `terminal.profiles.linux` (`parA-m7-6`).
- **Worth a closer look, maybe real:** the terminal's failed-command Fix and suggestions in Git
  Bash (`terminal-m6-49`, `terminal-m7-7`: they pass in PowerShell); `terminal.fixWithAgent`
  finding no finished command (`features-m6-22`); the worktree overview's progress
  (`agentA-m7-6`); the cross-port browser tabs and popups (`browser-m7-6`); the attach process
  list (`debug-m7-5`); the killed debuggee check (`debug-m6-44`); and `explorer-m7-7`,
  `gaps-m7-4`, `ghost-text-m7-7`, `history-m6-40`, `md-m7-6`, `notebook-ext-m7-3`,
  `testing-m7-5`'s expected / actual.

**Left in the code:** the agent's
commands aren't parsed for read-only paths; a hook's own script isn't part of its approval's
signature; a background subagent's running hook isn't cancelled by Stop once the chat is idle;
WSL folders give hooks Windows paths in `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`; with Review edits on and commands on
full access, an external agent still gets its bypass mode (full access means never ask); a
retried message after a mode file changed keeps the old mode's rules.

### D229 — m7.8: section 2a of the feature gaps, the taskbar jump list

**Why:** the owner asked for the taskbar menu VS Code has (right-click the button: recent folders,
New window) and for section 2a of `docs/feature-gaps.md` closed as far as one pass can. The rule
for the pass: only what VS Code (Cursor / Claude Code for the agent) has in core; what VS Code
ships as an extension moved to 2c, what isn't standard was dropped (listed in 2d).

**Windows and the command line:**
- **Jump list** (`instances/jump_list.rs`, Windows): "Recent folders" (the IDE's pinned first, at
  most 10, folder icons) and the "New window" task, written through `ICustomDestinationList` on a
  COM thread of its own; each entry starts the IDE with the folder (quoted for
  `CommandLineToArgvW`) or `--new-window`, so an open folder is focused. Rewritten 0.5 s after the
  recent list changes (any window); a folder the user removes from the list leaves the recent
  list too (VS Code). The process's **AppUserModelID** is now set to the bundle identifier before
  the window exists: the NSIS installer's shortcuts carry it (`SetLnkAppUserModelId`), so windows
  started from the jump list or the command line group under the pinned button and the list is
  that button's. Debug builds use `<identifier>.dev`; test runs set neither. The `windows` crate
  gained features only (Shell Common / PropertiesSystem, EnhancedStorage, StructuredStorage,
  Variant, Console), no new dependency.
- **Bounds per folder** (`window_bounds.rs`): `window.json` keeps the last window's bounds and
  each folder's (50); the old one-window file still reads. A window the last session's restore
  starts (`--restored`, internal) opens at its folder's place; a window opened on a folder from
  the command line or the jump list too. Moves and resizes are written at most every 2 s, so an
  OS shutdown that closes every window keeps them.
- **`--help` / `--version`**: printed and exit; a release build (a GUI program) attaches to the
  parent's console first.

**Terminal, tasks, keybindings:** `terminal.join` (VS Code's Join terminals: moves other tabs'
terminals into one as splits); `terminal.hide { onlyThis }` hides one pane of a split; **Ctrl+`
with every terminal hidden shows the most recently hidden one** instead of starting a new one
(the owner's report: hiding a terminal left no obvious way back; `terminal.focus` does the same).
Suggestions list the shell's aliases and functions (`pty_shell_globals`: asked of the terminal's
own shell, cached 5 minutes) with a details pane. Tasks without an automation profile run in the
default profile's shell, args and env (VS Code); WSL folders use the Linux automation profile or
bash, with bash quoting. `.cmd` / `.bat` process tasks go through `cmd.exe /e:ON /v:OFF /d /c` with
the arguments quoted as Rust's standard library has since BatBadBut, passed in a variable so
portable-pty can't re-quote them. `~` in a WSL terminal's links is the distribution's home. When
clauses substitute VS Code's platform constants before comparing (`isMac && …` never conflicts on
Windows), understand `!(n < 2)`, and compare literal regex sets.

**Source control:** each conflicted file has its kind (VS Code's letters); staging a
delete/modify conflict asks Keep / Delete (agents pass `deletion`); the merge editor is offered
only where there are two sides. In "multiple" mode each shown repository has its own commit box,
and the Repositories list chooses which show (`git.toggleRepositoryShown`, per folder). A
**multi-file diff editor** (`editor.openMultiDiff`, the `multiDiff` tab): a folding diff per file,
created near the view and released far from it; for the working tree (editable), staged changes,
a commit and the Graph's incoming / outgoing rows.

**Debugger and testing:** DAP `startDebugging` (child sessions under their parent, stopped with
it); a disassembly tab that follows the paused frame, loads more as it scrolls, toggles
instruction breakpoints in its margin and steps by instruction while focused. **Node output:**
with `"console": "internalConsole"` or `"outputCapture": "std"` the program now runs with pipes,
as VS Code does: stdout and stderr apart (stderr colored), no input. This reverses D227's choice
of keeping it in a terminal for input; VS Code is the reference. Run without debugging is a
session (Stop, Restart) and captured too. The WebView2 debugging-port variable is removed from
every child process. `debug/controller.ts` split (1229 → 844 lines). Coverage: functions from
lcov, Istanbul and coverage.py, next / previous uncovered line in the editor title.

**Notebooks, editor, agent:** code actions, Format cell / Format notebook, inlay hints, semantic
tokens and breadcrumbs in cells; a completion's or server's edit for another cell (auto-import)
goes to that cell; `didSave` for the joined document, with text when asked; `x = !ls`, `%time`,
`obj?` masked without moving columns. Inline HTML in Markdown nests by the browser's parser. Ghost
text follows tsconfig `paths`, package typings and barrels (3 deep) and keeps its cache through
auto-closed brackets. Skills: `Read(…)` rules cover search and file finding (Claude Code's
behavior), nested skills that clash get `folder:name`, `effort` applies mid-turn.

**Extension API:** ten language providers (definition, references, formatting and range
formatting, code actions, rename, signature help, document symbols, code lens, inlay hints,
semantic tokens) with their results checked in `workbench/extensionProviders.ts` (paths in the
folder, the extension's own commands, limits; writes need `fs.write`); `ide.ui.withProgress`
(notification with Cancel, or window); `problemMatchers` / `problemPatterns` from manifests;
**extension bisect** (`extensions.startBisect` / `bisectAnswer` / `stopBisect`, kept across
restarts beside the user's own disabled list). **Ctrl+C on Windows** (`lsp/ctrl_c.rs`): a
process can only signal a console it's attached to, and attaching changes the whole process (its
ignore-Ctrl+C flag is inherited by programs started meanwhile), so the IDE starts its own
executable as a helper (`--send-ctrl-c <pid>`) that attaches to the program's console and sends
it.

**How it was done:** five helpers in parallel, one per area, then one build and the UI scripts.
New UI scripts: `terminal-m7-8`, `git-m7-8`, `debug-m7-8`, `notebook-m7-8`, `extensions-m7-8`.
A note for later sessions: Python on this machine writes CRLF in text mode and a bash heredoc can
eat backslashes; one helper's edit put raw CR/LF into a Rust string that way.

**Verified:** `npm run check`, 1089 unit tests, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, 271 Rust tests; the
five new UI scripts pass on Windows. The full suite was stopped at 121 of 148 scripts: 100
passed, and every failure but two was one D228 already lists (missing tools, Windows focus,
Linux-only steps, the Git Bash suggestion cases). The two new ones were fixed: terminal
suggestions waited for the shell's alias list (seconds for an interactive Git Bash) before
opening, so the list is now fetched in the background; and the bisect step of `extensions-m7-8`
could end early. Rename through an extension stays a manual check (Monaco's rename box doesn't
show in a window without the focus). `dev.type` now gives named keys (Enter, Escape, arrows, F1–
F12) their legacy `keyCode`, which the editor reads; typing in a repository's commit box selects
that repository, as focusing it does.

**Left** (in 2a now): see `docs/feature-gaps.md`; the larger ones are processes after a restart,
other sites inside the browser tab, best of N in one window, and extensions providing terminals,
tasks, source control, debug adapters and file systems.

### D230 — m7.9: agents with faces, chatting with an agent, AI features in the status bar, Ctrl+` hides

**Why:** the owner found the agent setup messy and unlike the tools people know: AI feature
switches sat on the Agents page, editing anything there turned a chip to "Unsaved" (it meant "no
saved preset matches", not unsaved work), subagents were raw files, custom modes another idea
again. They pointed at xAI's Grok bot and OpenBot (multi-agent apps where each agent is a small
character with a face) and asked for a simple, clean, intuitive flow for a provider-agnostic code
IDE. Research (VS Code custom agents, Claude Code / Cursor / Codex subagents, Zed profiles, Grok
bot, OpenBot): coding tools keep agents as Markdown files with front matter; Zed, Grok and
OpenBot give a form; OpenBot creates an agent in one dialog (name, purpose, a grid of faces, a
color, a model) with suggestion templates, and shows state on the face itself (working, waiting
for you, failed). OpenBot's code is PolyForm Noncommercial: ideas only, no code; our faces are
our own design.

**One idea: an agent.** An agent is a Markdown file (Claude Code's format, so `.claude/agents`
works unchanged) with three new optional keys: `label` (the name shown), `role` (a short tag)
and `icon` (its face, `shape-color-eyes`). The same file is a helper other agents hand work to
(`delegate`, as before) and **a chat of its own**: agents are chat modes (`agentAsMode`), so
`agent.chatWith { agent }` starts a chat whose instructions, tools and model are the agent's.
- **Faces** (`core/agent/faces.ts`, `ui/AgentFace.ts`, `agent-faces.css`): eight soft body shapes,
  eight colors (`--face-1…8` in both themes) and six eye styles; an agent without `icon` gets a
  stable face from its name. States: working (eyes glance, the body breathes, a ring turns),
  waiting for you (a dot), failed (droops); still with reduced motion.
- **The editor** (`agent.newAgent`, `agent.editAgent`, `agent.duplicateAgent`, `agent.createAgent`;
  a dock tab): a big face with Shuffle, 12 candidate faces and 8 colors; templates (Code reviewer,
  Test writer, Docs writer, Refactorer, Debugger, Researcher, Blank); name, role, "What does it
  do?", instructions, model, access (Read only / Can edit files / Full), where it lives (This
  project / Just me). A new agent has one "Create agent" button; afterwards every field writes the
  file as you type (`core/agent/agentFile.ts` edits the header in place and keeps keys it doesn't
  know, e.g. Claude Code's `color` or `hooks`), with "Open file" for the raw Markdown.
- **The Chats sidebar:** an agents row under the search box (the main agent, yours, +); a click
  starts a chat with that agent, and its face shows whether it's working or waiting for you. Each
  chat row has its agent's face in the same states instead of a spinner; chats waiting for an
  answer or approval come first under **Needs you** (OpenBot). The chat's header shows the face.
- **The Agents page** is cards: the main agent (models and the model setup), your agents, the
  built-in helpers, the delegation switch, external agents. The preset chip is "Model setup":
  "<name>", "<name> · changed" (Update / Revert / Save as new) or "None", never "Unsaved".

**AI features moved** off the Agents page (they aren't agents): a sparkle in the status bar opens
the list (Edit with AI, suggestions as you type, next-edit suggestions, commit messages, memory
tidy-up) with on/off and "Choose models…" (Settings → AI in the editor), as VS Code's Copilot
menu does (`agent.aiFeatures`, `ide://ai/features`). Their defaults don't change (D172–D194).

**Ctrl+`** now matches VS Code: shown but not focused → focus it; focused → hide its region (the
shells keep running); a hidden terminal comes back (D229); a terminal moved among the editors
returns focus to the editor instead of hiding them.

**Next (not in this step):** agents working together — a lead agent and helpers that change files
in their own worktree with a merge review at the end (Grok Build and Cursor do this), handoff
buttons between agents (VS Code's `handoffs`), and group chats of several agents (Grok bot's
2–6 bot chats). Agents talking freely to each other stays experimental elsewhere (Claude Code's
agent teams are behind a flag), so it waits.

### D231 — m7.10: agents working together (group chats, handoffs, helpers in worktrees), the chat's details panel

**Why:** after D230 gave agents faces and chats of their own, the owner asked for agents that work
together, as Grok bot's teams and the coding tools' parallel helpers do, and for the details
column Claude Code's desktop app shows beside a chat (environment, context use, changes,
background tasks), visible only when the chat has room for it.

**Group chats** (`core/agent/groupChat.ts`, `extensions/agent/groupChat.ts`): a chat can have
members (agents, the main agent too): `agent.newGroupChat { members }`, "New group chat" in the
Chats sidebar, "Start a group chat with…" on a face's menu. One transcript; the speaking agent
changes per turn and each turn runs in that agent's mode (instructions, tools, model). A message
goes to the first member it @mentions (the others it names answer after, in order); with none,
the agent that spoke last answers. An agent's reply that opens a line with `@Name` (or `→ @Name`)
hands the next turn to that member, up to `agent.groupChat.maxAutoTurns` (4) agent-to-agent turns
per message; Stop ends the round. Each member is told who's in the room and to answer only its
part. Every reply records its speaker: its face, name and role show above it when the speaker
changes; the chat row and header show the members' stacked faces; the composer's `@` lists the
members.

**Handoffs** (VS Code's `handoffs:` front matter: label, agent, prompt, send): buttons under the
agent's latest reply continue the chat with the other agent (the prompt in the box, or sent),
`agent.handoff { to, prompt, send }`, and a generic "Hand to another agent…".

**Helpers in their own worktree** (`core/agent/isolatedHelpers.ts`,
`extensions/agent/isolatedHelpers.ts`): `delegate { agent, task, isolated: true }`, or an agent
whose file says `isolation: worktree` (Claude Code's subagent option), asks the user first and
starts a worktree agent for it (D193's machinery: its own branch `agent/<agent>-…`, setup, a
window; the chat in the agent's mode). The tool returns at once; the parent chat follows the
helper's state, gets its final report as a message, and a notification offers Review changes
(the worktree compare page) and Merge (`agent.applyWorktree`, which asks). At most
`agent.isolatedHelpers.max` (3) at once; refused (with a reason the model can act on) in Ask or
Plan mode, outside a git repository, for read-only agents, or at the limit. Stop:
`agent.stopHelper` (the helper's window checks for the request every 3 s; windows share only
files). `ide://agent/helpers`.

**The details panel** (`core/agent/chatDetails.ts`, `view/details.ts`, `agent-details.css`): beside
the chat when the tab fits the reading column plus the panel (`agent.detailsPanel`: auto /
always / never); narrower, a header button shows it as a sheet (Esc closes). Cards, each folding
(remembered): Environment (this computer, folder, branch, model, the agent or mode), Context
(% used of the window, a stacked bar, the parts — system prompt, built-in and MCP tools, rules
and memory, skills, conversation, attachments, free — estimated from sizes and scaled to the
provider's count, "Summarize now" from 70%), Changes (+/−, files, Review / Keep all / Undo all,
Create PR), Background (worktree helpers with Stop / Review / Merge, subagents and commands each
with its own Stop and elapsed time, N finished), Plan. `agent.toggleDetails`,
`ide://agent/details`. `agent.stopSubagents` takes an `id` for one subagent.

**Not done:** group chats on an external (ACP) agent don't route by speaker; a helper's report
is lost if its parent chat isn't open in the main window when it finishes (the notification
still shows); free conversation between agents outside a group chat (Claude Code's agent teams)
stays out.

**Verified (D231):** `npm run check`, 1133 unit tests, clippy; the new UI scripts (details,
group, isolated) and 31 of 34 agent scripts pass on Windows (`agentA-m7-6` failed before this
work; `agent-m7-2-usage` counted the Chats nav, which gained "New group chat"). Fixed while
testing: a helper whose window can't open was cleaned up through the Delete worktree command,
which asks the user — now straight through git, silently (it's the IDE's own fresh worktree);
after a handoff in a one-agent chat the new agent's name didn't show above its reply; a group's
stacked faces ran into the title next to them; Stop on one background subagent stopped them all
(`agent.stopSubagents { id }`).

### D232 — m7.11: call and type hierarchy, colors, provider details, gaps closed, an agent audit

**Why:** the owner asked for another pass over the gaps (5–10 of them), a fresh look at the agent
for edge cases, then an audit, and a new feature-gaps list with what comes next.

**Language features** (`core/lsp/hierarchy.ts`, `core/lsp/colors.ts`, tested;
`extensions/lsp/hierarchy.ts`, `hierarchyView.ts`): the client advertises `callHierarchy`,
`typeHierarchy` and `colorProvider`.
- **The view:** Show call hierarchy (Shift+Alt+H, the editor's menu) and Show type hierarchy open
  one `hierarchy` dock tab, like VS Code's view. It has a "Callers of f" header and a tree whose
  levels load as they're opened. A toolbar switch moves between incoming and outgoing calls (or
  supertypes and subtypes), and a click opens the call site.
- **When it shows:** the keys and menu items show only while the active file's server offers them
  (`editorHasCallHierarchyProvider`, `editorHasTypeHierarchyProvider`, VS Code's context keys).
- **For agents:** `lsp.callHierarchy` / `lsp.typeHierarchy` `{path, line, column, direction?,
  depth?}` return the same data, at most 200 rows; the view's state is `ide://lsp/hierarchy`.
- **Colors:** document colors go through Monaco's color provider (swatches and picker), except in
  CSS, SCSS, Less and JSON, where Monaco's own modes draw them already.

**Extension providers** (D229's leftovers):
- **Code lenses** keep their whole range.
- **Rename** gets a `prepare` step (Monaco's `resolveRenameLocation`). A range that doesn't hold
  the cursor falls back to the word; a thrown error shows at the symbol.
- **Code actions** resolve lazily (`resolve`). The worker keeps the extension's own objects, at
  most 500, until Monaco drops the list. Only `edits` is taken from the answer, as VS Code takes
  only `edit`.
- **Semantic tokens** get a `refresh()` handle and an `onDidChange` option.

The extra calls go through the existing provider call as `<id>.<part>`, so the RPC protocol is
unchanged.

**Other gaps:**
- **Multi-file diff** (`git/multiDiffFollow.ts`):
  - An open Changes / Staged changes tab follows the repository's status, 300 ms after it
    settles, without taking the focus. The top file, folds, unsaved edits and the caret stay.
  - `git.multiDiff.nextFile` / `previousFile` move between files (Ctrl+Alt+PageDown / PageUp
    while one is active, `activeMultiDiff`).
  - Both are driven from git through the view's live object for now. They belong in
    `editor/multiDiffView.ts`, which is listed as a gap.
- **Test output in color:** Jest / Vitest failures and Go keep their ANSI codes. The Test results
  tab draws them with the terminal palette (the notebook's parser); agents get plain text.
- **Debug output without a newline** shows within 100 ms. Rust reads captured output in chunks
  (`Framing::Chunks`, keeping UTF-8 characters whole). The debug console continues an unfinished
  line from the same session and stream and applies carriage returns, as VS Code does.
- **Terminal drag:** a terminal tab dropped on another terminal's middle joins it as a split
  (`terminal.join`); near the edges the dock splits as for any tab. The dock gained tab drop
  targets (`services.tabDropTarget`).
- **A skill's `model`** now holds from the next request of the turn it was loaded in, as
  `effort` did (D229), with a line in the chat. It's refused, also with a line, when the model
  isn't there or calls tools the other way (text protocol vs native).
- **Group chats through an external agent** (Claude Code, Codex…): it answers as the member whose
  turn it is, told the room and that member's instructions. Replies record their speaker, and an
  `@Name` hand-off goes on as it does with the IDE's own models.

**The agent audit** followed `docs/agent-audit.md`'s list, D229–D231 first. What was verified and
fixed:
- **Helpers in worktrees escaped the chat's tools** (high). Only "can it edit" was checked, and an
  agent whose file wasn't committed ran in Agent mode in its window.
  - A helper now gets the delegating chat's tools intersected with its agent's, plus
    `update_plan` / `ask_user`.
  - Its window's chat keeps that as `toolLimit`, saved with it, whatever mode it ends up in.
  - An agent whose tools only read is refused a worktree, as a `readOnly` one was.
- **An agent's model was ignored when chatting with it** (high).
  - The model picked in the agent editor (`agent.subagents`) now beats its file's.
  - A Claude alias (`sonnet`) resolves to the newest such model.
  - A model that isn't there is reported in the chat instead of being silently replaced.
- **Starting a helper** couldn't be stopped, and a failure left its worktree behind.
  - Stop is checked after the question and after setup; the fresh worktree then goes.
  - A failure after the worktree exists removes it, its branch and its record.
- **Group chats:**
  - A message sent while a member answers no longer steers that member: it waits and starts its
    own round, and its @mentions pick who answers.
  - A member whose agent file is gone isn't routed to (it ran in Agent mode with every tool). The
    next member answers, with a line saying so.
  - Earlier replies by other members go to the model as `[Label] …` (`toMessages`'
    `speakerLabels`), so a member doesn't take them for its own.
  - Mentions inside any code (indented fences, `~~~`, multi-backtick spans, indented code) don't
    count.
  - `handoffs:` reads column-0 lists, block scalars (`prompt: |`) and quoted commas. Buttons for
    agents that aren't there are hidden.
  - A chat whose last item is a hand-off note says "Interrupted" when reopened.
  - The details panel shows the member that answered last.
- **Names:**
  - `agent`, `plan` and `ask` are refused as agent names, since such a chat would never show.
  - Agents' modes win over settings and folder modes of the same name.
  - An exact name beats another agent's label.
- **A helper's report** used to be lost when its chat wasn't open (D231); now it waits for that
  chat.
  - It arrives when the chat opens in this window, and the notification has "Open its chat".
  - It isn't trimmed with old helpers, and it's dropped if the chat was deleted.
- **Smaller fixes:** `agent.createAgent` returns once the new agent can be chatted with. Deleting
  an agent moves its file to the app's trash.

**The audit of this round** (a fresh review of its diff) found and fixed: a carriage return at
the 100 ms flush's edge lost (progress lines garbled: it's now held for what follows, as is an
escape sequence cut at a read's edge); a helper whose agent names an external agent escaped the
tool limit (helpers run on one of the IDE's models, and a chat with a tool limit refuses an
external agent); a removed member matched by another agent's label still answered (answering
needs the agent's own mode, by exact name); a skill's model switch kept the old model's budget
and vision setting, and didn't resolve Claude aliases; the hierarchy tab could show a stale
direction's rows (late answers dropped); reloaded test output cut its first escape again; an
external group hand-off's note had no turn and came twice in a fresh agent's history.

**Left (in the feature gaps):**
- Helpers run in a window each; in-process ones are the next step.
- A report for a chat that's open in another window waits for this window.
- A group turn that fails to start keeps its routing side effects (joined members).
- Several members can't answer one message at once.
- Per-agent MCP tools and `permissionMode: acceptEdits` aren't there yet.

**Verified:**
- Checks: `npm run check`, `npm test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test --lib`.
- New UI scripts: `hierarchy-m7-11`, `gaps-m7-11` and `acp-group-m7-11`.
- Extended or affected UI scripts: `extensions-m7-8` and `group-m7-10`.
- The full UI suite: 129 of 156 scripts passed (one skipped on Windows). Of the 26 still failing,
  25 fail the same way on a build of the state before this round; the 26th, `debug-browser-m6-97`,
  says Chrome wasn't found. So this round caused none of them. They
  need tools this machine lacks (Chrome for the browser debugger, a .venv, zsh), OS window focus
  (`.monaco-editor.focused`) or timing, and stay as they were. `ui-m7-5` only needed its count
  of chat nav items updated for D231's New group chat.
- After the audit fixes: 1162 unit tests, 272 Rust tests, clippy, and 18 new and agent-related UI
  scripts all pass.

### D233 — m7.12: the rest of section 2a; agents for every project, @mentions anywhere

**Why:** the owner asked to complete all of §2a of the feature gaps. During the work they added:
- agents available in every project by default, and a Builder template;
- @-mentioning an agent in any chat, and the main agent bringing one in;
- the details panel's folding lag and the Git graph's expand lag;
- what opens while a group is maximized;
- the border beside the details panel.

The work ran as seven parallel workstreams. The lead integrated and audited them.

**Editor and notebooks:**
- **Ghost text that was found but not shown.** Monaco asks inline-completion providers again only after typing, pasting, Backspace/Delete as commands in a focused editor, or edits during an active suggestion session. So Ctrl+Backspace, cut, undo/redo and deletes after a dismissal left a cached suggestion unshown.
  - The IDE now watches each editor's deletions, undos and redos (`monaco/zones.ts`).
  - When the cache has an entry for the cursor's spot (checked without counting), it calls the controller's non-explicit trigger. The cache answers and the model is never asked. This uses Monaco's internal controller, so a Monaco upgrade may move it.
- **Import context asks the file's language server first.** Each imported name gets a `textDocument/definition` request: at most 16 names, 700 ms, cancelled on the next key, cached for 30 s. The regex covers the rest (`ide://editor/inlineCompletions` `last.importsVia`).
- **Format notebook is one undo step.**
- **Cells' semantic tokens:** sent as deltas, and other cells are asked again only when their part changed.
- **A server edit across cells** is clipped to each cell (`ConcatDocument.splitEdit`).
- **`notebook/view.ts` was split:** `notebookFile.ts` and `cellHost.ts`.
- **The hierarchy tab** gained:
  - Refresh (`lsp.refreshHierarchy`);
  - "Show hierarchy of this item" (`lsp.showHierarchyOfItem`);
  - a row menu: Go to definition, Copy path;
  - a "Results may be outdated" bar after an edit or save in a file the tree points into, rather than rebuilding under the user.
- **Coverage branch columns** are drawn before the character (`GutterMark.columns` in `setLineMarks`).

**Terminal and tasks:**
- **Terminals survive a window reload** (VS Code's process revival).
  - When the main page reloads, Rust detaches its terminals instead of killing them and keeps their output in a 1 MiB ring with byte offsets.
  - The reloaded page takes each one back by id and a per-terminal secret from the tab state (`pty_attach`), draws the saved screen, then gets the bytes after the offset it reflects, then live output.
  - A page token keeps a new page's own terminals attached.
  - A terminal not taken back within 60 s is killed with its process tree. A real quit still ends everything.
- **Hidden terminals** are saved with the folder (`terminal.hidden`) and come back hidden.
- **The IDE starts ConPTY children itself on Windows** (`pty/conpty.rs`):
  - It loads a bundled `conpty.dll` by full path when `OpenConsole.exe` is beside it.
  - It creates children suspended, adds them to the job object, then resumes them. This closes D180's race; `job::spawn` does the same for std Commands.
  - It passes cmd.exe a verbatim `/d /s /c "<line>"`, so tasks with quotes work.
- **A WSL folder** applies tasks.json's `linux` blocks.
- **The newer ConPTY** is wired through `gen.mjs` and `scripts/fetch-conpty.mjs`. Only the owner's fetch of Microsoft's two files remains (`docs/windows-pending.md`).

**Browser preview:**
- **Sites inside the tab.** Other sites can show inside the tab (`browser.embedSites`, off until checked by hand) through Tauri's multi-webview API.
  - This is the `unstable` feature of the tauri crate already used: no new dependency, and Cargo.lock is unchanged (AGENTS.md rule 3).
  - The child webview follows the tab's page area. It hides while the tab is hidden or an IDE overlay covers it, and shows the last snapshot meanwhile.
  - Linux, and any failure, fall back to the site's own window.
- **What the feature changed in the IDE itself.** It makes every webview a child webview, so:
  - "main" is looked up by window or webview;
  - drops come from webview events;
  - the default capability is granted by webview label, so an embedded site in window "main" gets no IDE commands;
  - site webviews refuse the IDE's own origins.
- **Popups between tabs** act like cross-origin windows:
  - `document` throws a SecurityError;
  - `opener.location` navigates the opener's tab;
  - named targets reuse their tab.
- **A form POSTed into a new tab** keeps its body (a passing page, `/__ide/post`).
- **Downloads** get an IDE list: the `downloads` tab, a status entry, the `browser.*Download*` commands and `ide://downloads`. Windows has progress and cancel.
- **The preview proxy** streams request bodies and HTML. It inserts the bridge once `<head>` is seen.
- **Popped-out pages** come back popped out after a restart.

**Git, debugger, testing:**
- **Movable sidebar views.** A view whose descriptor says `movable` can become a `sidebarView` dock tab, as VS Code's views move between containers.
  - It moves with `view.moveView`, the section menu, or a drag either way.
  - Where it is persists with the dock.
  - Source control's Graph is the first such view.
- **The Graph's expand lag** came from reading each commit's full detail: its `--shortstat` diffs every file (0.5–0.7 s for 504 files).
  - Files now come from one `git diff --name-status` (0.09 s), with details and lists cached per commit.
  - The tree's sticky rows stopped copying every row each frame (0.23 → 0.03 ms).
  - The list pages on scroll (`git.graph.pageOnScroll`), up to 10 000 commits.
- **The multi-file diff's following and next / previous file** moved into the editor's view: `background` on `editor.openMultiDiff`, and `editor.multiDiff.nextFile` / `previousFile`.
- **`debug/index.ts` was split** (1034 → 286 lines).
- **Coverage per test:**
  - pytest's dynamic contexts and lcov's `TN:`;
  - `tests.showCoverageForTest`, `tests.coveredBy`;
  - VS Code's floating coverage toolbar (`testing.coverageToolbarEnabled`).
- **Test runs force colors:** `FORCE_COLOR`, `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, pytest `--color=yes`. Results are parsed from the plain text, and each test's own output keeps its colors.

**Agent:**
- **A skill's model can take over mid-turn even when it calls tools the other way.** The switch runs before the step's messages are built, and the history is written in the new model's protocol.
- **A helper's report** for a chat open in another window goes to a store every window reads (`agent/reports.rs`). A claim renames the file, so exactly one window takes it.
- **Group routing is pure:** it's committed only when the turn starts, so a message a hook stops brings nobody in.
- **@mentions in a chat with one agent** turn it into a group, and the named agent answers. In the composer, "@" in any chat lists the agents, marking the ones that would join. The main agent can bring one in with `agent.inviteAgent`, and the delegate tool explains delegating vs inviting.
- **The details panel:**
  - Its context split uses the speaker's mode.
  - Folding a card redraws at once from the last data. It used to wait for the 250 ms throttle and recompute the context sizes.
  - It lost its left border.
- **The worktree overview** follows the saved-chats folder instead of a 2 s timer.
- **@docs:**
  - It can search by meaning through a configured embedding model (`agent.docs.embeddings.enabled`, off by default; BM25 fused with similarity, words as the fallback).
  - It can read pages that need JavaScript in a hidden incognito window (`agent.docs.renderJavaScript`, off; same origin only).
- **The stdio MCP proxy** opens the server's GET stream.
- **External agents:**
  - Without git, an external agent's turn compares a listing of the folder (`agent/tree.rs`). Git-ignored files no step names stay out, as in VS Code.
  - A user's save after the agent's write keeps the agent's change.
  - Codex's `/status` becomes `planLimits`.
