- **Best of N in one window** stays a design note in the agent README. It needs per-chat folder scoping in the tools, Rust's fs scope and the index.
- **New agents are saved in the user's agents folder by default**, so they're in every project. "Every project" comes first in Where it lives, and `agent.createAgent` defaults to `user`.
- **A Builder template** (first): it carries out an agreed plan, step by step, and checks it.

**Workbench and command line:**
- **Empty windows come back with their unsaved untitled text,** as in VS Code.
  - A backup per window is kept under the window registry.
  - The next start reopens it (`--restore-empty <id>`).
  - Closing an empty window while others run asks first.
- **macOS and Linux menus** (written on Windows, unverified):
  - macOS gets the Dock menu: `applicationDockMenu:` added to tao's delegate class, with no new dependency.
  - Linux gets a desktop New window action.
- **The shell command:**
  - On macOS it links into `/usr/local/bin` through the administrator prompt, falling back to `~/.local/bin`.
  - Plain `<cli>` through the Windows shim now detaches.
- **A file named on the command line in folders that don't exist** is created on save.
- **Maximized groups:** while a group is maximized, what opens without a place of its own goes into it. Bringing forward a tab behind it restores the layout. Background activations leave it.

**The command review:** `core/permissions/commandGuards.ts` runs for non-user callers before the policy.
- **`editor.runAction`** reached the IDE's own engine commands, which run any IDE command as the user. It now has an allowlist of engine actions and refuses files outside the folder.
- **`editor.openMultiDiff`'s `refresh`** is now user-only.
- **`lsp.setServerSetting*`** is refused to extensions (those settings can name programs).

The lead also fixed what the review listed for other owners:
- An extension's lens and code-action commands run only if its own answers carried them.
- `ui.copyText` and `explorer.copyPath` need the clipboard permission.
- Resolving a deleted-file conflict trashes the file.
- `workspace.mergeFolder`'s `confirm: false` is honored only for the user.

**Extension API:** the workbench providers VS Code has. Every callback uses the existing provider call (the protocol is unchanged), and features read DOM-free registries on `extensionFeatures`.
- **Terminals:** a pseudoterminal served in the page through a virtual pty, so its tabs are ordinary terminal tabs, plus `createTerminal`.
- **Task providers** with `taskDefinitions`.
- **Source controls:** a section of the Source control view, with its count joining git's badge and a quick diff fallback.
- **Debug adapters:** executable, server or inline, from `debuggers`.
- **Authentication providers.** Another extension's session requires the user's Allow. `ide.secrets` live in the OS keychain under an id Rust builds from the extension's id.
- **File system providers:** a scheme the editor reads and saves through, shown in the Explorer.

**The audit of this round** (a fresh read of its diff) found no critical hole and nine fixes:
sites embedded in tabs outlived a page reload, drawn over the new page (`page_loaded` closes the
window's embedded webviews); an embedded site opened twice, or closed while opening, leaked a
webview (each open is numbered, a superseded one closes itself); with revival off a reload left the
old terminals, dev servers included, running for the grace period (the terminal extension ends the
detached ones at once, `pty_kill_detached`); `agent.inviteAgent` let an extension or MCP client
change a chat's members and counted an agent's invitation as the user's (now refused to them, and
counted against maxAutoTurns with the inviter named); `editor.runAction` could still apply a code
action whose command runs as the user (the code-action, quick fix, source, refactor, organize
imports and fix-all actions are refused to other callers); the shared reports store dropped a
report on a transient read error (it's left, or put back, for the next look); a maximized group
took views that name their own place (only those without one, the others restore the layout when
brought forward); downloads of programs and scripts were saved without WebView2's prompt (they
keep it); Dock-menu launches on macOS weren't reaped.

**The UI test round** (fixing the full suite's failures on Windows) found real bugs too:
- On Windows the IDE couldn't find Chrome or Edge to debug a page, because its file access is
  limited to the workspace and the app's folders. A Rust command (`debug_find_browser`) now looks
  in both Program Files folders, LOCALAPPDATA, Windows' App Paths and PATH.
- Language-server documents were tracked by raw path, and Monaco's lower-case drive letter
  (`c:\…`) made one file look like two. A request could then re-open it from disk and close it, so
  the server lost the editor's unsaved text. The client now tracks documents by URI, and an editor
  takes over a document a request opened for itself (`openTemporarily`).
- Terminals started through ConPTY took their environment from the registry, which dropped the
  PATH the IDE was started with (a venv, nvm). The IDE's own PATH now comes first, then the
  registry's additions.
- Detected tasks are written in POSIX form when the task shell is POSIX (Git Bash as the default
  profile), instead of `.\x.cmd`, which bash mangled.
- An extension's debug adapter is no longer looked for on PATH under its label.
- The merge editor's keep/delete choice for a deleted file now reaches `git.stage`.
- IDE screenshots are git-ignored inside the workspace's IDE folder.
- `ide://notebook` lists the notebooks' real paths, not lookup keys.
- A terminal no longer takes focus late, after its shell starts, once focus has moved elsewhere.

Tests that assumed `/` separators, a focused textarea (Monaco now types into
`.native-edit-context`), Linux fonts, `make` or zsh were fixed to check the same behavior. `make`
gets a stand-in on PATH (`"fakeMake": true`, `tests/fixtures/fake-make`), and the zsh, xdotool and
Linux-profile steps moved to their own scripts marked for those platforms.

**Verified:** `npm run check`, 1252 unit tests, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and the Rust tests. The
full UI suite ran once: 133 of 167 passed, 2 skipped. Each script fixed since then was rerun alone
and passes, along with the related ones (about 30), including `group-m7-10`. Still failing, and
not caused by this round:
- terminal command marks under the system ConPTY (`terminal-m6-49`, `features-m6-22`,
  `terminal-m7-7`) and the suggest widget in Git Bash (`gaps10-m7-6` steps 30–31);
- auto-attach to a forked child or worker on Windows (`debug-m7-5`) and the compound debug step
  of `parA-m7-6`;
- `target=_blank` and `window.open` in WebView2 (`browser-m7-6`, `browser-m7-12`);
- Pyright not installed (`notebooks-m7-5`), `notebook-ext-m7-3`, and ghost text in a file with
  imports (`ghost-text-m7-7`).

**Left (in the feature gaps):**
- The UI failures just above.
- Best of N in one window.
- Accounts menu entries for extension providers.
- A provider file system's change doesn't reload an open editor; no rename/delete UI there.
- A task terminal taken back after a reload isn't re-linked to its task.
- The macOS and Linux parts, the embedded browser, downloads' WebView2 bubble and the hidden render window need a hand check.
- The ConPTY binaries need the owner's fetch.
- `session.ts`, `acp.ts`, `rpc.ts` and `browser/view.ts` are a little over 1200 lines.

### D234 — m7.13: the main agent's name and face, chat tabs with faces, a wider extension API

**Why:** in a group chat the owner asked Rev about the project. The main agent looked busy while
Rev worked, and "[Agent]" showed up in Rev's reply. They also asked for:
- a main agent they can name and give a face to;
- chat tabs that show which agents are in each chat;
- D233's extension API leftovers;
- an extension API that can carry ports of the most-used VS Code extensions.

**Agent:**
- **"[Agent]" in a member's reply.** A member's replies got their `speaker` only when its turn
  ended. Within the turn, each later request therefore labelled the member's own earlier steps as
  the main agent's (`[Agent]`, and a lone `[Agent]` for a step that only called tools), and the
  model copied the tag into its reply.
  - The loop now gives each reply its speaker when it's created (`core/agent/loop.ts`).
  - A step with only tool calls gets no label.
  - A leading `[Name]` in a group reply is taken out (`conversation.ts` `stripSpeakerTag`; Markdown
    links are left alone).
- **The main agent looked busy while Rev worked.** The chats bar showed each agent's busiest chat
  by the chat's mode, and a group chat's mode is the main agent's. It now goes by the member whose
  turn it is. `session.speaking` is a signal under `turnSpeaker`, so a hand-off within a round
  moves the busy face too.
- **The main agent's name and face** are user settings: `agent.mainAgent.name` and
  `agent.mainAgent.icon`.
  - Set them on the Agents page (a name field; the face opens the agent editor's face picker) or
    with `agent.setMainAgent`. State: `ide://agent/mainAgent`.
  - They're used in the chats bar, the chat header, group chats (labels, faces, the room brief,
    "@Name") and the Chat with picker.
  - Its member id stays `agent`, so saved chats, mentions and hand-offs survive a rename.
  - The system prompt doesn't name it: that prompt is shared with the user's own agents' solo
    chats, and in group chats the room brief already gives the name.
- **A chat's tab shows its agents' faces:** the group's faces, or its one agent in its state
  (working, waiting). Dock view descriptors' `iconElement` may now return undefined, which falls
  back to `icon`.

**Extension API: the D233 leftovers.**
- The Accounts menu lists extension sign-in providers' accounts.
- A provider file system's change events reach open editors: an unmodified one reloads, a
  modified one shows "changed on disk".
- Its Explorer section creates, renames and deletes through the provider: `extensions.fsNewFile`,
  `fsNewFolder`, `fsRename` and `fsDelete` (destructive, so it's confirmed).
- A restored tab of a provider's scheme waits up to 15 s for the provider. Extensions that declare
  the new `onFileSystem:<scheme>` activation event start for it.
- `editor.getText`, `editor.replaceRange` and `ide.editor.*` accept registered provider URIs,
  under the same `fs.read` / `fs.write` checks.

**Extension API: new.** `docs/extensions.md` now has a "Coverage versus VS Code" table: what the
most-used VS Code extensions need, against what's here. Added:
- **Ten language providers:** type definition, implementation, declaration, highlights, folding,
  links, colors, on-type formatting, inline completions and workspace symbols (merged into
  Ctrl+T).
  - Links open only web addresses, or files in the folder.
  - On-type formatting needs `fs.write`.
  - An extension's inline completions are its own feature, not the IDE's AI completions (rule 8
    doesn't apply).
- **Decoration types.** Colors are theme names or VS Code ThemeColor ids (which follow the theme),
  or literal colors that are validated before they reach a stylesheet. So Better Comments or
  indent-rainbow colors that a user chose work. At most 50 per extension.
- **Also new:**
  - the active editor's change, selection and visible-range events;
  - `findFiles` (from the file index, honoring .gitignore) and file watchers;
  - `settings.update` (through `settings.set` and its checks) and `workspaceState`;
  - `env`: `appName`, `language`, `openExternal` (web and mail links only) and the clipboard
    (needs the `clipboard` permission);
  - quick pick separators and password input;
  - `registerDebugConfigurationProvider` with `resolveDebugConfiguration`. Its result merges into
    the launch, but `type` and `request` and launch.json's own `program` / `args` / `cwd` win.
- **Left** (see the feature gaps):
  - webview panels at run time;
  - a Testing API;
  - `provideDebugConfigurations`;
  - Vim's `type` override;
  - URI handlers, comments, chat and `lm`;
  - workbench color customizations;
  - multi-select quick pick.
- `rpc.ts` was split; the language API lives in `rpcLanguages.ts` (976 lines left).

**Trade-off:** an editor tab for a scheme no provider serves now waits 15 s before it shows its
error, where it used to show it at once. That's the price of restoring provider tabs.

**Verified:** `npm run check`, 1271 unit tests and clippy pass. New UI scripts `agent-m7-13` and
`extensions-m7-13` pass. Related scripts also pass: `group-m7-10`, `acp-group-m7-11`,
`agent-m7-12`, `extensions-m7-12`, `extensions-m7-8` and `extensions-api`. The full suite wasn't
rerun (the owner asked for spot checks). Restoring a provider tab after a restart was only
checked by unit tests.

### D235 — m7.14: a group member's own model in a chat on an external agent
**Context:** in a group chat on Codex, Rev (set to OpenRouter on the Agents page) answered as
Codex: D232 had the external agent play every member, so a member's own model was ignored there,
though it's used in chats on the IDE's own models. Separately, adding an agent left an open group
chat's header with a stand-in face for a member until the chat was reopened.
**Decision:** a member whose agent file names an IDE model answers on it, through the IDE's loop,
even in a chat on an external agent; "Same as the chat", an `acp/…` model or a model that isn't
there keeps the external agent. The external agent's own session didn't see that reply, so its
next message carries what was said since its last turn (`session.externalSeen`), with speakers
named, as do its recaps. The chat header's face effect reads the agents list, so it redraws when
the list changes.
**Alternatives:** keep the external agent for every member and label the reply honestly (simpler,
but the Agents page's model choice would mean nothing in those chats); start a second external
agent session per member (heavier, and only for external models).
**Verified:** `npm run check` and 1272 unit tests pass. New UI script `acp-group-m7-14` passes
(Rev on mock Ollama in a chat on the mock ACP agent; the ACP agent sees Rev's reply on its first
start and again mid-chat). `acp-group-m7-11`, `agent-m7-13` and `group-m7-10` pass. The full
suite wasn't rerun.

### D236 — m7.14: "+ ▾", which agent a new chat starts with
**Context:** + in the Chats view and in a chat's header always started a chat with the main agent;
a chat with another agent or a group chat was a few clicks away (the agents row, a command).
**Decision:** a narrow ▾ beside each + (VS Code's "+ ▾" in its chat and terminal panels, already
the terminal's here) opens `agent.newChatMenu`: the main agent and the user's agents with their
faces and roles, New group chat…, and from a group chat a new chat with the same agents. + itself
is unchanged, so the common case stays one click. `MenuItem.iconElement` puts a face in a menu's
icon slot; the sidebar's `ViewAction.dropdown` mirrors the dock's `TabAction.dropdown`.
**Alternatives:** make + itself open the menu (an extra click for the common case); a split button
component (heavier than reusing the dock's ▾).
**Verified:** `npm run check` and the unit tests pass. New UI script `agent-m7-14` passes. Related
scripts `agents-row-m7-9`, `details-m7-10` and `agent-m7-13` pass. `gaps10-m7-6` failed its terminal
suggestion steps twice (the popup needs the test window to have keyboard focus; terminal code
wasn't touched), so that wasn't verified this round.

### D237 — m7.15: channels, direct messages and threads (Slack's layout), on its own branch
**Context:** the owner wants the agent side to feel like Slack (and later Linear) rather than a
chat list: people now describe agent tools as "Slack, then Linear" (OpenBot's channels and Tasks
inbox; Slack's own August 2026 agent DMs, Agents tab and Slack Code task channels). The Chats list
grouped chats by day, every chat opened a tab, and group chats were ad hoc.
**Decision:** a dramatic overhaul on the `channels` branch (the earlier version is kept on
`classic-chats`):
- The sidebar becomes **Inbox / Channels / Direct messages**. A channel is a named room with
  standing agents and a purpose; a direct message is one agent's room. Every chat is a **thread**
  in one of them, with its own context, so a channel never becomes one endless conversation.
- The middle shows **one channel** (a timeline of threads, a message box that starts one); the
  right shows **one thread** (the existing chat view). Both reuse their tab (VS Code's preview
  tabs); pinning or "new tab" keeps one.
- Every folder starts with `#general` and a **team**: the main agent (named after the IDE) plus
  Builder, Reviewer and Tester, built from the agent templates and replaceable by a file.
- Agents can use channels: `agent.startThread` and `ide://agent/channels` aren't hidden from them.
- In code, channels are "rooms" (a Tauri Channel is something else here).
**Not taken from OpenBot** (whose license, PolyForm Noncommercial, allows learning from its design
but not copying its code): an AI coordinator that routes each message (an extra model call that
can fail; our @mention / last-speaker routing stays), a workspace folder per agent, running agents
without approvals.
**Later:** threads in a channel reading each other (a tool), channel memory, unread state, Slack
Code's task channels (a channel per big task, closed when done), a Linear-style board over the
Inbox.
**Also changed on the way:** a closed tab's view element now leaves the page (groups kept it,
hidden; replaced thread tabs made it show); the user's own chat modes win over a team agent of the
same name; the team's Reviewer keeps the built-in reviewer subagent's instructions (delegating a
review works as before).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, 1278 unit tests, new UI script `channels-m7-15`, and the full UI
suite: every agent script passes (old ones updated for the new sidebar and the main agent's name).
Eleven scripts fail on this machine on both branches alike (a build of `classic-chats` fails the
same steps): browser-m7-6 and -m7-12, debug-m7-5, parA-m7-6, notebooks-m7-5, notebook-ext-m7-3,
terminal-m6-49 and -m7-7, gaps10-m7-6, features-m6-22, fixes-m7-4; they're not from this change.

### D238 — m7.15: channels are conversations, threads are optional
**Context:** D237 made every message in a channel start a separate chat: you couldn't talk in a
channel, which isn't how Slack, OpenBot or Grok's group chats work, and the owner found it
confusing.
**Decision:** a channel is a conversation: opening it shows its chat (the chat view on
`Room.session`) and you talk there with its agents (@Name picks who). A direct message is an
ordinary chat with one agent; @mentioning another brings them in (the group chat rules, D231).
Threads are optional: **Reply in thread** on any message starts a side conversation on the right,
told the message it answers; the message shows its replies. Also finished from D237's list:
- **Unread:** when each conversation was last seen; bold rows and an Inbox count.
- **Channel memory:** notes told to every conversation in the channel; agents can add them.
- **Agents reading conversations:** `agent.readThread`.
- **Task channels** (Slack Code's): a channel per task, opened with the task, closed and archived
  with a summary.
- **The Inbox as a board** (Linear's columns: Needs you, Working, Failed, Done), cards moving as
  the agents work.
**Context growth:** a channel's conversation can get long; the chat's own compaction applies, and
**New conversation** starts it over.
**Also:** the Channels sidebar's rows line up with its search box (the owner's report); UI tests
can build into `src-tauri/target-uitest` while a dev build holds `target`.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, 1283 unit tests, `channels-m7-15` (talking in #general, Reply in
thread, the replies row, memory, reading a conversation, a task channel, the board, one tab each)
and `agent-m7-14`, then 64 agent scripts: all pass except `features-m6-22` (fails the same on
`classic-chats`) and two that pass on a rerun (`ghost-text-m7-7`; `agent-m7-1`, which types
before a new file's editor is ready, as `fixes-m7-4` does).

### D239 — m7.15: start free with OpenCode
**Context:** a first-time user had to add a key, run a local model or sign in to an agent CLI
before the agent could do anything. OpenBot starts at once: it runs the OpenCode CLI as an
external agent with no key, and OpenCode serves its free models to anyone (its free tier, on
opencode.ai). OpenRouter's free models still need an account and a key (50 requests a day).
**Decision:** OpenCode is a fifth preset agent (`opencode acp`, installed with
`npm install -g @opencode/cli`, OpenCode 2, run as `opencode2 acp`), next to Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot, and
counts as the ACP registry's `opencode`. An empty chat with no model shows **Start free with
OpenCode** under Set up AI models: `agent.startFree` installs it when it's missing (in a
terminal, without the sign-in step other agents get) and makes it the chat's agent. An OpenCode account or key later: its row's Sign in
(`opencode2 auth login`) adds its paid models. OpenCode 2 and not
OpenCode 1 (`opencode-ai`): both share one database, and OpenCode 1 can't open one OpenCode 2 made
("Database is not empty and has no session table", the owner hit it); `opencode2` is OpenCode 2's
own command name, so an OpenCode 1 on PATH never answers instead. A CLI's error text has its
terminal colors removed before the chat shows it.
**Easy to remove:** the start is all in `freeStart.ts` (two calls in `index.ts`); if OpenCode drops
its free tier, delete those and keep OpenCode as an ordinary preset.
**Not done:** checking OpenCode's terms for an app offering its CLI this way (OpenBot keeps a
provider-terms doc for that). **Its icon:** a preset agent without a logo in `src/assets/brands`
shows the icon its ACP registry entry has (`brandMark.ts` `presetIcon`), which OpenCode publishes
there; a logo file from OpenCode's brand kit would replace it.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, the catalog and registry unit tests, UI scripts `free-start-m7-15`
(the card in an empty chat, OpenCode on the AI models page; not clicked, since it installs with
npm) and `agent-m6-62`.

### D240 — m7.15: an empty chat greets you
**Context:** an empty chat said "Ask, or describe a change", which model answers, and two tips on
what the agent can do; modern chat apps just greet ("Good morning, Sam", "What are we building
today?"). The owner shared the lines Codevre (their web IDE) uses.
**Decision:** an empty chat shows one greeting line, picked at random and kept for that chat
(`core/agent/greetings.ts`, tested): a set for a folder with a project and one for no folder,
with the user's first name when their IDE account is signed in (`ide://accounts`, read now and
then), and lines for the time of day only at that time. No tips and no model line (the composer
shows the model). When no model can answer yet, the greeting comes with what's missing and the
setup buttons, as before.

### D241 — m7.15: empty chats follow the main agent; the team is the user's; open to the side
**Context:** after Start free picked OpenCode, Builder's direct messages still showed the setup
card: its conversation had been made earlier (when the channels loaded), and a chat took the main
agent's choice only when it was created, never when opened by id. The built-in team couldn't be
edited or deleted ("built in: duplicate it"). And a channel or thread always took over its tab,
with no way to see two side by side but dragging.
**Decision:**
- A chat with nothing in it follows the main agent's choice when it changes (an external agent,
  or back to the IDE's models), and one opened by id that was never saved takes it
  (`sessions.ts` `applyMain`).
- Builder, Reviewer and Tester are written once into the user's agents folder as ordinary agent
  files (`subagents.ts` `seedTeam`, global state `teamAgentsSeeded`): edited, renamed or deleted
  like the user's own, a deleted one doesn't come back, and with no model line they use the
  chat's. The `team` source of D237 is gone.
- **Open to the side** (`agent.openChannel` / `agent.openThread` `side`, `threadTabs.ts`
  `openBeside`): a tab that stays, in a new group split to the right of the chats. In the
  sidebar's right-click menus (channels, direct messages) and the Inbox's cards.

### D242 — m7.15: an agent's chat runs on the agent's model
**Context:** Builder set to openrouter/free on the Agents page, the main agent on Claude Code:
Builder's direct messages showed Claude Code in the composer and answered as Claude Code. D235
let a group member on its own model answer on it in a chat on an external agent, but a chat with
one agent never looked at that agent's model.
**Decision:**
- A chat with one of the user's agents runs on that agent's own model when it has one (the turn
  goes through the IDE's loop on it, as for a group member, D235); "Same as the chat" keeps the
  chat's (`chatAgentModel.ts`).
- Its composer pill shows that agent's model, and picking a model there sets the agent's model
  (`agent.setSubagent`), as the Agents page does. Picking an external agent (an agent's own model
  can't be one) puts the agent back on "Same as the chat" and the chat on it.
- A group chat's pill says **Models** and opens each agent with its model (own, or the chat's);
  picking one changes that agent's (`agent.chooseModel` subagent / main), with Agents and models…
  at the end.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, unit tests, UI scripts `agent-m7-7-picker`, `group-m7-10`,
`acp-group-m7-14`, `agents-row-m7-9`. The solo agent chat on an external main agent wasn't
scripted (it needs Claude Code): to check by hand.

### D243 — m7.15: a group chat's agent reads your message while it works
**Context:** in a group chat (#general), a message sent while an agent worked waited until the
agent's whole turn was done (D232, so its @mentions could pick who answered next). The owner wrote
"dont build anything bro" while Builder was making tool calls, and Builder kept going.
**Decision:** a message sent mid-turn in a group chat reaches the agent answering now at its next
step (as in a chat with one agent, D151), so it can stop or change course; one that @mentions a
different agent still waits and starts that agent's turn when this one ends. The note under the
waiting message says which. External agents (Claude Code, Codex…) still take it after their turn:
ACP has no way to add a message to a running turn.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, unit tests, UI scripts `agent-m6-50`, `agent-m6-72`, `group-m7-10`.

### D244 — m7.15: an audit of the channels, the agent's turns and the UI before the alpha
**Context:** after D237–D243 the owner asked for a full audit before the alpha. Four read-only
reviews ran in parallel: the channels and threads code, the agent's turn logic compared with
OpenBot, the UI and edge cases, and release readiness. Each finding was checked in the code before
it was fixed.
**Fixed:**
- **Agents can't act as the user:** a post to a channel, a thread or a task channel by an agent
  is marked "(Posted by an agent, not the user.)", can't run a slash command, and asks first (the
  commands' effects are `write`, so the permission gate applies); an agent opens at most 8 task
  channels; a note an agent keeps in a channel's memory is shown to the user, and the brief says
  notes are information, not instructions. `agent.readThread` reads only this folder's
  conversations and makes nothing to read.
- **Channels survive a restart:** a channel's or DM's conversation that was never saved gets its
  room and agents again once loaded; the channels' state restores before the dock (a new `early`
  flag on state contributors), so a restored channel tab opens the saved conversation; a tab for
  a channel that's gone shows the Inbox.
- **Tabs:** a preview tab replaces only previews of its own kind (`previewKind`), so opening a
  thread no longer closes its channel; Open to the side opens before closing (it deleted a tab
  alone in its group); New conversation replaces every tab of that room; a chat holding a draft,
  attachments or a waiting folder question isn't reused for another chat.
- **The agent's turns:** an external agent's steps reach an IDE model as text (their names,
  `acp:execute`, aren't valid tool names for providers); Stop while an external agent is starting
  stops it; a handoff to an agent no longer in the chat ends the round with a notice; a message
  sent as a round moves on is queued, not refused; a Retry or Edit doesn't repeat the hooks'
  context; what an external agent last saw is saved (a restart doesn't lose what it missed); a
  group chat's summary keeps who said what.
- **Names:** "inbox" is reserved; a bare name is an agent's DM before a channel of that name
  ("#name" for the channel); `dm:Builder` and `dm:builder` are one conversation; restoring an
  archived channel checks its name is free.
- **Performance and focus:** the thread list publishes at most every 150 ms and only when
  something shown changed (the sidebar and the Inbox were rebuilt on every streamed chunk); seen
  is marked at most once a second; a chat's threads per message are worked out once per list; the
  saved-chat list refreshes every 30 s and only while the window is in front; the sidebar and the
  Inbox keep keyboard focus on the same row across a redraw (`ui/focusKeep.ts`).
- **Terminal cursor:** our own hide and show carry a private OSC marker (counting could blame the
  program's sequence); while output streams, a program's plain `?25h` (ConPTY sends one with each
  repaint) waits until the output pauses.
- **UI:** archiving asks first and **Archived channels…** brings one back; the header buttons'
  accessible names match their tooltips; the model picker in an agent's DM says it sets that
  agent's model everywhere; a message with several threads lists them; the greeting doesn't change
  under you when the account name arrives; the sidebar is a `nav` with groups (not a tree without
  tree keys); the replies link uses `--accent-text`; the Inbox board fits its columns to the width.
- **Start free** checks npm is there first and opens the Node.js download if not. The guide and the
  manual tests caught up with D237–D243; the activity bar menu says Channels; the history is
  "Sessions…" everywhere; the dev build's `dist` cleanup retries on Windows.
**Not fixed:** listed in `docs/feature-gaps.md` §1 "From the D244 audit" and §4.


### D245 — m7.16: the planner and Chat on the team, @all, follow-ups, agents from a description, Recent
**Context:** the owner's list from `docs/feature-gaps.md` §4 (generate an agent, follow-ups to a
running helper or subagent, several members answering at once and `@all`, per-agent MCP tools and
permission keys) plus asks: the most common workflow is planner, builder and chat; recent chats in
the sidebar; quieter focus on fields; the Extensions filter like the other side bar searches.
**Decision:**
- **The team** is Planner (read-only, hands an agreed plan to `@Builder`), Builder and Chat
  (read-only, talks things through, hands work on). Reviewer and Tester stay as templates (Code
  reviewer, Test writer) in the agent editor. Seeding is per agent now (`teamAgentsWritten`; the
  old flag stands for the first team), so a user who had the first team gets the planner and Chat
  once and keeps theirs. A `#general` still exactly as the first team left it gets the new agents
  (`withNewTeam`); a changed one is left alone. The members pill's menu shows each agent's face.
- **`@all` / `@everyone`** (`mentionsEveryone`, `routeTogether`): every member answers. The one
  whose turn it is answers with its tools; the others at the same time (`groupTogether.ts`), on
  their own models, read-only, from the conversation so far, without seeing each other's answers.
  Their answers join the chat when the turn is over: one in the middle of the turn's tool calls
  would split a call from its result. `agent.groupChat.answerTogether` (off) does the same for
  several `@Name`s; off, they answer one after another as before. An external agent's turn queues
  them instead. "@" suggests `@all` in a group chat.
- **Follow-ups:** a background subagent takes messages (`message` on its record, read before its
  next model call through `takeQueued`); a worktree helper too (`sendToHelper`, D246). The agent
  has `message_subagent` (the ids are in delegate's results); the user has
  `agent.messageSubagent` and a button on the subagent's row in the chat's details.
- **Agent files:** `mcp__server__tool` and `mcp__server` (or `mcp__server__*`) in `tools` are kept
  (ours are named as Claude Code names them); `disallowedTools` removes tools whatever `tools`
  says, for delegated runs and the agent's chat; `permissionMode: acceptEdits` keeps the agent's
  edits without review in its chat (the protected-path and risky-folder questions still ask).
  `bypassPermissions` stays unsupported.
- **Generate an agent** (`agent.generateAgent`, **Describe it…** in a draft): a model drafts
  label, role, description, instructions and access as JSON (`core/agent/agentDraft.ts`, tested);
  the draft opens for checking. It runs only when asked, so like Generate commit message (D173)
  it isn't behind an `….enabled` setting; the owner asked for it (AGENTS.md rule 8). It uses the
  memory tidy-up's model (the agent's own upkeep) rather than a new model setting.
- **Recent** in the Channels sidebar: every conversation by time, this folder's first, then other
  folders' saved chats (all by time with no folder open); 8, then Show more (40) and All
  sessions…. Another folder's chat opens with the "Started in" banner (Open it / Continue here).
- **Focus:** text fields show focus with their accent border only (the chat prompt's way): no
  2px ring and no halo. Buttons, rows and toggles keep the ring (DESIGN.md §11). The Extensions
  filter is a plain `.input` like Search's and Channels'.
- **Code health:** `acp.ts` → `acpAgents.ts`, `mcp.ts` → `mcpConfigFiles.ts`, `view/view.ts` →
  `view/permissionCards.ts`, `session.ts` split, `pty/mod.rs` → `pty/shell.rs` (D77).
**Trade-offs:** answers given together appear when the turn ends, not while it streams; they
can't change files (several agents editing at once would collide).

### D246 — m7.16: helpers without a window: worktree helpers in the window's own process
**Context:** feature gaps top-20 item 8. A window per helper (D231) is heavy on Windows; Claude
Code and Cursor run worktree helpers in process.
**Decision:** `agent.isolatedHelpers.window` (off) keeps the old mode. Headless, the helper's
branch, worktree and setup are made as before, and its chat runs here (`startHere`): its folder,
model, the D232 tool limit, auto-apply, and the agent's mode or instructions. Its tools are tied
to the worktree by chat id (`toolRoots.ts`), so explore and subagents in it follow: paths, search,
find_files, `run_command` with PORT / WORKTREE_*, background commands. A path in the main folder
maps onto the worktree; IDE commands that act on the window's folder are refused. Rust's
`fs::Workspace` takes extra roots, only a linked worktree of the open folder's repository: let in
at start, forgotten when the helper ends, let in again by a tool gate for a later turn, cleared on
a folder change; `search_start` and `index_query` take a `root`. Progress, the report back,
Review / Merge, Stop, the limit, cleanup and `ide://agent/helpers` (now with `headless`) work as
before; a helper's chat opens here, without Continue here. Follow-ups: `sendToHelper` (queued for
a busy helper, a new turn for an idle one, `agentHelperMessages` in the global state for a window
helper).
**Not done:** diffs and checkpoint restore after a helper ends need its root again; rules,
memory, skills and the code index stay the main folder's (design note step 4); best of N in one
window.

### D247 — m7.16: Extension API: run-time webview panels, test controllers, provided debug configurations
**Decision:**
- `ide.ui.createWebviewPanel` reuses the webview views' machinery (WebviewFrame, the folder's
  proxy origin, CSP, the theme message). The HTML the code sets is served at
  `/__webview-<name>.html` (new `ext_webview_page`, a new name per change), so relative URLs reach
  the extension's files. Dock tab `extpanel:<id>`, not restored after a restart, 50 per extension.
- `ide.tests.createTestController` follows VS Code's shapes (items, profiles, runs,
  resolveHandler). `ExtensionFeatures.tests` feeds the Testing view (a group per controller; Run /
  Debug call the profiles; `tests.runAll` / `tests.cancel` include them), `tests.runExtension`,
  `ide://tests/extensions`. Coverage profiles aren't offered: the IDE's coverage reads report files.
- `provideDebugConfigurations` joins Add configuration… (awaited, 5 s, 20 per provider, its type
  forced); both trigger kinds are offered (no dynamic picker yet).
- Detached windows pair each copied `<style>` with its original instead of by position, which is
  why decoration types didn't reach editors there.
- A task's terminal taken back after a reload keeps its task (`restoredTask`) and the runner adopts
  it: exit, problem matchers from then on, the running list.
- `browser/view.ts`: the toolbar moved to `viewToolbar.ts`.

### D248 — m7.16: Extension API: typing, links, edits across files, comments, lm, colors
**Decision:**
- **`type` override:** registering `"type"` (needs `fs.write`) takes over Monaco's typing while
  the extension owns it (one at a time); `default:type` is `editor.typeDefault`. A notice names it
  the first time (Keep / Turn off → `extensions.typeOverride.blocked`); a failing handler or a
  dying worker gives typing back. `ide.editor.setOptions({ cursorStyle })`.
- **URI handlers:** `ide.ui.registerUriHandler`, `env.uriScheme`, activation `onUri`, delivered by
  `extensions.openUri`. The OS scheme registration (installer, single-instance forwarding) is
  still to do.
- **Edits and saves:** `workspace.applyEdit` (text, create, rename, delete through the explorer's
  commands, in order); `onWillSaveTextDocument` / `…Notebook…` with `waitUntil`, 1.5 s each.
- **Comments:** controllers and threads drawn with what the editor has (a gutter mark with a
  hover, code lenses: the latest comment, Reply); replies go to the controller's `replyHandler`.
- **`lm` and chat participants:** opt-in (`extensions.languageModelAccess`, off; rule 8) plus a
  one-time consent per extension; the user's model through `services.languageModel`. Participants
  register and answer `extensions.askChatParticipant`; the agent's chat doesn't route `@name` to
  them yet.
- **Peacock:** `workbench.colorCustomizations` takes VS Code ids; the title, activity and status
  bars have tokens of their own; user, `.vscode` and workspace layers merge; `[Theme]` blocks.
- Also `canPickMany`, tree drag and drop within a view, tree checkboxes; `mergeView.ts` split
  (`mergeCommands.ts`). The Accounts menu and file system UI leftovers were done in D234.
**Trade-off:** typing round-trips through the extension's worker while it owns it, as in VS Code.


### D249 — m7.17: who answers and how, apart; an agent on an external agent; a quieter Channels view
**Context:** the composer's one menu mixed the modes (Agent, Plan, Ask) with the agents (Builder,
Chat, Planner), and Plan sat beside Planner, Ask beside Chat. The owner asked whether modes are
still needed now there are agents, and for a default mode per agent. Also: an agent's model menu
didn't offer the external agents, and the Channels view repeated what its headers and title bar
already had.
**Decision:**
- **Keep the modes, apart from the agents** (Claude Code's plan mode is apart from its subagents;
  Cursor's modes are apart from its models). The agent is who answers (its face, instructions,
  tools, model); the mode is how: Agent does the work its access allows, Plan looks and writes a
  plan for Build, Ask answers read-only. Plan and Ask apply to any agent: `chatMode` stays the
  agent (`custom:<name>`) or, for the main agent, the mode, and `session.workMode` holds Plan or
  Ask on one of the user's agents (`session.work()`, `overlay()`, `setWork()`, `setAgent()`).
  Plan or Ask on an agent keeps its instructions and its tools that only read (plus the plan for
  Plan), with the mode's rules; a group chat's members answer in their own modes as before.
- **The composer's menu** has two headed groups: **Agent** (the main agent and the user's, with
  faces; .github/chatmodes and `agent.customModes` entries are agents too, as VS Code now calls
  them) and **Mode**; then New agent…. The pill shows the agent's face and name, with "· Plan" or
  "· Ask". Shift+Tab cycles the mode only. `agent.setChatAgent` (new) and `agent.setChatMode`
  (agent / plan / ask set the mode for whichever agent; `custom:<name>` still switches agent).
  The menu draws headings (`MenuItem.heading`) and keeps a checked face (the check goes right).
- **Each agent starts in a mode of its own:** `mode: plan | ask` in its file (written by the
  editor's **Starts in**, `agent.createAgent { mode }`). The planner plans, Chat answers (their
  templates say so; team files from D245 read the same through `TEAM_START_MODES` until they say
  otherwise); the main agent and Builder start in Agent. Switching to an agent takes its mode.
  **Build** on an agent that can't edit (the planner) hands the plan to Builder, else to the main
  agent, and the "Plan ready" note says which.
- **An agent on an external agent:** its model menu (card and editor) lists Claude Code, Codex
  and the others; in a chat on any model, that agent's turns go to its external agent
  (`sessionTurn.ts` `memberExternal`), which is told the conversation when it takes over from
  another. Delegated work and answers given together (D245) can't run on one and use the chat's
  model.
- **Channels view:** no "+ Add …" rows (each header has its + on hover), no Inbox bell (the Inbox
  row is at the top), no pages under the lists and no "All sessions…" (the history button). Its
  title bar's ⋯ (`agent.channelsMenu`) has Agents, Usage, Manage providers, MCP servers, Agent
  memory, Tidy up memory, Archived channels and Agent settings.
- The Agents page's "New agent" card has no height of its own: it stretched a row's agent card.
**Trade-off:** two values say how a chat with one of the user's agents works (its agent and its
mode) where one did; members of a group chat on different external agents restart them in turn.


### D250 — Opening a big folder: the file index's watcher without a file-id cache
**Context:** the owner found opening a folder slow. Measured with a throwaway UI script on this
repository (node_modules, Rust build folders): 26 s the first time, 16 s again, against 0.3 s for
`docs/`. `workspace_open` starts the file index's watcher, and `notify-debouncer-full`'s
`new_debouncer` uses `RecommendedCache`, which on Windows and macOS is `FileIdMap`: `watch()`
walks every file under the folder (following links, ignoring .gitignore) and opens each one for its
file id, synchronously, before the folder shows.
**Decision:** the index's watcher is `new_debouncer_opt` with `NoCache`. The cache only pairs
renames by file id; the index needs the changed paths (Source control's list, a rebuild on a
structural change), which it still gets. Now 0.18 s the first time, 0.25 s again. The explorer's
watcher watches its expanded folders one level each, and the git watcher `.git` and `.git/refs`:
small, left as they are.


### D251 — Multi-root workspaces (several folders in one window)
**Context:** feature gaps top-20 item 15: projects split across folders (an app and its API, a
monorepo's packages, a library checked out elsewhere). VS Code's multi-root workspaces are the
reference: a `.code-workspace` file (`folders`, `settings`, `launch`, `tasks`), each folder its own
`.vscode`. Everything in the IDE assumed one folder: 421 sites in about 170 files, plus Rust's
scope, index, search and git.
**Decision:**
- **The first folder stays `root`** (the primary): everything that works on "the folder" keeps
  working, and a single-folder window behaves exactly as before (same paths, same `ide://` output,
  same JSON from Rust). The others are added on top: `WorkspaceService.folders` (all, the first
  first), `file` (the workspace file; null for a single folder), `onDidChangeFolders` (added and
  removed live), and three helpers that replace the single-folder patterns one for one:
  `contains` (was `isWithin(root, …)`), `resolve` (was `resolveInRoot(root, …)`; a relative path
  may start with a folder's name) and `relative` (was `relativePath(root, …)`; the folder's name
  first when there are several, VS Code's `asRelativePath`, read back by `resolve`).
- **Live changes:** adding a folder to a single-folder window makes it an *untitled workspace*
  (`<data>/workspaces/untitled/<ms>.code-workspace`) in place: Rust keys the window's state and
  its place among windows by the file from then on, and the state is written there at once, so
  tabs and layout stay. Adding and removing other folders is live (Rust's scope, the index, the
  explorer, settings, git, LSP's `didChangeWorkspaceFolders`, the extension API's event); a
  change of the first folder reopens the workspace, since so much is keyed to it. The last folder
  can't be removed (close the workspace instead). **Save workspace as…** names it; **Open
  workspace from file…** and the recent list open one; `<cli> x.code-workspace` and `--add`.
- **The file** (`core/workspace/workspaceFile.ts`, tested): JSONC; folders relative to the file
  when inside or beside its folder (so a workspace file in a repo moves with it), else absolute;
  `file://` URIs read, remote URIs skipped; edits keep comments. A folder it lists that isn't
  there is listed as missing (`ide://workspace` `missing`), kept in the file, removable.
- **Rust:** `fs::Workspace.folders` and `file`; every scope check covers every folder (a folder
  itself, nested ones too, is never renamed, moved or deleted); the file index has a list and a
  watcher per folder (`QueryItem.root` only for non-first folders); search runs over every folder
  (`roots`); git finds each folder's repository (kind `folder`); processes may start in any
  folder; the workspace file commands only touch local `*.code-workspace` files.
- **Settings:** VS Code's layering. The workspace file's `settings` are the workspace layer
  (written back into the file); each folder's own settings files (the IDE's and `.vscode`) are a
  folder layer for its files (`settings.getAt` / `getForLanguageAt` with a path; a folder can't
  set user-only keys, nor restricted ones before it's trusted). With one folder, unchanged.
- **Trust:** a multi-root workspace is trusted when every folder is, restricted when any is;
  trusting it trusts each folder; a folder added later that isn't trusted makes it undecided.
  Opening a workspace file asks the risky-folder question for each folder it lists.
- **The per-folder `.vscode` cache** (`workspaceFolder.ts`) is per folder now: it was one module
  global, so a second folder's `.vscode` was read only when the first had one.
- **Explorer:** the folders are the tree's top rows (the hidden root is the workspace); each folder
  its own files.exclude, reveal and drop scope; a folder row's menu has Rename in workspace and
  Remove folder from workspace (no rename, move or delete of the folder itself). The menus moved
  to `viewMenus.ts` (D77).
- **The areas** (each README has a "Multi-root" section):
  - *Agent:* its sandbox (`core/agent/workspaceFolders.ts sandboxPath`) covers every folder and
    nothing else; each folder its own `.aiignore` rules, hooks (one approval signature for every
    folder that sets hooks; with one such folder exactly the old one), MCP config (risk-checked per
    folder, the server runs in its folder), rules, skills, commands, modes and subagents (labelled
    `api/…`); the prompt lists the folders. A chat stores `meta.workspace` = the folder (one
    folder, as before) or the workspace file, and matches either. A single folder's codebase index
    keeps its store; a multi-root workspace has one store named from its file.
  - *Tasks, launch:* every folder's files plus the workspace file's; a folder's are labelled
    "build (api)"; `${workspaceFolder}` and the cwd are the task's folder; `${workspaceFolder:Name}`
    everywhere; compounds name configurations as "Name (folder)" or `{ name, folder }`.
  - *Language servers:* one per language, `initialize` with every folder,
    `didChangeWorkspaceFolders` when the server takes it (not restarted when it doesn't).
  - *Terminals:* without a cwd, the active editor's folder; **New terminal in folder…**.
  - *Search:* per folder with each folder's `search.exclude` (runs chained into one result set);
    an include like `api/**` or `./api/src` searches that folder; results grouped by folder.
  - *Source control:* each folder's repository (kind `folder`), labelled by the folder.
  - *Editor:* options per file (`settings.getAt`); breadcrumbs start with the folder's name; a
    folder's tabs close when it's removed (asking about unsaved ones); `.code-workspace` files get
    VS Code's schema. The settings editor has a Folder tab (`settings.updateAt`).
  - *Extensions:* VS Code's API (`workspaceFolders`, `getWorkspaceFolder`, `asRelativePath`,
    `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`, `updateWorkspaceFolders`; adding a folder asks the user); the
    folders only with `fs.read`; their fs gate covers every folder; `workspaceState` is keyed by
    the workspace file in a multi-root workspace (a single folder made into one starts a new
    store, as in VS Code).
- **Remote windows** (D252) have one folder for now: their workspace file would have to live on
  the remote, as VS Code keeps it.
- **Audit** (three reviewers: security, correctness, single-folder regressions; then fixes):
  - *Folders nobody picked:* a workspace file that changes on disk (an edit, a `git pull`, an
    extension, the agent) can't widen the scope silently: folders it adds are confirmed by the
    user, then pass the risky-folder question and trust; declined ones stay listed as not added
    for the session. Network folders a workspace file names are asked about before Windows
    connects to them (D161). Folders that open under another name are asked about as the folder
    they are. `*.code-workspace` files are protected agent config (writing one asks).
  - *Trust:* adding a folder nobody decided about to a trusted workspace asks (Trust and add /
    Add restricted / Cancel; `workspace.addFolder { trust }` answers it); a saved workspace
    file's own place counts; the risky-folder dialog's answer stays with the folder it asked
    about.
  - *Names* are unique and slash-free ("app", "app (2)"; the file keeps what the user wrote), so
    `relative` ↔ `resolve` never lands in the wrong folder.
  - *One queue* for opens and folder changes; changes check they still belong to the workspace
    after each wait; a cancelled reopen writes the file back; missing folders keep their place in
    the file; Save workspace as… from a single folder reloads its settings; the workspace file is
    let in (an outside file, D190) so it can be edited and saved wherever it is; a folder named
    `x.code-workspace` opens as a folder; the folder state changes in one batch.
**Trade-offs:**
- One language server per language for the window (with every folder in its `workspaceFolders`),
  as VS Code.
- In a multi-root workspace a folder's own settings apply to its files (`getAt`); settings read
  for the window (the agent's, git's, the layout) come from the user and the workspace file, as in
  VS Code.
- State keyed by the workspace's location starts over when a single folder becomes a workspace
  (an extension's `workspaceState`, as in VS Code; the codebase index of a multi-root workspace
  is built again). Chats stay: they're kept by the first folder.
- Going from one folder to two renames tasks, launch configurations and test ids (the folder's
  name is added), as VS Code does.

### D252 — Remote development over SSH: a server on the remote, a window connected to it
**Context:** feature gaps top-20 item 14 (the most asked-for remote mode; dev containers next).
D192 designed it: the backend's services behind one transport. A remote window needs a server
there, a way to talk to it, and everything it does with its folder sent there, without every
caller of git, the shell or the file commands learning about remotes. No CDN at runtime (AGENTS
rule 4): the server ships inside the app.
**Decision:**
- **The server** (`src-tauri/remote-server/`, binary `ide-server`, its own crate, no Tauri; the
  protocol in `docs/remote.md`): length-prefixed JSON over its stdin/stdout; the app's own rules
  ported (workspace scope, sorting, atomic writes, the `ignore` index with the fuzzy ranking,
  search with the app's event shapes, watching with polling where inotify can't, processes and
  terminals (`openpty`) in process groups that die with it, TCP for forwarded ports, the
  ports listening there). Static musl builds for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux (2.7 / 2.2 MB), built
  on any host with rust-lld (`scripts/build-server.mjs`), tested end to end in WSL
  (`scripts/test-server.mjs`, 18 checks). It reads the login shell's environment once, so git and
  language servers find the user's PATH. Its dependencies are the app's own (MIT/Apache-2.0,
  MIT/Unlicense, CC0, ISC).
- **The window's side** (`src/extensions/remote/`): **Connect to host…** (`~/.ssh/config` hosts or
  user@host; a new window, or `here` in an empty one), a remote folder picker in the quick input
  (Open folder… in a remote window uses it), the "SSH: host" status item and its menu (open a
  folder, forward a port, the log, reconnect, close), sign-in prompts (a masked password, a
  host-key question with its fingerprint), `ide://remote`. Remote folders are `ssh://host/path`
  in the recent list and the window registry (`core/workspace/remoteLocation.ts`: hosts that look
  like ssh options are refused); one of another host opens in a window of its own. A remote
  window has one folder for now (its workspace file would have to live on the remote).
- **One remote per window, process-wide** (`remote::active()`; every window is a process). A
  window is remote from its first call when launched with `--remote <ssh:host|wsl:distro>`
  (`app_new_window { remote }`, the CLI, a `ssh://host/path` argument, the restore of a window
  the registry keeps as `ssh://…`), or after `remote_connect` in an empty window. `app_info`
  reports `remote`. The authority is validated (no leading `-`, `[A-Za-z0-9._@:\[\]%-]`) and goes
  to ssh after `--`.
- **Routing by path:** `remote::is_remote_path` is the one rule (Windows: a POSIX path, `/` not
  `//`, in a remote window; other hosts: a remote window's path outside the app's own folders).
  `fs::Workspace` keeps a remote root (`open_remote`, the server's canonical path; scope checked by
  name here, links by the server), `location()` is `ssh://host/path` (state, registry, bounds).
  The fs, watch (server watcher sets by name: explorer, settings, docs), index, search (by id:
  the view's "view" replaces itself, extensions' are their own), replace (read, replaced here,
  written back), trash (moved to `~/<serverDir>/trash` with `mv`, undoable from the window),
  git's own checks (repository root, git dir, operation files, the nested-repository scan) go to
  the server. Local history keeps local files only; a remote window's file has none.
- **One connection, one sign-in:** ssh runs one sh script (`install.rs`) that prints `uname`,
  starts the installed server or reads the upload (`head -c` of the exact size) and starts it;
  the same pipe then speaks the protocol. The install folder is
  `~/<serverDataFolderName>/<version>-<first 12 hex of the bundled binary's SHA-256>` (hash
  cached per file size and time), so a rebuilt server is never mistaken for an installed one.
  `serverDataFolderName` is new in product.json; `scripts/gen.mjs` bundles the built servers.
- **ssh's prompts** (password, passphrase, new host key) go through the existing askpass program
  (`SSH_ASKPASS` + `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force`), on a route of their own (`askpass::route`, its own
  token) to the connect call's channel as `{ kind: "askpass", id, prompt, secret }`; answered with
  `remote_askpass_answer`. Never logged or kept. git's own prompts stay git's: the askpass
  variables are now set for git only once the git extension listens.
- **Programs through a relay** (`remote::command`): the IDE's binary with `--remote-relay`, which
  connects back over loopback (port and token in `IDE_REMOTE_RELAY`, variables named in
  `IDE_REMOTE_ENV`), runs the program with `proc.spawn` and passes stdin/stdout/stderr and the exit
  code (signal: 128 + n) through; killing it kills the program there, Ctrl+C on its console sends
  SIGINT. git, the agent's commands (`$SHELL -l -c` there), language servers and debug adapters
  started through the stdio host use it unchanged.
- **Terminals are remote ptys in-process** (`remote/pty.rs`, a `Console::Remote` beside ConPTY),
  not a relay inside a local ConPTY as first planned: the release binary is a GUI program, which a
  ConPTY can't host as a console client, and the remote pty already renders once and resizes for
  real. A terminal has no local pid (nothing can `taskkill` a remote pid); closing it sends SIGHUP,
  then SIGKILL. Tasks run in the remote login shell (a Windows automation shell is ignored there).
- **Not in a remote window yet** (a clear error): dropping files from the OS, dragging files out,
  an interactive rebase, local history, project formatter detection (the editor's or a language
  server's formatter applies), a second folder (the frontend refuses it). Git's sign-in prompts
  don't cross (the remote's credential helpers apply). The git directory is polled every 2 s
  (the server's watcher reports nothing inside `.git`).
**Trade-off:** a local process per program (git status included) where a direct stream would
do; it keeps every caller unchanged, as WSL's wrapping does (D192). Stream output is buffered
without a cap on the app side (the server's queue bounds the connection).

### D253 — m7.19: calls that run together, schedules and wake-ups, images and PDFs; the D244 list closed
**Context:** asked how the agent compares with Claude Code's own tools, the gaps were: every call
of a step ran one after another (five reads, or three delegates, waited for each other); nothing
could happen later ("check the deploy in 20 minutes", "every weekday at 9"), so one agent couldn't
leave another work for later; a background command never woke the agent when it ended; read_file
refused images and PDFs. The MCP page's "12 tools and 409 IDE commands enabled" undercounted both
(only the core tools; only the commands usable at that moment). And D244's audit list was still open.
**Decision:**
- **Calls of a step run together** when they only read (`AgentTool.concurrent`, default
  `readOnly`; ask_user says false): the loop groups neighbouring ones (`callGroups`) and runs a
  group with at most 8 at once (`inParallel`, `core/agent/loop.ts`); a write or a command is a group
  of its own, so nothing runs out of the order the model gave around it, and rows and results keep
  the order asked. After Stop, calls of a group not started yet aren't. Subagents run in parallel
  too (delegate is read-only at the call): one started while another uses the turn's own requests
  gets requests of its own (`runSubagent`'s `ownRequests`, as background ones did), and its own
  steps run together the same way. Two edits of one file never overlap (`KeyedLock` per path,
  `fileLockKey`, for every chat in the window). The prompt and delegate's description say to put
  independent work in one step. `agent.parallelToolCalls` (default on) turns it off.
- **Schedules** (`core/agent/schedules.ts`, tested; `extensions/agent/schedules.ts`): "in 20
  minutes", "at 15:30", "tomorrow at 9am", a date, "every 2 hours", "hourly", "daily at 9:00",
  "every weekday at 9am", "every monday and thursday at 17:00". A schedule sends its prompt to a
  chat (into the running turn or a turn of its own, as a background report does:
  `deliverAutoMessage`), a channel or an agent's DMs (`agent.postToChannel`), or a new chat with an
  agent each time. At least a minute ahead, repeats at most every 5 minutes, at most 30 days ahead,
  50 per folder; repeats stop after 7 days (`expires_in_days`, at most 30). Kept with the folder's
  workspace state; they run only while the IDE is open (one timer, at most a minute long, so a
  computer waking from sleep catches up); one missed while it was closed runs once when the folder
  opens (8 s after), and a repeat keeps its rhythm, skipping what it missed. The agent's `schedule`
  tool (add / list / cancel) asks the user before a repeat or work sent elsewhere ("this session"
  covers the rest of the chat; full access doesn't ask); a one-off wake-up in its own chat doesn't.
  Commands `agent.schedule`, `agent.schedules`, `agent.cancelSchedule`, `agent.runScheduleNow`;
  state `ide://agent/schedules`; the details panel's Background card lists a chat's (Run now,
  Cancel); the chat's ⋯ has Schedule a message…, the Channels ⋯ Scheduled messages. A schedule's
  message is a quiet line in the chat (`auto: "schedule"`).
- **Wake-ups:** run_command's `notify_on_exit` (with background): when it ends on its own, the
  agent gets its exit and last 40 lines (`exitNotice`, `auto: "process"`; not when it was killed,
  nor when it ended during run_command's own wait, whose result says so). process_output's
  `wait_for` waits (up to `timeout_seconds`, default 120, at most 600) until a new line matches or
  the command ends, as Claude Code's Monitor does.
- **read_file on an image** attaches it for vision models (a PNG at most 1568 px, `pngBase64` as
  pasted images); **on a PDF** returns its text with page markers, paged with offset
  (`core/agent/pdfText.ts`, tested): objects and object streams, FlateDecode through the
  platform's DecompressionStream, ASCII85/Hex, the page tree (else every /Page), ToUnicode maps
  (bfchar, bfrange), simple encodings with /Differences, Form XObjects, TJ gaps and line changes.
  No library: pdf.js would add ~2 MB for what the agent needs, the words. Scanned and encrypted
  PDFs say so. `readFileOutput.ts` holds read_file's paging, images and PDFs.
- **The MCP page counts** the tools a new chat has (`chatTools`, shared with the session; MCP
  servers' tools are marked `mcp`) and every command the agent may call (`agent !== "hidden"`);
  the built-in server's page says how many are usable right now (the others wait for a folder, a
  repository, an editor…).
- **D244's list:**
  - Every member's messages in a group are labelled `[Name]`, the one answering too, so a handoff
    no longer changes the history's bytes (the provider's cache holds); the brief says so and asks
    for no tag in the reply. The brief no longer names the last speaker.
  - A member's brief and a channel's line go with a message only when the latest of their kind
    the model reads (since the last summary) differs, or is 12 messages back (`newContext`).
  - A channel's or a DM's own conversation is summarized past `agent.channels.contextTokens`
    (default 32,000; threads keep the model's context).
  - Continue after a handoff that failed, and a background subagent's or a worktree helper's
    report, go to the member they were for (`Item.to`, `pendingFor`): reports for another member
    wait for their member's turn.
  - A round's next member waits up to a minute for a busy chat, and a round that can't go on says
    who didn't answer.
  - The saved-chat list caches each chat's meta by file stamp, in memory and in
    `agent/sessions/.meta-index` (atomic, only a hint: checked against each file's stamp, so a
    stale or corrupt one costs a re-read).
  - Local git on Windows runs with `-c core.longpaths=true` (`git::command`; remote and WSL git
    are Linux).
  - A thread's parent quote runs `agent.showMessage`: the conversation opens centred on that
    message and lights it (`--bg-selected`, fading over `--motion-deliberate`).
  - Relative times ("2 min ago") stay current on one shared minute timer (`ui/relativeTimes.ts`,
    visible views only).
  - Greetings that presume an earlier visit are only for users with saved chats.
  - `agent-channels.css` uses size, space and text tokens.
  - **OpenCode's terms** (opencode.ai/docs/zen, read for this): its free models are for OpenCode
    itself, which is what Start free runs; they're offered for a limited time, and some providers
    keep prompts or use them to improve the model (NVIDIA's are trial-only, no personal data). The
    Start free card now says "Free for a limited time; some models keep what you send", with the
    details in its tooltip.
  - **WebView2:** kept `downloadBootstrapper`. Windows 11 and an up-to-date Windows 10 already
    have the Evergreen runtime (it ships with Edge), so the bootstrapper rarely runs; an offline
    installer would add ~127 MB to every download for a rare machine. If a tester is offline or
    behind a proxy without it, build them an `offlineInstaller` variant.
  - The bundle identifier and landing the branches are the owner's: they moved to the owner steps
    in `docs/windows-pending.md`, with the Windows checks the UI scripts don't cover.
  - **The UI scripts that failed on Windows**, each run alone and probed. Real bugs found and fixed:
    - The opener plugin's click script ran inside the browser pane's page frames on WebView2 and
      took a page's `target=_blank` links (then refused them: not the IDE's origin), so they
      never became tabs: it's off (`open_js_links_on_click(false)`); the IDE's own links go
      through its commands (browser-m7-6 passes).
    - WebView2 doesn't apply the page's CSP `frame-src` to a frame's own later navigations:
      `frame_guard.rs` cancels a navigation of a frame directly in the IDE's page (or a pop-out
      window's) to anything `frame-src` doesn't allow (`http://127.0.0.1:*`, `about:`), so a
      notebook renderer can no longer send itself elsewhere. Frames inside those (a site's own
      embeds in the browser pane) aren't touched, as the CSP doesn't touch them.
    - The terminal's command tracker dropped commands whose line came after C: bash and
      PowerShell send it (E) when the command is done, and Windows 10's ConPTY draws the typed
      text after the marks. A command without a line waits for E (`pending`), then for D (the
      typed line, only if the user typed it); E also corrects a line read off the screen. The
      prompt's input start is confirmed at the first key after B (on that ConPTY the prompt is
      drawn after its mark, maybe on rows below), so suggestions see the typed word, not the
      prompt. A dot made before its command was known gets its number (its menu works).
      features-m6-22 and gaps10-m7-6 pass.
    - A Node debug launch read "Debugger listening on ws://…" off the terminal, and a narrow
      terminal (a compound's sessions side by side) wrapped it inside the address: the address
      is now read with the line breaks out (Node's ends in a UUID), and a garbled line's port is
      enough (its `/json/list` gives the address).
  - Tests that were out of date: group-m7-10 (the built-in team's planner answered the check for
    the files' planner before they were read; the "@" list counted the `@all` row);
    ui-m7-5, agent-m7-5 and customize-m7-5 for this decision's menu entry and the MCP card.
  - Still failing on this machine, with the cause:
    - Windows 10's own ConPTY: the release doesn't bundle the newer one yet
      (`scripts/fetch-conpty.mjs` is an owner step). It mangles long shell-integration marks, so a
      long command the IDE typed loses its line (terminal-m6-49's large-output part, the sticky
      line of a running command in terminal-m7-7).
    - debug-m7-5: Node 24.20 itself crashes (a V8 fatal check in the inspector) with a function
      breakpoint while its child process and worker attach; not reproduced without the
      bootloader. A Node bug; the rest of the script waits on it.
    - notebooks-m7-5: no Pyright on this machine (the script expects it).
    - Open, not yet explained: parA-m7-6 (a compound started after the terminal moved to a group
      of its own: the second session's program ends at once); notebook-ext-m7-3 (the frame's
      navigation is cancelled now, but the renderer's message after it doesn't arrive);
      browser-m7-12 (named targets and forms into a new tab on WebView2); ghost-text-m7-7 (the
      cached suggestion answers without a request but isn't drawn, likely CRLF). Listed in
      `docs/feature-gaps.md` §1.
**Not done:** schedules don't run while the IDE is closed (that needs a system scheduler and a
process the IDE doesn't keep); a deleted chat's schedules go when they come due, not at once;
multi-column PDF pages come out in the content stream's order; an image read by a model without
vision becomes its description.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (loop, keyedLock, schedules, pdfText, groupChat,
conversation, greetings), `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib`, UI script `agent-m7-19`.

**Later the same day:**
- **The newer ConPTY is bundled:** `Microsoft.Windows.Console.ConPTY` 1.25.260930003 in
  `src-tauri/conpty/x64/` (the `CI.Microsoft…` repackage pinned before is deprecated). The fetch
  script now checks the download against the SHA-512 nuget.org publishes, finds the files where
  this version keeps them (`runtimes/win-x64`), shows their signers (both Microsoft), and writes
  the MIT notice. Its SHA-256 is pinned. terminal-m7-7 passes; `conpty-win-m7-19` checks the
  terminals use it.
- **A terminal tab shows a spinner while its shell starts** (until its first prompt, at once
  without shell integration, at most 10 s), so a blank terminal says it's getting ready. Dock
  views gained `busy()`; the tab strip draws a small ring in the icon's place
  (`.dock-tab-busy`; no motion with reduced motion). UI script `terminal-busy-m7-19`.
- **Found:** large output is very slow through the terminal on Windows (200,000 lines: about 1,600
  after a minute), with either ConPTY; terminal-m6-49's large-output part fails on it. Open
  (`docs/feature-gaps.md` §1).
- **A restored terminal's text** (reported: a restored PowerShell showed a run of dashes thousands
  long, and a "Restored session" line for every restart). Two causes: the saved text was xterm's
  serialized screen, which redraws wrapped rows with cursor moves that only fit the width it was
  saved at (a wrapped row of dashes smeared across a terminal of another width); and each save
  took the whole screen, earlier sessions' restored lines and separators included, so even a
  session where nothing ran added one. Now each terminal also saves this session's plain lines
  (`SavedOutput.lines`, wrapped rows joined: `logicalLines`, from the row below the restored
  lines, `plainOutput`), and a restart shows those, reflowed at any width; the serialized screen
  stays for a page reload's reattach (same width). A restored session where nothing ran (no
  command, at most a prompt) keeps the last save as it was, with its time. A save from before has
  no plain lines and is replaced at the first save. Unit tests in `persist.test.ts`; UI script
  `terminal-restore-m7-19` (three reopenings: the long line whole, one separator, the newest
  session's lines only).

### D254 — m7.20: the top-10 pass (terminal speed, Windows scripts, large repositories, accessibility basics, the agent when you're away, the extension store)
**Context:** the owner asked for the ten items ranked next from `docs/feature-gaps.md`, minus what
needs the GitHub repository or the website (Report a problem's `issuesUrl`), with only a spot
check at the end and no installer build.
**Decision:**
- **Large terminal output.** D253's "200,000 lines at about 25 a second" was wrong about the
  cause. Profiling the page over WebView2's DevTools port showed about three quarters of its time
  in IPC: ConPTY hands a flood over in many small reads, each became a Channel message and each
  message an ack (`pty_ack`), and every one is a round trip on WebView2; once 5 s of acks were
  late Rust stopped waiting and the page fell further and further behind (it printed 89,000
  lines with node already done, then 250 a second). Now Rust reads on one thread and sends what
  arrived within 5 ms (at most 256 KiB) as one message (`read_loop`, `deliver`, VS Code buffers 5
  ms too), the page acks in batches (64 KiB or 15 ms, `TerminalService.ack`), and the sticky
  command line follows scrolling once a frame instead of once a line (a full scrollback moved
  its row every line, and each move read layout). 200,000 lines: 3.5 s, the page caught up when
  the command ends. Also: a command wider than the terminal no longer counts its wrapped rows as
  output (`outputStart`), and terminal.runCommand types into a new terminal only once its first
  prompt is up.
- **The four Windows scripts.** ghost-text-m7-7 passes (flaky before). parA-m7-6's failing step
  ran its `echo` in whichever terminal was most recent after an unsplit, which depends on timing:
  it names the terminal now. browser-m7-12: the mock server answered only `/about`, so
  `/about?first` was a plain-text 404 that never connected (fixed in the fixture); and finding an
  element by name in a tab behind another failed, since a hidden frame lays nothing out and every
  box was empty: visibility is then judged by styles up the tree (`bridge.js`). notebook-ext-m7-3:
  a renderer frame navigating itself is refused by the IDE page's frame-src; WebKit keeps the
  page, Chromium shows its error page in the frame. The Navigation API can't cancel it first (an
  opaque origin gets no navigate events), so the step asserting "stayed" is gone; the frame never
  reaches the other site on either engine. terminal-m6-49 passes on Windows: its "nothing above
  to scroll to" assumed every command fits on screen (Git Bash's prompt has three rows), and a
  terminal left scrolled up doesn't follow new output, which broke the steps after it.
- **Large repositories** (100,000 files, debug build, Windows with Defender): the index had
  them all; Quick Open took 2.5 s a query, now 0.5 s (`fuzzy::might_match`: each word's letters in
  order, as bytes, before `score` allocates anything; almost every path fails there). Text search
  read every file on one thread; now one thread walks and up to 8 search (`search::run`), each
  with its own searcher, the totals, the cap and Stop kept on the collecting thread. A search on
  this machine is bounded by opening 100,000 files (plain `grep -r`: 90 s, `git grep` 12 s, a
  first read slower while Defender scans each new file). Explorer reveal 0.6 s, the agent's repo
  map 2.5 s (it reads at most 2,000 files), `git status` 3 s. `big-repo-m7-20` measures it
  (30,000 files, since generating 100,000 takes 25 minutes here: Quick Open 96 ms, explorer
  reveal 0.4 s, repo map 2 s, text search 77 s on the first read and 26 s after); the script runner's `"time": true`
  logs a step's time and a script's `"testTimeout"` lifts the 240 s limit.
- **Keyboard and screen reader basics:** `dev.checkAccessibility` lists the visible controls a
  screen reader can't name and the ones that show nothing when the keyboard focuses them;
  `a11y-m7-20` runs it on the workbench, search, source control, extensions, the agent chat,
  settings and the terminal. What it found: a list with no active row yet (the first Tab into
  the explorer or search results) showed no focus; it shows the ring now. Everything else passed.
- **The agent when you're away** (`attention.ts`): a chat that asks a question or an approval,
  or whose turn ends (a group round counts once: 1.5 s quiet), while the window isn't in front,
  flashes the taskbar button (bounces the Dock icon, marks the window urgent on Linux:
  `app_request_attention`, Tauri's `request_user_attention`, no new dependency) and leaves a
  notification with Show. `agent.notifyWhenAway` (on).
- **One turn per agent, file locks by the real path:** one of the user's agents answers in one
  conversation at a time (`agentTurns` in `sessionTurn.ts`): a turn for an agent busy elsewhere
  waits with a notice ("Builder is answering in #general; this starts when it's done") and Stop
  works while it waits. The main agent isn't limited (several chats with it at once is how it's
  used). The window-wide file lock keys on the resolved path, so two chats naming one file
  differently still wait for each other.
- **A backup model at a usage limit:** `agent.fallbackModel`, or an agent file's
  `fallbackModel:`. A usage limit (`isUsageLimit`: 402 / 429, quotas, credits, a free tier's
  cap) after one retry moves the turn to it: `SwitchModelError` makes the loop take the step
  again after `beforeStep` switched the model (at most twice a turn), and the chat says so.
- **The extension store** (Open VSX, `extensions/store.ts`, Rust `extensions/store.rs`):
  search from the Extensions view's box ("Open VSX" under the installed ones, after a pause;
  `@category:Themes`), Install, Updates (`extensions.checkStoreUpdates` /
  `extensions.updateFromStore`), `extensions.browseThemes`, `ide://extensions/store`. A download
  comes over https from Open VSX's hosts only (redirects checked too) and must match the SHA-256
  Open VSX publishes for it; it then installs through `extensions.installFromVsix`, so the same
  permission question comes up. Only their declarative parts work (themes, icon themes,
  grammars, snippets, settings), as with any .vsix. `extensions.store.enabled` (on); nothing is
  fetched until the user searches, installs or checks. Reqwest and sha2 were already there.
- **VS Code extensions' code is a phased plan now** (`docs/vscode-extensions-plan.md`, the
  owner's direction): parity in the IDE's own API with a Node extension host, then a `vscode`
  shim on top. PLAN.md §9.5 and §18 changed from "a non-goal".
- **First hour:** a walk-through with screenshots at 1280×800 and 860×560 found: the Welcome
  page's recent projects listed the folder already open (left out now, as VS Code does); Source
  control without a repository showed the Graph section, which squeezed the "No repository" page
  until its text was cut off (views may say `sectionWhen`; the Graph shows with a repository);
  the composer's bottom row in a narrow chat cut every word (the mode and access keep theirs now).
**Found, open:** a long command typed into a terminal that had just been created in a small
window, with focus moving between views, once lost its first character (`cp …` ran as `p …`):
most likely an Escape reaching bash just before (readline reads Escape + `c` as Alt+C); not
reproduced in a narrower script (`docs/feature-gaps.md` §1).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1,456), `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test --lib`
(351); UI scripts (a spot check, as asked): a11y-m7-20, terminal-m6-49, browser-m7-12,
notebook-ext-m7-3, parA-m7-6, agent-m7-19, group-m7-10, git-m7-12, extensions-m7-12,
terminal-restore-m7-19, terminal-busy-m7-19, ui-m7-5, big-repo-m7-20 (all passing at the end;
parA-m7-6 failed once in the batch, its `echo` finding no terminal with the id the `export` ran
