in, then passed twice, and a focused check showed an unsplit keeps the terminal's id), and one live install from Open VSX (Dracula 2.25.1, which found Open VSX's
files are served from `openvsx.eclipsecontent.org` now). No installer build.

### D255 — Phase 1 of VS Code extension support: the IDE's own API at parity, a Node host, a builder skill
**Context:** the owner chose a path to VS Code extensions (`docs/vscode-extensions-plan.md`):
first the IDE's own extension API at parity with VS Code's, in its own design, with a Node
extension host; then a `vscode` shim on top (phase 2); then a full audit. Keep the IDE's own
format (sandbox, permissions, commands with schemas the agent can call) and make it the base
VS Code support plugs into, rather than switching formats.
**Decision:**
- **The agent builds extensions with a built-in skill** (`agent/builtinSkills/build-extension.md`):
  the workflow (create, read the guide, validate, grant, reload, try every command, read the log),
  VS Code's API mapped to `ide` (models know VS Code's API well; the table turns that into
  correct calls here), and what tends to go wrong. Skills can now come with the IDE: read after
  every folder's, so a user's or project's skill of the same name replaces one; the Skills page
  offers Customize (a copy in the user's folder). The system prompt's long paragraph on building
  extensions became a pointer to the skill (a short fallback when it's turned off).
  `extension-builder-m7-20` has the mock model follow it end to end.
- **Positions stay 1-based.** VS Code's are 0-based; every extension, the bundled ones and the
  agent's tools use 1-based lines and columns, so the shim will convert instead of the API
  changing (the plan said 0-based; corrected).
- **The coverage table's gaps, in VS Code's shape** (names, providers, events):
  - Languages: linked editing, selection ranges (Expand selection), call and type hierarchies
    (an extension's answers Show call hierarchy where no language server does: a
    `HierarchySource` over LSP's shape, `lsp/hierarchySource.ts`, tested), evaluatable
    expressions (what the debugger's hover evaluates; asked before the built-in guess).
  - Debugger: breakpoints (list, add, remove), sessions (active, all, start, stop), events
    (`onDidStartDebugSession`, terminate, active, breakpoints) and `customRequest` (DAP
    sessions; `debug.customRequest`).
  - Tests: `run.addCoverage` from a coverage profile becomes the Testing view's coverage report
    (gutter, coverage view; Run with coverage on the controller's row); test tags (a profile with
    a tag runs only items that have it).
  - Comments: reactions (`reactions`, `reactionHandler`) and editing a comment in place
    (`editHandler`; VS Code does it with a comment's mode and menu commands, which the shim can
    translate); Add comment in the editor's menu while an extension takes comments.
  - Chat: a message to the agent that starts with an extension participant's `@name` goes to it
    (the user's agents and the chat's own mentions like `@git` keep their names).
  - `ide.editor.open`'s selection, preserveFocus and toSide (showTextDocument's options);
    `ide.env.machineId` (random, made once per installation, never derived from the machine) and
    `sessionId`.
  - Links from other programs: `<scheme>://<extension id>/…` on the command line (the OS opens
    it) reaches the extension's URI handler, in the window used last or a new one (`open_url`,
    the instance protocol's `url`); Windows registers the scheme for the user at start
    (`url_scheme.rs`, installed builds only). macOS and Linux declare it in their bundles: their
    platform pass.
  - Not done: product icon themes (the IDE's icons aren't VS Code's codicons: a mapping first),
    the gutter "+" for comments (the menu entry stands in), debug adapter trackers, one
    extension calling another's API. The coverage table in `docs/extensions.md` is now per
    namespace with what's left of each: phase 2's checklist.
- **Activation:** VS Code's `activationEvents` name works for `activation`; `onNotebook:<type>`
  and `onDebug` activate.
- **The Node extension host:** `"host": "node"` (with the new `node` permission, asked like any
  other, and only in a trusted folder) runs the extension's main file in a Node.js process of its
  own (`src/workers/extension.node.ts`, built to `workers/extension-node.cjs`, written to the data
  folder by `ext_node_host_script` and started on the stdio host with ndjson framing, so it ends
  with the window). The `ide` API is the worker's (`createWorkerApi`, the same messages) over a
  `HostTransport` (`webWorkerTransport` / `nodeTransport`); `require` loads the extension's own
  modules, npm packages and Node's built-ins. What it prints goes to its log; stdout stays the
  protocol's. It uses the user's Node (18+, on PATH) and says so when there is none; the pinned
  download the plan describes is left. `node-host-m7-20` runs one.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib`; UI scripts (a spot
check, as asked): node-host-m7-20, extension-builder-m7-20 and the extension, hierarchy, testing,
debug and agent scripts these areas touch.

### D256 — Phase 2 of VS Code extension support: the `vscode` shim, its first part
**Context:** phase 2 of `docs/vscode-extensions-plan.md`: run VS Code extensions' own code by
giving them `require("vscode")` on top of the IDE's API (phase 1, D255), so extensions from Open
VSX work as written, not only their themes and grammars.
**Decision:**
- **A VS Code package with a `main` runs in the Node host** (`format: "vscode"`, `host: "node"`).
  Its code can do what any installed program can, so it asks once for that
  (`node`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `shell`, `terminal`, `network`, `git`, `clipboard`; the dialog
  says it isn't sandboxed), asked at install. Until it's allowed it stays what it was before
  (themes, icon themes, grammars, languages, snippets, settings; `declarativeOnly`), so a theme
  package with code installed under D254 keeps working without a dialog at startup; allowing it
  restarts it with its code (`codeWaiting` on the record, `ide://extensions` shows it).
- **`package.json` in the IDE's shapes** (`core/extensions/vscodePackage.ts`): commands (a VS Code
  id the dispatcher can't take is camelCased and the original kept as `vscodeId`; `"when":
  "false"` in `menus.commandPalette` keeps one off the palette; `enablement` is `when`; agents may
  run them but are asked, as their effects are unknown), `contributes.configuration` as settings
  (types, enums, machine scopes as user-only, the title as category; keys in the IDE's own areas
  skipped), keybindings to its commands, views (the Explorer's and Source control's as their
  sections, `sectionOnly`; its own containers as activity bar icons), menus (editor, explorer,
  view title, tree rows), activation events plus VS Code's implicit ones (`onLanguage:` for its
  languages; commands and views start it on use), `%key%` strings from `package.nls.json` (Rust
  reads it beside the manifest). Context keys its code sets may use its commands', settings' or
  views' first segment (`contextNamespaces`). An extension may write its own settings even when
  their keys don't start with its id.
- **The shim** (`core/extensions/vscode/`, DOM-free, written from VS Code's documented API): VS
  Code's classes and enums; documents mirrored from the editor (a new `documents.didClose` event;
  a change is the difference between the old and new text as one replaced range, so language
  clients' incremental sync works; files over 50 MB aren't synced, as in VS Code); configuration
  read before activation so `get` is synchronous; commands under VS Code's ids, with arguments
  for code lenses, tree rows and status bar items kept in the shim behind one hidden command
  (`<name>.runVscodeCommand`) so they arrive as the same objects; every language provider of
  D234/D255 adapted, diagnostic collections merged per file; window (messages, pickers,
  `createQuickPick` as one pick, status bar, output and log channels, progress, the active editor
  with selections, edits, snippets and decorations, tree views, webview panels with
  `acquireVsCodeApi` and VS Code's message events and CSS variables injected, terminals and
  pseudoterminals); workspace (documents and events, `fs` on Node's file system so an extension
  reads its own files, findFiles, watchers, `applyEdit`, trust, folders, content and file system
  providers); env, l10n, `getExtension` for itself, and the ExtensionContext (Mementos in its
  storage, secrets, storage and log folders under the host's data folder, subscriptions disposed
  at deactivation). VS Code's version is given as 1.95.0. Positions convert at the edge (D255:
  the IDE's API stays 1-based).
- **What isn't there yet is logged**, once per name, in the extension's log and at
  `ide://ext/<id>/vscode` (the namespaces are proxies): webview views, custom editors, file
  decorations, the debugger, tasks, SCM, tests, comments, authentication, notebooks, chat / lm,
  language configuration, other extensions' APIs. Next, by what installed extensions call; then
  the full audit the owner asked for after phase 2.
- A VS Code extension gets 60 s to activate (language clients often start their server first).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (the shim's types, documents, package conversion and an
end-to-end test over the worker protocol with a fake host; 1,483), `cargo clippy -D warnings`,
`cargo test --lib` (353; `remote::connection`'s `responses_find_their_requests_in_any_order`
failed once under load, it orders two calls with a 100 ms sleep, and passes alone); UI scripts (a spot check, as asked): `vscode-shim-m7-21` (a VS Code-style
extension: localized commands, settings, documents, its own files, state, problems, editor
events), extensions (its VS Code theme package with a `main` keeps its theme, no dialog),
node-host-m7-20, workbench-m7-1, extensions-api, extensions-m7-12, extensions-m7-13. No
installer build.

### D257 — VS Code extensions near complete: the rest of the shim, and the store like VS Code's
**Context:** after D256 the owner asked for VS Code support "as close to 100% as possible" before
the full audit, and for the Extensions view's Open VSX side to match VS Code's: real icons, a
page for an extension that isn't installed, a Recommended section, settings in the Settings
editor.
**Decision:**
- **The rest of the `vscode` shim** (`core/extensions/vscode/`), each on the IDE's own API:
  `debug` (adapter factories for executables, servers and inline adapters; configuration
  providers; sessions and events; synchronous `breakpoints` with add / remove / change events;
  a declared debugger's `program` + `runtime` started as its adapter, as VS Code does), `tasks`
  (Task, ShellExecution, ProcessExecution, CustomExecution, groups, presentation; `fetchTasks`,
  `executeTask` by label), `scm` (source controls, input box, groups, resource states, quick
  diff from the original's file or the extension's content provider), `tests` (items, profiles,
  runs, TestMessages, coverage from FileCoverage details or `loadDetailedCoverage`), `comments`
  (threads, reactions; replies and edits run the commands of the package's comment menus, as VS
  Code does), `authentication`, `notebooks` (serializers ↔ nbformat cells, controllers as kernel
  sources whose executions stream outputs, cell status bar items, renderer messaging), `chat` /
  `lm` (participants named from `chatParticipants`, models with text parts), the system's file
  dialogs, and `getExtension("vscode.git")`: VS Code's Git extension API (repositories, HEAD,
  refs, remotes, index and working tree changes kept current, `show`, `toGitUri`) on the IDE's
  git, read-only (changes go through the IDE's git commands).
- **Pages from code:** VS Code's webview views and custom editors write their HTML in code, the
  IDE's views and viewers loaded a file. A view or viewer may now say `"codePage": true` (in the
  IDE's own format too): `ide.ui.webview(id).setHtml(html, instance?)` serves the page from the
  extension's origin like a panel's (`runtimeCodePages.ts`); a viewer's tabs get an `instance`
  so each file has its own page and messages. A webview view resolves when its provider
  registers (its page stays while the view is closed); custom text editors edit the document
  (saved through `applyEdit`); editable binary editors' `saveCustomDocument` isn't called yet.
- **More of package.json:** `customEditors` (by `filenamePattern`; "option" priority only in
  Reopen with…), `notebooks`, `notebookRenderers`, `debuggers`, `taskDefinitions`, webview views;
  while a package's code waits for permission none of these load. `contributes.configuration`
  now registers for packages without code too.
- **New in the IDE's API** (parity, both formats): `ide.ui.showOpenDialog` / `showSaveDialog`.
- **Left, logged when called:** file decorations, language configuration set from code,
  `TreeView.reveal`, debug adapter trackers, saving editable binary custom editors, language
  model tools, notebook editors' API.
- **The store** (`store.ts`, `storePage.ts`, `storeMedia.ts`, `core/extensions/openVsx.ts`,
  `recommendations.ts`; Rust `ext_store_file`): Open VSX icons on result rows (fetched by Rust from
  Open VSX's hosts only, size-capped by kind and content-type checked, lazily for rows in view,
  cached per session); a page for an extension that isn't installed (VS Code's extension editor:
  icon, publisher, verified, downloads, stars, Install / Update / Manage; Details with its README
  beside facts and links, Features from its package.json, Changelog; `extensions.showStoreDetails`);
  a Recommended section under Installed, from `.vscode/extensions.json` and the workspace's file
  kinds (a built-in map of Open VSX ids, each checked to exist), with Ignore
  (`extensions.recommendations.enabled` / `.ignored`, `extensions.ignoreRecommendation`).
  D254's "nothing fetched until the user searches" now also allows: opening a store page,
  icons of rows in view, and, while the Extensions view is shown with recommendations on, the
  recommended extensions' details. Settings: an extension's configuration sections share one
  Settings page (titled sections) instead of a page per title; its page's Settings tab shows them
  as cards, and "Open in settings" filters with `@ext:<id>`.
- Built with a subagent for the store side while the shim was written; reviewed and checked
  together.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1,496), `cargo clippy -D warnings`; UI scripts (a spot
check): `vscode-shim-m7-21` (now also a webview view and a custom editor talking through
`acquireVsCodeApi`, a task type, a source control, a test controller run, VS Code's git API),
`store-pages-m7-21` (live Open VSX: icons, the Prettier page, a workspace recommendation; needs
the network), extensions, extensions-api, extensions-m7-12, extensions-m7-13, node-host-m7-20,
workbench-m7-1. No installer build.

### D258 — VS Code extensions to 99%: the last API gaps, extension actions, the view's panes
**Context:** the owner asked to close what D257 left (file badges, language configuration from
code, `TreeView.reveal`, debug adapter trackers, editable custom editors, language model tools
and the like) before the audit, and noticed along the way: VS Code's extension actions (Set Color
Theme…), themes not coloring menus, tooltips and scrollbars, an installed extension's README
images, and the Extensions view's sections not being panes like VS Code's.
**Decision:**
- **The IDE's API gained, for both formats:** a tree row's image (`iconPath` / `iconPathDark`, a
  file of the extension, shown as a blob URL), `reveal(path, …)` and `onDidChangeSelection` on
  tree views (reveal waits for a section that just opened to load); file decorations
  (`ui.registerFileDecorationProvider`: the Explorer asks synchronously, so the runtime keeps the
  answers and asks for missing paths in batches of 200, `runtimeFileDecorations.ts`); language
  configuration from code (`languages.setLanguageConfiguration`, merged over the language's in
  Monaco; `onEnterRules` now read from files too); debug adapter trackers (a registry the
  debugger's DAP transport passes every message through, both ways, then stop and exit); a
  code-page viewer tab's unsaved state (`webview.setDirty`: the tab's dot, closing asks).
- **The shim:** tree icons, reveal (via `getParent`) and selection; `FileDecoration` and its
  provider; `setLanguageConfiguration` (RegExps sent as patterns); trackers; editable custom
  editors (the page bridge sends Ctrl+S / Z / Y, which a page's keys never reach the IDE with:
  `saveCustomDocument`, the edits' undo / redo, the dot follows); language model tools
  (`contributes.languageModelTools` become hidden commands the agent sees as tools, effects
  "exec" so it asks first, answered by `lm.registerTool`; `lm.tools`, `invokeTool` for its own);
  `setTextDocumentLanguage`; language status items as status bar items; and a table of VS Code's
  command ids mapped onto the IDE's (save, close, quick open, terminal, tasks, views, debug,
  reveal in Explorer / OS, copy path, Markdown preview, open folder, `vscode.diff`,
  `installExtension` from Open VSX).
- **Extension actions like VS Code's** (`actions.ts`, the ⚙ menu, the context menu and the page):
  Set color theme / file icon theme; Disable / Enable (workspace) (the registry's `disabledIn`,
  by the workspace's first folder; a folder change refreshes); Auto update (per extension, else
  `extensions.autoUpdate`, off by default so nothing goes online unasked; a minute after start,
  updates only those); Install specific version… (Open VSX's `allVersions`; pins it); Copy, Copy
  link, Add to workspace recommendations (`.vscode/extensions.json`, comments kept); Download
  VSIX / a specific version. The page has VS Code's split Disable ▾ and Uninstall ▾ and an Auto
  update checkbox; Apply to all profiles has no counterpart (profiles here are settings').
- **The Extensions view's panes:** the search box stays put and the installed list scrolls on its
  own; Recommended (nothing typed) and Open VSX (something typed) are sections of the view, the
  Explorer's Outline / Timeline mechanism (`sectionOnly`, collapsible, resizable, scrolling on
  their own), sharing the view's search text.
- **Themes:** menus, tooltips and pickers take a theme's menu colors, else VS Code's fallbacks
  (its widgets', dropdowns' and hovers' background; Night Owl has no menu color); scrollbars take
  its `scrollbarSlider` colors (new `--scrollbar-thumb*` tokens; the editor's already did).
  An installed extension's README loads its web images like the Markdown preview does.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`; UI scripts (a spot check): vscode-shim-m7-21 (now 37
steps: Explorer badges, tree icons and reveal, the agent tool, the extension actions),
store-pages-m7-21 (the sections; live Open VSX), extensions, extensions-api, extensions-m7-12,
extensions-m7-13, node-host-m7-20; screenshots of the view's sections. No installer build.

### D259 — Installing asks first: Cancel installs nothing
**Context:** the owner pressed Install on an Open VSX extension, then Cancel in the permission
dialog, and it stayed in the installed list: the folder was copied in before the question, so
Cancel only declined its permissions.
**Decision:** a new extension (not an update of an installed one) that asks for permissions is
asked about before anything is copied (`manager.installFrom`, every install path: Open VSX,
.vsix, folder, repository). Cancel installs nothing (the commands return `{ id: null,
cancelled: true }`); "Allow and install" installs it with them; a VS Code package whose code
would run can also be installed without its code (its themes, languages and snippets work, as
before D256; allowing its code later is on its page). An update that asks for more still asks
after installing, as before.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`; the install scripts run as tests (no dialog) are
unchanged. The dialog itself by hand (`docs/manual-test.md` D259). No installer build.

### D260 — Claude Code for VS Code runs: view `when` clauses, icon files, themed pages, platform builds
**Context:** the owner installed Claude Code for VS Code from Open VSX: its view was a white
panel, the activity bar had two box icons instead of its logo, and the Open menu listed it twice.
**Causes:** (1) a race in code-written pages (`runtimeCodePages.ts`): the frames were taken before
the page was stored and the page recorded after, so a frame that opened in between (a view shown
while the extension writes its page at startup) stayed on the empty page; (2) the empty page and
VS Code pages had no `color-scheme`, so Chromium painted the frame white, and pages got only ~20
`--vscode-*` colors, after loading; (3) `when` clauses on views and view containers were ignored
and `viewsContainers.secondarySidebar` became a second sidebar view, so both of Claude Code's
layouts showed; (4) container icon files weren't read (only `$(name)` icons); (5) Open VSX's
default answer for an extension built per platform is any platform's build (alpine-arm64 here),
so its program was missing; (6) schemes with `_` (`_claude_fs_left`) were refused.
**Decision:**
- **Views:** a view's and its container's `when` are kept (`ContributedView.when`, both formats)
  and the view registers only while they hold, following context keys; keys a package's views
  test are its own to set (unless the namespace is the IDE's or VS Code's: `config`, `view`…).
  `secondarySidebar` (and `"location": "secondary"`) is a dock tab on the right, beside the agent.
  An icon file (`iconPath`) is the activity bar's and the tab's icon, a mask in the icon color as
  VS Code draws it (`imageIcon`). A view without a name takes its container's title; `<view
  id>.focus` reveals one of its views; the Open menu offers only views whose `when` holds.
- **The shim reports VS Code 1.106** (was 1.95): extensions pick their current layout (Claude
  Code's chat in the secondary side bar, its sessions in the activity bar).
- **Pages:** `CodePages.set` asks for the frames after storing the page. VS Code pages get about
  190 `--vscode-*` colors from the IDE's tokens (`core/themes/webviewVars.ts`), `color-scheme`, the
  body's `vscode-dark` / `vscode-light` class and `data-vscode-theme-kind`, and VS Code's default
  page styles (a cascade layer, through CSSOM so a page's CSP doesn't block it), from the first
  line: the IDE writes the current theme into the bridge when it serves the page. The empty page
  follows the frame's color scheme.
  Frames send the theme again on `ThemeService.onDidChange` (after the colors are in effect):
  switching between two imported themes of the same kind left pages one theme behind, since
  the theme's colors land after the setting changes.
- **Open VSX:** details and installs ask for this platform's build first
  (`/api/{ns}/{name}/{platform}[/{version}]`, `target_platform()`), else the universal one.
- **File systems:** schemes may contain `_` (VS Code allows it); a VS Code package's file systems
  get no Explorer section (they back its own editors; VS Code shows none).
- **State:** `ide://ext/<id>/vscode` lists webview views (resolved, page length, shown, error);
  `ide://extensions?id=` has `live.codePages` (each view's page and what its frames show). A
  page the IDE refuses is now logged instead of dropped.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1,510), `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib store::`;
in the app, Claude Code installed from Open VSX shows its sign-in page in the theme's colors, one
activity bar icon (its logo) for its sessions and its chat as a tab on the right; UI scripts
vscode-shim-m7-21, store-pages-m7-21, node-host-m7-20, extensions-api, extensions-m7-12,
extensions-m7-13. No installer build.

### D261 — Audit of the extension system: security, races, the shim, Windows
**Context:** after D255–D260 (VS Code extensions running in Node, the Open VSX store), the owner
asked for a full audit in six areas: security of extension code, leaks and races, the shim's
correctness, Windows specifics, the UI in small windows and light themes, and the whole UI suite.
Four read-only reviews (one per code area) reported 47 findings; each was checked against the
code before fixing (traced line by line, or reproduced by a probe or a unit test).
**Fixed — security:**
- An extension's short name owned any setting under it: `evil.python` could set the Python
  extension's `python.defaultInterpreterPath` (a program it runs) with only "fs.write". A
  setting another extension registered is never the caller's own now
  (`extensionMayWriteSetting(…, owner)`), so the user-only rules apply.
- Node extensions kept running after the folder stopped being trusted (trust revoked, or an
  untrusted folder opened in the window): their code stops (`ExtensionRuntime.stopCode`; themes,
  views and settings stay) and asks for trust again on next use.
- An extension with "fs.write" could install a version, disable, or turn off auto update of
  other extensions (`extensions.*` commands): those now need the user's yes.
- Installs skipped `node_modules` at every depth, so a .vsix that doesn't bundle its
  dependencies failed on its first `require`: they're kept for code that runs in Node (up to
  100,000 files); a web worker extension (bundled) still leaves them.
- `known_root` took the IDE's own scratch folders (`.downloads`, `.removing`) for extensions.
- Context keys: a VS Code package's key must be `<namespace>.<name>` (a bare key is the IDE's),
  and a view's `when` claims only namespaces starting with the package's own name.
**Fixed — leaks and races:**
- Stopping an extension while its worker was still starting (Disable, Reload, the dev poll, the
  trust dialog open) left that worker running against a disposed runtime: its requests then
  registered language features, events and decorations nothing removed (duplicate hovers after
  a reload). `stopping`, the starting worker disposed with the runtime, `request()` refused
  after disposal, and an activation waiting 60 s ends at once.
- Uninstall and update returned before Node had exited, and the dev poll could start the old
  version again mid-install ("in use" on Windows): stopping awaits the process's exit, and ids
  being installed or removed are skipped by refreshes (`busy`).
- A failed refresh made every later refresh fail (`refreshAgain` kept the rejection).
- `postMessage` right after `webview.html = …` went to the old page and was lost: posts wait
  for a page being served (views, viewers and panels), then queue until it loads.
- Webview pages the old page wrote stayed in Rust across window reloads; at 200 per extension
  new ones were refused (a blank view): a main-page reload clears them.
- Each notification added a disposable to the extension's store for its whole life; file icon
  themes made new blob URLs on every load without releasing the old ones.
- Linux/macOS: a stdio server (a Node extension host, a language server) gets its own process
  group, killed as a group, so what it started goes with it (Windows already used taskkill /T).
**Fixed — the `vscode` shim:**
- After `TextEditor.edit` / `workspace.applyEdit` resolve, documents show the edit (they were
  stale until an event arrived, so the next edit's positions were wrong).
- `TextDocument.isDirty` follows editor changes and saves (it was never true).
- A range past the last line ends at the end of the text (`Range(0,0,lineCount,0)` kept the
  last line).
- Completions keep their replace range, `sortText`, `filterText`, `preselect` and
  `additionalTextEdits` (auto-imports) through to Monaco.
- Code actions get the extension's own Diagnostic objects (with `source`, `data`).
- `Uri.toString()` keeps a port and user (`localhost:3000`, not `localhost%3A3000`) and encodes
  `#` in a query; `with({ query: null })` clears it.
- `editor.selections = […]` selects; a QuickPick shown then made busy opens with the items it
  loads; a document closed during a sync isn't reopened as a ghost; `openTextDocument({ content
  })` is untitled, in `textDocuments`, and `showTextDocument` opens it in the IDE;
  `vscode.execute…Provider` resolve `[]` (`undefined.forEach` threw); `showWorkspaceFolderPick`
  returns a WorkspaceFolder; `NotebookEdit` exists (applying it is logged as unsupported);
  `TestItem.range` reads back as set; breakpoints an extension adds are its own objects.
**Fixed — Windows:**
- Node not found (installed since the IDE started, or by an installer that changed PATH for new
  processes only): PATH is read again and Node tried once more; the message names fnm/nvm; a
  Node older than 18 says so; Node's last stderr lines are in the error.
- A task's `ShellExecution(command, args)` was quoted for POSIX but ran in PowerShell: it's
  quoted for the shell that runs it (`& '…'` in PowerShell, `"…"` in cmd), and
  `options.executable` / `shellArgs` are passed on. A task's `&&` works in Windows PowerShell 5.1.
- `sendText` sends line breaks as Enter (and one at the end), as VS Code.
- `env.shell` is the shell the IDE's terminals start (PowerShell 7, else Windows PowerShell),
  not `%ComSpec%`.
- `createTerminal({ shellArgs: "…" })` splits the string as Windows does.
- The `.git` write guard also refuses `.git.` and `GIT~1` (Windows opens both as `.git`).
- A .vsix entry with a reserved name says so; old `node-host-*.cjs` copies are removed.
**Fixed — the UI suite:** `editor.insertText`, `editor.runAction` and `editor.select` failed
with "No active text editor" when run right after a file opened (its tab was there, its text
not yet loaded; fixes-m7-4 and ghost-text-m7-7 failed under load, on the build before this audit
too): they wait up to 3 s for the active tab's editor. The small-window check shows the
Extensions view, an extension's page and a VS Code webview view hold up at 640×480 in both
themes.
**Left (logged here for a later round):** a job object per stdio server on Windows (a crashed
Node host's children run until the IDE closes); `TestMessage.location` (the Testing view has no
per-failure location); one extension's commands taking another's same-named ids (first loaded
wins); preview and webview cookies sharing `127.0.0.1` (suspected, not shown). UI scripts that
fail on this machine before and after the audit, outside the extension system: debug-m7-5 (a
multi-session Node debug test), big-repo-m7-20, editor-m7-2 (the welcome page's recent folders),
notebooks-m7-5 (Python), and ghost-text-m7-7's cache step (AI ghost text timing, passes on some
runs).
**Verified:** `npm run check`; `npm test` (1,522); `cargo clippy`; `cargo test --lib` (356); new
unit tests for each fix that is DOM-free; the full UI suite (182 of 191 passed in one run; the
rest are the ones above, and each extension script passes); `extensions-small-light` (new: the
Extensions view, a page and a VS Code webview view at 640×480, light and dark). No installer
build.

### D262 — Extensions' title buttons with their own icons, `config.*` in when clauses, recently used commands first
**Context:** the owner noticed, with a VS Code extension installed, that its button on the
editor's title bar was missing its icon, that an extension's two views of one name looked the
same in its Open menu, that typing "t" in quick access didn't put the command they'd just used
first (VS Code does), and that the quick access field was darker than its box.
**Decision:**
- **Menu icons from files:** a VS Code command's `icon` that is a file or a `{ light, dark }`
  pair is read (as a blob URL, before the menus are added) and drawn as a mask in the icon
  color on the editor title bar (`MenuContribution.iconImage` / `iconImageDark`,
  `TabAction.iconImage`), the dark one with a dark theme.
- **`config.<setting>` in when clauses** is the setting's value, as in VS Code: the context key
  service answers keys nothing set from a fallback (main.ts: settings), and a setting's change
  is announced as `config.<key>` changing.
- **Views of one name** in an extension's Open menu (and View → Tools) say where they open
  ("Name (side bar)", "Name (secondary side bar)") only when two are offered at once; one alone
  keeps its name.
- **Quick access:** commands run from it are remembered across sessions (`recentCommands` in
  the global state, 12), and with something typed, the recently used ones that match come
  first, most recent first, then the rest by how well they match (VS Code's "recently used"
  group). Its field has the box's own background (`--bg-overlay`), the border marking it.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1,523); UI scripts quick-access-m7-22 (new),
vscode-shim-m7-21, extensions-api, extensions-m7-12, extensions-m7-13, features-m6-32; a VS
Code extension's title button drawn with its icon file in the app. No installer build.

### D263 — Each webview keeps its own saved state; a webview panel's own icon
**Context:** with a VS Code extension that opens chats as pages, "New session" opened a page
showing the previous chat, and a page in the editor area lacked its header buttons. The cause
was ours: VS Code gives each webview its own `getState` / `setState`; the bridge kept it in
sessionStorage under one key, and all of an extension's pages share one origin, so every page
(its side bar view, its secondary view, each panel) read and overwrote the others' state — the
session shown, the kind of page it was (full editor or side bar).
**Decision:** the bridge reads and writes its state under a key the IDE fills in when it serves
the page (`STATE_KEY_SLOT`, `withPageSetup`): `view:<id>` for a view (kept across its page
changes and window reloads, as VS Code keeps a view's), and for a viewer tab and a panel their
own id with the run's stamp (a new one starts empty; ids start over after a reload). A webview
panel's `iconPath` (a file of the extension, or a light / dark pair) is its tab's icon, read as
an image (`WebviewPanelsDeps.image`).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`; in the app, a VS Code extension's side page and a new
panel each show their own session, the panel with its header buttons and its icon on the tab;
UI scripts vscode-shim-m7-21, extensions-api, extensions-m7-12, node-host-m7-20. No installer
build.

### D264 — The terminal for VS Code extensions, a job per server, the audit's leftovers
**Context:** after the merge to main, the owner asked to finish four things: the shim's terminal
gaps (Claude Code logged `environmentVariableCollection` as unsupported at every start, which is
how `claude` in a terminal finds the IDE), a green UI suite, a Windows job object per server, and
D261's leftovers.
**Decision:**
- **Terminal environment:** VS Code's EnvironmentVariableCollection (`core/extensions/vscode/
  terminalEnv.ts`) sends its whole set a tick after each change (`ide.terminals.setEnvironment`,
  "shell": `NODE_OPTIONS` or `PATH` change every program started there). The workbench keeps each
  extension's set (`extensionFeatures.terminalEnv`); every new terminal, task terminals too, gets
  them under its own variables (`terminalEnvVars`: append / prepend as `${env:NAME}`, which Rust
  expands). As in VS Code, open terminals keep their environment; the set goes when its code stops.
- **Terminal links:** `registerTerminalLinkProvider`: the line the pointer is on goes to the
  extension ("terminal"), answered within 500 ms, as links where no other link is; Ctrl+click
  calls `handleTerminalLink` with the extension's own link object.
- **Terminal profiles:** `contributes.terminal.profiles` (and a manifest's `terminalProfiles`) are
  in the terminal's ＋ ▾ menu and profile picker before the code runs; picking one starts it and
  asks its provider (`registerTerminalProfileProvider`), whose options make the terminal.
- **A job per server (Windows):** `job::spawn_owned` puts a stdio server (language, MCP, the Node
  extension host) in a job of its own nested in the IDE's; stopping or reaping it closes the job,
  so what a crashed server started doesn't run on until the IDE closes. Unix: a process group
  (D261).
- **Leftovers:** a test failure's `TestMessage.location` is where its row opens and is in the
  results (`failedAt`); extensions start earliest installed first (`registry.installedAt`, kept
  across updates), so a later one can't take an earlier one's command ids by its folder's name.
  Not done: extension webviews and dev-server previews still share 127.0.0.1's cookies — a second
  loopback address (127.0.0.2) doesn't load in WebView2 (tried, reverted).
- **The UI suite:** git finds a repository made outside the IDE (`git init` in a terminal; the
  file watcher leaves `.git` out, so nothing told it), a rescan at most every 3 s when files
  change outside the known repositories — big-repo-m7-20 failed on this; editor-m7-2 opens a
  second folder (the open one isn't a recent folder since D254); notebooks-m7-5's language-server
  steps are notebooks-lsp-m7-5 with `"requires": ["pyright-langserver"]` (the runner skips a
  script whose program isn't on PATH); debug-m7-5's process list checks for a Node process among
  the matches. Still flaky on this machine: debug-m7-5's Client session (a 300 ms timing the
  compound depends on; a longer one ended the run first) and ghost-text-m7-7's cache step (the
  cached answer is used but Monaco sometimes shows nothing after two quick inputs).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1,530), `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib` (358);
UI scripts terminal-ext-m7-23 (new), editor-m7-2, notebooks-m7-5, big-repo-m7-20,
vscode-shim-m7-21, extensions-api, node-host-m7-20, store-pages-m7-21, extensions-m7-12;
notebooks-lsp-m7-5 skips without Pyright. No installer build.

### D265 — Other extensions' APIs, the notebook editor API, store notices, webviews on localhost
**Context:** the owner asked to finish VS Code extensions (feature-gaps §3): extensions that build
on another's API got nothing from `extensions.getExtension(id)` but `vscode.git`; the notebook
editor API was missing and `NotebookEdit`s were only logged; updates were installed only when
Auto update was on, with no notice otherwise; an extension whose code can't run here (no Node)
was found out only after installing it; extension webviews shared 127.0.0.1's cookies with
dev-server previews (D261, D264).
**Decision:**
- **Other extensions' APIs:** each extension runs in its own Node process, so exports cross as a
  description (`core/extensions/rpcExports.ts`, replaced by the shared host in D296): plain data is copied (Uris revived), functions
  become calls forwarded to the extension that made them and return promises (VS Code's are
  often sync; extensions `await` them anyway), a function passed as an argument (an event
  listener) is called back across, and an object a call returns that has methods (a Disposable,
  an API object) stays where it is and is used by handle (released on `dispose`).
  `getExtension(id)` finds any installed VS Code package (`init.vscode.others`); `activate()`
  starts it first (as VS Code does), `exports` is there once it has activated, `packageJSON` is
  read from its folder; `extensions.all` lists them. The manager routes the calls (only code
  running in Node may call; a callback goes only to a caller that passed one).
- **Notebook editor API** (`core/extensions/vscode/notebookEditors.ts`): a NotebookDocument has
  its cells from `notebook.read` (new `outputs` option: nbformat), refreshed on the notebook's
  changes with VS Code's content and cell changes (kept cells stay the same objects);
  `window.activeNotebookEditor` and its selection follow the IDE's notebook tab (a new
  `notebook.didChangeEditor` event, `ide.editor.onDidChangeNotebook`, read from ide://notebook
  after tab changes, clicks and keys); `showNotebookDocument`, `openNotebookDocument(uri)`
  (untitled ones aren't: the IDE's notebooks are files). A WorkspaceEdit's NotebookEdits are
  applied after its text edits through the IDE's cell commands (delete, insert, a cell's
  language, metadata replaced as a merge with removed keys null), one after another against the
  notebook as the previous one left it. VS Code's "jupyter-notebook" is the IDE's Jupyter type,
  so a VS Code kernel controller for .ipynb is offered for them.
- **Store:** `extensions.autoCheckUpdates` (default on, as VS Code's): a minute after start, with
  extensions from Open VSX installed, their newer versions are a notice (Update all / Show) and a
  number on the Extensions icon; nothing is installed unasked. The install question says when
  Node.js isn't on this computer.
- **Webviews on localhost:** an extension webview's proxy origin is `http://localhost:<port>`,
  previews keep `127.0.0.1` (the same listener answers both): cookies are kept by host name, so
  theirs stay apart. The CSP's `frame-src` and the Windows frame guard allow `localhost` too.
  Tested in a scratch worktree's build first (D264's 127.0.0.2 attempt broke the live build);
  that worktree linked `node_modules`, and removing it deleted through the link: restored with
  `npm install` (never link it again).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib`; UI scripts
vscode-exports-m7-24 and vscode-notebook-m7-24 (new: a provider extension started by
`activate()`, data, calls, a listener until disposed, an object by handle; the active notebook,
its cells, an inserted cell and replaced metadata), webview-hosts-m7-24 (new: the extension page
on localhost, the preview on 127.0.0.1), vscode-shim-m7-21, extensions-api, notebooks-m7-5,
browser-m7-12, and 39 more scripts that use webviews, previews, notebooks or extensions (all pass;
explorer-follow-m6-87 failed once in the batch, its first step running before the bundled
extensions had loaded, and passed twice alone). The update notice needs Open VSX: a hand check.
No installer build.

### D266 — Dev containers
**Context:** the owner asked for dev containers: a folder's `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`
(VS Code's Dev Containers, GitHub Codespaces, the containers.dev spec) opened inside its
container, reusing the SSH remote (D252) with `docker exec` instead of ssh.
**Decision:**
- **A container is a remote:** a third transport, `container:[user@]<id>` (`remote/transport.rs`):
  `docker exec -i [-u user] <id> sh -c <setup script>`, then everything is the SSH window's (the
  upload, the server, programs through the relay, ptys, forwarded ports). The container part is
  never option-like (`node@-it` is refused). The docker program is `docker` on PATH or
  `remote.containers.dockerPath` (podman), set before each connect (a container window launched
  with `--remote` too).
- **Bringing it up is the frontend's plan** (`core/workspace/devContainer.ts`, DOM-free and
  tested: the configuration with VS Code's defaults and `${…}` variables, the docker arguments,
  docker's and the CLI's answers), run by argv through a new `remote_docker` IPC (docker or the
  devcontainers CLI, never a shell; each line to the log). With the devcontainers CLI installed it
  does the work (`devcontainer up`: features, Compose, the image's metadata; required for
  those two); else docker alone: the folder's container found by VS Code's labels
  (`devcontainer.local_folder` / `config_file`), started if stopped, else the image built
  (`vsc-<folder>-<hash>`) or pulled and run with the folder bind-mounted at `workspaceFolder`, its
  mounts, environment, user, `runArgs`, a sleep loop unless `overrideCommand` is false; the
  lifecycle commands in VS Code's order (`initializeCommand` here, `postAttachCommand` once the
  window is in). Ids are docker ps's short ones.
- **Commands** (category "Dev containers"): Reopen in container (closes the local folder, then
  connects this window), Rebuild container, Reopen folder locally (from the container's labels
  when the window started in it), Attach to running container…, Show the dev containers log; the
  remote menu has them; a notice offers Reopen when a folder with a configuration opens and
  Docker is installed (`remote.containers.showReopenNotice`). A status item shows the bring-up's
  step. `ide://remote` has `container` (id, local folder, configuration).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib`; UI script
devcontainer-m7-24 (new; `"fakeDocker": true` puts tests/fixtures/fake-docker on PATH, whose
containers are WSL's Ubuntu: the configuration read, the container started with the folder
copied in and its postCreateCommand run, files and a terminal in it through `docker exec` — the
fake is a `.cmd` shim, so the setup script also survived Windows' batch quoting — Reopen locally,
the same container found again). Docker Desktop wasn't running on this machine: a real Docker,
a Dockerfile build, features with the CLI and Attach are hand checks (`docs/manual-test.md`). No
installer build.

### D267 — The last of VS Code extensions: update delay, notebooks, Node, product icons
**Context:** the owner asked to finish what D265 left: untitled notebooks, outputs on cells an
extension inserts, a pinned Node download for machines without Node, product icon themes, and a
delay before a brand-new extension version is offered.
**Decision:**
- **Update delay:** `extensions.updateDelayHours` (24; 0 offers at once): a version out for less
  is not offered as an update (notice, badge, auto update); the newest version that is old enough
  is, looked up in Open VSX's details (at most 4 more versions, `offeredUpdate`). A version
  published by mistake, or by someone who took over an account, is usually pulled by then.
  Installing a specific version isn't held back.
- **Outputs on inserted cells:** `notebook.insertCell` takes `metadata`, `outputs` (nbformat,
  read through `readOutput`) and `executionCount`, inserted as one step; the shim's NotebookEdits
  send a new cell's outputs and execution order with it.
- **Untitled notebooks:** a notebook view for `untitled:Untitled-N<ext>` starts from what it was
  opened with (or empty) and has no file; its first save asks where (or uses its target, for
  `untitled:<absolute path>`), then the view becomes that file (extensions see the untitled one
  close and the file open). Closing it unsaved asks; a cancelled Save dialog keeps it open
  (`confirmClose` now checks it was saved). `notebook.newUntitled` opens one (`notebook`: cells to
  start with, as serializers give them; `path`: show an open one). The shim's
  `openNotebookDocument(type, data)` uses it — shown in a tab, since the IDE has no hidden
  documents — and untitled notebooks are `untitled:` Uris with `isUntitled`.
- **Pinned Node:** Node.js 24.22.2 (the LTS line), each platform's archive SHA-256 from
  nodejs.org's SHASUMS256.txt in `node_runtime.rs`. The extension host uses `node` on PATH, else
  the downloaded one, else asks (once per session) and downloads it through the ACP agents'
  installer (`install_into`: streamed, hash checked, unpacked safely) into
  `<data>/runtimes/node/<version>/`, progress in the status bar. Not bundled: the installer stays
  small. `extensions.downloadNode` does it on request; the install question says it's offered.
- **Product icon themes:** `contributes.productIconThemes` (fonts + glyphs for VS Code's
  codicons). The IDE draws Lucide icons, so `CODICON_FOR` maps each that has a counterpart to its
  codicon (activity bar, actions, layout, debugging, status…); `icon()` draws the theme's glyph
  when it has one, else the IDE's own; icons on screen are swapped on change.
  `workbench.productIconTheme` ("Default"), Preferences: Product icon theme…
- **A latent bug fixed on the way:** the page's CSP takes fonts from `data:` and itself only, so
  fonts loaded as `blob:` URLs never loaded — file icon themes drawn with a font (Seti) showed
  nothing. Theme fonts are now `data:` URLs.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1,554), `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib` (361),
rustfmt; UI scripts product-icons-m7-25 (new: a theme made at run time with Windows' Segoe MDL2
Assets font; the activity bar's icons drawn as its glyphs, Default restores them),
vscode-notebook-m7-24 (an inserted cell with its output; an untitled notebook from an
extension's data, active and unsaved), and a one-off script (not kept: it downloads 30 MB) in
which `extensions.downloadNode` downloaded Node 24.22.2 from nodejs.org, its hash matched, and
the program printed `v24.22.2`; and 31 more scripts across extensions, notebooks, webviews,
menus and the dev container (all pass; notebook-m7-12 read the cell menu's HTML cut at a fixed
length, which the icons' new `data-icon` attribute pushed "Copy" past: it reads more now). Saving an untitled notebook goes through
the system's Save dialog: a hand check. No installer build.

### D268 — Graph badges alike, a calmer folder card, extensions in an empty window
**Context:** the owner's screenshots: in the Graph, one ref badge (a local branch's) was tinted
while the ones beside it were filled, so it looked like another control; the agent's "Where
should this project live?" card looked crowded; and Claude Code for VS Code didn't start with
no folder open (an empty activity bar slot, its page blank), where VS Code runs it.
**Decision:**
- **Badges:** every ref badge is filled in its kind's color (current branch and branches blue,
  remote branches purple, tags yellow, the lane colors in All branches mode), as VS Code's
  colored labels; the current branch stays bold. Their text and icon are dark on a light badge and white on a dark
  one, picked from the badge color's own lightness (CSS relative colors), so every theme's colors
  stay readable.
- **Folder card:** labels above their fields in the UI font (not a column beside them, not
  monospace), a quiet icon (a folder isn't a warning: no permission-yellow), the folder that will
  be created as a hint under the location, plain button labels ("Open folder…", "Just chat",
  "Create and start") without the key glyph.
- **Empty window:** trusted, as VS Code's is by default (`security.workspace.trust.emptyWindow`):
  `trust.require` passes with no folder open, and `lsp_start` lets an extension's own program
  (the Node extension host) start with its folder as the working directory when no workspace is
  open (everything else still needs one). Code started there stops when a folder that isn't
  trusted opens in the window (checked on open, after trust reads the folder's decision; it starts
  again on its next use, asking first).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib`; UI script
empty-window-ext-m7-25 (new: a VS Code extension loaded and run with no folder open, stopped when
an undecided folder opens); screenshots of the Graph (wide and narrow) and the folder card;
git-m7-7, scm-m7-6, agent-m6-59 and the extension scripts. Installer built (`npm run build`).

### D269 — Extensions starting don't change the layout; Claude Dark; no full screen in Help
**Context:** with extensions now starting in an empty window (D268), Claude Code for VS Code
took over the default layout at start: the side bar switched to its sessions list and its page
opened on the right. VS Code keeps its layout. The owner also asked for a Claude-like dark theme
and to drop Help → Toggle full screen (in the frameless window it hides the title bar, which
looked broken; the window's own maximize button is there).
**Decision:**
- **The cause:** some extensions call `webviewView.show(true)` at the end of
  `resolveWebviewView`. VS Code resolves a view only when it's being opened, so there that
  `show()` is a no-op; the shim resolves every view when it registers (so its page is ready), so
  the same call opened every view at startup. A `show()` made while its view is being resolved now
  opens it in the background, as VS Code's layout has it: a panel or secondary view's tab is
  added behind its group's active tab (`dock.openView(…, { background })`, `webview.reveal`'s
  `background`), nothing takes the focus, and a side bar view is its activity bar icon. Later
  `show()` calls (a command the user ran) reveal the view as before. For every extension.
- **Syntax colors after a start:** the editor engine applied a picked color theme's syntax
  colors only on a theme switch, so after a start every Shiki, extension or Claude Dark theme drew
  Dark+ syntax; it now loads them when the engine starts.
- **Side bar pages:** a webview page in the side bar gets the color the side bar paints (read
  from the page: which token that is depends on the theme and panel style) as its
  `--vscode-editor-background` and `--vscode-sideBar-background`, so its body matches the side
  bar's header.
- **The command palette's order** (`quickOpen/commandRank.ts`): how well a label matches comes
  first (the query starting a word, then consecutive letters, then scattered letters), then
  recently used, then the score: a recently used command whose label only had the letters
  scattered ("Git: Keep or delete the file in merge editor" for "theme") came first. Typing a
  start of "theme" (`t` … `theme`) puts Color theme first, as the owner asked.
- **External agents' model label:** before the agent has started (Claude Code over ACP takes a
  few seconds), the composer names the model it reported last time and the one chosen for it,
  not the agent alone.
- **Claude Dark:** a built-in color theme in VS Code's format (`core/themes/claudeDark.ts`), its
  colors sampled from screenshots of the Claude desktop app's dark mode (its editor and chat):
  neutral near-black surfaces (editor and panels `#191919`, side bar `#1f1f1f`, fields `#252525`,
  borders `#303030`), light gray text, the clay orange `#d97757` as the accent, and its code
  view's syntax colors (keywords `#cb7bf3`, functions and built-in types `#6cb8fe`, types and
  parameters `#f9ad5e`, strings `#9ae960`, numbers and constants `#4fe8e8`, object keys
  `#f37b80`, comments `#808898`, brackets gold / orchid / blue by depth). Listed first among the
  bundled themes (Color theme…).
- **Help menu:** Toggle full screen is gone from it (View → Appearance → Full screen and the
  command stay, as in VS Code).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (the shim's show-while-resolving test, a background
tab in the dock, Claude Dark's token mapping); in the test app with the installed Claude Code
and no folder open: the agent's chat stays active on the right with Claude Code's tab beside it,
the side bar stays on Channels; the sample file in Claude Dark draws its syntax colors. No
installer build.

### D270 — Agents show their model's logo; Delete in the side bar's menus; Customize's breadcrumb
**Context:** the owner asked that an agent can show the logo of the model it uses (Codex's for a
builder on Codex) wherever its face shows, as the default for every agent but the main one, with
the character faces still a choice in the agent editor; that every view follow at once when it
changes; Delete in the side bar's menus for chats and channels; and a breadcrumb on the Customize
page back to the agent's settings, instead of the Providers page's Agent settings button.
**Decision:**
- **The icon code `model`** (`core/agent/faces.ts`: `MODEL_ICON`, `isModelIcon`, `iconCode`): an
  agent file's `icon: model` — or no icon at all — shows its model's logo. `agentFace(icon, name,
  model)` returns the name's face with `model` set (the agent's model key, `""` for the default
  model), so the face stays for where no logo is found. A face code works as before.
- **Drawing** (`ui/AgentFace.ts`): a face with `model` asks the resolver the agent extension sets
  (`setModelFaceResolver`: an external agent's logo for `acp/…`, else its provider's badge, the
  same as the composer's model pill) and draws that badge in the face's box (`.is-model`), with
  the working ring and the waiting dot as before. The element carries what a redraw needs
  (`data-model`, `data-face`), so `refreshModelFaces()` redraws them in place when the default
  model, the providers or the registry agents change.
- **Which model:** the agent's own (`agent.subagents` or its file), else the default; in a chat's
  header and details, the model that chat runs on.
- **Defaults:** new agents (the editor, `agent.createAgent` without `icon`) and the team write
  `icon: model`. The team's files written before move to it once (`withTeamModelIcon`, global
  state `teamIconsModel`) when they still have the face they were written with; a face the user
  picked stays. The main agent keeps its own face; `agent.setMainAgent {icon: "model"}` (and the
  picker on the Agents page) gives it the logo too.
- **The editor:** Model icon / Character above the face picker. Picking a face, a color or
  Shuffle is Character; Model icon writes `icon: model`, the character face kept for going back.
- **Following changes:** the side bar, the Inbox, the chat's header and the details panel already
  redraw when the agents list does; a chat's reply headers now also redraw (the speaker's face is
  in the reply's signature, and the list re-renders when the agents or the main agent change).
- **Delete:** Recent's menu has Delete (`agent.deleteSession`, which asks); a channel's has Delete
  channel (`agent.deleteChannel`, new, destructive: asks once, closes its tab, removes it and
  deletes its conversations and threads). Archive stays for keeping them. The body of
  `agent.deleteSession` is now `deleteChat()` (`commands.ts`), shared by both.
- **Customize:** "Agent settings › Customize" at the top (the agent editor's breadcrumb style);
  the link opens Settings at Agent. The Agent settings buttons on Providers, Rules and
  Auto-approve are gone.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (the model icon codes, the team's move), the UI script
`agent-faces-m7-26` in the test app.

### D271 — The agent's memory on par; Claude Dark by default; a held Escape; folders closing
**Context:** the owner asked for the agent's memory to work like Claude Code's own (corrections
saved as they're made, with why, updated rather than duplicated) without costing more tokens;
Claude Dark as the default theme; the Windows bug where a typed command lost its first letter;
a hand-check list for the installed build; a skill that teaches the agent this repo's test loop.
Found meanwhile: closing the folder failed running VS Code extensions, and an agent's model icon
showed Ollama's logo when new chats run on an external agent.
**Decision:**
- **Memory** (`core/agent/memory.ts`, `extensions/agent/memory.ts`): `remember` takes `why` (kept
  on the note's line, `- fact — why: reason _(date, session)_`, not in the index) and `replaces`
  (words from the note it corrects: that note is replaced, or with an empty note removed;
  `replaceNote`; nothing matching adds it as new). A note that differs only in its why isn't added
  twice. The prompt's instructions say to save the user's corrections and stated preferences
  right away (user scope when they hold everywhere), with a short why, and to replace an
  outdated note. Tokens: the instructions stayed about the same length; the index lost a third
  (1800 characters, two notes per topic, facts only); the user's own notes show in full up to
  their 1200 characters, since they're the preferences. User-scope notes still ask the user first
  (a prompt injection in one folder mustn't follow them everywhere).
- **Claude Dark is the default color theme** (`workbench.colorTheme`, `DEFAULT_COLOR_THEME`).
- **A held Escape:** bash's readline holds a lone Escape until the next key with no timeout, so
  after the user pressed Escape in a Git Bash terminal, a command typed for them lost its first
  letter (`cd .` ran as `d .`: Alt+C). Reproduced in the test app. Typing a command line
  (`terminal.runCommand`, tasks, Run recent command) now goes through `typeCommand`, which first
  sends Ctrl+G (Escape Ctrl+G is readline's abort) when the last key sent was a lone Escape and
  the shell is bash (`typing.ts`). zsh, fish and PowerShell resolve a lone Escape on their own.
- **Closing the folder** stopped every stdio process, an extension's Node host among them: the
  extension failed ("Node ended") and its views went away. `workspace_close` now stops the
  folder's servers only (`stop_folder_servers`): an extension's own processes (`ext-node:…`,
  `ext:…`) stay, as the browser's extension proxies already did. A reload still stops them all.
- **The model icon** for the default model is an external agent's when new chats start on one
  (`agent.model` `acp/…`, which isn't in the providers' list); the editor's big icon has no
  circle behind a logo.
- **`docs/hand-check.md`:** what the suite can't run, as a checklist for an installed build.
- **The `ui-test` skill** (`.agents/skills/ui-test/SKILL.md`, which the agent and other tools
  read): build the test app, write and run a script, keep its folder (`UI_TEST_KEEP=1`, new in
  `scripts/ui-test.mjs`) and look at the screenshots.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (memory's why and replace, the held Escape),
`cargo test --lib` (what a folder closing keeps); in the test app: `terminal-escape-m7-26` (the
raw keys ran `d .`; typed through the fix, `cd .`), `close-folder-ext-m7-26` (failed before the
fix with "Node ended"), `features-m6-34` (the default theme). `a11y-m7-20` couldn't be
confirmed: it runs past its time limit in a different step each run, on Dark+ as on Claude Dark
(feature-gaps §1, flaky).

### D272 — The default agents: Jonna, Plato and Gabby, one per mode; Reset to defaults
**Context:** the owner asked for the main agent to show its model's logo by default too, for the
default team to be two agents named for what they do (a planner and a chat partner, beside the
main agent that builds), for the side bar to say each one's mode (Agent, Plan, Ask) instead of
"Main agent", "Plans" and "Talks it through", and for a way to put the agents back as a new
install has them.
**Decision:**
- **The main agent** shows its model's logo unless a face is picked (no icon setting: the logo;
  Character in its picker writes a face code).
- **The team** is the planner, labelled Plato (role Plan, starts in Plan mode), and the chat
  partner, labelled Gabby (role Ask, starts in Ask mode): Plato for the thinker who plans before
  acting, Gabby for someone who likes to talk. Their ids stay `planner` and `chat`, so their files,
  channels and choices carry over. The builder is no longer written for new users (the main agent
  in Agent mode builds; the Builder template is still in the editor); a builder written before
  stays. Their channel instructions hand work to the main agent or the planner by @name.
- **Roles as modes:** the main agent's tag in the side bar, the new-chat menu and the composer's
  agent menu is "Agent", its role in a group's member list too.
- **Reset to defaults** (`agent.resetAgents`, a button beside "Your agents" on the Agents page):
  asks first (destructive), then every agent in the user's agents folder goes to the app trash,
  the team's files are written again as they first were, and their model and on/off choices
  are cleared. Project agents, Claude Code's and the main agent aren't touched.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (the team's names, roles and modes); in the test app:
`agent-faces-m7-26` (the logos, the side bar's Agent / Ask / Plan, Reset), the channel and team
scripts updated for the two-agent team.

### D273 — Auto means nothing waits; a new project keeps its extensions; each agent's effort and access
**Context:** the owner's screenshot of a group chat in a project the agent had just made: the
review bar above the message box had square top corners, the composer said **Auto** while the
agent's file waited for Accept / Reject, Claude Code for VS Code's icon was gone from the
activity bar, and a group chat's effort and access pills set one value for every agent, unlike
its model pill. Then: a folder closed with agent edits under review reopened without them; a
folder they made wasn't in the welcome page's Recent list after closing it; in Claude Dark the
activity bar's hover was brighter than its active icon; the jump-to-latest button didn't say the
agent was still working; and the minimap showed no git changes.
**Causes:** (1) `.agent-plan + .agent-changes` squared the bar's corners even while the plan
was hidden (it is always the element before it). (2) Auto (`agent.runCommands: "full"`) is a
global setting, but whether edits apply is per chat, started from the folder's last choice:
a new folder's chats started in Review edits under a pill that said Auto. (3) Claude Code ran
in the empty window (D268); the folder made by "Create and start" wasn't trusted yet, so its
code stopped when the folder opened (D261), its context keys went and with them the icon, and
trusting the folder later didn't start it again (only a later use would).
**Decision:**
- **Review bar:** only a plan that shows takes its rounding (`.agent-plan:not([hidden])`).
- **Auto** applies edits in every chat: new chats start applying while it's on (and saved or
  restored ones do when they load), and turning it on switches the chats in the window. Picking
  Review edits under Auto still works; the pill then says "Auto, review edits".
- **A folder the IDE makes for the agent is trusted** (`WorkspaceTrust.trustCreated`, saved
  before it opens): it's new and empty, nothing in it comes from anyone else. Its parent isn't.
- **Trusting a folder starts again** what was stopped because it wasn't trusted and starts with
  the IDE (`onStartupFinished`, `*`), as VS Code activates extensions once a folder is trusted
  (`ExtensionRuntime.resumeStartupCode`).
- **Group chats:** the effort pill reads "Effort" and the access pill "Access", like "Models":
  each lists the chat's agents with their own value and a submenu to change it. The main agent's
  are the chat's (`agent.effort`, the access menu). Another agent's effort and access are the
  user's choices in `agent.subagents` (`effort`, `access: "edit" | "read"`, through
  `agent.setSubagent`), not its file, so a project's agent can't give itself more access; the
  choice beats the file's `permissionMode` ("Its default" goes back to the file's). Access
  offers Accept edits and Read only, not full access: Auto stays one global switch. An agent's
  effort applies to its turns anywhere (a group, its own chat), after a skill's.
- **Edits under review come back:** a saved chat's meta says how many files wait (`pending`);
  when a folder opens (and at start), its chats with edits waiting load, so the editor's inline
  Accept / Reject and the review bar show them. Only chats with a tab loaded before.
- **Recent in every window:** each window kept its own copy of the recent and pinned lists, read
  again only when it wrote them, so a folder opened in another window was missing from this
  one's welcome page. A window reads them again when it gains focus and when its folder closes
  (`workspace.refreshLists`; nothing re-renders when they're unchanged). The owner's
  list on disk had the folder: the save worked, the page was stale.
- **The created folder's path:** `workspace_create_folder` returns the canonical path (as
  opening it names it), so the trust saved for it matches.
- **Activity bar:** the active icon's background is `--bg-active` (a step above hover), not the
  raised surface: an imported theme's raised surface (Claude Dark's `#252525`) was darker than
  the hover overlay.
- **Jump to latest** shows three pulsing dots after its label while the agent works (still with
  reduced motion, dimmed).
- **Minimap:** git's added / changed / deleted marks are drawn in the minimap's left edge, as
  VS Code's, in the same theme colors as the gutter; an agent's edits under review are marked
  on the scrollbar and the minimap in the accent color (`EditorDecoration.mapped`).
- **Handoff waits for a finished turn's save** (`session.settle()`, as sending does): a turn is
  idle a moment before it's released, and `agent.handoff` refused then ("still working").
- `dev.inspectDom` reports `borderRadius`.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (an agent's picked access and effort, its file's
read-only); in the test app: `group-access-m7-27` (new), `empty-window-ext-m7-25` (trusting
the folder starts the extension again); by hand in the test app with two launches on one
profile: an edit left under review in a chat without a tab is back after the restart; a folder
opened from an empty window and closed is listed under Recent.

### D274 — Claude Dark's dimmed text; @mentions colored; @channel
**Context:** in Claude Dark, text meant to be dim (the message box's placeholder, the side bar's
role tags and times, the effort pill) was as bright as the main text; Dark+ was fine. The owner
also asked for @mentions to stand out in the chat as Slack and Discord show them, a hover on an
agent's mention, and `@channel` (Slack) as the word the @ list offers, with Discord's
`@everyone` and `@all` working the same.
**Cause:** imported themes take `--fg-subtle` from `editorLineNumber.activeForeground`, and Claude
Dark's is its text color. Dark+ is built in and doesn't go through the importer.
**Decision:**
- **The importer** doesn't take a dimmed text color that's as bright as the theme's text
  (contrast with it under 1.5): the base theme's stays. Any imported theme with a bright active
  line number gets the same fix.
- **@mentions** in your messages and the agents' replies are a tinted chip (the accent mixed
  in; `@channel` in a warm tint, since it calls on everyone): an agent's label or name, by the
  routing's rules (not in a word or an e-mail address, longest name first), never in code or
  links (`core/agent/groupChat.ts` `mentionRanges`, `view/mentionMarks.ts`). Hovering an agent's
  mention names it, its role and what it does.
- **@channel** is what the @ list offers in a channel, **@everyone** in a group chat that isn't
  one (`everyoneWords`); typing another's start offers it, and all three call on every member
  (`EVERYONE_WORDS`) wherever they're used.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (the importer's dimmed text, mention ranges,
`@channel`); in the test app: `mentions-m7-28` (new).

### D275 — A quicker settings page; the side bar's color; Reset all keeps the agent's settings
**Context:** the owner found the settings page slow: opening it, typing in its search, a dropdown
and quick access over it all lagged. They also asked for floating panels' side bar to match the
panels (with their border) and the darker side bar to be an option of its own, for Reset all to
keep the agent's settings, for quick access to close on any click outside it, and for brighter
text in the chats side bar. @mentions of an older agent weren't colored, and Claude Code's
activity bar icon went away when the folder closed.
**Measured** (the test app, `settings-speed-m7-29`): All settings built its 360 rows at once.
The script's own work was small (about 50 ms), the page's style and layout weren't: typing in
search took 423 ms, a setting changed with the page open 1.3 s. Quick access in a folder of
20 000 files (`quick-access-big-m7-29`) opens in about 0.1 s with no long task: the folder's
size isn't the cause; the settings page open behind it was.
**Decision:**
- **The settings page builds the first screens' rows** (about 40) and each later section when it
  comes near (an IntersectionObserver on the page; until then its card holds about its height),
  and a section off screen skips style and layout (`content-visibility: auto`). A theme list's
  options are rebuilt only when they change, and the reset buttons read what's changed once.
  Measured after: typing 59 ms, a change with the page open about 230 ms, opening 39 ms.
  Left: moving focus with a long page on screen (quick access, a dropdown) still costs about
  0.2 s in the debug build (feature-gaps).
- **Quick access closes on a press anywhere outside it**, not only when its box loses focus (a
  click on what takes no focus, the status bar or an editor's margin, left it open).
- **Floating panels:** the side bar is a card like the editor groups (the panels' color, their
  border and corners), as flush has it. **`workbench.sideBarColor`** (`matching`, the default,
  or `distinct`; `ui.setSideBarColor`, in the Appearance menu) gives the side bar the color
  theme's side bar color in either style: a new token, `--bg-sidebar`, from a theme's
  `sideBar.background` (the built-ins: their sunken surface).
- **Reset all** keeps the agent's settings (`agent.*`: its models, agents and their choices)
  unless "Also reset the agent's settings" is checked; the dialog takes several options now
  (`confirmWithOptions`).
- **Chats side bar:** a row's text is at full strength, its icon stays dim until hovered or open
  (an agent's face keeps its colors); a section's head (Channels, Tasks…) is a row like the
  chats, with their height, corners and hover.
- **@mentions** are colored for every member of the chat (`mentionTargets`), not only agents
  with an agent file: an older agent's mention was answered but not colored.
- **Closing the folder** left trust "unknown" (no folder to decide), which extensions took as
  trust taken back: Node code stopped, and an extension's context keys went with it (Claude
  Code sets the one its activity bar icon waits for once, on activation). An empty window counts
  as trusted for them too, as for `trust.require` (D268).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`; in the test app: `settings-speed-m7-29`,
`panels-sidebar-m7-29` and `quick-access-big-m7-29` (new), `mentions-m7-28`,
`close-folder-ext-m7-26`, `empty-window-ext-m7-25`, `group-m7-10`, `quick-access-m7-22`.

### D276 — A second accent; accent shades from the accent itself
**Context:** in imported themes an accent button's hover was the built-in blue, and so were
info notes (the agent page's Customize card, the chat's "Started in…" note) and links: a theme
maps `--accent` but not its hover or text color. The owner asked for hovers to be a shade of the
accent, and for a second accent: Claude Dark keeps its clay orange for most things, but lists'
focus and selection, resize handles and drop targets take Claude's blue, as in the Claude app.
**Decision:**
- **`--accent-hover`** comes from `--accent`: with relative colors (`oklch(from …)`, behind
  `@supports`) a light accent darkens and a dark one lightens; without, a step toward the text
  color.
- **`--accent-secondary`** (with `-subtle` and `-border`) is the accent unless a theme sets its
  own. Claude Dark does, `#2C84DB` (Claude's blue), through a key of our own in its colors,
  `secondaryAccent` (not a VS Code color: other themes keep one accent, as the owner asked).
  It colors a focused list or tree's selection and focus outline (`--bg-selected-focus`), resize
  handles on hover and while dragging (they were gray), and every drop indicator (the dock's drop
  preview and caret, the activity bar's drop line, tree drop targets, the chat's drop zone, the
  notebook's drop line, the rebase list).
- **`--accent-text`** (links, info notes: `--status-info-*`) comes from the second accent,
  lightened in dark themes and darkened in light ones, instead of a fixed blue.
- Fields and buttons keep `--focus-ring` (the accent): only lists moved to the second accent.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`; in the test app: `accents-m7-30` (new: Claude Dark's
tree selection is the blue, Dark+'s its own accent; screenshots of the tree and the Customize
card).

### D277 — A distinct side bar colors what's inside it
**Context:** with `workbench.sideBarColor: "distinct"`, sticky rows (the explorer's folders,
Source control's "Changes") and other parts painted with the surface color kept the panels'
color, a darker band on the side bar.
**Decision:** the side bar sets `--bg-surface` to `--bg-sidebar` for itself and what's in it, so
everything painted with the surface color follows. The chats side bar's section heads (Channels,
Tasks, Direct messages, Recent) are a step dimmer than the chats again (`--fg-muted`, full on
hover), as section labels are elsewhere. Clicking a skill that comes with the IDE
(build-extension) opened its `builtin:` path as a file, which Windows refused ("filename
syntax is incorrect"): `agent.openSkill` opens a skill's SKILL.md, or a built-in one's text
read-only (Customize in its actions still makes an editable copy). Rules, commands and agents
list only what has a file.
**Verified:** `npm run check`; in the test app: `skills-m7-5` (clicking build-extension opens
its text).

### D278 — Tighter floating gaps; three tab styles; long Markdown previews
**Context:** with floating panels the gaps between panels felt wide at default density
(compact's looked right) and too wide at comfortable. The owner wanted a choice of tab looks:
today's, the classic square tabs with the accent on top, and VS Code's newer tabs, where the
active tab joins the editor under a strip of another color. A 10 000-line Markdown file
previewed with a long lag: every code block, once colored in the background, re-rendered the
whole document (about 240 of them), and scroll sync measured every block on each scroll.
**Decision:**
- **Gaps:** `--size-gap-split`, the gap where the splitters are, is 4px in compact and default
  density and 6px in comfortable (it was 4 / 6 / 8). The outer gap (`--size-gap-panel`) is
  unchanged.
- **`workbench.tabStyle`** (`ui.setTabStyle`, also in the Appearance menu): `rounded` (the
  default, unchanged), `classic` (square tabs side by side with a hairline between them, the
  accent along the active tab's top, dimmer in a group without focus) and `connected` (the
  active tab rises from the editor with rounded top corners and curved feet, its label level
  with the others'; the others stay rounded in the strip). Classic and connected paint the strip `--bg-tab-strip` (a step off the
  editor, lighter in dark themes and darker in light ones) and the active tab the editor's own
  color. It is a first-paint setting like the density.
- **Markdown preview:** a colored code block is patched into the page when it arrives (find
  searches again once the burst is over), not by re-rendering; the colored spans are parsed once
  and cloned. Pictures that load re-render once per burst (50 ms). Scroll sync measures the
  blocks once per render or resize and binary searches them, so scrolling either side and
  moving the editor's cursor no longer walk the whole document.
- **`morph`** returns at once for an identical subtree (`isEqualNode`, compared natively): a
  re-render after typing in that file went from about 175 ms of morphing to 13 ms; the whole
  re-render is about 130 ms. Opening it still lays out every block once (about 0.4 s).
  `content-visibility: auto` on the blocks was tried and dropped: measuring blocks inside
  skipped content for scroll sync forced layout block by block (10 s).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test`; in the test app: `tabs-m7-31` (new: each style's
active tab and strip, the gaps; screenshots), `md-big-m7-31` (new: a 10 000-line file previews,
every code block colored, the preview follows the editor to line 9000).

### D279 — Back and forward; VS Code's tab options; the debugger's extras; five settings
**Context:** from the Zed and IntelliJ comparison (`docs/zed-intellij-gaps.md`), the owner asked
for back / forward navigation with VS Code's arrows (and Zed's place for them as an option), the
tab options, triggered breakpoints, step into target, restart frame and inline values, each
matching VS Code's behavior and settings, plus five settings that add something without changing
how the IDE works.
**Decision:**
