- **Go back / Go forward** (`workbench.navigateBack` / `navigateForward`, Alt+Left / Alt+Right,
  Ctrl+- / Ctrl+Shift+- on macOS, the mouse's side buttons, the Go menu): `core/navigation`
  keeps the places the cursor was (VS Code's rule: another file or 10+ lines away is a new place,
  nearer moves update the current one; 50 kept), recorded from the editors' activity. The ← →
  sit left of the title bar's search box as in VS Code (`workbench.navigationControl.enabled`);
  `workbench.navigationControl.location: "tabBar"` puts them at the start of every tab strip
  instead (where Zed has them). The keys skip a focused terminal (its shell's own Alt+arrows).
- **Tabs**, by VS Code's settings: `workbench.editor.decorations.colors` / `.badges` (on: the
  tab's git color and letter, and now problems: `problems.decorations.enabled` colors files with
  errors or warnings and their folders, in the explorer too, the count first: "2, M");
  `tabActionLocation` (left / right) and `tabActionCloseVisibility`; **pinned tabs** (VS Code's
  sticky tabs: `layout.pinEditor` / `unpinEditor`, Ctrl+K Shift+Enter, the tab menu; first in the
  group with a pin that unpins; Close others / to the right / saved / all and the limit leave
  them; `pinnedTabsOnSeparateRow`); `workbench.editor.limit.*` (off; closes the least recently
  used saved, unpinned tabs past the value, per group or all); `focusRecentEditorAfterClose`
  (on, as VS Code: closing the active tab shows the one used before it, where it used to show its
  neighbor). `workbench.editor.tabPlacement` (ours, IntelliJ's idea): an editor group's tabs as a
  list on its left or right (`--size-tab-list`); panels keep theirs on top. Drag and drop finds
  the slot in rows or a column (`core/dock/tabs.ts`, tested).
- **Five settings**, VS Code's names: `window.autoDetectColorScheme` with
  `workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme` / `preferredLightColorTheme`; `editor.formatOnSaveMode`
  (file / modifications / modificationsIfAvailable: the lines changed since the git index, with
  the language's range formatter); `markdown.preview.fontFamily` / `fontSize` (14, VS Code's) /
  `lineHeight`; `workbench.editor.focusRecentEditorAfterClose` (above); `editor.wrappingIndent`.
- **Debugger, as VS Code:** **triggered breakpoints** (`debug.addTriggeredBreakpoint`, "Wait for
  breakpoint…" on a breakpoint; kept back from a session until it stops on the trigger, then sent
  to that session only, reset when it ends; a dashed ring in the margin and the Breakpoints view
  while waiting); **step into target** (`debug.stepIntoTarget`, the editor menu while paused, when
  the debugger reports `supportsStepInTargetsRequest`: the target under the cursor, else a
  picker); **restart frame** (`debug.restartFrame`, the call stack's menu and a hover button, when
  `supportsRestartFrame`; Node and browser pages through the inspector's `Debugger.restartFrame`);
  **inline values** (`debug.inlineValues` on / off / auto): `name = value` after the lines up to
  the stop, VS Code's generic matcher (scopes' line ranges, comments and strings skipped, 100
  names, 150 characters). One departure: VS Code's "auto" shows values only with an extension's
  provider, which nothing here registers, so "auto" uses the matcher for the languages the built-in
  debuggers cover (JS/TS, Python, Go, Rust, C/C++, C#). `ide://debug` has each breakpoint's
  `triggeredBy` / `waiting`, the session's `canStepIntoTargets` / `canRestartFrame`, and
  `inlineValues`.
- Also: Loaded scripts' section title had its chevron stretched across the row, the label pushed
  right (a rule growing the title's first span, which there is the chevron); `debug-m6-44` sets
  Dark+, whose token classes it checks (failing since Claude Dark became the default, D271).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1596); in the test app: `tabs-nav-m7-32` (new: back /
forward and both button places, pinned tabs and their row, the close button's side and none,
the most recent tab after closing, a problem's color and count on its tab, the limit, tabs on the
side, the theme following the system) and `debug-extras-m7-32` (new: a triggered breakpoint chain,
its dashed ring, inline values, restart frame, step into target on the mock adapter); the full
suite: 205 of 212 before the fixes above; the rest fail on D278's commit too (feature-gaps, Code
health). Not checked: step into target and restart frame with real debugpy / lldb-dap / GDB, the
system's mode switching live, format on save's modifications mode with a real formatter.

### D280 — Every UI script passing: the races behind the failures
**Context:** the full UI suite had seven scripts failing (some for weeks, on and off). The owner
asked for zero, looking past the tests for real causes: loading, timing, popups, the test
machine.
**Decision:** each failure traced to its cause; the IDE's bugs fixed, the tests' assumptions
corrected.
- **Debugging a compound (real bugs, `debug-m7-5`):** the sessions of a compound start together,
  and each prepared the auto-attach folder (`debug/autoattach.rs`) at the same moment. One
  shared temporary name for the bootloader failed the second session ("cannot find the file
  specified"); a session's clean-up of stale folders removed another's folder made a moment
  before (no `alive` file yet, or one dated after the clean-up began), so its child processes
  ran without the debugger. The bootloader is written through `store::atomic_write`, retried
  briefly (a file being replaced can't be read for a moment on Windows), and a folder counts
  as fresh by its own time until `alive` exists. Then V8 itself: function breakpoints paused
  before every script (an instrumentation breakpoint), and in a program with a worker thread
  V8 failed a check in its scope walk and ended the process (exit 0x80000003). Function
  breakpoints now find declarations as each script is parsed (`Debugger.scriptParsed`), as
  before for scripts already loaded.
- **The file watcher on Windows (`git-m7-7`):** notify's Windows backend dropped what a burst
  of changes overflowed (a git checkout, an install: ReadDirectoryChangesW returns nothing, or
  `ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR`, on which it stopped watching for good, logging to nowhere). notify
  8.2.0 is now a patched copy (`src-tauri/vendor/notify`, CC0, `PATCHED.md`, through
  `[patch.crates-io]`): lost changes keep the watch and send a rescan, which the file index
  turns into a rebuild and "many changed" for Source control. Also, the index's listener is
  registered one call at a time (opening a folder fired two registrations that could reach Rust
  in either order). The test itself deleted its file within the watcher's 300 ms debounce, where
  a file made and removed is one no-op: it waits a second now.
- **Tests that assumed timing:** a step with a timeout runs again until its expectation holds,
  so a `debug.start` expecting two sessions started the compound again when a child attached
  first (also in `gaps10-m7-6`, `parA-m7-6`: now started once, the sessions waited for after);
  `acp-group-m7-11` read a reply's speaker before the reply ended; `parA-m7-6` matched the
  terminals from before the folder reopened; `a11y-m7-20` read focus rings in a window that
  wasn't in front (no focus styles apply there: the check brings its window forward, or says
  `windowFocused: false`); `ghost-text-m7-7` raced the TypeScript suggestion
  list, which hides ghost text (it turns quick suggestions off); `terminal-m6-49` hovered a
  failed command while ConPTY was still redrawing its rows, and expected 5000 lines of a
  200 000-line flood, of which Windows' ConPTY passes on about 4000 (the scrollback is 1000
  there, so the command line still scrolls off); `vscode-shim-m7-21` expected the badge "H"
  alone, now "1, H" with its problem count (D279); `debug-m6-44` checks Dark+'s token classes.
- **The debug view (the owner's report):** opening Loaded scripts pushed Breakpoints past the
  bottom with no way to scroll there. The sections now shrink to fit (each list scrolls), the view
  scrolls when even that isn't enough, and a long exception's text scrolls past four lines.
- **Agent faces** in the chats side bar's direct messages and the chat's header are 16 px, as on
  their tabs (they were 18 and 20).

### D281 — Files dropped from the system open, as in VS Code
**Context:** the owner: dropping a file from the system onto the window (anywhere but the
explorer) should open it, as VS Code does. Only files inside the open folder opened; others did
nothing, and a dropped folder did nothing either.
**Decision:** `explorer.openDropped` (what the drop handler runs once the explorer's folders and
the parts that take drops themselves, the terminal and the agent's chat, are ruled out): dropped
files open in an editor of the group under the pointer, from any folder (the user's own choice,
as D190 lets a typed or clicked path in); a dropped folder opens as the workspace when none is
open, else a picker offers "Add to workspace" or "Open folder" (VS Code asks the same). Telling
folders from files outside the workspace needs Rust: `fs_dropped_entries` describes only the
paths the OS reported in the last drop, so the page can't probe the disk with it.
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `cargo clippy`; by hand (the UI suite can't make a system drag):
`docs/manual-test.md` D281.

### D282 — One border color on every theme; built-in themes named; dropdowns open the IDE's menu
**Context:** the owner, three reports: on some themes (Monokai) the explorer side bar's border
looked a different color from every other panel's; Settings' theme list showed two "Night Owl"
with no way to tell the bundled one from an extension's; and dropdowns opened the system's list,
which looks nothing like the IDE's menus.
**Decision:**
- **Borders:** a panel's border is translucent, so it took the color of what's under it: the side
  bar's own background (a theme's distinct side bar color) instead of the window's, as the dock's
  panels have. The side bar, the dock and its groups now clip their background to inside the
  border (`background-clip: padding-box`), so every border blends with the same window color.
  Those rules set `background-color`, since the `background` shorthand resets the clip.
- **Theme names:** bundled themes (Dark+, Light+, Shiki's) say "(built in)" in the dropdown (the
  setting's value is still the name). When an installed extension and the bundle have a theme of
  the same name, the extension's is the one listed and applied: the user installed it on purpose.
  Loaded themes are cached by source and name, so the switch isn't served the bundled one's colors.
- **Dropdowns:** `ui/SelectMenu.ts` takes over every single-choice `<select>` in every window (one
  capturing listener per document, no change to the pages): a press, or Alt+↓/↑, F4, Space or
  Enter, opens the IDE's menu right under the field and at least as wide, the chosen option checked
  and in view, option groups as headings, a search box past 15 options. Picking sets the value and
  fires `input` and `change`, so pages listen as before; arrows on a closed field still step
  through values. A long list goes on the side with more room, shortened to fit, never over the
  field (`MenuOptions.flush` / `minWidth`). `data-native-select` keeps the system list.
**Verified:** `select-menu-m7-33` (the built-in label, the menu under the field and checked, typing
filters, Enter changes the setting); the side bar's border by pixel on Monokai, flush and floating;
`npm run check`, `npm test`, all UI scripts.

**Context:** the owner asked for a full pass over the Markdown in the repository: the user guide
brought to VS Code's documentation standard, the README and the feature gaps brought up to date,
the two gap lists (VS Code / Cursor, Zed / IntelliJ) merged with finished items dropped. Along the

in the channels side bar's menus and on Go to references, the pinned tab row's line running

  New pages: the user interface, search, the agent's team and channels, customizing the agent,
  tasks, notebooks, keyboard shortcuts, remote development, workspaces and trust, troubleshooting.
  Writing it found old errors, now right: `@lang` settings do write `"[language]"` blocks; four
  bundled extensions, not two; menu paths under Git → Branch / GitHub; the Customize chips; quick

  a ranked "Next up", the owner's alpha items, then open items by area with where each comes from

- **Docs brought up to date:** `README.md` (VS Code extensions, remote, multi-root, the team, test
  counts), `PLAN.md`'s status, What's new (`release-notes.md`: m7.12 to m7.33), status notes on the

- **Tables:** a Markdown table is a card as wide as its content, 1px `--border-subtle`,

- **Menus:** the channels side bar's channel, task, agent and chat menus and the Inbox's have

- **Fixes found on the way:** Git → Branch → "Create branch…" pointed at a command that doesn't

**Verified:** a link check of the guide (every page link, anchor and `command:` id resolves, no

### D284 — Extensions like VS Code's: Update buttons, search syntax, verified publishers; one Go Live
**Context:** the owner couldn't find how to update Claude Code for VS Code (its row under
Updates, its page and its gear menu had no Update), asked for VS Code's search (`publisher:"…"`
found nothing; Microsoft's extensions seemed missing), Install ▾, verified marks, the stars and
downloads on an installed extension's page, and clicking a publisher to search for it. Also: Live
Server's status icons drew as a dot, our Go Live sat beside Live Server's, a preview opened in an
outside browser didn't reload on save, and Claude Dark left CSS custom properties uncolored.
**Decision:**
- **Updates, as VS Code:** a row with a newer version on Open VSX has **Update** (its tooltip the
  version); its page leads with **Update to x.y.z** (Open turns secondary); its gear menu starts
  with it; "Updating…" while it installs (`store.ts` `pendingUpdate`).
- **Search syntax** (`core/extensions/extensionQuery.ts`, tested): VS Code's `publisher:`,
  `@category:`, `@tag:`, `@id:`, `@sort:`, `@popular`, `@recentlyPublished`, `@installed`,
  `@enabled`, `@disabled`, `@builtin`, `@updates`, `@recommended`, `ext:`; the installed-only
  ones ask Open VSX nothing. Open VSX has no publisher filter, so `publisher:` searches each of
  the publisher's namespaces and keeps those results; "Microsoft" stands for its namespaces there
  (`ms-python`, `ms-vscode`, `ms-toolsai`…). A filter button in the box lists them
  (`extensions.show {query}`).
- **Verified publishers:** Open VSX's `verified` is shown as VS Code's check (`badge-check`, the
  second accent) on store rows, installed rows (as far as the window has seen the namespace) and
  both pages.
- **An installed extension's page** fetches its Open VSX facts once: downloads, the stars (which
  open its reviews on the website, `extensions.openStorePage {reviews}`), the verified mark. The
  publisher's name searches `publisher:"…"`; categories and tags search `@category:` / `@tag:`, on
  the store page too.
- **Install ▾** on store rows and the store page: Install specific version….
- **Codicons from extensions** (`$(circle-slash)`, `$(broadcast)`) map to the IDE's icons through
  the reverse of the product icon map, everywhere `knownIcon` is used; `$(name~spin)` in status
  text shows the icon.
- **One Go Live:** ours stays (the agent and the browser pane use it) but leaves the status bar
  while Live Server, Live Preview or Five Server is installed and enabled (context key
  `liveServerExtensionEnabled`), or when `browser.goLive.statusBar` is off. A static preview opened
  in an outside browser waits on the proxy's `/__ide/live?since=N` (a change counter bumped by
  saves and live edits, `Shared::bump_live`; a long poll, 25 s) and reloads, as Live Server's
  pages do; a dev server's pages (proxied) don't get it, they have their own reload.
- **Claude Dark:** CSS custom properties, SCSS and Less variables and vendor-prefixed properties
  take the property color; keyword values, font names, units and colors the constant color.
- Not on Open VSX, by Microsoft's license: Dev Containers, Remote - SSH, Live Share, Pylance (the
  guide says so; the IDE has its own remote development).
**Verified:** `npm run check`, `npm test` (1601), `cargo check`; in the test app:
`ext-update-m7-34` (live Open VSX: Dracula 2.24.1 → Update on the row, the page and the gear menu,
updated from the row; the page's mark, downloads and stars; the publisher click; `publisher:"Microsoft"
python`; `@builtin`; the filter button; Install ▾) and `go-live-m7-34` (the setting hides Go Live; a
waiting request on `/__ide/live` answers when a file changes).

### D285 — VS Code extensions survive another IDE version and quick trust changes
**Context:** the owner: after opening or closing a folder, Claude Code for VS Code sometimes lost
its activity bar icon and status item ("Not started yet"), and a freshly installed Live Server
showed "failed". Their session log had the cause: `Cannot find module …\extension-hostnode-host-<hash>.cjs`, then "Node ended (exit code 1)" for both. A newer build had started
beside the open window (an update installed) and, writing its own Node host script, removed
every other version's; the open window's next Node start (a folder change restarts extensions'
code) found nothing. Claude Code's views wait for a context key its code sets
(`claude-code:doesNotSupportSecondarySidebar`), so without its code they disappear.
**Decision:**
- **The host script is asked for before every Node start** (`workerHost.ts`), not once per
  session: the backend writes it only when it's missing, so a removed copy comes back.
- **Other versions' copies are removed only after a week** untouched (`ext_node_host_script`): an
  installed build and a dev build open together no longer delete each other's.
- **Stopping and starting an extension's code can't cross** (`runtime.ts`, found while looking):
  a start waits for a stop still finishing (its clean-up, `workerGone`, removed the new worker's
  status items, context keys and processes); a start a stop overtook gives up, and a resume right
  after a stop no longer receives that doomed start (it starts afresh); an old worker's exit
  doesn't touch the current one.
- The test extension (`vscodehello`) sets a status item at activation, `$(broadcast) Hello live`,
  which also checks D284's codicon map.
**Verified:** `trust-flip-ext-m7-34` (new): the status item after trust flips (also while its
Node process starts), after closing and reopening the folder, and after its host script is
removed (the owner's case; it failed on the build before this fix with "Node ended");
`close-folder-ext-m7-26`, `empty-window-ext-m7-25`, `vscode-shim`, `ext-update-m7-34`;
`npm run check`, `npm test`, `cargo clippy`.

### D286 — Agents only: one list, one model each, the main agent in the editor; live background output
**Context:** the owner found the agent setup confusing: built-in helpers (explore, plan, reviewer,
general) beside "your agents", the main agent's Chat / Plan / Build models beside Plato (who plans
on a model of his own), modes (Agent / Plan / Ask) beside agents that are those modes, and the main
agent edited in a different place from the others. OpenBot and Grok Bot keep one list of agents
you make and talk to; neither has helpers to configure (OpenBot only shows a turn's subagents as a
card in the chat). VS Code merged its chat modes into custom agents in one picker.
**Decision:**
- **The Agents page** is the main agent, your agents and "Let agents hand work to each other". The
  built-in helpers left it: explore and the reviewer keep working (their models are the settings
  **Explore model** / **Review model**, `agent.exploreModel` / `agent.reviewModel`, beside
  `agent.explore` and `agent.autoReview`; a choice in `agent.subagents` still counts); general is
  "the agent itself in a fresh context"; the built-in plan is used only when you have no planner of
  your own (`delegable()`, `get("plan")`). Claude Code's `Plan`, `general-purpose` and `Explore`
  map to those. `ide://agent/subagents` has `delegable`.
- **One model per agent:** the main agent's card has one model, like the others; Plan mode's and
  Build's own models are advanced settings (planning on another model is Plato's).
- **The main agent in the agent editor** (`agent.editAgent {name: "agent"}`, its card, the Channels
  menu): its face, name and model, with links to the rules and memory that are its instructions;
  what can't change isn't there (`mainAgentEditor.ts`).
- **The face picker** on Model icon shows no faces, colors or Shuffle.
- **Modes are agents:** the composer's picker lists agents only (VS Code's), each working its own
  way (the editor's **How it works**: builds, plans, answers); Plan and Ask with the main agent are
  offered only when no agent of yours does them. Shift+Tab steps through the main agent, the
  planner and the chat partner (Claude Code's Agent → Plan → Ask). Under the hood a chat still has
  its agent and a work mode, so Build, group chats and external agents' own modes are unchanged.
- **Hand-offs read as such:** a delegate step says "Handed to Plato: …" ("a fresh context" for
  general).
- **Background commands** (Claude Code's View live output): **View output** under the step that
  started one opens `agent.processOutput`, a panel tab that follows its output while it runs, with
  Stop; the chat's list stays five minutes after the last one ends.
- No new default agents: the team stays the main agent, Plato and Gabby.
**Verified:** `agents-one-list-m7-35` (new), `agent-m7-2-processes` (live output, the list after the
end), the agent scripts touching modes, the picker and the team; `npm run check`, `npm test`.

### D287 — The Agents page as one grid; Model setup (presets) removed
**Context:** the owner, on D286's page: Explore and Review were meant to be agents, not hidden; the
main agent's separate card and its Model setup chip looked like a different kind of thing; and
presets were pointless now that each agent has its own model.
**Decision:**
- **One grid of cards:** the main agent first (a card like the others: face, name, role Agent,
  what it does, its model, a Main badge; always on, so no switch; opens its editor), your agents,
  then **Explore** and **Review**, built in (a Built in badge, a switch, a model; their names
  aren't links since they can't be edited, Duplicate is in **⋯**), then New agent. Explore's switch
  is `agent.explore`; its and Review's models are `agent.exploreModel` / `agent.reviewModel`
  (`agent.chooseModel {for: "subagent:explore"}` writes them). The page's lead says who works in
  your chats; "Models and providers" left the header (Customize has a Providers tab).
- **Model setup (presets, D196) is removed:** the chip, the model picker's Presets button,
  `agent.savePreset` / `applyPreset` / `deletePreset`, `agent.presets` and `ide://agent/presets`.
  A setting left in a settings.json does nothing.
**Verified:** `agents-one-list-m7-35` (the grid with the main card, Explore and Review; no Model
setup), `agent-m7-13`, `m6-96`, `m6-97` (its presets steps removed); `npm run check`, `npm test`.

### D288 — Agents and subagents, as in Claude Code; agents hand work to each other in the open
**Context:** after D286–D287 the owner asked why Explore and Review couldn't be edited or chatted
with, then whether they were really tools, and settled on Claude Code's model: subagents in the
agent's settings with a model each, the old modes (Plato, Gabby) as agents, and agents still able to
pass work to each other. Claude Code has subagents (workers run with a task, private context,
report back; `.claude/agents` files; built-in Explore, Plan, general-purpose); team bots (OpenBot,
Grok's) have teammates who hand the conversation over in the open.
**Decision:**
- **Two kinds, kept apart.** Agents are the personas you talk to (the agents folders: the main
  agent, Plato, Gabby, yours). Subagents are workers: built-in Explore, Plan, Review, General
  purpose, and Claude Code's files in the project's and the user's `.claude/agents`, now read as
  subagents (they were agents before). `SubagentDef.kind`, `isSubagent`; each kind has its own
  names; Claude Code's names for its built-ins map to ours.
- **Two ways to pass work:** `delegate` runs a subagent (privately, a report: "Ran Review: …";
  `agent.delegate`, "Let agents run subagents"); the new `hand_off` tool brings an agent into the
  chat to answer next in the open, and it can hand back (`agent.handOff`, default on, "Let agents
  hand work to each other"; `agent.inviteAgent` now queues an agent already in the chat too). Your
  agents are no longer run as hidden subagents. Subagents get neither tool.
- **Where they're set up:** the Subagents section of the main agent's page in the agent editor
  (a model and a switch per subagent, the master switch, New subagent, Customize/Edit); the Agents
  page shows agents only, the hand-off switch and a link. `agent.newSubagent` now writes a Claude
  Code file in `.claude/agents` (was: an agent); new `agent.editSubagent` (a built-in one is
  copied there with `subagentFile` and the copy replaces it). `agent.exploreModel` /
  `agent.reviewModel` are gone (models are in `agent.subagents` like any subagent's).
- **Per agent, as Claude Code's `Agent(…)` tool list** (the owner asked for the section on every
  agent's page): an agent file's `subagents:` says which it may run (no key: all; `none`). Every
  agent's page shows the section; there the switches write that list, while a subagent's model
  and instructions stay shared (the main agent's page switches them on or off for everyone). The
  delegate tool offers the answering agent's list; an agent not allowed Explore loses the tool.
- **AI features on the Agents page** (the owner's ask): above External agents, a row per AI
  feature outside the chat (Edit with AI, suggestions as you type, next-edit suggestions, commit
  messages, memory tidy-up), each with its switch (its `….enabled` setting, D172) and its model
  (`agent.chooseModel {for: "feature:…"}`). Settings and the status bar's sparkle keep theirs.
- **Every model chip opens the chat's model picker** (the owner's ask: the plain list had no
  external agent's own models, so "Claude Code · Sonnet" couldn't be picked for Plato). The
  picker takes a target (`ModelTarget`: its current model, a "Same as the chat" row, whether
  external agents may be picked) and `showModelChooser` / `chooseModelAt` (`modelChooser.ts`)
  open it from the Agents page's cards and AI features, the agent editor's Model and the
  Subagents rows; a pick runs agent.chooseModel. Subagents and the typed-against features can't
  pick an external agent.
- **An agent's own model of an external agent** (the owner: Plato set to Claude Code · Sonnet
  answered on Opus, and the main agent lost Opus, since `agent.externalAgentChoices` is one per
  external agent): one of your agents keeps `agentModel` beside `model: acp/<agent>` in
  `agent.subagents` (agent.setSubagent `agentModel`, `agentExternalModel`). Before each turn on
  the external agent, `AcpBackend.syncModel` sets the connection's model to the answering
  agent's own, else back to the remembered one (the main agent's), without remembering it; a chat
  switched to an agent (agent.setChatAgent, `syncExternalModel`) follows at once so its pill is
  right. An agent whose model is a launch flag (`--model`) keeps one model: switching restarts it.
  The chat's picker in an agent's chat now sets that agent's external model too (it used to hand
  it to the chat). Chips read "Claude Code · Sonnet 5.5" (`modelChipLabel`). Search
  results in the picker sit under each provider's or agent's name (OpenCode's free models looked
  like OpenRouter's), and no longer repeat Recent's.
- **Plan model and Build model are removed** (`agent.planModel`, `agent.buildModel`, chooseModel's
  `mode:plan` / `mode:build`): with one model per agent they repeat Plato's model (the plan) and the
  main agent's (the build, which Build hands to). Claude Code's "opusplan" is Plato on one model
  and the main agent on another.
- **Model settings open the model picker in Settings too:** a `SettingPicker` hook
  (`settings.registerPicker`; the editor draws a button) for the default model, the backup model
  and each AI feature's model, so every model choice in the IDE is the same picker.
- **External agents have no model control on the Agents page:** their model is always an agent's
  (the main agent's is `agent.externalAgentChoices`, the others' their own `agentModel`), and the
  row's second control for the same value overwrote the main agent's (the owner set Jonna to Opus,
  the row to Default, and Jonna opened on Default).
- **The editor's "How it works" is "Mode": Agent, Plan, Ask** (was Builds, Plans, Answers), the
  names the chat's mode menu, Cursor and VS Code use.
**Verified:** unit tests (kind, the Customize file round-trip, no hand_off/delegate inside a
subagent, `subagents:` parsing and writing, Explore denied); `agent-external-model-m7-36` (an
agent on the mock ACP agent's smart model, the main agent on fast, one connection);
`agents-one-list-m7-35` (no subagent cards on the Agents page; the section's rows;
New subagent; its switch; Customize Review; Gabby's own list) and the agent, team and channel
scripts (their test agents moved from `.claude/agents` to the agents folder);
`npm run check`, `npm test`.

### D290 — Fixes kept from the tasks experiment

The Linear-style tasks (D289) stay on the `agent-tasks` branch for now; these fixes made there
aren't about tasks, so they're on main:
- **A terminal hard-wrapped to 2 columns:** a terminal created before its panel was laid out
  measured 2 columns and told the shell, which wrapped everything it printed to that width for
  good. A size that tiny is never sent; the terminal starts at 80×24 until it has a real one.
- **The sidebar view is remembered per folder** (Channels, Source control…), as VS Code does;
  a folder with none saved still opens on the Explorer.
- **A tab brought forward in a hidden region shows the region** (the chat panel toggled off), as
  VS Code reveals a hidden panel for what opens in it. Background activations leave it hidden.
- **The extension store's verified mark is filled**, in the rating's filled-star color.

### D291 — A plain chat panel (the `simple-chat` branch)

The owner's call: Slack's layout (channels, direct messages, task channels, the Linear-style
board of D289) felt like a plugin on top of what most people want, a chat with an agent, as in
other AI editors. Several agents stay (the agent picker in the composer, @mentions, group chats,
subagents with their own models); the layout around them goes:
- **The sidebar is a Chats list** (`chatsView.ts`, the `agent.chats` id kept), laid out as chat
  apps' side bars: the search field on top, rows for New chat, Usage, Agents and Customize, then
  the chats by folder, this folder's first and each other folder's latest under its name, newest
  first; a folder folds. A row shows its agent's face or a group's faces, its age, working and
  needs-you. No Inbox, Channels or Direct messages sections. The title bar keeps only ⋯
  (Sessions… is in it); right-clicking New chat opens it to the side or in a new tab, with one of
  the agents, or as a group chat (`agent.newSession { side, newTab }`). The chat on screen is the
  selected row, another folder's too, and it's listed even past Show more or a folder's latest few.
- **Every conversation opens in the chat panel:** `showRoomTab` gives a channel's or a direct
  message's conversation to `showThreadTab` (`setRoomConversation`), so everything that opened a
  channel (commands, notifications, agents' posts) opens a chat; only the Inbox keeps the channel
  tab. A channel tab saved in a layout opens its conversation as a plain chat.
- **The chat's header** has no "#channel ›" link (a thread's says "Thread ›" back to its chat)
  and no ▾ beside + (who answers is the composer's agent picker; the side bar's ▾ starts a chat
  with an agent).
- **No "Reply in thread"** on messages: in one chat panel a thread would replace the chat it came
  from, and a chat app's chat has none. A message that has threads still shows its replies row.
- **The chat's cost isn't under the composer** (the Usage page has the costs; the context meter's
  tooltip says this chat's): it shows only near or over a chat budget (`agent.budget.perChat`).
- The agent pill under the composer has a little more room between the face and the name.
- The channel code stays (rooms, posting, the Inbox command) so agents' hand-offs keep working
  and the change is easy to compare; it goes for good if the owner keeps this layout.

### D292 — The agent's tools beside a coding agent's (Claude Code's, on `simple-chat`)

The owner asked to compare the IDE's agents with what Claude Code can do in its desktop app and
upgrade where it makes sense. Most of it was there already: files (images and PDFs read), search
and find, commands in the foreground or background (with a message when one ends), the IDE's
own commands and state, the browser, web search, subagents (background, in a worktree, handing
off), plan mode, a to-do list, memory, skills, hooks, MCP (tools loaded on demand), scheduled
messages. What was missing or awkward:
- **`web_fetch`, a tool of its own.** Reading a page was `call_command web.fetch {url}`, a step
  models missed. It runs web.fetch as the agent, so approval, `agent.webFetch.enabled` and the
  `WebFetch(domain:…)` rules (`toolRules.ts`, `slash.ts`) apply the same; `web_search` and the
  system prompt point to it.
- **`ask_user` like Claude Code's question:** a line under each option (`descriptions`, or
  options as `{ label, description }`), and `multi_select`: picks toggle, **Send** sends them
  comma-separated, each shown as chosen after. Strings alone still work.
- **`edit_file` with `edits`:** several changes to one file in one call, in order, all or none.
  `editsFrom` read them already; the schema now says so (`old_string` / `new_string` aren't
  required when `edits` is given).
- **A Mode submenu in the agent picker** (the owner's ask: the pill said "Jonna · Ask" but the
  menu had no check to match, its Plan / Ask rows only offered when no agent of yours does them).
  The agents are checked by who answers; **Mode ›** (Agent, Plan, Ask, the current one beside it)
  sets how the answering agent works in this chat (agent.setChatMode).
- **A schedule may repeat for up to a year** (was 30 days; still 7 by default): "every day at
  9am" is something people keep. Each one is approved when it's made, and listed with Cancel.

Not taken: the desktop app's own surfaces (artifacts, sessions in the cloud, a terminal panel it
reads, computer use) have the IDE's equivalents already (the browser preview, worktree agents,
`ide://terminals`) or don't fit an editor.

### D293 — Audit before merging the plain chat panel

Three read-only reviews (the agent runtime by `docs/agent-audit.md`, the D290-D292 changes, the
rest of the app and Rust), each finding checked in the code before it was fixed:
- **Agent runtime.** Stop's "hung agent" timer is cleared when the turn ends, so a message sent
  within 3 s of a Stop isn't ended by it. `process_output` `wait_for` looks only at unread output
  (`tail(0)` was the whole buffer, so an old "ready" matched at once). Stop on an idle chat answers
  a background subagent's waiting question (deny), so it ends. The idle sweep keeps a chat with
  background work (a subagent, a command it waits to hear end), and a `notify_on_exit` end loads
  its chat if it was put away. Two chats waiting for the same agent can't both take it (the check
  and the claim run with no await between them; a turn lets go only of its own claim).
  `edit_file`: `edits: []` falls back to the top-level edit, an `edits` item without
  old_string/new_string fails the call (all or none), and a failing edit's own text and region are
  shown. A schedule's days are worked out once, the same in the question and in what's saved.
- **The plain chat panel.** A channel tab saved before D291 keeps its conversation across a
  restart (its state is `{ session }`) and counts as on screen. With no folder open, the chats
  started without one are listed ("No folder"). A thread that needs you, works or is unread shows
  on its chat's row. Several `ask_user` picks are matched against the options, so one with a comma
  in it still shows as chosen. Showing a hidden region shows all of its groups.
- **The rest.** A finished command isn't its window's any more (`ExecService::run_with_input`), so
  a page reload no longer marks its id "cancelled early" and a later run reusing it (hook ids
  restarted at each load; now unique per load) runs: a PreToolUse hook could be skipped. Global
  state kept `recentCommands`, `teamAgentsSeeded`, `teamAgentsWritten` and `teamIconsModel`
  (they were dropped on every read: recent commands were always empty, deleted team agents came
  back). Debugger sockets close with the page that opened them. The network log frees what it
  truncates (a big static asset stayed allocated per record). Closing the folder waits for an
  open or folder change in progress. Local history doesn't read a file too large to keep.
  `127.evil.com` isn't a local address for the preview. A second stop of an extension's code
  waits for the first. Ending detached terminals and interrupting a language server run on the
  blocking pool.

Left: static HTML in another encoding than UTF-8 is shown re-encoded in the preview (rare; a
byte-level injection is a larger change), and extension install/uninstall copy trees on an
async worker (they're user-initiated and short).

### D294 — Chat ages on hover; a quick optimized build

- **The Chats list shows a chat's age on hover** (or keyboard focus), as other chat apps' side
  bars do: the titles get the room. Working and needs-you stay shown.
- **`npm run build:fast`** (the owner: a release build takes ~20 minutes). The release profile's
  whole-program LTO with one codegen unit relinks everything on any change, the frontend
  included (it's embedded in the binary). The `fast-release` profile inherits release with LTO
  off, 16 codegen units and incremental compilation, and builds only the NSIS installer:
  measured here, 12.5 minutes the first time, 5.5 after a CSS change (the release build: ~20).
  `npm run build` stays what's shipped; `npm run dev` is still the quickest way to try changes.
- **No ring turns around a working agent's face** (tabs, the chat header, the lists): the chat
  list's dot and the chat's own progress already say it works; the face still glances and
  breathes. **A working chat's title shimmers** in the Chats list, as "Thinking…" does.
- **Chats are named when the model doesn't do it** (the owner: the list was the first words of
  every message). The first message still asks the model to open its reply with a `<title>`
  (D124); a reply without one (small and free models often ignore it; an external agent isn't
  asked) is followed by one short request to the chat's model (`chatTitle.ts`, ~24 tokens out,
  logged as the chat's usage) that names it from the first message and the reply's start. Only
  while the name is still the one made from the message, and with `agent.autoTitle` on.
- **An external agent's turn that made a folder of files no longer hangs** (the owner's report:
  Claude Code cloned two repositories, asked a question and ended its answer, but the chat stayed
  "Working…": the IDE was comparing ~1000 new files one by one and putting each under review; Stop
  didn't end it, the queued message waited, Accept all looked usable while the list grew, and
  Retry stayed hidden). Without git, a folder that didn't exist at the start and now holds 100 new
  files or more (`bulkCreatedFolders`) is left out of the review and named in the turn's "Changed
  files" note ("freqtrade/ (540 new files) was made by a command…"). Stop ends the comparing and
  the adopting (what's left counts as not compared). While the changes are gathered the review bar
  says so and its buttons wait (`AgentSession.gathering`).

### D295 — VS Code extensions as in VS Code: the compatibility audit and four decisions

An audit of how the IDE runs Open VSX extensions (Jupyter and its pack, Python, debugpy, Python
Environments, Pyrefly, Claude Code, Live Server) against VS Code's own behavior found about 60
gaps; about 40 are fixed (the list, and what's open: `docs/extension-compat-audit.md`). Four
choices came out of it:

1. **One shared extension host for VS Code packages (decided; not built yet).** VS Code runs every
   extension in one Node process, so another extension's API is a live object: synchronous calls
   (`environments.getActiveEnvironmentPath`), getters, events returning Disposables, `instanceof`
   and stack-based caller checks (Jupyter's). With a process per extension those are asynchronous
   proxies, and Jupyter, debugpy and Claude Code get Promises where Python's API returns values.
   Every VS Code package already gets the same full Node permissions (VSCODE_PERMISSIONS), so a
   process per package isolates little between them; the IDE's own-format extensions keep a
   process each (their permissions are enforced per extension). Until the shared host lands,
   `rpcExports.ts` bridged the gap (the caller's folder on the stack, objects of functions,
   callback results).
2. **A built-in language server steps aside for an extension that serves its languages**
   (`yieldTo` in languageServers/extension.json): Pyright while Pyrefly, basedpyright or ms-python
   (unless `python.languageServer` is "None") is enabled, rust-analyzer for rust-lang's, gopls for
   golang.go, and so on. VS Code has no built-in servers for those languages: one set of
   diagnostics, hovers and completions, not two. A notice says so once; `lsp.servers.<name>.yieldTo:
   []` keeps both; `ide://lsp` lists `yielded`.
3. **An extension's debugger for a type the IDE debugs itself runs it** (debugpy's `debugpy`,
   ms-python's `python`, js-debug's `pwa-node`): the type is no longer refused, the launch waits
   for the extension's adapter, and the built-in adapter is the fallback (with a notice) when the
   extension doesn't supply one. Configuration providers may register for any type or `*`.
4. **No download of Python's native environment finder.** Open VSX has only the universal build of
   ms-python.python, without `pet` (Python Environments' finder: `spawn … pet.exe ENOENT`). The
   IDE doesn't fetch programs at runtime (AGENTS.md rule 4); Python's own defaults
   (`python.locator: "js"`, `python.useEnvironmentsExtension: false`) find the environments
   without it, which is what Jupyter's Python kernels use. Python Environments stays installable
   (Python's pack) and reports its missing finder itself.

### D296 — VS Code extensions as in VS Code, second pass: one shared host and the gaps closed

D295's audit left about 20 gaps; five parallel pieces closed most of them, merged and tested
together (`docs/extension-compat-audit.md` lists them).

- **One shared Node host for VS Code packages** (D295's first decision, built). Each package keeps
  its own `vscode` shim (`require("vscode")` resolves by the requiring file's folder) and its own
  side of the RPC (messages tagged with its id), so the host still authorizes every request per
  extension. Other extensions' exports are the live objects, which retires the cross-process
  exports bridge of D265 (`rpcExports.ts`, removed). The IDE's own-format extensions keep a
  process each. A crashed host restarts the extensions that were running, at most 3 times in 5
  minutes (VS Code's budget).
- **Activation as VS Code's** (`core/extensions/activation.ts`): a failed `activate` keeps what it
  registered and isn't retried; dependencies activate first, with VS Code's refusal messages;
  fired activation events are remembered for extensions enabled later; startup activation runs in
  the background; VS Code packages have no activation timeout (a "Slow activation" log line at
  10 s).
- **Live quick input sessions** replace the one-shot pick for extensions: the list, busy state,
  buttons, checkboxes and validation change while it's open, as VS Code's QuickPick/InputBox do.
- **Language features without the IDE's limits**: no 1.5 s timeouts or 200-completion cap, real
  cancellation, providers for files outside the folder (reading only; edits stay in the folder),
  untitled documents and notebook cells; `editor.defaultFormatter` with VS Code's
  multiple-formatters prompt.
- **Settings**: `machine-overridable` and program-path settings of VS Code packages become
  restricted (a trusted folder may set them, D209) instead of user-only; `configurationDefaults`
  apply; reserved namespaces stay only for the IDE's credential areas.
- **An extension command that collides with an IDE command id stays skipped** (VS Code would let
  the newest registration shadow it): IDE ids are what agents and the UI run under permission
  checks, so shadowing `editor.save` would route them into extension code. The extension's own
  keybindings for it still run its code.
- **Jupyter widgets**: notebooks whose kernel is a VS Code controller get one output page holding
  every output, the extensions' `notebookPreload` scripts and controller messaging, as VS Code's
  notebook webview; the IDE's own kernels keep their frames and widgets (D189).

### D297 — VS Code extensions, third pass: the gaps D296 left, and Import installs extensions

- **Webviews**: panels come back after a restart (`registerWebviewPanelSerializer`, the page's
  `setState` saved per folder); `localResourceRoots` are served (workspace folders and declared
  roots, checked in the page proxy); tree and webview view titles and descriptions from code.
- **Terminals**: terminals the user opened are listed to extensions; `TerminalShellExecution.read()`
  gives the command's output (between the shell integration's marks); a "Set log level…" command
  per extension output channel; `Hover.range`.
- **Notebooks**: VS Code's notebook context keys (`notebookKernel`, `notebookCellListFocused`…);
  `inputFocus` is true in editor text too, as in VS Code, so single-key notebook commands only fire
  in command mode; ipynb metadata laid out as VS Code's ipynb serializer gives it; extension
  diagnostics in cells; one TextDocument per cell; every output in a controller's page;
  `rendererScripts`; a basic Interactive Window (no input box yet).
- **Editor**: Format document with… / Format selection with…; grammars' `embeddedLanguages` and
  `tokenTypes` (a configured TextMate grammar); injection grammars without a restart; VS Code's
  editor context keys (`editorTextFocus`, `editorLangId` in VS Code's ids…) in the IDE's context
  for extensions' keybindings.
- **Shared host**: it starts in its first extension's folder (where the IDE lets a process start)
  and moves to its own; an extension's timers are cleared when it unloads; one that loaded native
  addons restarts the host (planned, not counted as a crash) so Windows can delete its folder.
- **Import from VS Code** installs the user's extensions from Open VSX before their settings and
  shortcuts (so `python.*`, `prettier.*` and their keybindings import too), says which aren't on
  Open VSX, and what's also built in; only exact built-in replacements (auto close tag, path
  completion) stay settings.
- The VS Code API coverage probe against vscode.d.ts finds nothing missing; where the IDE has no
  feature behind a member, it behaves as VS Code does when no provider answers.

### D298 — An extension pack's page lists its members; extension icons as VS Code's

- **Extension Pack (N)** at the top of an extension's Details tab, as VS Code's extension editor
  shows it: a card per member (icon, name, description, publisher with the verified mark,
  Install / Installing… / Installed). A card opens that member's page; Install runs
  `extensions.installFromStore {id}`. Both pages have it: the store page from Open VSX's
  `bundledExtensions` (`StoreDetails.pack`, at most 50), an installed one's page from its
  Open VSX details. A member Open VSX doesn't have (Pylance) gets a card saying so, without a
  button. `extensionPack.ts`, one component for both pages.
- Why Open VSX's list rather than the installed package.json's `extensionPack`: the store page
  has nothing else, and one source keeps both pages the same. An installed pack that didn't come
  from Open VSX shows no section (rare: packs come from a store).
- The rows' icons are centered on their text block, and a picture icon has VS Code's slight
  rounding (`--radius-xs` in the list, `--radius-sm` on a page); a glyph icon none.

### D299 — A closed notebook never asks for anything by its path

- After Close folder the notebook came back on the empty window (the owner's machine, with VS
  Code's Jupyter): the audit log shows `editor.openFile` / `viewer.open` for it, as the user,
  right after `workspace.closeFolder`, and no command around them that finished. That's
  `target(path)` in a notebook command still waiting: a run queued before the close waits for a
  kernel (trust, the kernel sources, which stop with the folder's extensions), then asks for one
  by the notebook's path (`notebook.selectKernel {path}`), and a path that isn't open is opened.
- So a notebook view, once disposed, runs nothing by its path (`run`, `pickKernel`), and its
  runner stops waiting runs (`runToken`) and refuses to start or pick a kernel after its awaits.
- Not reproduced in a UI test: it needs a run waiting on a real extension's kernel across the
  close. `close-folder-vscode-notebook-m7-43` covers Close folder with a VS Code extension's
  notebook API following the notebook (the tab goes, nothing reopens it).

### D300 — The agent's plan works like Claude Code's app's

The owner's ask: the IDE's plan card should work and look like the one Claude Code's desktop app
shows for its own work. What it does there, and so here:

- **Where:** a card under the conversation's latest message (after messages queued while it works,
  above the "Working" line), not docked over the message box. No collapse, no "Plan" title or
  0/N count: the steps are the card.
- **Marks:** a dashed ring waits, a turning arc is the step in progress, a filled gray circle with
  a check is done (its text dimmed, not struck through). A plan written before the user's latest
  message says "Plan from before your last message" over it while steps are left.
- **The tool:** `update_plan` takes the whole list (as before) or a small change: `advance: true`
  (the step in progress done, the next started), `done: [n]` and `start: n` (1-based). The
  description and the agent's rules say to send the whole list with the first other tool call and
  `advance` with the call that starts each next step, never in a reply of its own, so keeping the
  plan costs no request. One step in progress at a time (`core/agent/plan.ts`, tested).
- **Turn end:** a turn that ends normally marks the step it was on done (the model needn't spend a
  call on the last tick); stopped or failed, it stays. Unfinished steps stay pending.
- Plan updates no longer count in a work line's summary ("updated the plan 3 times"): the card
  shows them. Rewind rebuilds the plan from the remaining calls with the same fold.

### D301 — wrap_up: the next-step box at the end of a turn

- After Claude Code's app: `wrap_up { recap, ask?, actions?: [{ label?, action? }], blocked? }`,
  called once at the end of a turn that kept a plan, changed files or ran commands, before the
  closing message (ordinary text after it). Skipped for short answers and conversation (the tool's
  description and one line in the agent's rules, `context.ts`).
- Checked like Claude Code's app checks it, with a short error the model can fix and the count it
  ran ("this one ran 303"): recap required, at most 300 characters; ask at most 100; actions only
  with an ask (and an ask needs 1–2 actions); a reply's label 1–3 words (4 at most), at most 24
  characters, not starting with `/` or `!`, no two the same (`core/agent/turnTools.ts`, tested).
- App actions are IDE commands, offered only when they make sense now; another is refused with
  the list of those available: `review` and `keep_all` (the chat has changes under review:
  `agent.review`, `agent.acceptAll`), `commit` (the repository has changes: Source Control with a
  generated message, `git.generateCommitMessage`, the user commits, as VS Code), `create_pr`
  (`agent.createPullRequest` when GitHub is there), `new_chat`, `archive`. The app names the
  button, not the model. One command runs them all from the box: `agent.runWrapUpAction`.
- The box: under the latest turn's answer, after the plan card; the recap (muted), the question,
  the buttons (the first, the recommendation, is the primary one). A reply's button sends its label
  as the user's message (`agent.send`); buttons work once the turn has ended. A recap without a
  question draws no box (as Claude Code's app). Older turns show nothing: the answer says it, and
  only the next step matters (VS Code-quiet).
- Saved as the tool call (its arguments), so reload and rewind keep it; the latest turn's is the
  last `wrap_up` after the user's latest typed message. `wrap_up` finishes the plan's step in
  progress (`finishPlan`) and gets no plan reminder.
- Its first sentence is the chat's status: `recap` in the saved meta and `ThreadRow`, shown as the
  Inbox card's line and in the Chats list's tooltip (the list's rows are one line high and stay
  so); `blocked: true` marks the chat as needing the user (its "Needs you" badge) while it's idle.
- `ide://agent/session` has `wrapUp`.

### D302 — mark_chapter: dividers and a table of contents

- `mark_chapter { title, summary? }`: title under 40 characters; refused for the chat's very first
  message before any work, and for the same title twice in a row.
- A divider (the title between two hairlines; the summary on hover). A chapter marked before
  anything of its turn shows (its first step's calls, no text) opens the turn: its divider goes
  above the user's message, where a new phase starts (`layoutTurns`); later in a turn it stays
  where it was marked.
- The table of contents: a bookmark button in the chat's header, shown once there's a chapter; its
  menu lists them (the summary as the item's tooltip: `MenuItem.tooltip`, new) and picking one
  runs `agent.showChapter { chapter }` (number, title or id), which reveals the divider like
  `agent.showMessage`. A menu rather than a floating panel: it keeps the conversation clear and
  holds up in small windows.
- `ide://agent/session` has `chapters`.

### D303 — propose_task and dismiss_task

- After Claude Code's `start_session` offer and `dismiss_task`: `propose_task { title, brief }`
  shows a "New task" card (title, the brief's first line, the whole brief on hover) with **Start in
  a new chat** (`agent.startTask`: `agent.newSession`, then the brief as its first message) and
  **Dismiss** (`agent.dismissTask`). Started, the card says so and offers **Open chat**.
- Rules in the description: real follow-up work that's a task of its own, never what it's about to
  do anyway, the brief complete on its own; at most 3 a turn (refused past that).
- `dismiss_task { task_id, reason? }` withdraws a stale one (the id is the call's, returned by
  propose_task); a started one can't be withdrawn.
- What became of a task is the call's `summary` ("Started in a new chat" / "Dismissed", the new
  chat's id in `detail`), so it's saved with the chat without a new field.
- `ide://agent/session` has `proposals` (`id`, `title`, `state`, `chat`).

### D304 — enter_plan_mode asks to plan first

- After Claude Code's EnterPlanMode: the agent asks before a non-trivial implementation; the user
  decides. A card ("Plan first?") with **Switch to Plan** / **Keep going** waits through
  `session.question` (as `ask_user`); a typed message answers it too.
- Yes: `agent.setChatMode plan`, and the rest of the turn works in it (`ToolHost.followChatMode`
  sets the turn's mode, so edits and commands are refused) and ends with the plan and **Build**,
  as a Plan mode turn does. No: it carries on in Agent mode.
- Kept from overuse by its description: only for multi-file work or a real choice of approach, not
  for small or clear changes, nor when the user gave detailed instructions. Not read-only, so Plan,
  Ask and read-only agents don't get it. With full access nobody is asked: it says so and goes on.

### D305 — notify

- After Claude Code's PushNotification: `notify { message }`, one line under 200 characters.
- No OS notification plugin in the IDE (none added): it uses what the agent's away-notice uses
  (D254): the taskbar flashes (`windowIpc.requestAttention`) and a notification with **Show**
  waits in the window.
- Not sent when the window is focused and visible ("Not sent: the user is at the window…"), with
  `agent.notifyWhenAway` off, or a second time in a turn. The description says to err toward not
  sending one and not at a turn's end (the IDE already says when the agent finishes).
- The turn tools aren't given to small models (fewer tools) nor to subagents (`subagentTools`).

### D306 — search as capable as Claude Code's Grep
- `search` takes Claude Code's Grep arguments: `pattern` (a regular expression), `output_mode`
  ("content" / "files_with_matches" / "count"), context lines, case, `-o`, `multiline`, `path`,
  `glob`, `type`, `head_limit` (default 250, 0 for all) and `offset`. The schema advertises
  readable names (`context`, `before`, `after`, `ignore_case`, `only_matching`, `line_numbers`)
  because a hyphen in a property name (`-C`) isn't accepted by every provider's schema check;
  Claude Code's own names (`-A`, `-B`, `-C`, `-i`, `-n`, `-o`) are accepted too, so a model
  trained on them works unchanged. The older `query` (literal unless `regex: true`) and
  `include` still work: `query` keeps its literal meaning, `pattern` is a regex unless
  `regex: false`. A `pattern` that isn't a valid regex is searched as plain text, and the result
  says so.
- Default mode stays "content" (matching lines as `path:line: text`, what the model is used to):
  one call answers most questions, where files_with_matches would cost a second call to see the
  lines. Context lines use ripgrep's marks (`path-12- text`, `--` between groups).
- Case: `ignore_case` true / false as asked; unset means smart case (insensitive unless the
  pattern has a capital), so the old insensitive default holds for lowercase queries and a
  Claude-style `TODO` stays case-sensitive.
- Paging: head_limit counts matching lines (content), files or count entries; a page is also cut
  at 20 000 characters at a match boundary. A cut result says `… N more … pass offset: X`, so
  the model knows there's more. Files are sorted by path (matches by line): Claude Code sorts by
  time, but paging needs the same order on every call.
- It runs over a new command, `search.find` (gitignore, files.exclude and search.exclude as
  before; every workspace folder), instead of `search.run`: the agent's searches no longer
  replace the user's query and results in the search view, and the engine's full results (up to
  20 000 matches) are paged in TS. Context lines are read from the shown files only (the open
  buffer first). Rust's `SearchOptions` gains `multi_line` (a regex may span lines and `.`
  matches a line break), the only engine change.
- `type` maps ripgrep's common names (js, ts, py, rust, go, java, c, cpp, cs, css, html, json, md,
  yaml, sh…) to globs; an unknown type is an error that suggests `glob`. A glob without `/`
  matches a name at any depth, as ripgrep's `--glob`. Read rules (`Read(secrets/**)` in a
  command's disallowed-tools) cover the new `path`, and the new line formats are filtered too.

### D307 — find_files takes globs
- A query with glob characters (`*?[]{}`) is a pattern (Claude Code's Glob): matching paths from
  the file index (gitignore respected), newest first (by mtime; past 2 000 matches by path). A
  pattern without `/` matches at any depth (`*.md`), as search's glob; `path` makes it relative
  to a folder. Plain words stay the fuzzy name search.
- `limit` (default 100, at most 1 000) and `offset`; a cut list says how many more and the next
  offset. A fuzzy search, which the quick-open command answers 200 at most, says "more may
  match" instead.

### D308 — changed-on-disk notes
- Each chat remembers what the agent last saw of every file it read or wrote
  (`Changeset.reads`, `core/agent/readTracker.ts`): the text up to 256 KB (a hash past that),
  200 files, 8 MB in all, in memory. After every tool call (subagents' too) and with the user's
  next message (inside `<ide_state>`), the 50 most recent are looked at: an open editor's text
  as read_file reads it, else the disk file, skipped by size + mtime when they match what was
  last checked. A change made by anyone else comes back once as a note: "<path> changed since
  you last read it … The changes (- before, + now…)" with a short diff; a change past 2 500
  characters / 60 lines, or a file too large to keep, is only named, with "read it again before
  you edit it". A deleted file is named and forgotten. Notes are capped at 6 000 characters.
- The agent's own writes update what it saw (`noteSeen` in `propose`), so they're never news,
  and a file with a staged proposal is skipped (its text is the agent's).
- A change shown whole counts as read: the fingerprint edit_file checks is updated, as Claude
  Code lets the model edit after such a note. One only named doesn't: edit_file asks for a read.
- Checks run one at a time per chat, so calls of one step finishing together tell a change once.
  Not saved with the chat: after a reload there are no notes until the agent reads again (the
  saved fingerprints still guard edits, D309).

### D309 — read before edit
- edit_file, and write_file over a file that exists, are refused unless the agent read the file
  in this chat or wrote it itself (`Changeset.hasSeen`, the saved fingerprints, so a reloaded
  chat keeps them), and refused when it changed since (edit_file now checks that too, as
  write_file did). An attached file sent whole with a message counts as read, as Claude Code's
  @-mentions do; so does a change shown whole in a note (D308). Creating a file needs nothing.
- The error names the exact next call for every model, small ones and the text protocol alike:
  `Error: you haven't read <path> in this chat, so edit_file was refused and nothing was
  changed. Call read_file with {"path": "<path>"} first, then call edit_file again.` The tool
  descriptions say it too ("a file you have read with read_file in this chat").
- Mock scenarios that edited without reading ("rename the title", "break the code") now read the
  file first, as a model would (the scenario hook `pkgBScripted` in the mock); the other
  scenarios write new files or files the same chat wrote, which count as read.

### D310 — read_file: notebooks and PDF pages
- A `.ipynb` file reads as its cells: `<cell id="…" type="code" execution="3">` with the source
  and an `<output>` block (streams, text/plain results, error tracebacks without colors; images
  and HTML named, not shown; 2 000 characters per cell). `offset` / `limit` count cells; a long
  notebook stops at a cell and names the next offset. Older notebooks without ids get
  `cell-<n>`. The file's JSON is what the read guard and edit_file see.
- PDFs take `pages` ("1-5", "3", "2,4-6"; at most 20 per call; a page past the end is an error).
  A PDF over 10 pages read without `pages` (and without `offset`) returns its first 10 pages and
  says how to ask for the rest, rather than Claude Code's error: one call still gives something
  useful. `offset` / `limit` still page by line through what's read.

### D311 — a cut command output stays readable
- A foreground run_command whose output passes the 16 000 characters the result shows keeps the
  whole output (up to 4 MB, its start dropped past that) in memory as `out1`, `out2`… for the
  chat, the last 5 per chat, 16 MB over all chats; deleting the chat drops them. The result says
  `[The output was cut. All N lines are kept as out1: read any part with process_output {"id":
  "out1", "offset": 1, "limit": 300}, or only the lines you need with {"id": "out1", "filter":
  "error|warn"}.]`.
- process_output reads them: numbered lines from `offset`, `limit` (300 default, 2 000 at most,
  30 000 characters), `filter` keeps matching lines with their numbers. Kept in memory rather
  than a file: read_file is confined to the workspace, and writing outputs into the project or
  opening the app data folder to the agent would be worse than losing them on reload; the
  background commands' outputs already work this way (D201). The result still shows the tail
  (16 000 characters, not Claude Code's 30 000) since the rest is a call away.

### D312 — ask_user asks up to four questions in one card, with previews

- `ask_user` takes `questions`: 1–4, each with `question`, a `header` chip (12 characters asked
  for), 2–4 `options` (`label`, `description`, optional `preview`) and `multiSelect`, as Claude
  Code's AskUserQuestion does. The description asks for a recommended option first with
  "(Recommended)", and keeps the tool for decisions that are the user's, not facts to look up.
- The older single-question arguments (`question`, `options` as strings or objects,
  `descriptions`, `multi_select`) still read: they're one question, drawn and answered as before
  (one click answers; with several picks, **Send**), and the result keeps the one-line
  "The user answered: …" form.
- Several questions show their header chips as tabs (a check once answered); a pick moves on to
  the next unanswered one, and **Submit answers** sends them all. Every question has an "Other"
  field (on `--bg-input`); typed words replace a single pick or join several picks.
- A preview shows beside the options when the card is at least 560px wide (a container query),
  under them when it's narrower; it follows the hovered or focused option (else the picked one,
  else the first with a preview). It's monospace text (a Markdown fence around it is dropped):
  mockups and code read as written, and nothing in it runs.
- Keys: 1–9 pick, ↑↓ move between options, ←→ between questions; Enter in "Other" moves on or
  sends.
- The answers come back as one result keyed by question (several picks joined by ", ", the user's
  own words marked as such), and are kept in the call's `detail` so the answered card shows them
  after a restart. A message typed in the chat while it waits still answers it.
- `agent.answer` takes `answers` (keyed by question, header or number; a list for several picks)
  besides `text`; every question needs one. `ide://agent/session` has `questions`: the cards
  waiting, with their questions, headers and option labels.
- Why: several related decisions in one card cost the user one interruption instead of four, and a
  preview lets them compare layouts or code without the agent describing each in prose.

### D313 — report_findings: a review's findings as a card the user acts on

- `report_findings { findings: [{ file, line, summary, short_summary, failure_scenario, category,
  verdict?, outcome? }] }`, as Claude Code's ReportFindings: called once with the verified
  findings, most severe first (an empty list for a clean review); `outcome` (fixed, skipped,
  no_change_needed) when re-reporting after fixes. Parsing is lenient (a string line, a Windows
  path, a long short summary cut to 60 characters, a category made kebab-case), but a finding
  needs a file and a summary.
- The card: a row per finding (short summary, file:line, category, "plausible" for a PLAUSIBLE
  verdict) that opens the file at the line; the sentence and failure scenario under it; **Fix**
  per open finding and **Fix all**. A re-report shows each outcome (a check for fixed).
- **Fix** runs `agent.fixFindings { item, index? }`: it sends a message listing the open findings
  and asking for a re-report with outcomes. A chat in Ask mode (a /review chat) switches to Agent
  mode first, as Build does for a plan; if the send fails the mode goes back.
- The review prompt (`reviewPrompt`: /review, Review changes…, a worktree's review) asks the
  reviewer to verify each finding and call `report_findings` when it has the tool (an external
  agent without the IDE's tools lists them in text as before).
- `ide://agent/session` has `findings`: the latest card's findings with their outcomes.
- Subagents don't get `report_findings` or `suggest_extension` (their calls aren't in the
  conversation the user sees).

### D314 — suggest_extension: an install card from Open VSX

- `suggest_extension { query | ids, reason }`, the IDE's take on Claude Code's SearchPlugins +
  SuggestPluginInstall: the agent searches Open VSX (or names extensions it found) and up to three
  show as a card with the store's icon (`storeAvatar`), name (opens its store page), publisher
  with the verified mark, description and **Install** / **Installed**.
- The agent never installs: **Install** runs `agent.installSuggestedExtension`, which runs
  `extensions.installFromStore` as the user's click (the permission question comes as for any
  store install) and marks the card installed. While it installs the button says so.
- Rules in the description and enforced: only when the task needs a capability an extension
  gives and nothing installed covers it; once per conversation unless the user installed from the
  card or wrote about extensions since (`suggestionRefusal`). Off with the store
  (`extensions.store.enabled`).
- The search goes straight to Open VSX rather than through `extensions.searchStore`, so the
  Extensions view's results aren't replaced by the agent's search. The card's data is kept in the
  call's `detail` (it draws the same after a restart).

### D315 — Typed memory notes

- `remember` takes `type` (user, feedback, project, reference, as Claude Code's memory types) and,
  for feedback and project notes, `why` and `how` (how to apply). A typed note is still one line:
  `- [feedback] fact — **Why:** reason — **How to apply:** how _(date, session)_`, so replacing,
  de-duplicating (the same fact, typed or not, is one note) and the tidy-up keep working; untyped
  notes (` — why: `) read as before.
- The description says what not to save (what the repository records, committed fixes, details
  of the task at hand), to use absolute dates in project notes and `[[topic]]` links. A feedback
  or project note saved without its why or how gets a nudge in the result.
- The index counts each topic's kinds ("3 notes: 1 feedback, 1 project") and tags its preview
  lines; `ide://agent/memory` has `types` per file; `recall { type }` lists the notes of one kind
  in both memories; recalling a topic lists the topics it links to (missing ones marked).
- The tidy-up's prompt keeps the tags and the why / how parts, tags an untyped note when its kind
  is clear, turns relative dates in project notes into absolute ones, keeps links to topics that
  still exist and drops notes the repository already records.
- Scope stays separate from type: a `user` or `feedback` note that holds in every project still
  goes to the user memory with `scope: "user"` (and its yes / no question).

### D316 — Claude Code's browser tools as modes of the IDE's, plus browser_eval and browser_batch

- What was there: the browser tab's page is driven by the injected bridge (`src-tauri/src/browser/bridge.js`,
  synthesized DOM events, refs from a snapshot), through `browser.*` commands; the agent had
  `browser_snapshot`, `browser_act`, `browser_inspect`, `browser_console` and `screenshot`. No CDP:
  the frame is WebView2 / WebKit, so input stays synthesized (untrusted events), as before.
- Every tool's description goes with every request, so Claude Code's tools became modes and actions
  of the existing ones where natural; only two new tools (`browser_eval`, `browser_batch`), whose
  behavior and permission don't fit an existing one.
  - `find` → `browser_snapshot find` (outline lines whose role / name / text contain the query,
    case-insensitively, up to 20 with refs; a phrase first, else every word). `browser.find`.
  - `get_page_text` → `browser_snapshot text` (+ `max_chars`): the largest `article` when it holds
    a fair share of the text, else `main` / `[role=main]`, else the body (`browser.text main`).
  - `computer` → `browser_act`: `click | right_click | double_click | triple_click | hover` by ref or
    `coordinate`, `drag` (`start_coordinate` → `coordinate`; HTML drag and drop with a DataTransfer
    when the source is draggable, else pointer moves), `scroll` with `scroll_direction` /
    `scroll_amount` (wheel ticks of 100 px) at a point (the nearest scrollable box, after a
    cancellable wheel event), `press` with `key` chords (`ctrl+a`, xdotool names, space-separated
    keys), `repeat` 1–100 and `modifiers`, `type` at the focus (keystrokes with their usual effect
    in text fields), `wait` `duration` (≤ 10 s), `action_summary` shown as the row's text. Claude
    Code's names (`left_click`, `left_click_drag`, `key`, `scroll_to`, `mouse_move`) are taken too.
    `zoom` and `scale` → `screenshot region` / `scale`. `planAct` (core, tested) maps it all.
  - Tabs → `browser_act new_tab / select_tab / close_tab`, `browser_inspect tabs` (listing is a
    read, so it lives with the read-only tool). New commands `browser.selectTab`, `browser.closeTab`.
  - `resize_window` → `browser_inspect resize` with `preset` mobile (375×812) / tablet (768×1024) /
    desktop (fills the tab) and `colorScheme` (D318).
  - `read_console_messages` → `browser_console` gains `pattern` (regex, else text) and `limit`;
    `read_network_requests` already matched (`network` url filter, `request` with bodies); `limit`
    added.
- The coordinate frame: the page's viewport in CSS pixels, scaled down to fit 1568 px (the size
  vision models get). `browser.screenshot inline` draws the page at exactly that size and reports
  it as `frame`; the bridge maps a point back with the same scale. So a point read off a screenshot
  is right on high-DPI screens and in device mode (where the frame is drawn scaled), and stays
  right without a screenshot first. A zoom crops the capture at its own device-pixel detail.
- `browser_batch {actions: [{name, input}]}`: browser_act, browser_snapshot, screenshot,
  browser_inspect, browser_console, browser_eval (only those the turn has; never itself); in
  order; stops at the first error or refusal and says which steps didn't run; screenshots come back
  in order and the text says which step each image is; at most 25 steps. Each step asks for
  permission as it would alone (Always on a page's question allows its site for the rest).
- The bridge's new half is `src-tauri/src/browser/input.js` (concatenated after devtools.js), so
  bridge.js keeps its size; bridge.js exposes a few more internals to it.

### D317 — browser_eval: REPL semantics, JSON results, and when it asks

- `browser_eval {code, max_chars}` runs JavaScript in the tab's page for debugging and inspection.
  Without `await`, indirect eval gives the last expression's value (its completion value) and
  globals persist as in a console. With `await`, the code becomes an async function body: the IDE
  lists candidate bodies with `return (<last statement>)` (`core/agent/browserEval.ts`: a small
  scanner that skips strings, templates, comments and regexes, and never splits a continued line),
  and the page's own parser picks the first that compiles; else the code runs as is (undefined).
- The value comes back as JSON (pretty, cycles marked, elements as `tag#id [ref=eN]`), with its
  type, capped at `max_chars` (default 10000); a thrown error comes back as `Name: message`.
- When it asks:
  - On the user's own pages (localhost, 127.0.0.1, `*.localhost`, workspace files) it is a page
    action like a click: `browser.eval` through the agent's permission handler (asks unless the
    mode runs commands automatically, or agent.autoApprove allows the site; browser protection
    asks each time).
  - On another site it runs only in a tab this chat has worked on (its browser tools acted on it,
    or it opened or chose it), so a page the user has open on their own is never scripted; and it
    asks first even in full access — once, or for that site for the rest of the chat (Always) — not
    with browser protection on (each time), and not when agent.autoApprove allows the site.
- Why not refuse other sites outright: debugging the user's staging site is a real need; asking
  with the code shown keeps it the user's decision.

### D318 — Color scheme emulation without CDP

- `browser.resize colorScheme: light | dark | auto` (and `browser_inspect resize colorScheme`):
  WebView2 and WebKit frames have no media emulation the IDE can reach, so the bridge rewrites the
  page's `(prefers-color-scheme: …)` media conditions (stylesheet rules, imported sheets,
  `<link media>`) to always / never true and keeps the originals to put back; `matchMedia` queries
  about it are rewritten the same way; a page that offers both schemes (`color-scheme: light dark`)
  gets the asked one on its root, for form controls and `light-dark()`.
- Styles added later (dev servers inject them from script) follow through a mutation observer and
  link loads; the tab's Page keeps the scheme and applies it again to each new document (reloads,
  navigation).
- Limits: rules in another origin's stylesheet can't be read (so stay as they are), and
  `matchMedia` lists made before the emulation don't fire change events.

### D319 — Deferred tools and tool_search (Claude Code's ToolSearch)
- **What:** with many MCP tools, a chat's requests carry their names only (with the first sentence
  of each description, at most 80 characters) in a note after the kept system prompt, plus a
  `tool_search` tool: `{ query, max_results? }`, where `query` is `select:a,b` (these exact tools,
  case-insensitive; unknown names get "did you mean"), keywords (ranked: a word of the name 4, part
  of the name 2, in the description 1; up to `max_results`, default 5), or `+word` (must be in the
  name, ranked by the rest; alone: every tool that has it). An exact tool name as the query loads
  that tool. The result is Claude Code's shape: `<functions><function>{"name", "description",
  "parameters"}</function></functions>`, then "Loaded: …".
- **When:** `agent.deferTools`: `auto` (default; more than 30 MCP tools, or their definitions over
  25 000 characters, about 6 000 tokens: Claude Code defers past 10 % of the context, and a fixed
  size keeps the list stable when the model changes), `always`, `never`. It replaces D204's
  `agent.mcp.toolSchemas` / `mcp_tool_schema` (every deferred tool was still sent with an empty
  schema and a longer description); the old setting is still read when the new one is on auto
  (onDemand → always, full → never). Names plus one line instead of names alone: the line is what
  keyword searches and the model's choice work from, at ~20 tokens a tool against hundreds for a
  schema.
- **Loaded for the chat, kept consistent:** what a chat loaded is read from its own done
  `tool_search` items (the result's `<function>{"name":…` blocks), not kept anywhere else. So it's
  saved with the chat and survives a restart; a rewind or an edit that drops the search unloads the
  tools; a summary keeps them (the summarized items stay in the chat, and the loaded tools keep
