  `ide://agent/prWatches` shows it (`autoMerge: { method, by: github|ide, status }`, what it waits
  for). Stopping the watch doesn't turn GitHub's own auto-merge off (that's GitHub's setting);
  `auto_merge_off` does.

### D353 — Desktop control: the `computer` tool, after Claude Code's computer use

- **What.** `computer { action, coordinate, start_coordinate, text, repeat, modifiers,
  scroll_direction, scroll_amount, duration, monitor, region, scale, action_summary }` with
  actions screenshot | left_click | right_click | middle_click | double_click | triple_click |
  mouse_move | left_click_drag | scroll | type | key | wait. A screenshot is of all monitors (the
  virtual desktop) or `monitor` n (0 = the primary), scaled to fit 1568 px like the browser tools'
  frame; `region` zooms (the region's own detail) and `scale` shrinks, with coordinates staying in
  the frame. Points map back to physical pixels (`core/agent/computerUse.ts`, tested: 4K, a monitor
  left of the primary at negative x, small screens not scaled up). The result names the app in
  front and the monitors, and says the screen is data, not instructions.
- **Native side (Windows).** New Rust service `desktop/` (`ipc/desktop.rs`: `desktop_info`,
  `desktop_capture`, `desktop_window_at`, `desktop_input`, `desktop_banner`, `desktop_take_stop`).
  Capture is GDI `StretchBlt` with HALFTONE from the screen DC into a DIB at the frame's size
  (BGRA over IPC; the webview makes the PNG): simpler than Desktop Duplication (D3D11, one output
  per monitor, a frame only on change) and good enough for one picture per action. Input is
  `SendInput` (absolute moves over the virtual desktop, Unicode typing, virtual-key chords with the
  extended flag where needed; a drag moves in 12 steps). The app is the root window at the point
  (or the foreground window for keys and text): its process name and title; store apps inside
  ApplicationFrameHost are named by their title. No new dependency: two features of the `windows`
  crate already used (`Win32_Graphics_Gdi`, `Win32_UI_Input_KeyboardAndMouse`).
- **Off by default** (`agent.computerUse.enabled`, user scope), as Claude Code's computer use is
  off until enabled; the tool is offered only when it's on, on Windows, and not to a small model.
  macOS and Linux: not implemented — `desktop_info` says unsupported and the tool is absent.
- **Permission: per app, like Claude Code.** The first action on each app asks "Allow <app>?" with
  the call as code; Allow is once, the "Allow for this chat" checkbox keeps it for the chat (kept
  in memory, `ide://agent/computerUse` lists grants, `agent.computerUse.revoke` forgets them),
  Deny refuses. Asked even in full-access mode (`evenWithFullAccess`). Screenshots ask once for
  "your screen" the same way. The permission card gained `alwaysLabel` for its checkbox words.
- **Tiers** (`classifyApp`): browsers read-only (screenshots only; use the browser tools);
  terminals and IDEs click-only (left/double/triple click, scroll, move; no typing, keys,
  right-click, modifier-click or drag; use run_command); system settings (Settings, regedit,
  Task Manager, mmc…) and the IDE's own window asked every time (no "for this chat"); password
  managers (and any window titled like a vault) and trading, brokerage and crypto-wallet apps
  refused. Budgeting/accounting apps stay at full, as in Claude Code. Text that looks like a
  payment card number (13–19 digits, Luhn) is refused before anything is asked. Links: the
  description tells the model never to click links from mail, chats or documents and to open a
  checked URL with the browser tools (not enforceable from pixels).
- **Stop.** While a turn uses the tool, a native always-on-top banner ("Controlling your
  computer. Press Esc or Stop to end." + Stop) sits at the top of the primary monitor: a
  no-activate tool window on its own thread, excluded from captures (WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) so
  the model's screenshots don't show it. Esc anywhere stops too (a key-state watch that ignores the
  IDE's own injected keys). The IDE polls the stop flag every 250 ms and stops those chats
  (`agent.stop`); a status bar item ("Controlling your computer — Stop", `agent.computerUse.stop`)
  shows meanwhile. The banner goes when the turn ends.
- Not done: macOS/Linux; a per-app "background" mode (Claude Code's app_* tools on macOS);
  clipboard actions; hiding the IDE window from screenshots.

### D354 — Recording the IDE window as a GIF

- D340's recorder gets a target: `browser` (the tab, as before) or `ide` (the whole window,
  `captureWindow` at the model's size, one frame a second). The agent starts and stops it with the
  `screenshot` tool's new `record: start | stop` (target `ide` by default, `page` for the tab), so
  it works with no browser tab open; `browser_act start_recording` is unchanged. The stop call
  draws the same card ("IDE recording · 12 frames · …", Save to project / Download).
- The user's clicks while the IDE is recorded add a frame 150 ms later with the D340 marker where
  they clicked and "Clicked <label>" (the element's aria-label, title or text) as the caption. The
  agent's browser actions add captioned frames (no marker: the page's coordinates aren't the
  window's).
- For bug reports: `workbench.recordGif` (Window category, the palette's "Record the IDE as a
  GIF") starts a recording of the user's own; run again (or `stop: true`, or the status bar item
  "Recording 0:12") to stop: a notification offers Save to project… / Download…
  (`agent.saveRecording`). Stopping also ends an agent's IDE recording (its stop_recording then
  reports it). Same limits as D340 (5 minutes, 300 frames, 30 MB) and in memory until the IDE
  closes; `ide://agent/recordings` now has each recording's `target`.

### D355 — show_widget drawn while it's written
- Claude Code draws a widget as the model writes it; D334 drew it once the call was complete. Now
  Rust (`ai/mod.rs` `ToolStreamProgress`) sends show_widget's arguments so far with its
  `toolProgress` events (`STREAMED_TOOLS`), at most every 150 ms, and every progress event carries
  the call's id. The loop keeps them on the streaming assistant item's `toolDraft.args` (left out
  when a chat is saved). Other tools' progress is unchanged (no arguments sent).
- `core/agent/widgetStream.ts` (tested): `partialJsonArgs` reads top-level strings and string
  arrays out of unfinished JSON (an escape cut in half waits; a loading line still being written
  isn't shown); `drawableMarkup` cuts the code to what's safe to paint: complete scripts left out,
  an unclosed `<script` cuts the rest, an unclosed comment, tag (a half-written attribute
  included, a quoted `>` doesn't end it) or entity is cut. The frame's parser closes open elements.
- The draft card (`widgetDraftCard`) sits where the finished card will be (after the turn's
  items). Its frame gets `{ draft }` messages (throttled to 150 ms in the view too) and morphs the
  markup into the page (widget.js `morphChildren`): what's drawn stays put, animations and images
  don't restart, no reload per chunk; scripts are removed again in the page. The loading lines show
  until the first paint.
- When the call is complete the tool's row adopts the same card and frame by call id: `{ render }`
  sets the finished code once and runs its scripts (the same path as D334, synchronous, so no
  flash). To keep the frame from reloading the chat column now removes nodes on their way out
  instead of moving the next node before them (an iframe moved in the DOM reloads). A failed call
  drops its draft; drafts left off screen go after 10 s.
- `loading_messages` now comes first in the schema (models write in that order, so the lines can
  show while the code streams); the widget_code description and the guide say to put `<style>`
  first and scripts last.
- Ollama sends whole tool calls, so its models draw at the end as before; the text protocol isn't
  streamed either. State: `ide://agent/widgets` `drafts` (call, title, chars, paints, height) and
  per widget `streamed`, `paints`, `loads`.
- Permission: none (show_widget never asked; it's sandboxed as in D334).

### D356 — Output styles
- Claude Code's output styles: built-ins Default, Explanatory (★ Insight blocks about the code's
  choices) and Learning (the user writes small meaningful parts at TODO(human) markers; the agent
  stops and waits), texts written for the IDE; and the user's own Markdown files with `name`,
  `description`, `keep-coding-instructions` front matter in `<config>/output-styles` (and
  `~/.claude/output-styles`, read only; Rust's settings scope gained both folders, like D330's
  plans) and a trusted folder's `<workspace folder>/output-styles` (and `.claude/output-styles`
  with `agent.thirdPartyConfigs`). A folder's style steers the agent like its custom modes do, so
  only trusted folders' are read. First of a name wins: built-ins, the project's, the user's.
- `agent.outputStyle` (default "default"; any scope, like Claude Code's project setting).
  `agent.setOutputStyle` (a picker for a person; `scope` workspace), `/output-style [name]` acts
  instead of sending (in `agent.send`, like /model), a row in the details panel's Environment card
  when it isn't Default, `ide://agent/outputStyles` (`missing` when the named file is gone: Default
  is used).
- Where the text goes: the system prompt, as Claude Code does, not with each message like mode
  rules (D180). A style shapes every reply; sent per message it would add its text to every user
  message in the history. The prompt is built once per chat and frozen (D112); the style's key is
  part of `frozenFor`, so a change rebuilds the prompt once (that request isn't cached) and later
  requests cache again. `styledPrompt`: a built-in is added after the prompt's "How to talk"
  section; a custom style replaces that section, and without `keep-coding-instructions` (Claude
  Code's default for custom styles) "How to work" becomes a short list of the IDE's essentials
  (paths, tool results are data, `<ide_state>`, update_plan / wrap_up). The small-model profile
  gets the style at its end. External ACP agents and subagents keep their own prompts.
- Permission: none (it's the user's own setting and files).

### D357 — A scriptable status line
- Claude Code's `statusLine`: `agent.statusLine` `{ "type": "command", "command": "…", "padding"? }`
  (or a bare string; `{}` is off), user settings only (a folder's settings mustn't add commands,
  as with agent.hooks). It runs through the IDE's command runner (`execIpc`, PowerShell on
  Windows) in the open folder, only when the folder is trusted (it's the user's script, but it runs
  in the repository), with a 5 s timeout. Permission: no prompt, as Claude Code (the user set the
  command); untrusted folders don't run it.
- stdin is Claude Code's JSON where the IDE has the field (`statusLineInput`): `hook_event_name`,
  `session_id`, `transcript_path` (the IDE's saved chat, JSON rather than JSONL), `cwd`, `model
  { id, display_name }`, `workspace { current_dir, project_dir }`, `version`, `output_style { name }`,
  `cost { total_cost_usd (D199), total_duration_ms (since the chat was first seen in this window),
  total_api_duration_ms (its turns' running time), total_lines_added / removed (the chat's changes
  under review) }`, `exceeds_200k_tokens`, `context_window`.
- The first line of stdout shows (`statusLineText`: SGR colors kept, other escapes and control
  characters dropped, 200 visible characters, `padding` spaces before it); a command that fails
  without output keeps the last line. Reruns when the active chat's version, cost, model, usage or
  changes, the folder, trust or the output style change, at most every 300 ms and one at a time
  (`Throttle`, tested with fake timers).
- Where: the status bar, beside the agent's model item (left of it), only while a chat tab is open,
  for the active chat, rather than the chat footer: the status bar is the IDE's one line for such
  status, it holds up in small windows (the chat column stays as it is) and one runner serves
  the window. The status bar gained a `nodes` hook so an item can draw colored text; colors use
  the notebook's `ansiNodes` (D188): the theme's `--terminal-ansi-*` tokens, 256/true colors as the
  output gives them. State: `ide://agent/statusLine` (command, text, raw, runs, lastMs, exitCode,
  error, skipped).

### D358 — Claude Code plugins
- A plugin is Claude Code's folder: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and any of `commands/`,
  `agents/`, `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` (plus the manifest's own
  `commands` / `agents` / `skills` paths and inline or file `hooks` / `mcpServers`). A marketplace
  is a folder or a git repository with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`; entry sources: a relative
  path (`metadata.pluginRoot` honored), `github` (owner/repo), `url` / `git`, and `git-subdir`
  (url + path + ref, what Claude Code's own marketplace uses). `strict: false` entries serve as the
  manifest. npm sources aren't supported (listed as a problem).
- Where: the app's data folder, `<data>/plugins` (not `~/<dataFolderName>`: a test run's profile
  gets its own, and nothing else reads it). `marketplaces/<slug>` holds a shallow clone (the
  user's git, `--depth 1`, `.git` dropped) or a copy of a local folder; `cache/<market>/<plugin>`
  each installed plugin's own copy, as Claude Code keeps one; `plugins.json` the record. Rust writes
  only inside that folder (`plugins_copy`, `plugins_clone`, `plugins_remove`,
  `plugins_save_record`; no links, no `.git`, 20 000 files / 512 MB at most); the fs commands may
  read it (`settings::resolve`). No new dependency.
- What a plugin brings counts where the IDE's own does, labeled `plugin <name>`: slash commands as
  `/<plugin>:<command>` (Claude Code's naming; the plain name works when nothing earlier has it),
  skills as `<plugin>:<skill>`, subagents among the user's (after `~/.claude/agents`, never where a
  new one is written), hooks with the user's own, MCP servers as a settings source.
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (and `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`) is the installed copy's folder, `/` separated.
- Permissions, as Claude Code: installing always asks (a dialog with what the plugin brings);
  its hooks and MCP servers are unticked there, each with what it runs, and run only if ticked
  (changeable later on the page). Once allowed they don't ask per folder (they're the user's, not
  a repository's). A plugin's commands are the user's commands: their `allowed-tools`
  pre-approve as a `~/.claude/commands` file's do (D207); the dialog says so. The agent can't
  install or remove plugins (the commands are hidden from it).
- `/plugin` acts instead of sending (a new `actionSlash` hook in `slashCommands.ts`, used by
  `agent.send`): `/plugin` opens Customize → Plugins; `marketplace add|remove|update|list`,
  `install`, `uninstall`, `enable`, `disable`.
- Hooks: only the events the IDE runs (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop); a plugin's
  others (SessionStart, Notification…) are ignored, as for settings hooks.
- Commands: agent.showPlugins, agent.addPluginMarketplace, agent.updatePluginMarketplace,
  agent.removePluginMarketplace (uninstalls its plugins), agent.listPlugins, agent.installPlugin
  { plugin, hooks?, mcp? }, agent.uninstallPlugin, agent.setPluginEnabled { plugin, enabled?,
  hooks?, mcp? }. State `ide://agent/plugins`.
- Not done: Claude Code's own installed plugins (`~/.claude/plugins`) aren't read (their record's
  format has changed between versions); a plugin's `outputStyles` and LSP parts are ignored;
  marketplaces aren't updated automatically.

### D359 — Agents across windows
- list_chats and message_chat (D325) reach the chats open in the IDE's other windows; no new tool.
  list_chats adds an "In other windows:" block (id, title, agent, status, the window's folder);
  message_chat with such an id leaves the message for that window. Same rules: asked once per pair
  of chats (the card says it's in another window), the rate limit, not in Ask or Plan mode.
- Channel: the IDE has inter-window IPC for launches (D209: a localhost port per window), but it
  answers in Rust and can't reach a window's chats; the global state (agentHelperMessages) is one
  big file every window rewrites. So: each window publishes its loaded chats to a file of its own,
  `<data>/agent/window-chats/<pid>.json` (written when they change, at least every 60 s, removed on
  close); the list keeps only windows whose instance answers a ping (D209's registry), and goes by
  age (3 min) where there's no registry (test runs). Messages go through `<data>/agent/chat-mail/`,
  the D233 reports store (same claim: exactly once, by rename), addressed to the chat; the window
  that has it loaded takes it within 2 s.
- It arrives as `Message from chat "T" (id) in window "folder"` and starts a turn (or joins the
  running one); its card names the window and doesn't open the chat here (it works there).
  notify_when_idle: the receiving window watches the chat and mails the idle note back to the
  sender's chat. A chat loaded in this window is always reached here, never through another.

### D360 — Notifications to the phone
- `agent.notify.webhook` { kind: ntfy | discord | slack | json, url } (user scope; default none).
  The notify tool (D305) sends its message there too, so only when the window isn't focused and
  the tool decided to notify; the result says whether the phone got it. One line, at most 200
  characters, code removed and secret-looking text (keys, tokens, `password=`, long random
  strings) replaced by `[hidden]`.
- Each kind's request: ntfy the text as the body (Title and Tags headers, ASCII), Discord
  `{ content, allowed_mentions: { parse: [] } }` (no @everyone), Slack `{ text }` (escaped), JSON
  `{ title, message, chat, folder, at }`.
- Rust posts it (`notify_webhook_post`, the agent's HTTP client): https only, plain http only to
  localhost / 127.0.0.1 / [::1]; 10 s timeout; 8 KB body; only Title / Tags / Priority headers.
- A URL anyone could post to (every ntfy topic, Discord and Slack webhook, and a JSON one with a
  sign-in, a query or a long random path part) goes to the secrets file (`notify.webhook`) and
  settings keep `{ kind, secret: true, host }`; a plain local endpoint stays in settings.
- Commands: agent.setNotifyWebhook { url?, kind? } (asks for both when a person runs it),
  agent.clearNotifyWebhook, agent.testNotifyWebhook ("Send a test"). State
  `ide://agent/notifyWebhook`. Opt-in, not a model feature (no `.enabled` setting needed).

### D361 — The terminal selection matches the editor’s

- The terminal always selected in the accent color at 35% (orange with the default accent). With a
  color theme the user picked, the editor selects in the theme’s own `editor.selectionBackground`.
  The terminal now picks its selection as VS Code does: the theme’s `terminal.selectionBackground`,
  else its `editor.selectionBackground`, else the accent (the built-in Dark+/Light+, where the
  editor uses the accent too). `themeColors` moved to core/themes/vscodeColors.ts for both.

### D362 — A program missing from an Open VSX build is one notice, not an error each start

- Open VSX has only the all-platform build of ms-python.python and ms-python.vscode-python-envs;
  Microsoft ships python-env-tools' `pet.exe` only in the marketplace's platform builds, which the
  IDE may not use. The Environments extension starts it anyway and shows "spawn …pet.exe ENOENT"
  as an error on every start. Its `python.locator` fallback is the Python extension's (the
  default already), and the envs extension has no setting to stop it.
- An extension message "spawn <path> ENOENT" whose program lies inside an installed extension's
  folder (core/extensions/missingProgram.ts) becomes one info notice with "Don't show again"
  (D344's showDismissible, key `missing-program.<folder>.<program>`) and a line in the
  extension's log. A missing program elsewhere (python, git: the user's to install) still shows.

### D363 — Send now

- A message sent while the agent works waits for its next step (D151) with **Send now** next to
  **Take back** (`agent.sendNow`), as Claude Code's app has. The IDE's agent: the step's request
  is cancelled (what was written stays) or, while tools run, its running commands are (the rest of
  the step's calls are skipped: "Not run: the user sent a message first."); the turn goes on and
  its next step reads the message. A subagent or a wait finishes first.
- The loop (core/agent/loop.ts) gets `interrupt`: `requested`, `clear` (each step) and `phase`
  (model / tools), so the session cancels the right thing (`session.sendQueuedNow`).
- An external agent (ACP) can't take a message mid-turn: Send now cancels its turn ("Stopped: you
  sent a message.") and the held messages go as the next message instead of back to the box.
- No button for a group chat message that calls on another member (it waits for that one's round).

### D364 — A chat's logo is the model it used

- The chat list showed each chat's agent face, and for the main agent that's the model's logo
  (D270), resolved against today's default model: every chat changed logo when the default did.
- Each reply now records its model's key (`modelKey`: "<provider>/<model>", "acp/<agent>"), the
  saved chat keeps the one that wrote most replies (`usedModel`, the latest on a tie), and the row
  shows that logo; a chat saved before this falls back to the model it's set to, else the default.

### D365 — External agents see the browser tabs and get browser_console

- An OpenCode chat (ACP) asked to "check the errors, I have it open" fetched the page's HTML with
  its own webfetch, which never runs the page's script, so the blank page's TypeError was out of
  sight. It had the IDE's tools (D211: OpenCode takes HTTP MCP servers, checked by starting
  `opencode acp` with a probe server), but only the core commands are listed and
  `browser.console` was discoverable: reaching it took ide_find_commands then ide_run_command, and
  nothing said a tab was open.
- `browser.console` is core: listed directly, as `browser_console` (the name the IDE's own agent
  has for its tool). The `core` flag only shapes the MCP list.
- The IDE state that goes with each message (`ideState`) gains the open browser tabs: url, title,
  tab id, console error and failed request counts, the latest error's first line, and "Read a
  tab's console … with browser_console" when there's trouble (core/agent/browserDigest.ts).
- External agents now get that state with each message too, as an `<ide_state>` context block,
  when the IDE's tools are lent to them (`ideTools: on`), naming the IDE's MCP server.

### D366 — A key that can't pay for the whole output limit is asked again with less

- OpenRouter refuses a request whose `max_tokens` (the model's whole output limit when none is
  sent, 65,536 for Claude) costs more than the key has left: 402 "can only afford 40434". That's a
  usage limit (D254), so the turn failed or switched models while the key could still answer.
- On that message, before anything streamed, the request is sent once more with 90% of what it
  can afford (`affordableOutput`, at least 1,024), with a retry notice saying so.

### D367 — Servers that are up aren't shown as work in progress

- A dev server the agent started in the background spun on the chip and in the Background tasks
  view like work still going, so a chat looked busy after its turn ended.
- A running background command that has printed an address (`urls`, D201) is `serving`: a server
  icon instead of the spinner, on the chip and its row, and counted apart ("1 completed, 2 servers
  running"). The chip spins only while something works toward an end. `ide://agent/background`
  marks such a row `serving`.
- The chat details panel's Background card shows the server icon for them too.
- The Background tasks view loses its own Expand and Close buttons: the tab closes and its group
  maximizes as every view does; only Clear finished stays in its header.

### D368 — Welcome can be closed beside a chat

- The editor area always held an editor-like tab, so Welcome came straight back when closed, even
  with a chat and Background tasks filling the window.
- Closing the last file still leaves Welcome in its place (the editor area stays where it is, so
  the next file opens there and not in the terminal's group). Closing Welcome itself while another
  tab is on screen leaves it closed (`hasShownTab` in core/dock/tree.ts); with nothing on screen it
  comes back.
- A file opened with no editor area gets one of its own: a new group on the left (60%), not a tab
  in the chat's or the terminal's group.

### D369 — TypeScript 7 can't run the TypeScript language server

- The install was `npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript`, and `typescript` is now
  7.x, the native port, which has no `lib/tsserver.js`. typescript-language-server then fails
  every start ("Could not find a valid TypeScript installation") unless the folder's root has its
  own TypeScript: a project in a subfolder showed every handler as `any` (13 false errors).
- The install pins `typescript@6` (6.0.3, the last with tsserver). A server that fails with that
  message offers **Repair** (`lsp.install` again), once per window; the manager's `onFailed` fires
  for a server that started and then failed.

### D370 — The image viewer beside the chat fades into it; a chat keeps its scroll behind a tab

- Beside the chat, the viewer's scrim ended in a hard edge a few pixels short of the chat (the
  splitter's room, D201) with a hairline border. The scrim is now its own layer that fades out
  over the last `--space-10` toward the chat, on whichever side the chat is (`is-chat-left` when
  the chat was moved to the viewer's left). The border is gone. `--media-scrim-soft` is darker
  (0.42 → 0.55), and the caption pill has the buttons' radius (`--radius-sm`), not a full round.
- A chat hidden behind another tab of its group has a log of no size. The resize observer took
  that for "nothing to scroll" and stuck the chat to its end, and Chromium drops a hidden box's
  scroll offset anyway: the reader came back at the bottom. The view now ignores the log's
  resizes and scrolls while it has no size, remembers where the reader last scrolled to, and puts
  it back when the tab shows again (unless the reader was following the end).
- The dock's scroll memory (D190) only put offsets back when a tab moved to another group. It now
  also does when a tab comes back in front of its group's other tabs, and for every shown view
  after the dock's tree is rebuilt (opening a split re-parents every group, which reset the chat
  to the top). UI test: `agent-scroll-m7-105.jsonc`.

### D371 — All of Claude Code's hook events
- Besides PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and Stop (D227), the agent now runs these:
  - **SessionStart:** a chat's first message, or the first after `/clear`, reopening the chat from
    Chats, or a summary (`source`: startup, resume, clear, compact). What it prints is context for
    that message, as in Claude Code, and is kept on a retry.
  - **SessionEnd:** `/clear`, a chat deleted or forgotten, the window closing. Nothing waits on it,
    and it runs only for chats whose start ran hooks.
  - **PreCompact:** `trigger` manual or auto, and `custom_instructions`. It doesn't stop the summary.
  - **Notification:** the agent waits for an approval or an answer, whether or not the user is away.
  - **SubagentStart:** what it prints goes with the subagent's task.
  - **SubagentStop:** it can send the subagent back once, like Stop.
- Each event's matcher is matched against its own field, as in Claude Code: the tool, the source,
  the trigger, the notification kind, or the subagent's name.
- Plugin hooks get every event (they share the parser).
- A chat that's ending doesn't ask about a folder's hooks; only approved ones run.
- Differences from Claude Code:
  - A summary made automatically mid-turn runs SessionStart "compact" with the next message, not
    right away.
  - Notification has no "idle" kind; the IDE's own away notice covers that.
- UI test: `agent-hooks-m7-106.jsonc`.

### D372 — Refused hosts for background commands and monitors
- A sandboxed command's network filter (D348) only knew which hosts it refused when the command
  ended.
- Rust now keeps each running command's set by id (`exec_blocked_hosts`). The background list
  reads it every 3 s while a sandboxed command runs, and takes the final list when it ends.
- Where the refused hosts show:
  - The Background tasks row says "Refused by the sandbox: example.org" (three hosts, then "and N
    more"; all of them in its tooltip).
  - `ide://agent/background` has `blockedHosts`.
  - process_output's description of the command names them, so the agent can ask for the host.
- UI test: `agent-sandbox-net-m7-92.jsonc` (Windows).

### D373 — Links in the status line
- The status line command (D357) may print OSC 8 hyperlinks, as Claude Code's does. They were
  stripped. Now they're kept (zero width, BEL endings turned into ESC \) and drawn as underlined
  pieces of the line.
- A click runs `agent.openStatusLineLink`:
  - http(s) and mailto open through agent.openLink (local addresses in the IDE's browser).
  - `file://` paths open in an editor at their line (`#L12` or `:12`).
  - `command:<id>?<JSON input>` (VS Code's command links) runs only commands that change nothing
    (no write, exec, network or destructive effect), because the line is a script's output.
- The status bar learned one generic thing for this: inside an item drawn with `nodes`, a span
  with `data-command` (and `data-input`) runs that command when clicked.
- UI test: `agent-statusline-m7-99.jsonc`.

### D374 — Desktop control: remembered apps, the clipboard
- **Remembered apps:**
  - An app's approval card has a second choice under "Allow for this chat": "Remember in every
    chat". It keeps the app in `agent.computerUse.allowedApps` (user settings), so it isn't asked
    about again, even after a restart.
  - Apps asked about every time (system settings, the IDE) and refused apps stay that way.
  - `agent.computerUse.rememberApp { app, remember }` adds or removes one. It's hidden from the
    agent, so only the user can give lasting access.
  - `ide://agent/computerUse` lists them.
- **The clipboard:**
  - New actions `read_clipboard` and `write_clipboard`, asked about once per chat like an app
    ("Allow your clipboard?"), since it can hold what was copied elsewhere.
  - Card numbers aren't written. The text read is capped at 20 000 characters and is marked as
    data.
  - Copying between apps stays ctrl+c / ctrl+v in each, under each app's own tier, so a terminal is
    never typed into.
- UI test: `agent-desktop-m7-95.jsonc` (Windows).

### D375 — Claude Code's installed plugins, npm sources, output styles and language servers
- **Plugins Claude Code installed** (`installed_plugins.json`, version 1 or 2, the user-scope
  install) are used in place, never copied:
  - They're listed as "From Claude Code" on the Plugins page.
  - They're on where Claude Code has them on (`enabledPlugins`) and the IDE hasn't turned them off.
    Rust reads Claude Code's settings and returns only that key.
  - Their commands, skills, subagents and output styles count at once. Their hooks, MCP servers
    and language servers only once allowed here (`record.claude`).
  - Installing the same plugin again is refused.
- **Claude Code's marketplaces** (`known_marketplaces.json`) are listed with "(Claude Code)". They
  are read from Claude Code's copy, never cloned again, and have no Update or Remove here.
- **Where Claude Code's folder is:** `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set (as Claude Code reads it), else
  `~/.claude`. Rust may read under its `plugins` folder.
  - `agent.thirdPartyConfigs` off skips all of this.
  - The UI test runner points it at an empty folder for each test, so the real one never shows in
    tests.
- **npm sources** (`{ "source": "npm", "package", "version", "registry" }`):
  - Fetched with the user's npm (`npm pack`; scripts never run) and unpacked with `tar` into the
    plugin's copy.
  - Names and versions are checked to plain characters (no spaces, `<`, `>` or `^`) before `cmd`
    sees them.
- **Output styles:** a plugin's `output-styles/` folder (and the manifest's `outputStyles`) join
  the style list, labeled with the plugin.
- **Language servers** (`.lsp.json` or the manifest's `lspServers`: `command`, `args`,
  `extensionToLanguage`):
  - Asked about at install like its MCP servers ("Start its language servers").
  - Once allowed, they join the LSP manager as contributed servers named `<plugin>-<server>`. The
    user's `lsp.servers` still goes over them.
  - The servers restart when the set changes.
- UI tests: `agent-plugins-cc-m7-107.jsonc` (a fake Claude Code folder), `agent-plugins-m7-100`.

### D376 — Widgets drawn while text-protocol models write them
- D355 drew show_widget as Rust streamed its arguments, for models with native tool calls.
- A text-protocol model writes its call into the reply as `<tool_call>` text. The loop now reads
  the arguments of a show_widget call in progress from that text, every 150 ms while it's being
  written, and gives them to the same draft card.
- The draft's id is the finished call's id, so the drawn card becomes the finished one without a
  reload.
- Ollama's native tool calls still draw at the end: Ollama sends a call only when it's whole, so
  there's nothing to draw earlier.

### D377 — Several chats at once in the Chats list
- Selecting, as in the explorer:
  - Ctrl/Cmd+click adds or removes a chat (the one on screen counts as picked first).
  - Shift+click takes the range from the last one clicked.
  - Escape lets go.
- Acting on a selection: right-click to open, archive or delete all of them; the Delete key deletes
  them.
- Ctrl+click used to open a chat in a tab of its own. The middle button and the menu still do.
- `agent.deleteSessions { sessions }` deletes several, asking once.
- Rows drag onto the dock like explorer files. Dropped on a group, an edge or a tab strip, the chat
  opens there; an open chat's tab moves there.
- The dock's drag learned a generic `views` payload (open tabs to move, or views to open), so it
  knows nothing about chats.
- UI test: `agent-chats-select-m7-108.jsonc`. The drag is checked by hand: the tests have no
  pointer-drag helper.

### D378 — Dropdowns open without moving focus
- A dropdown on All settings took about 170 ms to open.
  - Building the menu took 1 ms; our own listeners took 0.1 ms.
  - The rest was focus moving twice: into the field on the press, then into the menu's search box.
    Each move restyled the large page in the engine.
- A dropdown opened with the mouse now leaves focus where it was (`deferFocus`):
  - Hovering items doesn't move it (`:hover` shows the highlight).
  - The first key brings focus in: typing goes to the search box, arrows and Enter to the items,
    Escape closes.
  - Focus goes back to the field on close only if the menu had it.
- Opening with the keyboard is unchanged.
- Measured: 8 ms to open on the same page.

### D379 — A speed and soundness pass: long lists, search, settings, the newest code
An audit with three read-only reviewers (performance, users coming from VS Code or Zed, and the
code of D355–D378). What held up was fixed; the rest went into `docs/feature-gaps.md`.

**Speed**
- **The Search view:** while results streamed, every frame
  - listed every loaded node again, each file's matches too,
  - then expanded each new file with an `await` and a render of every row.
  That was quadratic: 8 000 files with 16 000 matches took 82 s in the debug build. Now:
  - only the root and folders list again while it runs, plus a file whose match list changed
    (a match dismissed, a new search reusing the row);
  - new files open together with `Tree.expandMany` (one render);
  - refreshes don't overlap.
  The same search took 11 s; most of the rest is the debug build's unoptimized search code.
- **One render instead of many:**
  - `Tree.refreshMany`: the explorer reloads the folders a checkout or install changed together;
  - `setRoot` restores expanded folders level by level;
  - the Testing view and Source control expand together.
- **Coalesced to a frame:**
  - the Problems view;
  - file decorations: the tab strips re-rendered with a layout read per group on every publish,
    and now skip it when the problem counts didn't change;
  - the Chats list and the Extensions view (also when their search is typed into).
- **Smaller wins:**
  - inline diagnostics group the diagnostics by file once, not once per editor;
  - the chat view finds each work group's answer in one backward pass;
  - the model picker reads the favorites once per draw;
  - the dock's layout save copies the tree once, not once per tab;
  - settings search waits 120 ms of quiet before filtering again.
- **Dropdowns:**
  - a letter jumps to the matching item, as a native list does;
  - while a dropdown waits for its first key, any other key closes it instead of editing the
    field that kept focus;
  - focus taken by a submenu goes back on close.
- **Not done:** sending search results to the page in batches (one message per file today). It
  changes the remote search protocol too; to measure in a release build first.

**Soundness**
- **The agent can't set what it couldn't change by asking:** `agent.hooks`,
  `agent.statusLine`, `agent.notify.webhook`, `agent.sandbox*` (it could have turned its own
  sandbox off) and `agent.computerUse.enabled` / `.allowedApps` joined the settings agents may
  not write.
- **A status line command link** runs a command the user confirms once per command and window,
  and never one hidden from agents. Some commands with no declared effects still act (a turn
  started, the folder closed).
- **Several chats dragged onto an edge** make one split, in order (each made its own).
- **The text protocol:**
  - a call knows which `<tool_call>` block it came from, so a widget's card keeps its own id
    when an earlier block wasn't a call;
  - an unclosed last call is found after an earlier unreadable block.
- **The chat:**
  - a message jumped to stays in place across a tab switch;
  - Send now ends a running hook;
  - a key's affordable output limit holds for the whole turn.
- **Rust:**
  - a sandboxed command's refused-host entry goes however the run ends;
  - `tar` gets the package's bare name (Git's tar read `C:\` as a host);
  - npm specs with a slash must be a scope (`owner/repo` is a GitHub fetch).
- **Small fixes:**
  - deleting several chats names the ones that failed;
  - `file://server/share` links keep the server;
  - the Outline highlights the symbol the cursor is in (copies of the symbols never matched, so
    it never had).
- **Dock views:** a view whose tab left the tree some other way than closing is disposed a
  microtask later (the leftover hidden Welcome from the gaps list).

**Coming from VS Code**
- **Object settings merge across levels**, as VS Code's do: default, user, `.vscode`, the IDE's
  workspace file, a folder's. A key set to `false` still turns one off. The terminal's
  automation profiles stay whole.
- **The terminal's VS Code settings come across:** font, line height, cursor (`line` is `bar`),
  blinking, scrollback, copy on select, right-click (`default` is the menu), contrast, keys to the
  shell.
- **An extension's `.vscode` settings** apply once it registers them.
- **VS Code command ids** in a hand-written keybinding run the IDE's command.
- **New default keys:** Ctrl+K Ctrl+W, Ctrl+K M, Ctrl+K Ctrl+T, Ctrl+K S, Ctrl+K Enter,
  Ctrl+Shift+U, and Shift+Alt+R / Shift+Alt+C in the side bar.

**Found by the full UI suite**
- **TypeScript symbols came twice in a trusted folder:** in the Outline, "Go to symbol" and
  breadcrumbs, and the built-in hovers, completions and references alongside the project server's.
  Monaco 0.57's TypeScript mode registers its providers once and never reads
  `setModeConfiguration` again, so turning the built-in service off when a server took over (D199)
  did nothing to providers already registered. Its adapters' methods now answer nothing while a
  server has taken over.
- **The outline could wait forever:** turning the built-in service off restarts Monaco's TS
  worker, and a request in flight to it never settles. Reading symbols now has a deadline (8 s,
  cancelled, then the Outline's own retry asks again), so the Outline, "@" and the
  `ide://editors/active/outline` state no longer hang.
- **"Check now" on a watched pull request** returned a look already running, which could have
  begun before the checks passed: the merge waited for the next scheduled look. It now lets that
  one end and looks again.
- **Stale expectations:**
  - Customize has nine sections since Plugins (D358).
  - VS Code import installs GitLens since commit 36659166, so the test downloaded it and timed
    out; it uses an exact built-in replacement (Auto Rename Tag) now.

**Tests:** unit tests for the dock sweep, the settings merge, the terminal aliases, call blocks and
UNC links; the Outline's follow-cursor highlight in `features-m6-30`; the status line test answers
the new confirmation; `browser.jsonc` waits for the page to settle after a resize before clicking.

### D380 — A document the language server lost is opened again; completions don't go silent
- **What was reported:** typing `fu` in this repository's `scripts/build-icons.mjs` offered no
  completions.
- **What the TypeScript server's log showed:**
  - The server had restarted.
  - A send to it failed ("typescript is not running").
  - Every request about the file then got "Unexpected resource": the server had never been told
    the file was open.
- **The cause:** `didOpen` counts a document as open before sending, and the transport doesn't
  report a failed send, so the client never told the server again. Since D379 the built-in
  TypeScript completions stay silent while a server runs, so nothing answered at all.
- **The fix:**
  - When a request about a document fails with "Unexpected resource", the client forgets it and
    reports it lost (`onDocumentLost`), and the editor opens it there again with its current text.
  - A completion request the TypeScript server fails is answered by the built-in service instead
    (`builtinCompletions`, its own adapter asked directly).
- **Tests:**
  - A unit test for the lost document.
  - `editor-ts-suggest-m7-109.jsonc`: `fu` in a `.mjs` file of a trusted folder, with the server
    running, offers the `function` keyword.

### D381 — Images in the chat: models that draw, generate_image, save_image
- **What was asked:** "if I ask it to generate an image or make an image for our project, anything
  should work (depending on the model)", and the agent should be able to add them to the project.
- **Before:** a model's image in its reply was dropped (the OpenAI-compatible stream only read
  text), an MCP tool's image became the text `[image]`, an external agent's image block was
  skipped, and nothing could put a picture into the project.
- **Chat images:** every image a model, a tool or an external agent makes is a chat image with an
  id that is never reused (`img1`, `img2`…; `core/agent/chatImages.ts`). The model is told the ids
  in its own reply and in the tool's result. Each one shows large under the reply, or under the
  work line for a tool's (they're the result, not a step's detail), with rounded corners, as
  ChatGPT shows them: on hover its id floats top left, **Add to project** bottom left and
  Download bottom right; a click opens the image viewer. While `generate_image` works, a
  placeholder of the requested shape says "Creating image" over a field of dots that a light
  sweeps across (still with reduced motion). There's no progress figure: the APIs don't report
  one.
- **Kept whole, beside the chat:** the bytes go once to `<data>/agent/media/<chat>/<id>.bin`
  (`agent_media_put` / `agent_media_get`); the transcript keeps a small preview (D156). Download,
  Add to project, the viewer and `save_image` use the whole image, after a restart too. Deleting
  the chat deletes its media.
- **Models that draw:** OpenRouter lists a model's `output_modalities`; one with `image` is
  marked (`outputImages`), and a chat request to it asks for `modalities: ["image", "text"]`. Its
  images come back in `delta.images` (or as image parts of `content`), as data: URLs. A plain link
  stays a link in the text: nothing is loaded from the network.
- **`generate_image`** (`chatImageTools.ts`): the agent makes an image from a description, with
  an optional size, reference images (chat images or the user's attachments) and a path to save it
  to. The model: `agent.imageGeneration.model`, else the chat's own model when it draws, else a
  listed model that draws (the chat's provider first), else `gpt-image-1` on an OpenAI provider.
  OpenAI's image models go through the Images API (`ai_image_generate`, `b64_json`); the others
  get a chat request that asks for images. With none, the tool says how to set one up and
  suggests an SVG meanwhile. A stopped turn cancels the request.
- **Not behind an opt-in:** it runs inside the chat when the user asks for a picture (rule 8 is
  about model calls outside the chat), like web search's question model. `agent.imageGeneration.enabled`
  (on) removes the tool.
- **`save_image`:** a chat image or a user's attachment into the project. The path's extension
  picks the format; another one is converted through a canvas (an SVG can be rasterized, a
  picture can't become an SVG). It never replaces a file unless `overwrite`, and follows the
  agent's write rules (excluded files, rule files).
- **MCP and external agents:** an MCP tool's image parts and embedded image resources become chat
  images (and a vision model gets them as PNG); an ACP agent's image in its message too.
- **State:** `ide://agent/session` lists each item's images (id, type, name, source), not their
  bytes.
- **Also in this release:**
  - **A long link no longer widens the chat:** paragraphs, list items, quotes and headings of a
    reply wrap a word that can't fit (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`); tables keep their columns.
  - **The image viewer's fade toward the chat is half as wide** (20 px, D370 had 40), which
    looked odd on some themes.
  - **A widget opened in a tab is centred vertically** (`body.is-fill`: a flex column whose
    content has `margin-block: auto`), as the chat card shows it.
  - **Development builds have their own taskbar icon:** debug builds set an orange copy of the
    logo as the window icon (`dev_icon`, `icons/dev-icon.rgba`, raw 256×256 RGBA so no PNG decoder
    is linked), so a dev build and the installed app are told apart at a glance. Release builds
    and the logos inside the app are unchanged.
- **Tests:** unit tests for chat images and the model's note, the loop's image events and a
  tool's images, an MCP result's images; Rust tests for the stream's images and the request's
  modalities; `agent-images-m7-110.jsonc` with a mock provider whose model draws.

### D382 — The code font is the OS's default, as in VS Code
- **Why:** `--font-mono` was a list (JetBrains Mono, Cascadia Code, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, …)
  whose first installed font won, and we don't bundle any of them. So the code font changed from
  PC to PC: on Windows it was Cascadia Code wherever Windows Terminal is installed (it shares the
  font with every app), Consolas elsewhere. Cascadia is heavier and wider, so code looked bolder
  than in VS Code.
- **Now:** VS Code's defaults for each OS: Windows `Consolas, "Courier New", monospace`, macOS
  `Menlo, Monaco, "Courier New", monospace`, Linux `"Droid Sans Mono", "monospace", monospace`.
  `main.ts` sets `<html data-platform>` before the first paint, and `tokens.css` picks the stack
  from it.
- **Where it applies:** everything that uses `--font-mono`: the terminal (when
  `terminal.fontFamily` is empty), code in the chat and tool cards, and the editor and diff
  editor, which read the token (`monoFont()`, since Monaco measures a font family string) unless
  `editor.fontFamily` is set.
- **Choosing another font:** `editor.fontFamily` and `terminal.fontFamily` are unchanged, so
  JetBrains Mono or Cascadia Code is one setting away, as in VS Code.

### D383 — Status bar items hidden one by one; Follow the agent; shorter form dialogs
- **Status bar items (VS Code's):** right-clicking the status bar lists its items by name with a
  check, in their order on the bar (left side, a line, right side); right-clicking an item
  starts the menu with Hide "<item>". Then Show all (when something is hidden) and Hide status
  bar. The menu lists what's on the bar now and what the user hid, not the items that show
  nothing yet (a download's progress, the dev container's steps): VS Code's entries don't exist
  until they show, and listing all 38 made a menu taller than the window. The choice is
  `workbench.statusBar.hidden` (item ids, user scope, every folder), set by
  `statusBar.setItemHidden` (`id`, or `all` with `hidden: false`). `ide://statusbar` lists the
  items (id, name, side, what they show, hidden). Every built-in item got a `name` (also its
  screen reader label, which now leaves out the `$(icon)` codes); an extension's nameless item is
  labelled by the extension, as in VS Code; a pending key chord's message can't be hidden
  (`hideable: false`). The order and the hidden list are DOM-free (`workbench/statusItems.ts`).
  The status bar's commands moved to `extensions/workbench/statusBarCommands.ts`.
- **Follow the agent (Zed's), as a setting only:** `agent.followEdits` (off) opens each file the
  chat you're looking at edits, in a preview tab at the first changed line, as it happens. The
  owner wanted no new chat UI for it, so there's no toggle in the chat. It never takes focus from
  the chat (`preserveFocus`), waits while you've typed in an editor in the last 3 s, and opens
  the last of a burst of edits (150 ms). The changeset emits `agent.didEdit` (session, path,
  line, staged) for every edit, the IDE agent's and an external agent's (`adopt`);
  `firstChangedLine` is tested. Off by default: jumping the editor around is disruptive, and
  it's not a model call (rule 8 doesn't apply).
- **Form dialogs are at most 600 px tall** (they could fill a tall window): the content scrolls
  and the title and buttons stay. The built-in server's tool list (Customize → MCP) was the case.
- **Checked against the gap list, already there:**
  - Terminals after a full restart: they come back with their name, folder and last output
    above a new shell, and Run recent command keeps its history (D204, D253). The restore test
    now checks a renamed terminal's name too.
  - Scratch files: VS Code and Cursor have untitled files, kept across restarts by hot exit
    (D120), as here. Scratch files as IntelliJ has them stay in the gap list.
  - The settings page's focus lag: no longer noticeable after D378 (the owner).
- **Tests:** `statusItems.test.ts`, `follow.test.ts`; `statusbar-items-m7-112.jsonc`,
  `agent-follow-m7-113.jsonc`; `terminal-restore-m7-19.jsonc` extended.

### D384 — Dictation without a key: Whisper on this computer; the mic apart from Send
- **Why:** dictation needed a Groq or OpenAI key. VS Code's dictation runs a model on the
  computer, downloaded on first use; the owner wanted the same, and the model not in the
  installer (the IDE is ~16 MB).
- **The engine:** Whisper on the CPU through candle (Hugging Face's ML library: pure Rust,
  MIT/Apache-2.0, ~3 MB of the binary; it requires the `tokenizers` crate, built pure-Rust).
  whisper.cpp's own bindings (whisper-rs) were the other choice; they build whisper.cpp with
  cmake and a C++ toolchain, which the owner's machine doesn't have. All 173 crates under candle
  pass `deny.toml`.
- **The models:** whisper.cpp's files (MIT, the `ggerganov/whisper.cpp` repository on Hugging
  Face, pinned to commit 5359861 and each file's SHA-256): `base` (q5_1, 60 MB, the default) and
  `small` (q5_1, 190 MB, more accurate), both multilingual (99 languages). Candle's own quantized
  Whisper files exist only for `tiny`, from a repository with no license, so `speech/ggml.rs`
  reads whisper.cpp's format into candle (names mapped to Hugging Face's; the file's own mel
  filters and vocabulary). Downloaded to `<data>/speech/` through the agent registry's
  downloader (progress, cancel, stall timeout, redirects checked); a `.sha256` mark beside the
  file says the download was verified.
- **Speed (Ryzen 7 2700, base, one sentence):** 14 s with candle's q5_1 matrix code, 3.9 s with
  the weights widened to f16 on load (~150 MB of memory), ~2 s once the decoder keeps its own
  keys and values (`speech/model.rs`, adapted from candle's, which recomputes every earlier token
  each step) and the model stays loaded (3 minutes after the last use). `small` is ~9 s. Dev
  builds compile candle optimized, so the UI tests transcribe in seconds.
- **Quality guards:** Whisper's suppressed tokens, its no-speech probability (> 0.6: nothing),
  a silence gate (no 25 ms window above a whisper's loudness: nothing; Whisper invents "Thank
  you." for silence), a loop guard, and the language from `agent.voice.language` or heard.
- **Found on the way:** candle reads a tensor's bytes in place, which needs aligned memory; in
  whisper.cpp's files a tensor starts wherever its name ends. Release builds don't check, so the
  first prototype "worked"; the debug-build unit test caught it. Each tensor is copied to an
  8-byte-aligned buffer first.
- **Where a recording goes** (`voiceRoute`, tested): `agent.voice.provider` empty: a downloaded
  model first (the user chose it: private, no key), then Groq, then OpenAI; `device`: this
  computer's model only; a provider id: that provider. Nothing: the mic's first click shows
  **Set up dictation** (Download (60 MB) / Use an API key (adds Groq) / Not now; on Windows it
  mentions Win + H). The page decodes the recording and resamples it to 16 kHz mono
  (`toSamples`: decodeAudioData and an OfflineAudioContext), sent as a raw body.
- **Commands and state:** `agent.voice.setup`, `agent.voice.downloadModel` (`model`; `url` and
  `sha256` only in test builds), `agent.voice.cancelDownload`, `agent.voice.removeModel`,
  `agent.voice.transcribeFile` (an audio file in the project → text, any route);
  `ide://agent/voice` (enabled, route, language, models with size and download progress).
  Setting `agent.voice.localModel` (`base` | `small`). Not opt-in under rule 8: it isn't a model
  call outside the chat, and nothing downloads until the user asks.
- **The mic apart from Send (the owner's ask):** the mic used to take the send button's place in
  an empty box. Now the mic is always last and Send shows to its left once something's typed or
  attached (or as Stop while the agent works), so typing and speaking mix. While recording, only
  Stop (if working) shows beside the mic's ✓. With `agent.voice.enabled` off, Send stays as it was.
- **Not changed:** an MCP server's sampling request with audio still goes to a speech service
  (D223).
- **Tests:** `speech::` Rust tests (the file reader on a synthetic model, names, the whole
  pipeline on a synthetic model, decoding rules, languages, the verified mark) and an ignored
  one for the real model (`IDE_TEST_WHISPER_MODEL`); `voiceRoute` unit tests;
  `agent-dictation-m7-114.jsonc` (the setup dialog, a download from the mock at its SHA-256, a
  file transcribed on this computer, a wrong SHA-256 refused, removal) and
  `agent-modes-m6-79.jsonc` (the two buttons). By hand: the real base model downloaded from
  Hugging Face in the app and a spoken sentence transcribed word for word.

### D385 — Quiet Send and Stop; text fields focus with a brighter border, not the accent
- **Send, Stop and the microphone** are now one style (the owner's ask, after Claude Code's
  composer): quiet 30 px icon buttons with no fill, the icon in the text's color, a `--bg-hover`
  square on hover. Send is ↵ (Lucide's `corner-down-left`, added to the sprite), dimmed when
  there's nothing to send (dictation off); Stop is a small filled square; the recording ✓ is
  quiet too (the waveform says it's recording). The accent-filled round button is gone.
- **A focused text field's border** is a step brighter on dark themes (darker on light ones)
  instead of the accent: `--border-input-focus`, the theme's text color at 35 %, so built-in and
  imported themes all get it right. For every text field: `.input`, the chat box, the command
  box (its accent halo is gone too), the browser's address bar, a notebook cell's editor,
  Monaco's find fields, the ask_user "other" answer, extensions' source-control box. Keyboard
  focus rings on buttons, rows and cards keep the accent (`--focus-ring`): they're what a
  keyboard user follows.

### D386 — An extension that's stopping doesn't show messages
- **Why:** Live Server (ritwickdey) puts its app model in `context.subscriptions`, and the model's
  `dispose()` calls `GoOffline()`, which says "Server is not already running" when no server
  runs. Every time the IDE stopped the extension (a host restart after installing or updating
  extensions, a folder switch), the owner got that notification. VS Code never shows it: its
  extension host is going away, so the message is dropped.
- **Now:** from the start of an extension's deactivation (`shim.beginStop()`, before its
  `deactivate()`, and in `dispose()`), `window.showInformationMessage` / `Warning` / `Error`
  resolve to `undefined` without showing anything; the text goes to the extension's log
  ("(while stopping, not shown) info: …").
- **Tests:** `shim.test.ts` ("an extension that's stopping logs its messages…").

### D387 — F11 toggles full screen
- **VS Code's:** `workbench.action.toggleFullScreen` is F11 on Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Cmd+F on
  macOS, and View → Appearance → Full Screen; while debugging is paused F11 is Step Into. The
  IDE had the command (`window.toggleFullscreen`) and the menu item but no key.
- **Now:** F11 / Ctrl+Cmd+F, with `when: debugState != 'stopped'` so Step Into's F11 (`when:
  debugState == 'stopped'`) wins while paused whatever the rules' order. F11 is also on the list
  of the web view's own keys that are cancelled (`browserDefaults.ts`). The command returns
  `{ fullscreen }`. The menu item and the palette show the key.
- **From a maximized window** (the owner's report): on Windows the page kept its maximized
  height in full screen, a taskbar-high strip below it (measured: 1032 of 1080 px; from a normal
  window it was 1080). The window is now restored before going full screen and maximized again
  on the way out (`windowIpc.toggleFullscreen`).
- **No window buttons in full screen,** as in VS Code: minimize / maximize / close hide while
  the window is full screen (the title bar's resize sync checks `isFullscreen`).
- **Tests:** a resolver unit test (both orders, no debug session, paused, macOS) and
  `fullscreen-m7-115.jsonc` (F11 from a maximized window, the buttons hidden and back, the
  palette's label).

### D388 — An extension's hidden terminals stay hidden and aren't saved
- **The owner's report:** "Python" terminal tabs appeared in projects where none had been
  opened, came back after being closed, and piled up across restarts.
- **Why:** the Python extensions create terminals with `hideFromUser: true` every session
  (shell-integration probes, environment deactivation scripts) and leave them nameless, so they
  were labelled with the extension's name, "Python". The shim ignored `hideFromUser` and opened
  each one as a background tab; extension terminals were then saved with the folder and came
  back after a restart as ordinary shells. Closing them didn't help: the next session made new
  ones.
- **Now (VS Code's behavior):** `hideFromUser` makes the terminal hidden (no tab: it runs among
  the hidden terminals, every terminal tool still reaches it by id) until the extension calls
  `show()`, which gives it its tab; the extension disposing it ends it where it is. Such a
  terminal, and one made with `isTransient`, carries `transient` in its state: its tab isn't
  restored (`TerminalView.persist()`), nor its place among the hidden ones. The IDE's own
  extension API has `hidden` and `transient` options to match.
- **Found on the way:** a terminal tab's state is filtered to known fields (`split.ts`
  `PANE_FIELDS`), which dropped `transient` silently; the UI test caught it (the terminal came
  back after reopening the folder).
- **Already saved "Python" tabs** (from before) aren't marked: close them once and they stay
  closed.
- **Tests:** `split.test.ts` (the mark survives), `ext-hidden-terminal-m7-116.jsonc` (a VS Code
  extension's hideFromUser terminal: hidden, shown by `show()`, gone after reopening the
  folder).

### D389 — Slash commands after Claude Code's, inline "/" and "@" lists, flat model logos
- **The owner's ask:** the commands Claude Code and other harnesses have (/undo, /btw…), as good
  as theirs; the "/" list over the message box like Claude Code's, not in the command palette;
  the "@" list the same; and the logos of models and providers as agents' faces without the chip
  behind them (the model picker keeps its chips).
- **Commands:** `BUILTIN_COMMANDS` gains Claude Code's: `/btw`, `/undo`, `/rewind`, `/fork`,
  `/resume`, `/rename`, `/export`, `/copy`, `/context`, `/usage`, `/effort`, `/plan`, `/todos`,
  `/tasks`, `/security-review`, `/memory`, `/agents`, `/skills`, `/rules`, `/mcp`, `/hooks`,
  `/permissions`, `/add-dir`, `/config`, `/help`, `/release-notes`, `/bug`, with other names
  (`aliases`: `/new` and `/reset` are `/clear`, `/cost` `/usage`, `/subagents` `/agents`,
  `/settings` `/config`, `/allowed-tools` `/permissions`, `/bashes` `/tasks`, `/feedback` `/bug`).
  Most run a command the IDE already had (each through the dispatcher, as the caller), so an
  agent and a keybinding reach the same thing. `/undo` restores the newest checkpoint; with none
  it says so in a note instead of failing. `/context` is a note (tokens of the limit, messages,

- **/btw:** a side question answered by the chat's model from the end of the transcript, with no

  never reach the model, so the answer doesn't become part of the conversation, and a running

  starts: "co" doesn't find "uncommitted"). ↑/↓ choose, Tab fills in, Enter fills in and runs a

  opens the same kind of list in every chat (before: only in group chats, the rest went to the
  picker): files, @problems, @git and the other mentions, web addresses and symbols
  (`agent.mentionItems`, what the picker loads), the agents, and "Browse files and context…".
- **Faces:** a model's or provider's logo as an agent's face (D270) is drawn flat, in the
  surrounding text's color, with no chip, border or tint; a colored logo as it is, letters as
  text. The model picker and the providers page keep the chips.
- **Tests:** `slash.test.ts` (ranking, other names), `agent-slash-m7-108.jsonc` (the lists, the
  keys, /context, /undo, /btw with the mock checking it got the chat, the flat face).

### D390 — The agent's rarely used tools load on demand; dimmer flat logos; menu-height rows
- **The owner's question:** 22k tokens of context for a greeting. 18.8k of it was the tool
  definitions: 52 tools, about 54 000 characters, in every request. Claude Code starts at a
  similar size, but defers its own rarely used tools (worktrees, cron, monitors…) behind
  ToolSearch.
- **Now:** the IDE's own rarely used tools (`ON_DEMAND_TOOLS`: workflows, monitors, schedules,
  pull request watches, hand-offs, other chats, worktrees, images, suggestions, the guide) are
  deferred like many MCP tools (D319): named in a note, loaded with `tool_search`. A new chat's
  request went from 52 tools and 54 200 characters to 35 and 36 300 (plus a 1 800-character note);
  Ask mode from 36 900 to 28 100. With no folder open, the worktree and pull request tools aren't
  sent at all.
- **Without making the agent worse:** a deferred built-in called by name just runs (an MCP tool
  still asks for the search: its schema is someone else's), and stays loaded in that chat after;
  the IDE's own messages that name `save_image` or `chat_attachments` give the arguments. What
  every turn uses, and what the IDE's prompts ask for by name (`wrap_up`, `report_findings`,
  `schedule_wakeup`, `widget_guide`), is always sent. `agent.deferTools: never` sends everything.
- **Not done:** shortening the descriptions of the tools still sent. They're what the model reads
  to use each tool well (when to delegate, how to search, what a recap holds); trimming them would
  trade quality for a few hundred tokens.
- **Logos (the owner's ask):** a flat logo (D389) takes the other icons' dimmer color
  (`--fg-muted`) instead of the text's; the model picker's rail and rows are flat too (the rail's
  brightens with its tab). The providers page keeps its chips.
- **"/" and "@" rows:** 26 px with the context menu's padding, corners and highlight
  (`.menu-item`), the list the menu's padding.
- **Tests:** `deferredTools.test.ts` (built-ins deferred on auto, a direct call runs and stays,
  never sends all); the UI scripts that use those tools.

### D391 — A full audit: every area read again, the verified bugs fixed; the extension shim's stubs made real
- **The owner's ask:** a meticulous audit of every aspect of the IDE, its bugs fixed, and the VS
  Code extension shim checked for anything missing. Ten read-throughs, one per area (the
  agent's runtime, view and core logic; core; the workbench; the editor, explorer and notebooks;
  git, terminal, tasks, testing, debug; extensions and the browser; the Rust back end; the shim),
  then six more on what the first round didn't reach. Only bugs traced line by line or reproduced
  were fixed, with the smallest change and a test where the code is DOM-free.
- **Freezes and crashes:** a malformed show_widget stream looped forever (the UI thread); a crafted
  PDF looped or ran for minutes four ways; `htmlToText` was quadratic (a 300 kB page, 66 s); a
  repeated `**/` glob backtracked exponentially; the problem report's redaction was quadratic; a
  malformed `when` threw on every key press; one unreadable key dropped every keybinding; a damaged
  theme cache stopped the app starting; a dock rebuild during a splitter drag left the whole window
  unclickable; Rust panicked slicing non-ASCII paths (`is_unc`, a deep-link argument at start).
- **Safety:** an Ask pattern (`"git push": false`) was dodged by spacing, case, `git.exe`, a path or
  `git -C`; the denylist missed a Windows program path (`C:\…\taskkill.exe`) and programs run
  through git's config (`-c alias.x=!…`, `core.pager`, `core.fsmonitor`…) or the environment
  (`GIT_PAGER=…`, `NODE_OPTIONS=…`, `$env:…`), which now ask; a trailing-dot host dodged a
  domain rule; protected config files were reachable as `::$DATA` or through `..`; `isWithin`
  took `root/../x` as inside; several Rust paths touched a network path before checking it
  (D161); the sandbox's allowWrite check was dodged by case or `..`; dev containers ran the
  folder's commands without asking for trust; extensions' will-save edits and viewers could write
  inside `.git`; "Copy as cURL" didn't quote the page's method; deep links could carry flags
  (the handler now passes `--`).
- **Lost work and wrong writes:** Stop while a message waited for a busy agent lost the message;
  history restore and extension edits damaged files that aren't UTF-8 (UTF-16, a code page, a
  BOM); with nesting off, deleting `package.json` still took `package-lock.json`; notebook
  replace on CRLF cells changed the wrong text; an answer cut short when the IDE closed got no
  Continue.
- **Stuck states and leaks:** a debug start that missed `initialized`; a stop shown after the
  program resumed; test runs started twice; notebook cells left "running"; every opened document
  kept by quick diff; widget drafts' timers; a chat put away while reports waited.
- **The extension shim (owner's ask):** every stable namespace member, class and enum of VS Code
  1.106 was already there. Fixed: answers that can't be serialized now fail instead of never
  answering; snippet edits in a WorkspaceEdit; `Uri` paths for file and web schemes; the
  `disposables` argument of events; surrogate pairs in document changes; language model message
  parts; a session's configuration; git state read during a change. Made real: the
  `vscode.execute…Provider` commands (Monaco's own `_execute…` commands ask every provider —
  language servers, built-in services, extensions — and merge as VS Code does;
  `ide.languages.execute`), `activeColorTheme` and its event, `cursorMove` and `editorScroll`.
  Still stubs (they need IDE features that don't exist yet): timeline, port attributes, drop and
  paste edits, language model and MCP definition providers, `onWill…Files`, terminal data events.
- **The unit tests can load `.svg`** (as the build does), so modules that draw an icon are testable.
- **Left for the owner (design, not fixed):** the command sandbox leaves the repository's `.git`
  writable, and the IDE's own unsandboxed git then runs what a sandboxed command put in
  `.git/config` (fsmonitor, sshCommand, filters) or `.git/hooks`; on Linux bubblewrap still allows
  Unix sockets (the D-Bus session bus) and has no pid namespace; on macOS the profile allows
  mach-lookup and Apple events (`open -a Terminal`). The IDE's MCP server info file is readable
  from the sandbox. A notebook's output page reads workspace files without `fs.read`.
- **Tests:** the new and extended unit tests in each area (2 142 pass), `cargo test --lib` (410),
  the full UI suite run locally, `vscode-shim-m7-21.jsonc` (execute providers, theme kind).
- **Found by the UI suite run:** on Windows, Edge's `msedge.exe` hands off to the browser and
  exits at once, so debugging a page in Edge failed with "Edge closed before the debugger
  connected"; the port is now watched for a few seconds after the program ends, the session
  ends when the browser's connection does, and Stop closes the browser through it
  (`Browser.close`). A tree whose load was replaced by a newer one (D233's handed-over groups)
  gives the newer load the rows it was asked to expand. `alpha-m7-5.jsonc` expected the release
  notes of m7.33.

### D392 — The command sandbox can't change git's settings or the agents' configuration; the IDE's git pauses when they change anyway
- **Why:** D391 left it open: a sandboxed command could write `.git/config` (core.fsmonitor,
  sshCommand, filters) or `.git/hooks`, and the IDE's own git, outside the sandbox, ran what it
  put there the next time it refreshed Source control. A project's agent settings
  (`.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json`, the IDE's own folder) decide what later runs without
  asking, so they're the same kind of way out. The owner asked for the industry standard.
- **macOS and Linux, as Claude Code's sandbox does** (`exec/sandbox_protect.rs`): inside the
  writable folders, writes are refused to git's `config`, `config.worktree`, `commondir` and
  `hooks` (the repository's, its submodules' under `modules/`, its linked worktrees' under
  `worktrees/`), to the repository's `.git` itself (so it can't be renamed and replaced), and to
  `.claude`, `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.mcp.json` and the IDE's own folders (product.json's
  `workspaceFolderName` and its aliases, sent with the policy as `protectFolders`). macOS:
  `deny file-write*` rules after the folders' `allow`, any depth, any case (APFS ignores case).
  Linux: bubblewrap binds what exists of them read-only, and `.git` onto itself (a mount point
  can't be renamed or removed); what doesn't exist yet can't be bound (a bind would create it in
  the folder). Commits, branches and fetches still work in the sandbox; `git config` and a hook
  installer (husky) are refused, and run outside the sandbox when the user allows it.
- **Windows: the IDE's git checks instead** (`git/guard.rs`). Measured on Windows 11: a
  medium label on `.git/config` inside a low-labelled folder stops writes to it but not its
  deletion or renaming (the folder's own low label grants that), nor renaming `.git`; Windows
  has no way to keep such a file while the folder stays writable. So before a sandboxed command
  the settings of the repository holding each writable folder are recorded (once: a later
  command doesn't take over what an earlier one changed), and every git call the IDE makes
  first checks them. Changed: that repository's git is paused, Source control says which file
  changed and offers **Trust git settings** (`git.trustSettings`, a dialog that says what git
  runs from them; only a person can run it, not an agent or an extension). A repository made
  under the folder later is paused if its settings are newer than the first sandboxed command.
  The IDE's own git commands that may change settings (`remote add`, `push -u`, `config`)
  update the record after them; only those (in the app, a change made while the IDE's
  background `status` and `stash list` ran was first taken for theirs). The record is kept in the data folder (`git-guard.json`), so a restart
  doesn't skip the check; a sandboxed process ends with the IDE (D180), so a record from an
  earlier session is dropped once it matches. It runs on every system, behind the sandbox's
  own rules there.
- **What it doesn't cover:** git run by the user in a terminal (a prompt that shows the branch
  runs `git status`) reads the settings without this check; on Windows the agents' and the
  IDE's configuration folders stay writable (the agent's own scan of command lines still asks
  before one that names them, D213); a file a repository's config includes from the work tree.
  A user's own change to `.git/config` while the folder is guarded pauses git once too. A
  paused nested repository leaves Source control's list until trusted (`git.trustSettings`
  with its folder). The check and git's own read of its settings aren't one step.
- **State and commands:** `ide://git/problem` (`paused`), `git.trustSettings`, `git_trust_settings`;
  the error code `GitSettingsChanged`.
- **Tests:** `sandbox_protect.rs` (the macOS rules, the git pattern against what must stay
  writable, the bubblewrap binds), `guard.rs` (pause, a later command, read-only commands, trust,
  hooks, the IDE's own change, a new repository, a restart), `sandboxPolicy.test.ts`;
  `git-guard-m7-117.jsonc` in the app.

### D393 — Read-only files as in VS Code with a lock in the status bar; secret values hidden on request; Paste from history
- **Why:** the owner picked these from `feature-gaps.md` ("Next up" 4 and 9), with two rules:
  match VS Code where it has the feature, and where it doesn't, a setting that's off by default.
  They also asked for the Restricted mode badge where VS Code puts it, and decided the title bar
  stays as it is: no branch, project or worktree pickers there (the status bar, Source control and
  File → Open recent have them), so those rows left the list.
- **Read-only (VS Code 1.79's):** `files.readonlyInclude` / `files.readonlyExclude` (glob maps,
  matched against the path in the folder or the absolute path) and
  `files.readonlyFromPermissions` (a file without write permission, asked once per file);
  "Set active editor read-only / writeable in session", "Toggle …" and "Reset …"
  (`editor.setReadOnlyInSession`, `setWritableInSession`, `toggleReadOnlyInSession`,
  `resetReadOnlyInSession`; VS Code's `workbench.action.files.*ReadonlyInSession` ids run them, in
  keybindings and from extensions). The session's choice wins over the settings until reset or
  the window closes, and follows a rename. `EditorFileRules` (`fileRules.ts`) decides; the editor
  is kept read-only on top of its document (`EngineEditor.setForcedReadOnly`), so Monaco's
  "Cannot edit in read-only editor" shows, Cut / Paste leave the menu, `editorReadonly` is true
  and `editor.insertText` refuses (`EditorView.readOnly`). It's the editor only, as VS Code's
  text editor: agents' file tools still write the file. `ide://editors/active` has `readOnly`.
- **The lock** (IntelliJ's): a status bar item beside the line endings, open or closed, a click
  toggles the session's choice; a file that isn't UTF-8 shows it closed with the reason. Hidden
  with `workbench.statusBar.editorInfo` like its neighbours, or one by one (D383).
- **Secret values** (`editor.hideSecrets`, off; `editor.secretFiles`, Zed's `private_files`
  list): VS Code has nothing built in, Zed has `redact_private_values` (off). In those files
  each `KEY=value` / `key: value` value, and every other line of content (a key file's body; its
  `-----BEGIN…` lines stay), gets a gray bar of its own width (`.editor-secret`: the text turns
  transparent, so columns don't move), except on the lines a cursor or selection touches.
  Copying copies the real text. `secretValues.ts` is DOM-free and tested.
- **Paste from history** (IntelliJ's Ctrl+Shift+V, which here is VS Code's Markdown preview):
  Ctrl+K Ctrl+V and the editor's right-click menu. The last 30 texts copied or cut in any
  editor (the keyboard's copy and cut events, captured before the engine's own handler so a cut's
  text is still there, and the menu's Copy / Cut), newest first, a repeat moving up; the system
  clipboard's text joins at the top when it came from another program. The picker previews the
  selected entry in a zone below the cursor's line (`QuickInput.pick`'s new `onActive`), Enter
  pastes it at every cursor. Memory only, never on disk, in the state tree or offered to agents
  (the command is hidden from them): copies include passwords. `editor.clearClipboardHistory`.
- **Restricted mode:** the badge already sat in the status bar, as VS Code's does; it moved to
  the far left, after only the remote indicator (priority 100.5), where VS Code shows it. That
  showed a bug: the status bar ordered items with CSS `order`, which takes whole numbers only, so
  a fractional priority (common in VS Code extensions) was ignored and the item fell to the end.
  Items are now placed in the DOM by priority (`StatusBar.place`).
- **Not done:** the history doesn't see copies made outside the editor inside the IDE (the
  terminal, a chat) except through the system clipboard's latest text.
- **Icons:** `lock`, `lock-open`, `clipboard-clock` from Lucide.
- **Tests:** `readOnlyFiles.test.ts`, `secretValues.test.ts`, `clipboardHistory.test.ts`;
  `editor-files-m7-118.jsonc` in the app (the lock, the session commands, readonlyInclude, the
  covered values and the cursor's line, the paste preview and paste, the Restricted mode badge).
