### D400 — The full UI suite on CI's runners: what was ours, what the runners lack

The first full run of every UI script on CI's runners (D396) left 19 failures on Windows and 20
on Linux. All of the Windows failures passed on the owner's machine.
- **Ours:** the fake `gh`, `docker` and `make` were stored without the executable bit, so Linux
  ran the runner's real GitHub CLI (four scripts); `kill-matching.mjs` used `pkill -f`, which
  matched its own command line and its shell's and ended them (exit 143), so it lists with
  `pgrep` and leaves out itself and its parent; the Outline's sort by name compared by code point
  where the locale is plain C ("Zed" before "alpha"), so names are lowercased first;
  agent-external-model set the subagent before the subagent list had loaded, so it waits for it
  now; big-repo's helper retries git while the IDE's own git holds `index.lock` and prints git's
  message otherwise.
- **The runners lack it:** scripts declare what they need and are skipped without it: zsh and
  fish, xdotool, typescript-language-server, WSL, and debugpy. For debugpy, `"requires"` takes
  `"python:<module>"`, a module python3 (else python) can import. fullscreen-m7-115 runs on
  Windows and macOS only: xvfb has no window manager to make a window full screen.
- **Logs:** a step whose expectation fails logs what it saw (`got:`, up to 1,500 characters).
  The 127s on Windows (commands not found in a terminal) and the Linux webview failures (widgets
  not drawn, synthesized clicks not focusing a field) don't show their cause in the log and
  don't happen on the owner's machine. The next run's `got:` lines are for those.
- **Rules:** New is always in the "In this project" heading. With no folder open, it opens one.

### D401 — Agents: tabs that shimmer, sign in and out, a slow start explained, OpenCode V2, rules open as files

- **Why:** the owner asked for shorter Customize tabs, OpenCode V2 in place of OpenCode, a chat's
  tab to shimmer while it works, and a way to sign in or out of Claude Code. Claude Code then
  failed with "initialize timed out" though its sign-in was fine: it starts with
  `npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`, and npx was downloading a new version of the
  adapter. That took over two minutes once (50 s on the next try, 4 s cached), and nothing said

  on the first row; the old names still find them in the search box.
- **Shimmer:** a dock view descriptor's `working(state)` puts `is-working` on its tab, and the
  title shimmers like the chat's row in the Chats list. A chat is working while its status is
  running (not while it waits for an answer).
- **Slow start:** for an agent launched through a package runner (`packageRunner`: npx, uvx,
  bunx, pnpm, yarn, deno), `initialize` waits up to 10 minutes instead of 2, and after 15 s the
  chat says it's still starting because the runner is downloading it.

  own login in a terminal) and **Sign out** (`agent.signOutAgent`: `claude /logout`,
  `codex logout`, `copilot /logout`). Gemini CLI has no sign-out; its sign-in changes the
  account.
- **OpenCode:** no longer a preset (the npm `@opencode/cli` as `opencode2`). The registry's

  from opencode.ai after the usual confirm, with no Node.js. Start free installs the same,
  always from the download, because an `opencode` on PATH can be OpenCode 1, which can't read
  OpenCode 2's database. `signInOptional` went with the preset. A chat set to `acp/OpenCode`
  needs another agent picked.
- **Rules:** clicking a rule opens its file in the editor, as a skill's SKILL.md opens. ⋯ has
  Open and **When it applies…**: the form for scope and subagents, without the text box.

### D403 — An external agent's turn counts only what changed while its steps ran

- **Why:** the owner asked Claude Code to review the project without changing anything. Its turn
  showed "Edited a file" and two changed files: edits made in the same folder at the same time
  by another agent (the D402 change). An external agent writes files itself, so the IDE watches
  the folder during its turn (D208), and every changed file no step named went into the turn's
  "Changed files", whoever changed it.
- **What:** each step's start and end are recorded (`stepWindows`, by tool call, with ACP's
  kind). A changed file that no step named counts as the agent's only if it was modified while
  one of its steps that can write was running (any kind but read, search, fetch and think), with
  2 s either side (`changedByAgent` in `core/acp/turnChanges.ts`). Other files stay out of the
  review and the turn's "Changed files", and a line of its own in the chat names them ("Changed
  while none of Claude Code's steps ran, so not counted as its work"): not on a "Changed files"
  step, so a turn that changed nothing never looks like an edit.
- **Kept as before:** files a step named, files the person saved over the agent's change, files
  with no time (deleted), and every file of an agent that reported no steps at all (nothing to
  judge by). A background process the agent left running (a dev server) writes outside its steps:
  noted, not reviewed.
- **Test:** `acp-foreign-changes-m7-117`: the mock agent pauses between a read and a command; a
  file written from the terminal in the pause isn't the agent's, the command's file is.

### D404 — The activity bar's count badge centers its digits

- **Why:** the owner saw the number in the activity bar's badge (Source control's count) sit low
  in its circle. The badge centered its line box; the UI font's digits sit low inside that box.
- **What:** where the webview supports `text-box`, the badge is a block trimmed to the digits'
  cap height and baseline (`text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic`), with padding of half of
  `16px - 1cap` above and below, so the figures themselves are centered (measured: 5 px above and
  below in a 16 px badge). Elsewhere it stays as it was.

- **Why:** the owner's chat with Codex showed Claude Code's logo in the Chats list: the model
  selected now, not the one that answered. D364 shows the model that wrote most of a chat's
  replies, by each reply's `modelKey`; the IDE's own turns set it, an external agent's never did,

- **Agents row:** the Chats view's rows are New chat, Usage and Customize. Agents is one of

  recommended (no folder, or nothing for its files), the Recommended section is **Popular**:
  `POPULAR_EXTENSIONS` in `core/extensions/recommendations.ts`, five widely used extensions the
  IDE runs (docs/extensions.md's table) and checked on Open VSX: Prettier, ESLint, Python, Error
  Lens, Material Icon Theme. Installed and ignored ones are left out, as for any recommendation.

### D407 — Audit of D392–D406: the git guard's self-unpause, and what else was verified

The owner asked for a full audit. D391 had read every area; this pass read everything changed
since (D392–D406) and the code it touches, in three parts (Rust, IPC and git; the agent and
external agents; the editor, dock and workbench), with each finding traced line by line or
reproduced before it was fixed.
- **The git guard (D392):**
  - **Unpaused itself.** `git::run` called `guard::settle` even when `check` had refused, so
    after a sandboxed command changed `.git/config`, the next refresh's `git remote` took the
    change as the IDE's own and git ran its programs. Now `settle` runs only when git ran.
  - **Listings counted as writes.** Only the forms that write settle (`writes_settings`):
    `remote add`, `branch -u`, `worktree add`, `submodule update`, `lfs install`, `push`,
    `checkout`, `config <name> <value>`, `init`; not `remote -v`, `branch --list`,
    `worktree list` or `submodule status`, which refreshes run all the time.
  - **Fetch, pull, push and `gh`.** They didn't go through the guard. `remote_op` now checks and
    settles (so `push -u` publishing a branch is the user's own change, not a pause). The GitHub
    CLI checks before every operation but `auth status`, and records what repo create, PR
    checkout, merge and create leave (`guard::record`).
  - **A folder inside the repository.** An earlier session's record was dropped when the
    workspace was `repo/sub`; armed folders are matched both ways round, as `check` does.
  - **New repositories.** Initialize repository records the new repository, so it isn't paused
    in a folder a sandboxed command ran in.
  - **Still open:**
    - Repositories the guard never recorded are judged by file times, which a sandboxed command
      can set back.
    - Armed folders aren't kept across a restart.
    - Hooks under `core.hooksPath` (husky) aren't in the print.
    - Every git call hashes the settings again while a record exists.
- **An external agent's own changes (D403):**
  - A file the agent moved, copied or unpacked keeps its source's time; a time from before the
    turn (or none, 0) now counts as the agent's.
  - A step first reported as already finished is timed from the turn's start.
  - A step id reused from an earlier turn gets a window.
  - The "not counted" line names ten files and how many more.
  - The "still starting" line isn't added to an idle chat (a start for the model menu).
  - **Still open:** a file the agent changed and something else changed again later in the turn
    is judged by the later time.
- **External agents (D401):** Start free says why it stopped (already installing). "OpenCode" is
  a reserved name, so the registry's OpenCode 1 installs as "OpenCode (opencode)" rather than
  answering old chats set to the removed preset. The Docs page's Add focuses the new form's
  field. `permissionCards.ts` is formatted (CI's lint would have failed on D402).
- **Editor (D393, D398):**
  - **Hidden secrets.** A bare base64 key ending in `=` padding (a WireGuard key) read as an
    empty assignment and showed whole; it's covered now. Secret files match in any case
    (`.ENV`, `server.KEY`), and a malformed `editor.secretFiles` falls back to the defaults.
  - **Paste from history.** A copy from a masked file is listed as "Hidden value": its text isn't
    in the list, the filter or the preview, and it stays hidden when copied again. Entries are
    capped at 100,000 characters (was a million: up to 60 MB held for a list of snippets).
  - **Read-only files.** Format document no longer writes a read-only file (the project's
    formatter wrote the model past Monaco's guard). Change line endings refuses a file set
    read-only in the session. The lock on a file that isn't UTF-8 shows it read-only at once.
  - **Maximized groups.** A hidden group's maximize no longer pulls files opened from the
    Explorer into it (D398).
  - **Still open:** secret values still show in the diff editor, Search and the agent's diff
    cards (D393 limits masking to the editor).
- **Checks:** unit tests (new cases for each fix), the guard's Rust tests
  (`only_the_writing_forms_settle`), clippy, and the full UI suite on the owner's machine.

### D408 — What the full UI suite on the owner's machine turned up

The full suite ran locally (D400: CI's minutes are spent): 279 of 281 scripts passed on the build
before D407, 6 skipped. What it found, and what the D407 rerun found:
- **Wide activity bar badges** (scm-m7-6): D404's trimmed badge kept its vertical padding only
  until `.is-wide`'s `padding: 0 3px` reset it, so "1234" was 6 px tall; `.is-wide` sets
  `padding-inline` only.
- **A script that never ran:** tasks-m7-12 said `"platforms": ["windows"]`, which matches no
  platform (the runner compares with Node's `win32`), so it was skipped everywhere. It's
  `win32` now.
- **The guard's self-unpause, shown:** on the old build, git-guard-m7-117's new steps failed:
  after the refresh, git ran in the paused repository. That is the bug D407 fixed.
- **A regression in D407 itself:** recording the repository Initialize repository made (meant
  for folders a sandboxed command ran in) happened everywhere, so every later change from a
  terminal (a branch, a remote, a worktree) paused git in repositories no sandboxed command came
  near; git-m6-38, features-m6-47 and agent-m7-5 failed, and a merge test showed "Git is paused".
  It records only inside a folder the guard watches now (Rust test
  `a_repository_no_sandboxed_command_came_near_is_never_paused`).

### D409 — The chat details panel as Claude Code's, and right-click menus on Usage and Customize

- **Why:** the owner compared our chat details panel with Claude Code's desktop session panel
  and asked for what ours lacked.
- **Context:**
  - A **Compact session** button is always there once the chat has messages, beside "N until
    auto-compact" (`untilAutoCompact`: 80% of the conversation's budget, 70% of the window or a
    channel's cap, as `needsCompaction` decides). It replaces the "Summarize now" link that only
    showed past 70%. An external agent's chat sends its `/compact` instead, and shows no count:
    it manages its own context.

    until loaded.
  - Built-in tools fold open to each tool's share, scaled like the row.
- **Environment:** the branch row switches branch (`git.checkout`'s picker) for the open folder.
- **Changes:** Create PR is a button on the changes' line, not a link under it.
- **Reordering:** each card's header shows a grip on hover. Dragging it moves the card
  (`agent.moveDetailsCard { card, before? }`, so agents and tests can too), and the order is
  kept for every chat (global state `agentDetails.order`, `sanitizeOrder`, `moveCard`).
- **Left out:** Remote Control (no such feature here) and a per-tool list for MCP servers (each
  server's total is listed).

### D410 — Agents named when a chat has two; another folder's chats keep their model's logo; the drag preview rounded in flush

- **Names:** a chat with one agent names no one; a group chat names every speaker. A solo chat
  only named the agent switched in (a handoff), so the first agent's replies looked nameless
  beside the second's. Now, once a second agent has answered, replies are named wherever the
  speaker changes, the first reply of the chat included (`speakerHeader`). A chat with one
  agent still shows no names, as the owner wants. Test: `chat-two-agents-m7-120`.
- **Logos:** another folder's chats (listed when no folder is open, or after this folder's)
  showed today's default model's logo: their rows (`OtherChat`) didn't carry the model that
  answered (D364/D405 only covered this folder's). They read `usedModel` (or the chat's model)
  from the saved chat too.
- **Drag preview:** a dragged group's preview used `--radius-lg`, which is 0 in the flush panel
  style, so it was square there and rounded in floating. It uses `--radius-lifted` (10px in
  both).

### D411 — Change bars line up with the editor in files with stray carriage returns

- `docs/decisions.md` (stored byte for byte, with `\r\r\r\n` endings) showed one change bar down
  the whole file, while its diff tab said "No changes". The editor (Monaco) ends a line at a lone
  `\r`, and its text comes back with every break as the file's line ending; `splitLines` split on
  `\n` only, so the index had a third of the editor's lines and every one compared as changed.
- `splitLines` now ends a line at `\r\n`, `\n` or a lone `\r`, like the editor, and lines compare
  without any of the three. Lines keep their own terminators, so applying a change still joins back
  byte for byte. Its callers (change bars, Stage / Revert change, the agent's read tracking, the
  notebook diff, worktree agents) all line up with the editor's line numbers, so they all needed
  this; staging a hunk in such a file no longer hits the wrong lines.
- The bar's click still opens the diff tab rather than VS Code's inline peek (D201).

### D412 — A restored tab's file is selected in the explorer; the two logs' line endings cleaned up

- **Explorer:** a file tab restored with its folder (at startup, or reopening the folder) wasn't
  selected in the explorer, and clicking its tab or into the file didn't select it either. The
  explorer follows the active tab as soon as the tab is there, which was before its tree had
  listed: the reveal found no tree and did nothing, but the tab and file were remembered as
  revealed, so switching to the same tab never tried again. Once a tree has listed, the
  explorer now forgets what it revealed and follows the active tab again
  (`explorer-restored-m7-121`).
- **`docs/decisions.md` and `docs/manual-test.md`:** every line before D365 ended in `\r\r\r\n`
  (and `\r\r\r\r\n` in the manual tests): plain newlines converted to CRLF several times over,
  which the editor shows as two blank lines between every line. Each run of `\r`s before a `\n`
  was one newline, so both files are back to plain `\n` with the text unchanged; editing them no
  longer needs the byte-level care AGENTS.md asked for.

### D413 — The Describe it chip's icon, popular extensions without the built-in icon theme, editor menu icons

- **Describe it…** (new agent): the chip laid out its sparkles icon inline at full size, so it sat
  on the text's baseline and looked too big. It's a centred flex row now, the icon at
  `--size-icon-sm`.
- **Popular extensions** (D406) is our own fixed list, not the store's ranking. Material Icon Theme
  came off it: it's built in and the default file icon theme, so offering to install it read as a
  mistake. Path IntelliSense took its place (on Open VSX, and in the table of extensions the IDE
  runs).
- **Editor menu icons:** every built-in row of the editor's context menu has one now. Format
  document with… / Format selection with… (`sliders-horizontal`), Edit with AI… (`sparkles`), and
  the gutter's Enable / Disable breakpoint (`circle-dot` / `circle-minus`) had none. Extensions'
  `editor/context` items keep only the icon they bring.

### D414 — The IDE account is live: its server set, tokens refreshed and kept in the keychain

- **The service exists** (a separate private repository, Firebase): product.json's `accountsUrl`
  is `https://jonna.dev`, so Sign in in the Accounts menu works for everyone. The contract is
  docs/accounts.md as D140 wrote it; the server's handback added what's below.
- **Refresh:** access tokens last 90 days, refresh tokens a year, and refresh tokens rotate (each
  works once and ends the old access token). `accounts::check` asks `/api/me` again and on a 401
  refreshes once; the new pair is saved before anything else can fail, and one mutex keeps two
  checks (or a check and a sign-out) from spending the same refresh token. A refused refresh
  (400 `invalid_grant`) or a 401 after it signs out here too; a server that can't be reached
  keeps the saved profile.
- **The profile is re-read** at startup and then at most hourly (window focus), so a new plan or
  name shows without signing in again. Before, the profile from sign-in was kept forever.
- **Tokens in the OS keychain** (the D207 vault, one credential per profile folder like provider
  keys): `account.json` keeps the server and the profile only. With no keychain (headless Linux,
  a locked one) the tokens stay in the owner-only file as before; a pre-D414 file's tokens move
  to the keychain the first time they're read.
- **Sign out** revokes the refresh token (the server ends the session for either).
- **Avatars:** GitHub sign-ins use `avatars.githubusercontent.com`, Google ones a public
  `{base}/api/avatar/{id}`; both pass the avatar check already (D140), so nothing changed there.
- Session code moved to `accounts/session.rs` (stored session, keychain, check); `mod.rs` keeps
  the browser sign-in. Tested with a fake keychain and a small local server (refresh and
  rotation, refused refresh, offline, another server's session).

### D415 — A channel's conversation keeps its name; demo chats for the website's screenshots

- **Bug:** a channel's or direct message's own conversation (still opened by `agent.openChannel`
  and by agents' posts since D291 made channels plain chats) was renamed by its first message:
  first to the message's text, then to the model's `<title>`, so "#general" became the
  conversation's topic in the tab and the Chats list. Such a conversation is now marked
  (`keepsTitle`, set whenever its room is opened): its first message doesn't rename it and no
  title is asked for, for the built-in agent and external ones alike. One renamed before this
  gets the room's name back when opened. `channels-m7-15` checks the title after the first post.
- **The website's screenshots** (`website-handoff/`, not tracked) were retaken at 1600×1000 with a
  demo project and scripted chats: the mock model (`demoScripted`) answers a few ordinary prompts
  with realistic work (a plan, searches, reads, two edits, the tests, a wrap-up), the team in a
  group chat, and short answers for older chats. `MOCK_OLLAMA_MODEL` / `MOCK_OLLAMA_CONTEXT` give
  the mock a real-looking model name and context window, and estimated token counts; unset, the
  mock answers as the tests expect.

### D416 — Caches bounded by size, not entry count

A post about T3 Code (its parsed search cache held 8,192 entries whatever their size; a byte
budget cut retained memory by 85% in its test) prompted a pass over ours. Most were already
right: the browser's network log (2 MB a body, 64 MB in all), remote images (64 MB), and the
rest hold small fixed-size things (when clauses, globs, ghost text, store metadata, path checks).
Three weren't:
- **Chat search** (D331) kept the text of up to 400 saved chats between searches: a count, and a
  long chat with pasted logs can be megabytes. Now 16 MB in all, 2 MB a chat; one evicted or
  bigger is read from the transcript store again on the next search.
- **@docs** (D204, D233) kept every source's index read since startup, and its decoded vectors
  (a 500-page source embedded is tens of megabytes), with no limit at all. Now 48 MB of indexes
  (sized by their saved JSON) and 64 MB of vectors; evicted ones are read again from app data.
- **Diagrams and formulas** in Markdown (D172) kept 64 renders each, oldest first by insertion
  (not use). Now 8 MB of diagram SVG (2 MB each) and 2 MB of formulas (256 KB each), least
  recently used first; the key (the source) is counted too.

`core/cache` has the shared `SizedCache` (DOM-free, unit-tested). Not changed: loaded chats stay
in memory until closed, as VS Code's do; that's the session list, not a cache.

### D417 — Source-available: PolyForm Shield, licensing files, and a public export

D13 said closed source. The first public release changes that: the IDE is source-available under
the **PolyForm Shield License 1.0.0** (the owner's choice over the Functional Source License,
which turns into Apache 2.0 after two years, and over a custom text). It allows any use except
providing a product that competes with the IDE, paid or free.

- `LICENSE` is the license verbatim with the required copyright notice; `COMMERCIAL-LICENSING.md`,
  `TRADEMARKS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md` explain it. `package.json` and
  `Cargo.toml` name it instead of `UNLICENSED`.
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists every production npm package (with its license text) and every
  Rust crate (with its license); `npm run notices` regenerates it. The logos in
  `src/assets/brands` have their license and sources beside them.
- The README leads with what the website says and no longer claims that everything ships under
  permissive licenses: the app is source-available, its dependencies are permissive.
- `docs/release-notes.md` starts again at 0.1.0, the first public version; the milestone notes
  (m7.x) stay in this repository's history.
- `product.json` `issuesUrl` points at the public repository's issues.
- **The public repository is an export.** `.publicignore` lists the working documents that stay
  private (the website handoff, the agent's memory, feature gaps, long-term goals, audits, the
  owner's checklists), and `node scripts/publish-public.mjs` copies the last commit without them into the
  public repository's folder, after checking that no file carries a personal home-folder path.
  It never commits or pushes. `PLAN.md` and `AGENTS.md` say that those documents may be missing.
  *(Replaced by D418: the export was used once, for the first release.)*

### D418 — One repository: the public one is where the work happens

D417 kept a private workspace and exported it to the public repository. After the first release
(0.1.0) the owner works in the public repository directly, so there is one repository and no
export.

- The private workspace is frozen as a record of the earlier history. Nothing is copied from it
  any more; `.publicignore` and `scripts/publish-public.mjs` were never part of this repository.
- The working documents D417 held back (the feature-gaps list, the long-term goals, audits, the
  owner's checklists) are not here. `PLAN.md` and `AGENTS.md` say to use the issue tracker where
  one of them is named.
- Releases are tagged here (`docs/releasing.md`).
- `.gitattributes` keeps text files with LF line endings in every checkout: on Windows, Git's
  CRLF conversion made the formatter (`npm run lint`) reject every file.
- The linter reports nothing now, so a new warning stands out. Two rules are off in `biome.json`:
  `noDescendingSpecificity` (false alarms across the stylesheets) and `noTemplateCurlyInString`
  (`${…}` in plain strings is deliberate here: task, launch and MCP placeholders). The debugger's
  bootloader keeps bare `require("fs")`, since it runs inside the user's own Node.

### D419 — External agents are their chat's agent, a guide for them, custom editor fixes

The owner asked Claude Code (an external agent, in a chat) for an extension that makes the IDE a
game editor. It wrote an ordinary VS Code extension, never read the extension guide, and couldn't
have installed the result. Reading why turned up one cause and several gaps.

- **An external agent's calls are its chat's (the cause).** The caller kind `acp` was checked in
  ten places and created nowhere: every call an external agent made through the lent MCP server
  (D211) ran as `{ kind: "mcp" }`, an anonymous client. Its questions were a modal dialog instead
  of a card in the chat, the chat's access mode didn't apply, nothing tied a command to the chat
  (tabs it opened, pull request watches), and commands that accept agents refused it. Now a chat
  that borrows the server gets a token of its own: the server's, a dot, a random key
  (`chatToken`, `core/mcp/agentAccess.ts`). The Rust server accepts the token with or without a
  key (`mcp/http.rs` `authorized`), the handler passes the key along with each call
  (`BridgeRequest.chat`), and the MCP extension runs calls whose key it knows as
  `{ kind: "acp", agent, session }`. The key rides on the token because both transports already
  carry it (an HTTP header; the stdio proxy's environment variable), so neither changed. A key
  the window doesn't know (a chat that ended) is an MCP client again. Any other client of the
  server is unchanged.
- **A guide for agents that aren't the IDE's own.** `help.agentGuide` (read-only, `agent:
  "core"`, so it is among the listed tools) returns what the IDE's agent has in its prompt and an
  external one never saw: this isn't VS Code, how commands and `ide://` state are reached, which
  commands drive the debugger, tests, terminals, browser and git, where the documentation is.
  `{ topic: "extensions" }`: which format to choose, how to load, check, install and update one,
  where its log is. The MCP server's instructions point at it. Text in
  `extensions/help/agentGuide.ts` (DOM-free, tested). A listed tool, not only instructions: some
  clients don't show a server's instructions to their model.
- **Agents can load and install a folder.** `extensions.loadUnpacked` and
  `extensions.installFromFolder` were hidden from every agent. They are reachable now for the
  user and an agent in a chat (the IDE's own or an external one): the agent must name the folder,
  the "change the IDE" question is asked in the chat even with full access, and the extension's
  permissions are asked as for any install. Extensions and MCP clients outside a chat are
  refused, as `extensions.installPermanently` refuses them. Installing the same folder again
  replaces the installed copy, which is how a folder-installed extension is updated; the command's
  description and the guide say so.
- **The guide says which format to choose** (`docs/extensions.md` "Choosing a format"): the IDE's
  own sandboxed format first, the same in Node when the sandbox is the obstacle, a VS Code
  extension when it must also run in VS Code or already exists. And where an extension's log and
  unsupported calls are read (`ide://extensions?id=`, `extensions.try`, `ide://ext/<id>/vscode`):
  agents had these, the external ones weren't told.
- **VS Code shim, custom editors.** `activeCustomEditorId` is set (the active tab's viewer id);
  a custom editor's tabs show `editor/title` buttons (`workbench/titleActions.ts`, shared with
  the text editor); `vscode.openWith` honors its view type (`"default"`: the text editor) and,
  with `vscode.open`, a column beside (`ide.editor.open`'s `with`); `WebviewPanel.active` /
  `visible` follow the tab (`viewerState` from `extensions/viewers.ts`, for code-page viewers)
  and `onDidChangeViewState` fires; a custom text editor keeps 100 earlier texts of its document
  for the `undo` / `redo` commands; `contributes.jsonValidation` works in both formats
  (`Contributions.jsonSchemas` → the editor's JSON service; no schemas from the network).
- **Not done:** a custom text editor's document is still written to the file at each edit (no
  unsaved state of its own), so `isDirty` is the shim's own flag. The build-extension skill is
  still the IDE's agent's only; `help.agentGuide` covers the same ground for external ones.
- **Tests:** `mcp/tests.rs` (the token with a key), `core/extensions/vscode/shim.test.ts`
  (openWith, panel state, undo / redo), `thirdParty.test.ts` and `editor/jsonSchemas.test.ts`
  (jsonValidation), `help/agentGuide.test.ts`. Not run in the GUI in this change: see
  `docs/manual-test.md` D419.

### D420 — After the first extension built that way: fewer questions, pages under handles, tabs that come back

The owner had Claude Code build and restyle the game editor extension with D419 in place. Four
things showed.

- **One question for one action.** An external agent asks its own permission question before it
  uses an MCP tool ("may I use ide_run_command?"), and then the IDE asked whether the command may
  run. The first says less and the IDE's policy decides every such call anyway, so a request
  whose title names one of the lent server's tools (`mcp__<server>__…`, `isIdeToolRequest` in
  `core/mcp/agentAccess.ts`) is allowed without asking (`acp.ts`). Only that form is recognized
  (Claude Code's); an agent that names its tools another way still asks twice. What the IDE asks
  is unchanged: "Change the IDE" once per chat ("Allow for this chat"), `agent.ideControl: false`
  to never ask.
- **Resize handles above pages.** Pages in the iframe layer and the handles were both at
  `--z-sticky`, and the layer comes later, so a page covered half of a handle's hover line and of
  its 6px grab area. Handles are one above (`workbench.css`).
- **A VS Code package's pages get the IDE's tokens.** The bridge applied only the `--vscode-*`
  variables of the theme message and swallowed the rest; it sets the IDE's own tokens too
  (`--bg-surface`, `--radius-sm`, `--text-md`…, `vscode/views.ts`). VS Code's variables carry no
  radius, shadow or type scale, so a page could not look like the IDE; with both, one stylesheet
  serves the IDE and VS Code (`var(--bg-surface, var(--vscode-sideBar-background))`).
- **The composer's Send icon is back.** `corner-down-left` (D385) was among `IconName`'s names
  but not in `scripts/build-icons.mjs`'s list, so the sprite had no symbol for it and the button
  drew an empty square. It is in the list and the sprite; `ui/iconNames.test.ts` fails when a
  name has no symbol or a symbol no name.
- **Files open in an extension's viewer come back after a restart.** They are `persist: false`
  for the dock, which restores its layout before extensions load and drops tabs of unknown
  types. The open files per viewer are now saved with the folder's state
  (`extensions.viewerTabs`, `viewers.ts`) and reopened when the extension registers the viewer.
  They return in the main group, in the background: their group and which one was active aren't
  kept (a real fix would let the dock hold a tab for a type that isn't there yet).
- Not run in the GUI: `docs/manual-test.md` D420.
